The study, which involved 3 years of intermittent participant observation & 44 interviews with NSF office personnel, program directors, & evaluation contractors, indicates that evaluations are heavily influenced by the way the work is organized & produced, as well as by the usual considerations that shape evaluations elsewhere. Two primary issues are identified as critical to the successful establishment of an evaluation office: (1) the evolution of an evaluation culture within the organization, & (2) the management of a semi-internal/external evaluation production process. 19 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: GOVERNMENTAL BUREAUCRATIZATION: GENERAL PROCESSES AND AN ANOMALOUS CASE
abstract: THE DEVELOPMENT OF BUREAUCRATIC GOVERNMENT HAS BEEN ACCOUNTED FOR IN SEVERAL WAYS. SOME HAVE LOOKED TO CIRCUMSTANCES THOUGHT TO RENDER GREATER RATIONALIZATION A NECESSITY, OTHERS HAVE SEEN THIS PROCESS AS THE OUTCOME OF THE LONG STRUGGLE BETWEEN THE PRINCE & THOSE WITH INDEPENDENT POWERS, WHILE OTHERS HAVE LOOKED TO THE CHARACTERISTICS OF THE SOCIAL ENVIRONMENT OF GOVERNMENT TO TRY TO IDENTIFY THOSE FEATURES OF SOCIAL STRUCTURE & CULTURE WHICH PROVIDE FERTILE SOIL FOR GROWTH OF BUREAUCRACIES. ALL OF THESE APPROACHES HAVE STRESSED THE ROLE OF CENTRAL ELITES. IT IS INSUFFICIENT TO VIEW BUREAUCRATIZATION AS A PROCESS IN ALL RESPECTS INITIATED FROM ABOVE BY PRINCE OR PRESIDENT & IMPOSED UPON THE REST OF US WITH MORE OR LESS RESISTANCE. THE PROFOUND CHANGES IN SOCIAL STRUCTURE--'MODERNIZATION'--RAISE THE POSSIBILITY OF POPULAR DESIRE, EVEN IN THE FORM OF OVERWHELMING DEMAND, FOR A MORE BUREAUCRATIC GOVERNMENT. IN THE CONTEXT OF FRENCH HISTORY, THE GREAT REVOLUTION OF 1789 HAS LEFT A BODY OF UNIQUE & REMARKABLE DOCUMENTS, THE CAHIERS DE DOLEANCES. AS PART OF THE CONVOCATION OF THE ESTATES-GENERAL, MORE THAN 40,000 RU COMMUNITIES, UR OCCUPATIONAL GROUPS, ASSEMBLIES OF NOBLES OR CLERGY PRODUCED LISTS OF GRIEVANCES IN WHICH THEY RECORDED FOR THEIR DELEGATES THEIR DISSATISFACTIONS WITH SOCIETY & THEIR PROPOSALS FOR A BETTER FUTURE. THE BETTER FUTURE INCLUDED NOT ONLY LIBERTY, QUALITY, THE END OF THE SEIGNIORIAL REGIME, & THE RIGHT TO PURSUE PROFIT-MAKING ACTIVITIES, BUT ALSO, A FAR MORE BUREAUCRATIC GOVERNMENT. THIS OBSERVATION JOINS WITH OTHER RECENT WORK WHICH SEES ADMINISTRATIVE CHANGE AS THE CENTRAL TRANSFORMATION WROUGHT BY THE REVOLUTION. AA.

title: A Temporal Analytical Approach to Decentralization: Lessons from Brazil's Health Sector
abstract: This article introduces a new concept to the study of decentralization processes: policy dynamism. At its core is the notion that the sequential and temporal process of health decentralization affect the nature of intergovernmental relationships and municipal bureaucratic capacity. Examining the case of Brazil, I argue that the rush to decentralize health services to municipalities has, in the absence of sufficient financial and technical assistance from the federal and state governments, increased state-municipal conflict over the management of health policy, limiting municipalities' ability to increase bureaucratic capacity. Consequently, some states have attempted to recentralize reforms, generating further conflict between both subnational levels of government. While some municipalities have tried to overcome these problems by creating associations and working with international organizations, several bureaucratic obstacles remain. This article attributes these outcomes not to federal institutions and economic constraints (the traditional approach in the literature) but rather to the noninstitutional, temporal policy dynamics of decentralization. Adapted from the source document.

title: When Laws Backfire: Unintended Consequences of Public Policy
abstract: Why is it that so many laws perpetually fall short of their intended goals? Why haven't humanity's greatest minds managed to solve basic social ills? This article amasses considerable evidence suggesting that (a) law is inherently incapable of producing major social change because legal restrictions unsettle social equilibria & generate counteractions & (b) the subconscious purpose behind many laws is the promotion of social solidarity for its own sake. The author concludes that laws & the politics that forge them are essentially religious practices that have little basis in rational analysis. Thus can be explained both the perpetual failure of many laws & their irreconcilable popularity. 83 References. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Inc., copyright 2004.]

title: Governmentality in Motion: 25 Years of Ethiopia's Experience of Famine and Migration Policy
abstract: In the 25 years since the 1984-85 Great Sahelian Famine, the Ethiopian state has used the management of mobility as a tool to control the poorest of its citizens. In this paper I examine three cases: the forced resettlement of people during the 1980s, the repatriation of refugees during the mid-1990s and the more recent resettlement of food insecure people in the early 2000s. I argue that in each of these cases, people's movements have been controlled so as to undermine their agency with the net effect of increasing their vulnerability. Such strategies have transformed and reinforced class, ethnic and religious hierarchies to such an extent that those being managed have become silently complicitous in their own exploitation. The paper argues that analyses of how governmentality functions should be set in motion, and that mobility management strategies may be a central tool for promoting governmentality on wider levels. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: BUREAUCRACY AND PARTICIPATION IN FOUR WISCONSIN CITIES
abstract: The level of bur'ization (specialized & diff'iated decisionmaking units within an authoritative system) & participation (group & individual activity intended to influence those decisions) is studied in 4 Wise cities: Madison, Racine, Kenosha & Green Bay. Empirical data are presented on form of gov, city employees, civil service, personnel officers, planning, budgeting, party activity, voting turnout, & the number of voluntary assoc's of various types. Fairly consistent patterns are found in the cities, from data taken from PO surveys as well as available documents. Madison was the most highly bur'ized & participatory of the 4 cities, Green Bay the least. The implications of these structural properties of local pol'al systems are discussed. More extensive data & theory are contained in a published book under the same name. AA.

title: Social Tensions at the Municipal Level. Methods of Assessing the Administration Performance
abstract: The mayor of the town of Mouravlenko (oil producing area in the Russian North) shares the experiences in monitoring the ratings of local executive & legislative bodies at the municipal level -- against the background of the all-Russian successes & failings in economic & social policies. The author has construed original methods to measure the degree of social tension in an area on the basis of the statistical data accumulated by municipalities in the course of their work. The results are periodically compared to sociological measuring of public feeling, a procedure demonstrating a growing degree of both methods co-incidence. Tables, Figures. Adapted from the source document.

title: Current Trends in Public Policy in Higher Education: A Comparative Analysis
abstract: This paper analyzes current trends in public policy in higher education in the US, Canada, & some countries of the European Union. These policies reflect the transformation of public management; some of them respond to the current demands of globalization & the information age. This analysis shows the expanding role of the state in the governance of higher education; concern for the accessibility & diversification of the services offered; progressive financial disengagement of the state; establishment of performance indicators; & internationalization of institutions & informational restructuring. These trends can be found, in varying degrees, in higher education systems on both sides of the Atlantic. 62 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucracy, Justice and Legal Pluralism: An Exploration Concerning Spaces of Power in Oaxaca
abstract: This article presents an ethnographic approach to the Indigenous Defense Procuracy in Oaxaca, an institution that embodies a dual aspect of the State. On the one hand, it is the expression of a State that promotes legal pluralism & the defense of indigenous rights. On the other hand, it is the materialization of a State that perpetuates the defenselessness of Oaxacan Indians through a cluster of corrupt practices, arbitrary abuses, disorganization & inefficiency. Based on ethnographic work in this institution, this work approaches this apparent contradiction, arguing that ambiguity & disorder are constitutive of the State & of the ways it establishes its domination. Through the ambiguity & illegibility of its own discourses & practices the State introduces the promise or anticipation of justice, while at the same time it shatters its fulfillment. References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Generic Social Work Skills in Social Administration: The Example of Persuasion
abstract: It is argued that though their educational preparations differ, both social welfare administrators & direct service workers require a basic set of social work practice skills. These generic skills are defined & related to the effectiveness of human service administration. Focus is on persuasive communication tactics, & various strategies are suggested by which administrators & direct service workers can maximize their utility; two case studies are offered as illustration. 1 Table, 33 References. K. Hyatt

title: Government policy on women offenders: Labour's legacy and the Coalition's challenge
abstract: After 13 years of a majority Labour government, a minority Conservative government was elected in the UK in May 2010. Within weeks, the Conservatives had created a Coalition government with the Liberal Democrats. In developing its policies on a range of social issues, the new administration will need to take account of what its immediate predecessor achieved and the lessons that Labour failed to take from its forerunners. In relation to women offenders, such an analysis shows that, while towards the end of its third and last term, Labour began to deal more effectively with the social exclusion needs of women offenders, through a range of community-based initiatives, its approach to diverting women towards such assistance and away from custody was, at best, half-hearted. The result is that more women than ever are being remanded and sentenced to custody. This came as a surprise only to those who had not noticed that this approach had also failed in the 1980s and 1990s. The Coalition might like to take note. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Individual Freedom and Capitalist Power Relationships
abstract: Power -- its nature & exercise -- in capitalist society is analyzed in Weberian terms as being of the legal type, & therefore projecting itself as bureaucratic authority. An analogy is drawn between the impersonal rationality of bureaucratic rule in the political sphere & the equally impersonal direction of capital in the SE sphere. S. Karganovic.

title: The impact of social research on education policy and reform in the Philippines*
abstract: This article examines the impact of social research on education policy and reform in the Philippines. It begins with a brief description of the key issues in Philippine education followed by analysis of three major studies conducted in the late 1990s that made specific policy recommendations on responses to inadequate quality of the Philippine education system and structural inefficiencies in its governing bureaucracy. The article then assesses the ways in which these studies were used in the policy process and their impact on education policy reform, with a particular focus on the key period 1998-2001. Consideration is also given to the socio-political context of education policy-making in the Philippines as well as on the mechanisms used to disseminate the research results and bring them to the attention of key decision-makers. The assessment shows that even overcoming the familiar reluctance of politicians to take account of research results does not guarantee effective implementation. While the studies considered in the article were policy-oriented and endowed with a high degree of credibility, in terms of methods, problems identified and proposed reforms that related to an existing policy agenda, implementation encountered numerous difficulties. Educational bureaucracies have their own agenda, and furthermore the reform process involves a wide range of social actors, some of whom represent powerful political constituencies. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: U.S. Defense Policy Options: The 1990s and Beyond
abstract: The Pentagon bureaucracy will continue as a major obstacle to rational national security policy through the 1990s.  The need to overhaul the US national security strategy is discussed.

title: Strange Parallels across Eurasia
abstract: Victor Lieberman's Strange Parallels is the culmination of an extended effort to compare many major polities of the Eurasian continent in the early modern age. Lieberman finds common cycles of administrative integration and disintegration that were increasingly synchronized over time. Although he does not give a single-factor explanation for this synchronization, his model provides a common vocabulary for political, economic, and cultural analysis that can inspire all comparative world historians. China, however, is missing from this analysis, even though its dynastic cycles share much with the other polities. China's ambivalent position in Eurasia deserves comparative study because of divergent interpretations of Chinese dynastic relations with frontier warriors, the strong influence of Chinese trade and power on its neighbors' polities, and China's long-lasting cultural and bureaucratic tradition. Adapted from the source document.

title: The limits of peer production: Some reminders from Max Weber for the network society
authors: Kreiss, Daniel; Finn, Megan; Turner, Fred
abstract: In the last few years, a powerful consensus has emerged among scholars of digitally enabled peer production. In this view, digital technologies and social production processes are driving a dramatic democratization of culture and society. Moreover, leading scholars now suggest that these new, hyper-mediated modes of living and working are specifically challenging the hierarchical structures and concentrated power of bureaucracies. This paper first maps the assumptions underlying the new consensus on peer production so as to reveal the sources of its coherence. It then revisits Max Weber's account of bureaucracy. With Weber in mind, the paper aims to expose analytical weaknesses in the consensus view and offer a new perspective from which to study contemporary digital media. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright holder.]

title: Secular Culture, Religious Culture, Civic Ethos and Public Administration of Symbol
abstract: Analyzes the judiciary's role in the construction of a public culture, specifically a civic ethos, using decisions rendered by the Supreme Court of Canada since 1982 as illustrations. Framing public issues in cultural & ethical terms is initially taken as part of a secularizing trend. In turn, norms & values become part of a public administration of meaning that is incorporated into law & imposed on religious actors & organizations. 89 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Dependency, Development and Constituency Appeals as Determinants of State Entrepreneurship in Industrializing Nations: The Taiwan Case
abstract: The developmental history of the Republic of China on Taiwan is examined to explore possible reasons for a state's becoming involved in entrepreneurial activities. In particular, two models that conceive state entrepreneurship as primarily a reward to the state's economic technocrats, or as a macroeconomic management device, are compared. State entrepreneurship evidently is a result of a complex interaction among growth conditions, external dependency, & the status of competing elite constituencies. This conforms to the predictions of the technobureaucracy model; the Taiwan case is consistent with several of its specific hypotheses about what influences the relative amount of rewards directed to the technocratic elite, although there clearly are some "developmental promotion" effects as well. 4 Tables. HA

title: Understanding the New Order: Bureaucratic Pluralism in Indonesia
abstract: Uses secondary empirical data on the military penetration of Indonesia's upper-level bureaucracy in 1981 (eg, % of each agency that is military, whether agency directors are military or civilian) & a case study of regional-level bureaucratic policy making to argue that Indonesia's New Order, which has ruled since 1966, can be described as limited bureaucratic pluralism. General Suharto's rule remains firm, & Indonesia's bureaucracy is primarily a military tool used to police internal security & promote economic growth. Nevertheless, civilian agencies do enjoy some autonomy, which is tied to the personalities involved & their access to President Suharto. It provides civilian agencies with some freedom to set policy related to industrial development, public works, & mining & energy. It is concluded that Indonesia's New Order is repressive & powerful, but not monolithic & homogenized. This conclusion of limited bureaucratic pluralism is placed on a spectrum of opinions that range from monism to polycentrism to particularism. 1 Table, 26 References. E. Blackwell

title: Civil Society and New Modes of Governance in Poland
abstract: The paper is focused on the introduction and operation of a novel model of EU-induced structure of governance networks-composed of public administration, business and civil society actors. It takes up a case of institutional structures to manage EU structural funds in Poland. In particular, the role of social partners, i.e. representatives of non-governmental organizations in the European Regional Development Fund-related region-level and nation-level steering and monitoring committees is analyzed. Following a brief exposition of regionalization principles, arrangement for regional development policy in Poland and changes induced by the country's accession to the EU, legal and institutional frameworks for the inclusion of social partners in the committees responsible for the programming, management and evaluation of the European Regional Development Fund are scrutinized. Empirical evidence of social partners' participation in the proceedings of such selected committees is introduced and analyzed. Opportunities, challenges and dilemmas of civil society actors faced with new modes of governance are discussed. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucrats as "Social Engineers": Federal Welfare Programs in Herbert Hoover's America
abstract: Historians studying twentieth-century US reform often seek to analyze the ideologies of political leaders separately from the institutions that these same leaders created. Such emphasis on ideas, as opposed to actions, has led "revisionist" US historians to argue that the presidencies of Herbert Hoover & Franklin D. Roosevelt were "conceptually continuous." Based on historical studies & government documents & reports, an examination of the major social welfare programs undertaken by the US federal government in the 1920s disputes this claim. Examination of the operations of the federal bureaucracy instead of the rhetoric of politicians demonstrates the existence of decided policy differences between the Hoover & Roosevelt eras. Background is provided for increased understanding of some of the policy implications of the US's contemporary welfare debate -- particularly concerning "rehabilitation" strategies & rationales for action in the social welfare field. Modified HA.

title: The Approaches of Public Administration in Solving the Romany Problem in the Czech Republic: An Outline of Issues
abstract: Recognizing the need to address the problems of the Romany minority in the Czech Republic of the new millennium, some of the most prominent issues are identified & discussed, including: (1) the definition of the Romany as an ethnic minority, (2) ethnic minority policy during the communist era & their objectives of assimilation & integration; the consequences for the Romany population, (3) a chronological periodization in the Czech social policy targeting the Romany in the postcommunist period: (A) November 1989 to June 1992, (B) 1992-1996, (C) 1997-1998, & (D) 1998 - present, (4) the social exclusion & stigmatization of the Romany & their economic difficulties (poverty, unemployment, inadequate housing, & incomplete education), (5) strategies on the levels of national & local government in dealing with these problems; the merits of external & internal assistance. It is concluded that the exclusion, marginalization, & stigmatization of the Romany require an enlightened policy on the part of both national & local government. However, such policy can only be developed & implemented when the plight of the Romany in the Czech Republic is recognized by the authorities as a real, urgent, & legitimate problem. Figures, References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucracy and Hierarchy -- what Else!?
abstract: Hierarchy and bureaucracy have been more or less welcomed companions of human civilisation from the very beginning. In almost every culture and epoch, ruling elites and followers, superiors and subordinates can be identified. Hierarchy and bureaucracy are quite flexible, adaptable and they are fairly persistent -- but why could, or even should we see this as a problem? This introduction will first provide a brief history of no change, followed by the second section where the advantages and disadvantages and the contested terrain of hierarchy are elaborated in some length. The discussion focuses on three areas: the functional, social and ethical qualities of hierarchy. In the final section, the chapters of this volume will be briefly introduced. The chapters are grouped into three sections: (I) Fundamentals and historical accounts of bureaucracy, (II) Organisational, cultural and socio-psychological aspects of hierarchy and (III) Alternative views on, and alternatives to hierarchy. Adapted from the source document.

title: Participation's Place in Rural Development: Seeking Clarity through Specificity
authors: Cohen, John M; Uphoff, Norman T
abstract: Over the past few years, development specialists have expressed increasing concern over the lack of progress in altering the plight of the Ru poor. Toward this end they have shifted from the capital investment growth models of the 1960s to the more people-centered basic-needs approaches that increasingly dominated development thinking in the 1970s. In the process, they have turned to a number of related development strategies, one of the most important & least understood of which is popular participation -- defined here as "the involvement of a significant number of persons in situations or actions which enhance their well-being, eg, their income, security, or self-esteem." Increasing numbers of studies & activities are being undertaken to bolster government & donor capacity to promote participation in development programs. Yet despite all these activities, the disturbing fact is that there is little agreement on what participation is, or on its basic dimensions. An attempt is made to provide some order to the emergence of participatory concerns in the development literature, & to offer an elaborated framework that clarifies the notion of Ru-development participation & makes it applicable to total development projects. 3 Figures. Modified HA.

title: Italian Organised Crime: Mafia Associations and Criminal Enterprises
abstract: The article reviews the different forms of organized crime in Italy. To begin with, it focuses on the Sicilian Cosa Nostra & the Calabrian 'Ndrangheta, Italy's two largest & most powerful mafia associations. With their centuries-old histories, articulated structures, sophisticated ritual & symbolic apparatuses & claim to exercise a political dominion, these associations have few parallels in the world of organized crime. In its second section, the article considers other groups & networks that are -- with varying degrees of justification -- also routinely described as organized crime: these range from the Neapolitan camorra to Apulian organized crime & the so-called new "foreign mafie" & other criminal entrepreneurs. Whereas the new Italian & foreign players are likely to expand their activities on Italy's illegal markets, the future of Cosa Nostra & the 'Ndrangheta is more uncertain & largely depends on the decisions made by the public administrations. 41 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Readings in Han Chinese Thought/The Government of the Qin and Han Empires
abstract: Quirky anecdotes such as the one about Zhang Tang who, as a boy, staged a mock trial of rats that had damaged his household's store and who eventually rose to become superintendent of trials - the empire's senior authority for the conduct of legal matters - might have been introduced more frequently in order to sustain the nonspecialist reader's interest.  Other problems to beset the imperial system were the lack of "opposing wills, ideas or argument in public" (p. 197); the failure to develop solutions for the difficulties involved in relations with non-Han peoples; the imperial government's lack of the means to organise economic production; and the reliance on an administration the effective functioning of which required its officials to be unquestioningly loyal, of high intelligence and of proven efficiency.

title: The Politicization of Bureaucracies in Developing Countries: St. Kitts-Nevis, a Case Study
abstract: The political history of Saint Kitts-Nevis (a Caribbean island) & its newly won independence from GB is examined. The state has inherited some British political values, including the theory of "political neutrality" in bureaucratic practice. This traditional approach is being challenged by forces for social change embodied in "bureaucratic activism," which usually results in the politicization of the state's bureaucracy. The characteristics of such bureaucracies are contrasted with those of "nonpoliticized" or "ideal" bureaucracies as defined by Max Weber. A typology of developing bureaucracies is presented, & common traits among administrative systems in less developed countries are identified. Ecological factors, eg, sociocultural, economic, & constitutional, are discussed in relation to Saint Kitts-Nevis. It is concluded that, since government responsibilities must include SE development, the expansion of politics in the state's administration is inevitable. Given the nation's history of relative stability, however, it is predicted that the conflict between social change forces & traditional values will be resolved. K. Carande

title: Rural Women's Access to Health Care in Bangladesh: Swimming Against the Tide?
abstract: Large segments of the population in developing countries are deprived of a fundamental right: access to basic health care. The problem of access to health care is particularly acute in Bangladesh. One crucial determinant of health seeking among rural women is the accessibility of medical care and barriers to care that may develop because of location, financial requirements, bureaucratic responses to the patient, social distance between client and provider, and the sex of providers. This article argues that to increase accessibility fundamental changes are required not only in resource allocation but also in the very structure of health services delivery.

title: The Rise of Post-Bureaucracy: Theorists' Fancy or Organizational Praxis?
authors: Johnson, Phil; Wood, Geoffrey; Brewster, Chris; Brookes, Michael
abstract: Theories of post-bureaucracy point to a breakdown of traditional modes of managerial authority in the face of a range of pressures commonly associated with globalization and technological advance. This may make for a proliferation of alternative practices and/or allow for a genuine sharing of power in the workplace, associated with higher levels of responsible autonomy. Based on the findings of a series of transnational surveys, this article confirms a tendency, over time, for organizations to make greater use of mechanisms to promote responsible autonomy, in a wide range of national contexts. This would seemingly support a central proposition of theories of post-bureaucracy: a tendency for organizations to delegate more power to employees over time, reflecting the breakdown of traditional bureaucratically ordered power relations. At the same time, however, the research highlighted an uneven and contested process of change, reflecting both the persistent effects of national, regional and sectoral modes of regulation, and the non-linear and episodic nature of organizational change. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright.]

title: The Birth and Demise of a Planning Unit in a State Mental Health Department
abstract: The development, over a 5 -- yr period, & the sudden dissolution of the Division of Planning & Evaluation Services of a major state Dept of mental health is described. The new division was set up with federal funds, with the intent to make it permanent. Insights into the effort to establish a rational base of planning in a complex bur'cy are presented. The characteristics of the division are explored in relation to the rest of the Dept of Mental Health & its relationship to the State Mental Health Planning Board & its avisory councils is described. It is found that rational planning & evaluation do not mix well with pol. The peculiar relationship of the Planning Division with the rest of the dept made it more vulnerable to changing admin's than other sections & units. The division's role was rather transitional & it did not have an adequately close liaison with the director's office on matters of policy & planning. Whether a more rational org'al structure will emerge, now that the division is dissolved, remains to be seen. Modified HA.

title: Citation Rankings of Public Administration Journals
abstract: Citation analysis to gauge actual use of public administration journals is proposed as a more suitable method to assess journal worth than prestige surveys. Based on data gathered from 1981-1986 Journal Citation Reports, which accompanies the Social Sciences Citation Index, thirty-five journals are ranked according to Instit for Scientific Information (ISI) citation rank, ISI impact factor, & a field-specific citation indicator. Comparisons made with these citation hierarchies & a prestige ranking confirm the importance of Public Administration Review, Administrative Science Quarterly, American Political Science Review, Administration & Society, & Journal of Policy Analysis & Management, but show differences between prestige & citation ranking of other journals. An appendix lists all prestige survey titles & citation study titles. 7 Tables, 63 References. V. Wagener

title: Municipal Residency Laws: Effects on Police Employment, Compensation, and Productivity
authors: Gonzalez, Rodolfo A; Mehay, Stephen L; Duffy-Deno, Kevin
abstract: An alternative disequilibrium/bureaucracy model of the effects of residency laws in municipal labor markets is developed which assumes that public employee labor markets are characterized by conditions of excess supply, & that public services are produced under noncompetitive conditions. The model also implies that productivity improvements increase rather than decrease labor demand, yielding different results with respect to the wage & employment efforts of residency requirements. The model is tested empirically using data on police officers in 138 large US cities, & results support it more than previous models based on a competitive equilibrium. 3 Tables, 27 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Local Social Policies and the Challenges of Citizen Participation
abstract: This text presents an analysis of the dimensions of participation & the possibilities of enlargement of citizenship, having as reference public policies of education, health, & environment at the local level. The articulating theme is popular participation in public administration & the qualitative transformations in the relationship between state & civil society, as a reference to a turning point & strengthening of public policies centered that emphasize active citizenship. Our challenge is to analyze, on one side, the impacts of participatory practices that point to new configurations of the quality of citizenship, &, on the other side, the characterization of those barriers that have to be overcome to enable the multiplication of management experiences that articulate efficiently complexity & democracy. The analysis is centered on the strengthening of the public space & the opening of public administration to the participation of Civil Society in the formulation of public policies, & in the always complex & contradictory institutionalization of innovative participatory practices that establish ruptures with the existing process. 13 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Public Officials: Details of the Collective Portrait
abstract: Qualitative characteristics of public officialdom in Russia & quantitative changes in its composition during the last several years are analyzed, drawing on 1995/96 data from 647 Russian public officials. The ongoing increase in public official personnel on every level of federal & regional hierarchy may be explained by the fact that after the fall of communism, the Russian Federation found itself in need of a full-fledged bureaucratic apparatus. Measures to provide adequate education & training for new public officials of democratic Russia are described. 6 Tables. J. Klimov

title: Local Budgets -- between Theory and Practice
abstract: The study is based on an on field research both at central and local levels. From this perspective, the study synthesizes the opinions of the main actors at central level involved in the process of projecting and adopting the local budgets. Interviews were conducted with representatives of the Public Administration Parliamentary Commissions, representatives of the Ministry of Public Administration and the Ministry of Finances as well as members of other central institutions with responsibilities related to the topic. The main component of the research though, was the evaluation of the existing situation at local level concerning local budgets making process. Adapted from source document.

title: Bureaucracy and Development in the Sudan
abstract: An analysis of the role of bureaucracy in the socioeconomic & political development of Sudan. Five distinct eras in the political & administrative history of the country since 1954 are delineated, & it is shown that all development plans have failed to achieve their goals. Despite the fact that Sudanese public servants have good educations & relatively high functional capabilities, administrative ineffiency, obsolete structures, bureaucratic infighting, & lack of coordination have caused government policies to be poorly implemented & executed. Modified HA

title: Social Capital and Government Performance in Iowa Communities
abstract: Putnam (1993) provides impressive evidence that the enduring geographic patterns of social capital in Italy influence regional government performance. His work has motivated other scholars to search for a link between social capital & performance among nations & other large subnational entities. The purpose of this study is to extend this line of research to the community level. To accomplish this a unique data set consisting of the opinions of approximately 100 people in each of 114 IA communities was collected. The analyses show a clear relationship: local governments are viewed as more responsive & effective in towns described as high in social capital by their citizens. Additional analyses reveal that social capital is also related to the upkeep of public streets & parks in the communities. Both of these relationships remain significant even after controlling for a variety of socioeconomic factors. 3 Tables, 1 Figure, 45 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Changing University Governance. Newer Contributions of Comparative University Research
abstract: Current diagnosis of the situation & efficiency of Universities in Germany show a crisis scenario of amazing dimensions. In order to overcome their crisis, universities have to be freed from their bureaucratic embrace & political paternalism by the State. New Public Management (NPM) is touted as a solution where the core concept is the new taring of the five regulation mechanisms that today are found in the governance regime of German universities: 1) decrease in governmental regulations of details; 2) increase of control by external stakeholders; 3) decrease of academic self-organization of professors; 4) increase in administrative self-control of universities by principals & middle management; & 5) increase of competition within & between universities regarding financial resources & elite students. A graphic equalizer model illustrates the transformation. References. E. Sanchez

title: Aspects of Inauthenticity
abstract: The concept of inauthenticity as it applies to contemporary society is examined. Human beings have six basic needs that any society must satisfy: affection & solidarity, recognition & esteem, social context, gratification, stability & consistency, & variance in social structure. Industrial societies basically have a bureaucratic structure. Classic bureaucracy exchanged rules to be followed for a promise to meet human needs; modern bureaucracy has largely forgotten those needs, creating an inauthentic society. The personal distress this generates is sometimes called burnout; it would be more valid to see it as response to destructive institutional circumstances. Only a change in the structure of society will make it possible for people's needs to be met. W. H. Stoddard.

title: Organizational Ethics and Bureaucratic Corruption in Chinese School
abstract: This paper takes issue with a central theme in the literature on corruption that a centralized bureaucratic structure necessarily promotes corruption. It argues that the growth of corruption after 1976 was not so much the result of a centralized bureaucratic structure as that of the changing organizational ethics in the schools. In an examination of the schools since 1949, it shows that their structures have not changed radically. But by separating the organizational ethics into their real & ideal dimensions, it demonstrates that despite the continuity in the official goals & codes of ethics, the "real" or fundamental organizational ethic have changed, & new standards of behavior have prompted members to break organizational rules in the more of less decentralized organizational structures. In this paper, I shall argue that while centralized organizational infrastructures do play a role in the growth of corruption in contemporary China, it seem its proliferation results more from the development of a materialistic & bureaucratic structure. A centralized structure may contribute to corruption, but it alone cannot account for the proliferation of corruption in recent decades. The schools are used here as an example of a centralized bureaucratic structure to illustrate my thesis. I shall compare the situation in the post-Mao or Dengist period (1977-1997) with the Maoist one (1949-1976) to demonstrate that a centralized system of control alone is not a sufficient reason for the growth of corruption. Rather, after 1976, it is the prevalence of an acquisitive ethos that triggers its proliferation. Adapted from the source document.

title: Using a Semantic Self-Organizing Web Page-Ranking Mechanism for Public Administration and education
authors: Poulos, Marios; Papaviasopoulos, Sozon; Belesiotis, V S
abstract: In the proposed method for Web page-ranking, a novel theoretic model is introduced and tested by examples of order relationships among IP addresses. Ranking is induced using a convexity feature, which is learned according to these examples using a self-organizing procedure. We consider the problem of self-organizing learning from IP data to be represented by a semi-random convex polygon procedure, in which the vertices correspond to IP addresses. Based on recent developments in our regularization theory for convex polygons and corresponding Euclidean distance based methods for classification, we develop an algorithmic framework for learning ranking functions based on a Computational Geometric Theory. We show that our algorithm is generic, and present experimental results explaining the potential of our approach. In addition, we explain the generality of our approach by showing its possible use as a visualization tool for data obtained from diverse domains, such as Public Administration and Education. Adapted from the source document.

title: Emotional Work of Public Workers
abstract: Work in the public sector encompasses clearly defined tasks, aims, & procedures to which the clients must submit. The clients are required to express their wishes & needs in a highly formal way, on the prescribed & standard forms. The task of public administration is to carry out public services for the users. The state has a monopoly upon certain services; it is their only provider & has no competition, but their users nevertheless expect quality, speed, & affability. The public administrators in Slovenia are more & more convinced that the efficiency of their administration depends first & foremost on the people who perform administrative services. Working with clients demands that the workers be trained in public relations & in emotional control. They are expected to maintain the appropriate attitude with their clients & to control their temper & emotions. 21 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Patients Who Get What They Want: Policy and Power in the Context of Prenatal Care
abstract: Offers a case study of a request for amniocentesis by a middle-class, professional couple in Ontario to analyze some practices employed in the Canadian & US health care systems. Focus is on how these practices can be influenced by participants' technical knowledge, social networks, & willingness to persevere in the face of bureaucratic obstacles to achieve their goal. 30 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Local Power: Risk and Dependence. Fuenlabrada in 1680
abstract: The functioning of the local administration in Fuenlabrada, Spain in 1680, a year of special significance, is documented as exemplifying many other Castillian towns in the relation of the town to the central administration, & in the power struggles between commoners & town officials. In 1680, the two yearly mayors ("alcaldes ordinarios") of Fuenlabrada were summoned because of an accounting variance in the town's debt to Madrid; they were fined & sentenced to prison, where one died. The economic situation in Fuenlabrada at the time of this event is analyzed. Income in Fuenlabrada from proprietors & communal lands was used to pay the heavy debt to Madrid, for functionaries' salaries, & for the celebration of feast days. Fuenlabrada was characterized as dependent on Madrid, & yet tied to the land & local patron saints. The moral of the event is that "it is risky to be a yearly mayor.". 2 Tables, 37 References. M. Pflum

title: How to Abolish Public Housing: Implications and Lessons from Public Management Reform
abstract: The paper examines how public or municipal housing in England & Wales is being abolished & transferred into the housing association sector. A new public management (NPM) analytical framework is adopted to provide seven dimensions: disaggregation, competition, private sector management, economy, hands-on top management, standards of performance, & measurement of outputs. It is argued that there are two NPM meta-themes -- externalization & managerialization. Hypotheses are developed to explain the differential impact of NPM reforms on the municipal housing & housing association sectors. These suggest that housing associations are externalized & highly managerialized organizations, whereas local authorities display lower levels of externalization & limited managerialization. Analysis of the transfer process indicates that externalization is driven by political & ideological approaches to public housing, in addition to NPM dimensions. As local authorities transfer their stock into the housing association sector, they are also likely to develop into similarly managerialized organizations. In conclusion, the NPM framework is demonstrated to need further development while systematic research is required on management reform in social housing provision. The lesson on how to abolish public housing suggests the following policy formula: starve it of resources, create a hostile environment, & wait for it to abolish itself. 3 Tables, 1 Figure, 87 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucratic Itineraries in Colombia. A theoretical and methodological tool to assess managed-care health care systems
authors: Abadia, Cesar Ernesto; Oviedo, Diana G
abstract: Steady increases in the number of Colombians insured by the health care system contrasts with the hundreds of thousands of legal actions interposed to warrant citizen's right to health. This study aims to analyze the relationships among patients' experiences of denials by the system, the country's legal mechanisms, and the functioning of insurance companies and service providing institutions. We conducted a mixed-methods case study in Bogota and present a quantitative description of 458 cases, along with semi- structured interviews and an in-depth illness history. We found that Colombians' denials of care most commonly include appointments, laboratory tests or treatments. Either insurance companies or service providing institutions use the system's legal structure to justify the different kinds of denials. To warrant their right to health care, citizens are forced to interpose legal mechanisms, which are largely ruled in favor, but delays result in a progressive and cumulative pattern of harmful consequences, as follows: prolongation of suffering, medical complications of health status, permanent harmful consequences, permanent disability, and death. We diagram the path that Colombians need to follow to have their health care claims attended by the system in a matrix called Bureaucratic Itineraries. Bureaucratic Itineraries is a theoretical and methodological construct that links the personal experience of illness with the system's structure and could be an important tool for understanding, evaluating and comparing different systems' performances. In this case, it allowed us to conclude that managed care in Colombia has created complex bureaucracies that delay and limit care through cost-containment mechanisms, which has resulted in harmful consequences for people's lives. [Copyright Elsevier Ltd.]

title: Dialectics of Authoritarian Bureaucracy: Extraction and Patrimony in Ancient Rome
abstract: Max Weber warned of the possible emergence of a monolithic power state, where practically all aspects of social & economic life are governed by a single bureaucracy. In his view, it would combine features of the ancient "forced labor state" with the formally rational domination of modern bureaucracy, & would impose enduring domination & social stagnancy. Weber's image of authoritarian bureaucracy is explored, & modern counterparts of this perspective are implicitly criticized for not providing sufficient emphasis on the dialectical interchanges between the mechanisms of domination & the responses of the ruled. Weber implied that domination under modern authoritarian bureaucracy would probably be a highly rationalized analogue of the imperial Roman state. Analysis of domination in Rome's ancient authoritarian regime shows that, though the bureaucracy organized the society into a structure of extraction & coercion, it also generated responses from below. An elaborate network of patron-client relationships, which provided means to avert extraction & arbitrary impositions of power, conflicted with the central bureaucracy. The dynamic of state control & clientelistic adjustment contributed significantly to the decline of classical society & to the rise of protofeudalism. Analytic questions are raised about authoritarian bureaucracy; most importantly, if they generate similar types of interchanges & have their own internal logic of change, contemporary authoritarian regimes may be less enduring than Weber intimated. 74 References. HA

title: The promotion of capabilities in Sweden: a case study of the contraction of shipbuilding in Gothenburg
abstract: Purpose - Using the example of a project dedicated to labour market re-activation in major shipyards in Sweden (Gothenburg) in the late 1970s, the purpose of this paper is to examine how integrated employment policies may be achieved using more deliberative public action than that offered by New Public Management (NPM). Design/methodology/approach - Based on original archival research and interviews with ex-participants, the research reconstructs how this project was designed and operated; its analysis is based on a capability perspective. Findings - The paper analyses the problems encountered by projects promoting labour market integration and personal capabilities in the context of a productivity drive in a contracting industry that requires the retention of the most productive workers to stave off industrial collapse. It argues that deliberative democracy offers the more effective means for co-ordinating integrated employment policies than governance strategies associated with NPM. Practical implications - This paper offers an example highly pertinent to the labour market conditions currently facing European economies in the current financial crisis. Originality/value - The paper offers original insights into the operation of the Swedish social model in practice, in a context of industrial crisis. Many scholars have analysed this model of labour market management from a national perspective: far fewer have addressed its practical limitations. Adapted from the source document.

title: Development Traps of Slovenian e-Government
abstract: The development of modern information-communication technology is pressuring states to reform their public administration into more effective and flexible organisations, able to provide all necessary services to citizens in the shortest time possible and in the most friendly manner. Slovenia is not an exception, it has adopted a necessary legal and strategic framework that enables development of administrative systems called e-government and/or e-governance. Slovenian public administration institutions first used the Internet and its applications for inter-organisational communication. Other elements of Slovenian e-governance will be represented in following articles. New public management theory is following the idea of efficient communication of public administration with citizens. In this part we are introducing some empirical research that shows that there are still discrepancies between theory and praxis in the case of using e-mail in Slovenian public administration communication with citizens. Especially in the case of Slovenian local administrations, there is great gap between theory and praxis. The situation is much better at the central level of administration and especially in the case of so called administrative units, which have most frequent contact with Slovenian citizens and which are understood as a special level of Slovenian public administration. Despite more sophisticated methods of e-governance having emerged, we are still interested in basic methods used already by Vintar et al. (2000) at the end of previous century. Adapted from the source document.

title: Employment relations and unions in public administration in Portugal and Spain: From reform to austerity
abstract: This article examines trade union responses to the transformation of employment relations in the public administration in Portugal throughout the Reform programmes launched after 2002 and the more recent austerity measures. It examines the relationship between conflict and concertation and analyses the perspectives and practices of the sector's ideologically divided trade unions. It finally considers comparative issues emerging from the application of similar austerity packages in Portugal and Spain and contrasts their paths of employment relations and union action in public administration. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright holder.]

title: Political clientelism and democracy: Clientelistic power and the internal differentiation of the political system
abstract: The article proposes a systems-theoretical approach to political clientelism. It places political clientelism in the theoretical framework of a democratic political system characterized by internal differentiation in government and bureaucracy, party politics and a politically relevant public. Against the background of existing research on the link between democracy and political clientelism, it uses Luhmann's concept of power and more specifically his model of the formal and the informal power cycle to point out parallels and differences between a political system based on expectations with regard to policies and a political system in which clientelistic expectations prevail. Democratic political systems are based on formal, legally codified power and informal power. Clientelistic power is a special form of informal power affecting this interplay, as the example of democratization in Mexico shows. Political systems with clientelistic expectations differ from those with a policy orientation with regard to the complexity of policies, the generalization of political support, the bases for personalization, the pattern of interest articulation and the most prominent external influences on the system. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications, Ltd. and the Scandinavian Sociological Association, copyright holder.]

title: Public service employment restructuring in the crisis in the UK and Ireland: Social partnership in retreat
abstract: The crisis has had major consequences for public service employment relations in the liberal market economies of the UK and Ireland. However, variations in the process of fiscal consolidation reflect different legacies of social partnership, prior patterns of public management reform and different relationships to the eurozone. The measures adopted nevertheless reflect a similar concern to decrease public sector employment, worsen pay and conditions and increase work effort. Despite the deterioration of terms and conditions of employment, industrial action has been muted, reflecting the severe weakness of trade unions. Both cases illustrate that governments have become less concerned to gain trade union support to push through austerity measures. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Evaluation in Latin America: Paradigms and Practices
abstract: This chapter addresses the development of evaluation, as a practice and as a field of knowledge, throughout Latin America in relation to the sociopolitical context, including characteristics of the state and its relations with civil society. It comes from the perspectives of evaluation as a learning tool, as a means to improve accountability and transparency in public administration, and as a dialogic device. The political context is described in terms of three historical moments: (a) the existence of the welfare state, (b) the withdrawal of the state in the framework of the Washington consensus and the emergence of neoconservative policies, and (c) the return of the state and the rise of civil society and active politics. Finally, there is an analysis of opportunities and challenges facing contemporary policy evaluators and decision makers. Adapted from the source document.

title: Towards an Agenda for Post-carbon Cities: Lessons from Lilac, the UK's First Ecological, Affordable Cohousing Community; [1]
abstract: This article explores an agenda towards post-carbon cities, extending and deepening established debates around low-carbon, sustainable cities in the process. The label post-carbon builds upon issues beyond those of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, energy conservation and climate change, adding a broader set of concerns, including economic justice, behaviour change, wellbeing, land ownership, the role of capital and the state, and community self-management. The article draws upon a case study of an embryonic post-carbon initiative completed in early 2013 called Lilac. Based in Leeds, Lilac stands for Low Impact Living Affordable Community and is the first attempt to build an affordable, ecological cohousing project in the UK. Its three aspects each respond to significant challenges: low-impact living and the challenge of post-carbon value change; affordability and the challenge of mutualism and equality; and community and the challenge of self-governance. I conclude the article by exploring six lessons from Lilac that tentatively outline a roadmap towards post-carbon cities: the need for holistic approaches that deal with complex challenges, prioritizing self-determination rather than just participation, engaging with productive political tensions, adopting a process rather than an outcomes-based approach, developing strategy for replicability, and finally, embracing a non-parochial approach to localities.[PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Australian Bureaucratic Elite: The Importance of Social Backgrounds and Occupational Experience
authors: Boreham, Paul; Cass, Michael; McCallum, Michael
abstract: The upper levels of the Australian federal bureaucracy exercise power in cultural, social, & economic areas. Examined are the attitudes & social & educational backgrounds of second division officers in the Commonwealth Public Service through a questionnaire survey in 1975 (number of cases = 703). Focusing on the notion of 'representativeness' of elites, it is found that the social attributes of higher level public servants separate them, to a large extent, from the population which they serve. The changing nature of their background characteristics reflects the historical development of Australian bureaucracy. The elite is recruited so as to share similar cultural backgrounds, lifestyles, & loyalties; it is increasingly dominated by a homogeneous group with high socioeconomic status backgrounds. For recruits from working class backgrounds, the effects of organizational socialization seem to cause them to develop a conservative view of the world. 10 Tables, Appendix. Modified HA.

title: On Interdisciplinarity and Models of Knowledge Production
abstract: The six UK Genetics Knowledge Parks (GKPs) were shaped and governed by two frameworks: a 'need' to harness 'new genetics' and the relations of accountability as seen in the context of entrepreneurial government. The remit of the Cambridge GKP (CGKP) was to develop public health genetics by building on the concepts of partnership and interdisciplinarity. In the course of its work, the CGKP emphasized the virtues of 'change management', seen as distinct from, and opposed to, an academic model of knowledge production. However, the model that the CGKP actually created was a research/management hybrid that resisted quality assurance checks developed for each model (research and management), presenting a formidable challenge for the evaluation and assessment of the CGKP's work. Adapted from the source document.

title: Voices of welfare reform: Bureaucratic rationality versus the perceptions of welfare participants
authors: Tickamyer, Ann R; Henderson, Debra A; White, Julie Anne; Tadlock, Barry L
abstract: This article compares the assumptions of welfare reform with the way the program is actually implemented to show the underlying contradictions in the way policy is politically justified and implemented. The results of focus group discussions with women on welfare in four rural Appalachian Ohio counties demonstrate the disparities between the top-down goals of welfare policy and the bottom-up perceptions of their outcomes.

title: Urban Policy Making in Germany: The Impact of Parties on Municipal Budgets and Employment
abstract: This study analyzes the impact of party dominance on local budget & employment decisions. Five policy indicators are examined for all 87 county-free cities in West Germany during the 1980s. These city counties combine administrative functions that are normally divided between municipalities & counties. The author offers an empirical investigation of political party impacts on local government policy. The result of micro- & macrolevel analyses show the crucial role of parties in local politics. The relationship between the spending preferences of local policymakers & their assessment of the electorate's preference are weakened by party ideology. Political party control impacts both municipal budgets & employment as illustrated by a multivariate analysis. 4 Tables, 1 Figure, 69 References. E. Sanchez

title: The Historical Conception Of The Intelligentsia And Its Power In The Process Of Decision-Making In The Middle Eastern And North African Countries
abstract: The intelligentsia (with the intellectuals included) is defined and perceived according to its socio-cultural and political position, function and vocation in various historical and national contexts. One its most prominent roles have been its contribution through its competence and savoir-faire to the process of socio-cultural changes. One of the aims of this paper is to provide a synoptically comparative and historical assessment of its conception and definition in general and especially of this of the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). The paper tries also to describe and analyse their different role in the process of decision-making regarding socio-cultural changes. It contends that this process includes various interdependent, causal and sequential stages of planning, evaluation, legitimisation and implementation. Moreover, the management of these changes demands an educated elite, the intelligentsia, which has the expertise to carry out this task. In this regard, the paper will mainly concentrate on analysing theoretically the different stages and tracks in a decision-making process related to the policy of social change in MENA countries, how the intelligentsia is defined and how their position and function are perceived in society. In addition the role played by the different groups of the intelligentsia in this process will be assessed in the light of their position and power in these countries. Any study of the intelligentsia and cultural production in society leads us inevitably to the analysis of political power. (Laabi 1983:152) A society which uses up all its energies in organization leaves little opportunity for introversion, contemplation and reflection in such society, the political and organizing elites would predominate, while reflective, scientific, artistic... elites would scarcely exist, and if they did, would be very ineffective. (Mannheim 1940:83) Job in the bureaucracy for an individual or one of his relatives represents access to sources of allocative and distributive power. Influence over decision-making related to important national or local projects represents one of the few available channels for 'participation' in the public affairs of the society. (Ayubi 1990:147) The central problem of government in the Arab world today is political legitimacy. (Hudson 1977:2). Adapted from the source document.

title: Training and the Elimination of Prejudice against Women: Some Lessons for Job Evaluation in the Context of Pay Equity
authors: Deom, Esther; Drouin, Diane; Mercier, Jacques
abstract: The aim of the 1996 Quebec Pay Equity Act is to eliminate the portion of the wage gap between male & female workers resulting from systemic discrimination based on prejudices against & biases regarding the value of women's work. To achieve pay equity, the law provides for the use of an analytical job evaluation method that requires evaluators to exercise their judgment; however, this could be subject to the influence of their personal values. Highlighted is the importance of training to eliminate gender biases in the job evaluation process. Here, the results of Quebec Public Service employee self-evaluations are examined, seeking two types of gender bias. It is concluded that awareness training in discrimination & biases against women's work, & technical job evaluation training are needed to achieve genuine pay equity. 6 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Production of Social Knowledge for Public Use
abstract: Review & evaluation of experience in applied social research has led to a growing consensus that social knowledge produced for policy action purposes should be substantially different from that which is produced for disciplinary purposes. Not all of the research procedures developed for disciplinary knowledge are applicable under the conditions of policy action research, & scientific techniques for the production of policy action knowledge of certain needed kinds have not been created. The organization & administrative procedures of academic institutions have been found inadequate for the production of many types of policy action knowledge. It is still widely agreed, however, that academic institutions should provide basic training for policy action researchers. Modified HA.

title: Bureaucratizing Democracy, Democratizing Bureaucracy
abstract: This article analyzes the relationship between how rationality is conceived & how democracy is practiced in the Bureau of Reclamation, a water development agency in the Dept of Interior. The efforts of some inside the agency to institutionalize rational decision-making models, partly in response to new environmental law, expanded the number & range of interest groups that participated in its decisions by incorporating their preferences into their models for evaluating plans. But, the terms under which people could express their values & interests were strictly controlled in ways that some felt misrepresented their concerns. How we conceive of rationality has important implications for how & which people are included in bureaucratic decision making. 70 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Responsibility and Citizenship in Public Administration
abstract: This text offers some thoughts about responsibility as a concept that, on the one hand, addresses the way in which the public administration system functions -- in terms of rendering account, professional performance, etc -- & on the other affects the generation of trust in administrative authorities & the government on the part of the man in the street. The issue of responsibility is analyzed on three levels: (1) an initial organizational one, which looks at the virtualities & limitations of accountability; (2) one that revolves around the institutional aspect, interpreted as political & administrative responsibility seen in the light of citizens' rights; & (3) one that covers the contractual aspect of political responsibility, which is addressed as a category that underlies democracy & governance in the risk society. 27 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Farmers Organizing Farmers: The Farmer Irrigators' Organizing Program of the National Irrigation Administration
authors: Laitos, W Robert; Ehera, Ted I
abstract: Effective local organizations use local people's specific idiographic knowledge of their own setting. Most students of development properly stress the importance of the appropriate structure for these local organizations. Local idiographic knowledge) however, is also important for development processes. The "how" of developing local organizations can be just as important as the "what." This paper describes some of the preliminary successes & problems of the Farmers Irrigation's Organizing Program (FIOP) of the National Irrigation Administration (NIA). 24 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Nonbureaucratic Phenomenon. Cooperation among Firms and Synchronic Just-in-Time Production
abstract: A model of "just-in-time" production practiced in a French automotive plant is analyzed in an attempt to explain interfirm cooperation as a hybrid form of organization between market & hierarchy that goes beyond the bureaucratic phenomenon. A comparison of intra- & interfirm cooperation in component-supplying activities (interfirm cooperation vs hierarchy effect) & suppliers close & far from the assembly lines (local effect) reveals that interfirm contracts are more efficient than the intrafirm hierarchy, & the just-in-time synchrony is an excellent economic solution, overcoming the traditional limitations & dysfunctions of the firm's bureaucratic structure based on power relations. 30 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Putting Power in the Anthropology of Bureaucracy: The Immigration and Naturalization Service at the Mexico-United States Border
abstract: The anthropology of bureaucracy should address the role of organized power in orchestrating complex & unequal societies. Here, the development of bureaucracy studies is reviewed, focusing on the thinking done by bureaucrats in their efforts to control the actions of others. The central concept of thought-work is placed within a series of queries about levels & relationships of power, with particular attention to the encompassing classifications & assumptions embodied in organizational worldviews. The worldviews of officers of the US Immigration & Naturalization Service, examined as a case study, are found to give cohesion to a contradictory policy that balances publicly visible arrests & invisible but effective perpetuation of undocumented labor migration. Both human rights abuses & avoidance of abuses are explainable as outcomes of these thought-work routines. A stronger theoretical approach to organized power enhances applied anthropology's ability to address the behavior of state & private bureacracies with respect to the rights & interests of nonbureaucrats. Comments are offered by: Ronald Cohen, Jorge Durand, Dale F. Eickelman, Don Handelman, Michael Herzfeld, Alex Stepick, & Scott Whiteford & Manuel Chavez. In a Reply, Heyman further explores the direction of the anthropology of bureacracy. 106 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucracy, Monopoly, and Competition: A Critical Analysis of the Budget-Maximizing Model of Bureaucracy
abstract: William A. Niskanen has argued that if government bureaus act so as to maximize their budgets, they will always produce an output greater than a private industry, resulting in efficiency losses to society ("Competition among Government Bureaux," American Behavioral Scientist, 1979, 22, 5, 517-524). Since the budget-maximizing model relates to a number of intersecting areas of organizational analysis from several disciplines, it is important to note the limitations of the model. Niskanen's result is only true, however, for a bureau that can exercise perfect price discrimination in its relationship with its financial sponsor; where this is not the case, the bureau may produce less than a private industry. Further variation is introduced by examining the effects on a bureau of specialized resources, public goods, competition, & low productivity. A bureau that would otherwise produce an output in excess of the competitive level will, when any of these factors are present, produce an output closer to the competitive output. These results may also have significant policy implications, since major industrial countries are favoring policies to return some governmental activities to the private sector. 1 Table, 6 Figures, 73 References. HA.

title: From professorial power to the power of worksheet
abstract: The point of departure of this article is auto ethnographic experience concerning transformation of Danish universities from independent and autonomous institutions to organizations more attuned to business concerns. Seen in a perspective of philosophy of science, this change is interpreted as a development away from the notion of scientific research as a privileged form of cognition, institutionally shielded against interference from social power groups, to a form of knowledge provision carried out by universities on terms rather similar to those of other organizations providing research and education governed primarily by external stakeholders. Seen in an institutional governance perspective, the change is explained as a trajectory starting with postwar liberating expansion and ending at tight and utilitarian management in the 'competition state'. In the 1950s and 60s students attacked the exclusive governance of the professors and their self-sufficient research and teaching. The professors fought to preserve the collegial self-government and thus professional autonomy. However, influential power groups had a desire for mass-education of effective academic labor to serve the provision of wealth in the welfare state. Simultaneously, the same groups had a wish for a fundamental showdown stressing independent and critical scientific research. In 1970 students thus obtained democratic in- fluence on university governance; however, governmental control gradually increased and in 2003 external stakeholders got the decisive influence in university boards and hence the mission accomplished. In conclusion, the article suggests that scientific staff at Danish universities tended to be transformed from autonomous persons with a mission in the service of truth, to become employees in search for business opportunities in the service of management and external stakeholders.

title: Administrative Subcontract
abstract: This paper attempts to demonstrate the significance, relevance and implications of 'administrative subcontract' as an analytical framework to understand China's intergovernmental relations, bureaucratic incentives, and administrative governance. As an ideal type, administrative subcontract refers to a subcontracting relation inside the government system, represent a hybrid governance structure between bureaucracy in a Weberian sense and pure subcontract which occurs among independent entities without any hierarchical relations. Administrative subcontract exhibits a coherent and consistent set of characteristics along the dimensions of authority relations, economic incentives, and internal control. With respect to authority relations, administrative subcontract features an allocation of authority between the principal and agent where the principal has the formal authority and residual control rights (such as the authority to appoint/remove, supervise and monitor subcontractors and the option to intervene when necessary), and the agent, by way of subcontracting, enjoys considerable discretion and de facto power to do things in his own way. Under the administrative subcontract regime, the agent is a residual claimant over the budget money or revenues either collected through service-provision or allocated by the principal. In terms of internal control, the administrative subcontract is outcome-oriented rather than procedure/process-oriented. I argue that these three dimensions are complementary and mutually supportive, and tend to commove if the system encounters systematic shocks. This new framework helps us pin down the key and durable features of China's intergovernmental relations and administrative governance. The notion of administrative subcontract enables us to reinterpret many puzzling observations and patterns regarding the workings of China's government system and to bring some important and yet long understudied issues to our attention. I will also combine the theory of administrative subcontract with that of political tournaments to extend our analysis of China's political incentives and governance. From the viewpoint of vertical subcontracting and horizontal (political) competition inside the government system, I attempt to explain the strength and weakness of China's state capacity in various areas of public services. Adapted from the source document.

title: Challenging Women: Gender, Culture, and Organization
abstract: Eisenstein reviews "Challenging Women: Gender, Culture, and Organization" by Su Maddock.

title: Categories of race: technologies of knowing and governing Australian aborigines
abstract: This article documents the first decades of the work of the Aboriginal Protection Board in Victoria, Australia in the mid-nineteenth century, as it oversees the establishment of mission stations to gather up Aboriginal peoples and provide protection from settler violence. It augments existing accounts of white settler governance of Aboriginal peoples by examining the social and historical conditions for the emergence of separations and distinctions between Aboriginal peoples through shifting governmental versions of the 'Aboriginal problem'. The production of race-based categories of persons is highlighted in the State's management of the Aboriginal children through the mission systems and their effects on Aboriginal ties to community and identity.

title: Feeling like a State: Design Guidelines and the Legibility of 'Urban Experience' in Singapore; [1]
abstract: This article examines how 'urban experience' is objectified and transformed into something that is legible to the state and its experts. It conceptualizes design guidelines as a political technology where bodies of expert knowledge, emplaced in a planning bureaucracy, shape the way the built environment is produced and experienced. Using Singapore as an example of a centralized planning bureaucracy, I analyze how lighting, public art and advertisement signs are targeted to produce a total environment with normative narratives. This article makes two contributions. First, it unpacks the processes that translate different modes of legibility in an attempt to make 'experience' legible for planners. The political efficacy of guidelines and pre-established bureaucratic boundaries means that planners can only intervene through a series of combinations, mediations and approximations. Thus, legibility proceeds in a way that is akin to 'feeling around'. Second, it foregrounds the 'middle layer of urban governance' that is often ignored in the discipline. Guidelines represent one coordinate in a system of political technologies that is concerned with producing the norm, that substrate of urban production mechanized through a series of repetitions, gradations and classifications.[PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Civil service reform in the countries of the West African Monetary Union
abstract: High cost, low average salaries, generally poor morale and mediocre performance are features of the civil service administration in the states belonging to the West African Monetary Union.
