Furthermore, the desire to see the NHS working more efficiently resulted in the expectation that the exercise should be done in a particular way-within a realist tradition of arriving at quick, simple and 'definitive' needs. We conclude by suggesting that if such work is to be meaningful then there needs to be a number of pre-cursors: an initial consensus on the nature of 'need'; an agreement between commissioners and researchers around common frameworks and realistic expectations of the process; and finally, an acceptance of the importance of history in this work and the way histories of local inter-agency work reflect embedded forms of local knowledge. We suggest that NHS volatility means that much of this knowledge is often lost. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Making of the Lombard League
abstract: Italy's Lombard League, a regional political voice for citizens who encounter problems with the country's bureaucracy, is discussed.  It has succeeded in mobilizing people living in small villages who had never taken part in protest politics.

title: Collectivists, Communists, Labor Bosses, and Treason: The Tea Parties as Right-Wing Populist Counter-Subversion Panic
abstract: The Tea Parties are a right-wing populist movement echoing earlier episodes of white nationalism in the USA. Power elites have encouraged similar counter-subversion panics using populist rhetoric and producerist narratives to enlist a mass base to defend their unfair power, privilege, and wealth. Typically, a large, middle-class white constituency sides with organized wealth as a way to defend their relative and precarious position in society. The blame for economic, political, and social tensions is transferred away from free market capitalism to mythical conspiracies of collectivists, communists, labor bosses, and other scapegoated subversives and traitors. At the same time, defense of unequal racial and gender hierarchies can be mobilized as part of these counter-subversion efforts. Patriots, economic libertarians, Christian dominionists, militia activists, nativists, and ethnic nationalists fit under the Tea Party umbrella in an uneasy coalition ostensibly built around reversing the 'big government' policies of the Obama administration. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Training South Africa's public administrators to realise and protect human rights
abstract: Proponents of human rights often focus on the legislative and judicial aspects of government in the promotion of socio-economic rights. They contend that political will and an independent judiciary are, on their own, sufficient precursors to realising socio-economic rights. There is little discourse on the role played by the executive of public administration processes in advancing, or indeed failing to advance, socio-economic rights. There is even less discourse on the role human rights education can play in enabling public administrators to protect socio-economic rights through better delivery of socioeconomic services. This article begins by clarifying the concept of separation of powers and the centrality of administrators in executing the will of the state (legislature); and drawing on contemporary discourse, it discusses the opportunities and challenges faced by administrators (the executive) in promoting human rights. The article advances possibilities of incorporating human rights education in the training of public administrators, while highlighting the opportunities and challenges. It is then concluded that human rights education for public administrators can play a pivotal role in enhancing the realisation of socio-economic rights, as these administrators are strategically placed at the coalface of the delivery of socio-economic services. Adapted from the source document.

title: LEADERSHIP AND DECISION-MAKING IN MANAGER CITIES: A STUDY OF THREE COMMUNITIES
abstract: A report on a continuing study of policy leadership in 3 middle-sized council-manager cities (CMC) in Michigan. Each has operated under the plan for over 25 yrs & no change in managers took place during the 5-yrs covered in the study. Tentative conclusions reached on data so far gathered indicate that the manager & his administration are the principal sources of policy innovation & leadership in CMC, though the manager seeks to avoid a public posture of policy leadership; that the manager has resources & techniques that enable him to withstand even strong attempts by some councilmen to take policy leadership away from him; that non-official groups provide a greater amount of leadership in CMC than is allowed for in the theory of the plan; & that this leadership is a result of councilmanic leadership falling short of the idealized role assigned to it by the theory. Councilmen who do seek to lead place their pol'al careers in greater jeopardy than do other councilmen. It was also found that there were few issues identified as `important' confronting city councils & that even some of these were settled with little conflict, particularly when few solutions seemed to be available. AA.

title: New Courses in Political Science and Public Administration
abstract: The social sciences must be understood by their horizontal links with the remaining fields of human knowledge. Humanistic disciplines' strength does not include ideological preaching but transmission of knowledge through facts. Therefore, rethinking them is indispensable to avoid delays, lack of production, & stagnation. It is thus urgent to develop a new perspective in curricula & programs in political science. 15 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The leisure construction in adolescents and this influence for development of criminal careers
authors: Navarro Perez, Jose Javier; Uceda i Maza, Francesc Xavier; Perez Cosin, Jose Vicente
abstract: The construction of leisure activities affects directly in the positive development of the teens, enable them to a healthy socialization of their lives. The complexity of the activity design and leisure programs requires a big effort by the different agents; so the public administrations, parents, professionals, teens and the management of these programs have to coordinate their efforts to develop a balanced space for the leisure activities. The activities that focus on the supervised leisure allow to grow positively. The alarm arises when the leisure spaces change without any notice into dangerous risk spaces. In this sense, this article will attempt to explain how the teen build their behaviours, leisure situations and how they are capable of generate incorrect dynamics that contribute in the negative development of the teen. Furthermore, this article will try to discover how to define public practices and to see how youngsters build their participation strategies and educational promotion to play constructive playgrounds. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Conflict of Professionals in Bureaucratic Organizations
authors: Sorensen, James E; Sorensen, Thomas L
abstract: A study of 264 certified public accountants in 4 large national public accounting firms showed that when professionals work in a professional bureaucratic organizations, conflict & deprivation result with predictable consequences such as job disatisfaction & job migration. The R's were asked to indicate agreement or disagreement (Likert scaling) with both specific behavioral incidents & attitudes toward selected incidents. The results, analyzed by linear r, revealed that the CPA in a large public accounting firm appears to resemble other professionals in bureaucratic organizations. The patterns in orientation & deprivation suggest that professional conceptions are challenged & transformed by the requirements of the bureaucratic setting. It is necessary to consider these processes that influence professional & bureaucratic orientations for the development of a dynamic model of occupations & organizations. Careful monitoring of the adaptive process of professionals to such settings might provide some valuable clues on professionalism & specific future changes for public accounting. 4 Tables. Modified HA.

title: Recognizing New Opportunities: Reconceptualizing Policy Advocacy in Everyday Organizational Practice
abstract: Policy advocacy is a concept that is of both practical and historical importance to the profession of social work. To keep up with developments in how advocacy is practiced at the ground level, however, social work research on advocacy needs to expand in scope. Changes in government contracting and public management practices have reshaped the opportunity structure for policy advocacy, incentivizing a kind of advocacy that is routine, professionalized, and collaborative. At the same time, these practices have raised questions about democratic representation and the degree to which social work advocacy adequately reflects client concerns. This article presents a model for how policy advocacy can be usefully reconceptualized to account for changes in the policy and funding environment and concludes by suggesting ways that social work research and theory can better reflect practice realities. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The return of the broker: consensus, hierarchy, and choice in South African land reform
abstract: The broker, a key concept in 1960s and 1970s political anthropology, merits revival in settings of rapid social transition. In South Africa, where state planning directs the course of change while attempting to privilege the market, brokers do not merely negotiate between fixed positionalities of 'state/market' and 'people'. Instead, they embody and bring into being socio-economic positions and identities. They blend together the egalitarianism and rights-based character of post-liberation society with the hierarchy of re-emerging traditional authority. Drawing on notions of consensus, they embody 'the people'; drawing on ideas of free choice and enterprise, they embody 'the market'. Simultaneously they bear the bureaucratic characteristics of 'the state'. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: How Parole Officers Use Records
abstract: A study is made of the record-keeping behavior of parole officers (POs) employed in Ur branch offices of a state parole agency. Data were collected by means of: (1) interviews with over fifty POs & Dept of Corrections officials, & (2) field observation of twenty-two meetings between POs & their parolees. Data revealed that routine career contingencies reward POs for underreporting violations of their clients. Thus, POs will ignore most crimes & incidents they observe among their clients except when such reporting results in some benefit to the PO. These benefits generally relate to the satisfaction of informal bureaucratic demands. These findings have implications for the validity of parole records & for the functional theory of parole bureaucracies. Modified HA.

title: Higher education: struggling for quality or encroaching on human potential? (part 2)
abstract: A higher quality of education is impossible without its considerably greater financing and social guaranties. At the same time, following measures are proposed: 1) de-bureaucratization -- that is, less indices for licencing, accreditation and controls of education institutions functioning; reduction of reporting indices; 2) democratization of education administering -- real electivity of rectors, heads of departments, institutes and chairs, evaluation of teachers performance quality with students opinions' taken into consideration; 3) USE (unitary state examination) reform towards greater numbers of creative assigments; 4) elaboration of special qualimetric characteristics to assess quality of education.

title: Complexity in a Varied Society: Diversity and Disability Management
abstract: Considers the marginalization of disabled people in the Dutch welfare state bureaucracy. Self-disability management is discussed as a means by which disabled persons negotiate their complex lives & manage diversity, an idea that does not fit with the constructed society. Deconstruction of the current welfare state into a varied society is suggested as a means to accommodate humanist citizenship with respect to disable persons, where individuals are declassified & accepted on their own terms. 12 References. M. Salinas-Veksler

title: The Road to Hell: Neutralization of Killing in War
authors: Kooistra, Paul G; Mahoney, John S
abstract: We explore how societies convince citizens to "go to hell," where they kill strangers and risk their own lives. Our premise is that killing is difficult for most, regardless of context and widely considered a form of extreme deviance. Using Sykes and Matza's techniques of neutralization, we show how this aversion to killing is neutralized by placing individuals in organized-both macro-level bureaucratic and micro-level small primary groups-to justify killing. Consequently, the neutralization of mass killing illustrates the role of power in defining deviance, and the failure of neutralizations may sometimes explain Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder.

title: Advocacy and Bureaucracy: The Life and Times of a Decentralized Citizen's Advocacy Program
abstract: An examination of the Governor's Branch Offices (GBO), a citizen's advocacy program in the ghetto area of Penn, during its 4 year development is presented. Data were obtained through analysis of files & records, participant observation, & interviews. This advocacy agency consisted of storefront operations in 21 ghetto neighborhoods & had direct communication to the office of the governor via a central coordinator. The GBO's philosophy, based on views of bureaucratic access, response time, responsiveness, & citizen advocacy, led to unusual organizational structures & procedures. The reduction of bureaucratic red tape in order to provide "quick response to the problems of disadvantaged people by the agencies" was the main goal of the program. The offices had 4 person staffs working 2 shifts to permit long operation hours. Problems typically handled by the agencies included medical, financial, housing, employment, legal & police, marital & family, & education. The program was allowed to expire after being in operation for 4 1/2 years under the administrations of 2 governors. The program raised issues about the feasibility & chances for success of an advocacy program in a bureaucratic setting, subject to forces such as routinization, inflexibility, changing executive support, & rivalries with other programs. 1 Figure, Appendix. Modified HA.

title: Management, Public Politics and Social Development: Toward the Professionalization of Public Management
abstract: One of the main objectives in the development of Latin American modernization policy is to create public management (PM) professionals. Understanding the complementary roles of PM as practice & discipline is important in moving toward professionalization. Here, an ecological vision is proposed; organizational practice elements at the microlevel are conceptually related to public policy elements at the macrolevel. The proposed ecological conceptualization supposes PM development in contexts similar to & different from private management. This framewok simultaneously delivers solutions to limits on the success of PM activities & intellectual solutions that overcome obstacles to professionalization on the route to social & economic development. 1 Table, 1 Figure, 25 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Value-oriented public management in vulnerable societies: assessing the impact of Public Value Management practices in three Caribbean countries
abstract: Innovative public management practices can greatly benefit citizens, but often fail due to a mismatch with the societal context. Public Value Management was developed in North America and Western Europe, emphasising public leadership, stakeholder involvement, and information sharing. This article examines whether these practices advocated in resilient societies which are large, egalitarian, and high trust also work in vulnerable societies which are small, hierarchical, and low trust. The article compares management practices at 16 public utilities in 3 Caribbean societies, concluding that Public Value Management can improve outcomes when applied comprehensively. Partial implementation, however, leads to worse outcomes instead.

title: CONTINUITY IN CITY MANAGER CAREERS
abstract: A report based upon interviews with city managers in 55 Michigan cities over a 2 yr period is offered as a step in formulating an occup'al model. The city manager is an appointed municipal official who, in the design of the councilmanager form of gov, is the chief administrative official. His office makes possible the existence of an outsider who is substantially involved in local affairs. The `Outsider' orientation of the manager requires a continuing adjustment to the local organization. He tends to be a perpetual newcomer in a locality. City managers can follow 2 main career lines: (1) of the 'Advancement-by-moving' career, & (2) the 'One-city manager' career. The former attempts to advance by moving to a larger or more prized city; the latter attempts to achieve prominence & prestige by being known as a man who has successfully maintained his managership in a single city throughout a long period. Managers of each type are faced with problems of regulating their involvement in local affairs. This regulation is a result of his problem of becoming substantially but not too substantially involved in local affairs: the manager is expected to be sufficiently free from local claims upon him so that he can leave gracefully if his obligations to colleagues require a resignation. Ordinarily he is expected not to remain in the city that is necessary to fight to retain his appointment & he is expected to remain sufficiently free from local commitments so that he can use a threat of resignation if the special character of his office is in jeopardy or if the city council becomes committed to a course of action which would require him to violate his ethical code. His colleagues tend to criticize him if he 'Moves too soon' or 'Stays too long'. The manager is regarded as having moved too soon if he fails to contribute substantially to a city's development before he leaves for a new job. He is regarded as having stayed too long if he becomes too involved in local affairs & cannot hold himself free of their demands so that he loses control. Either the one-city manager or the advancement-by-moving managers conceptualize their tenure in terms of unit of work. The advancement-by-moving manager tends to conceptualize for a shorter period of time & In neater packages of accomplishment, whereas the one-city manager tends to conceptualize tenure as a longer term aspect. Both types of city managers must maintain a 'potential to move' which is the ability to leave the job for a better one. The occup'al ideals of the city manager show aspirations to stay in one city to do a job or a unit of work & to make necessary preparations before moving to the next city. The potential to move within the limit of achieving these two aspirations is actually a summary of the conditions & processes of his tenure, & is the basis of his occup'al security & advancement. N. F. Washburne.

title: OPPORTUNITIES FOR NEUTRALIZATION OF CORRUPTION ELEMENTS IN THE LEGISLATIVE ACTS OF A SUBJECT OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION IN THE SPHERE OF STATE PROPERTY'S MANAGEMENT AND DISPOSAL
abstract: The paper is devoted to the topical issue of defining the legislative jurisdiction of a subject of the Russian Federation in the sphere of public property's management and disposal. The author draws attention to the fact that this sphere is susceptible to corruption and offers one possible way for reducing the opportunities to adopt corruption-generating legislative provisions in the subjects of the Russian Federation. Adapted from the source document.

title: 'Russia's Bureaucratic Ruling Elite'. Towards a Social Portrait of Russia's Higher Bureaucracy during the First Quarter of the 19th Century
authors: Kiselev, Igor N; Mironenko, Sergei V
abstract: The social structure of Russia's bureaucratic ruling elite during 1800-1825 is examined using service records for selected civil servants in 1802 & 1825 (N = 224 & 446, respectively). Findings disprove common stereotypes in Soviet historiography & widely-held beliefs that the real power & authority in Russia was connected with the landed gentry. Among the higher bureaucratic elites, 50% derived their entire income from their civil servant position rather than from ownership of land or serfs. Approximately 33% did not own any serfs, & a constant growth of this group was observed in the central bureaucracy. 5 Tables. Adapted from the source document.

title: Formalizing the Ban: My Experience in the Reagan Administration
authors: Korb, Lawrence J, PhD; Rothman, Alexander, BA
abstract: The repeal of Don't Ask, Don't Tell (DADT) is a success story. As of September 20, 2011, one of the most egregious cases of modern day government-sanctioned discrimination has been overturned. But my (Lawrence Korb) involvement with military policy toward gays and lesbians began early in our country's journey toward open service -- 18 years before the creation of DADT and 30 years before the Obama Administration successfully opened the armed forces to gay and lesbian service members. In 1981, I joined the Pentagon shortly after the Carter administration announced a new Pentagon policy stating that "homosexuality is incompatible with military service" (U.S. Naval Institute [USNI], 2011). As Assistant Secretary of Defense for Manpower, Reserve Affairs, Installations, and Logistics, the responsibility of writing the directive to implement this ban fell to my office. In this article, I detail my recollections from this period in American military history: the codification of the gay ban in U.S. Department of Defense policy. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: THE GROWTH OF BUREAUCRACY IN SCHOOL SYSTEMS
abstract: A number of diff factors have contributed to the growth of bur'cy in Sch systems. Some of these result from the size & functions of Sch's. As Sch's have become larger, specialized personnel can be supported; at the same time an increase in size has called for a more orderly org of behavior, which comes about through an org chart, rules, etc. The function of the Sch has expanded. The Sch has a much broader role than in the past; there are programs for handicapped, retarded, & emotionally disturbed children, vocation courses, evening Sch courses, etc. Stimuli, both external & internal, leading to the growth of bur'cy within the Sch system, are presented. Finally, the low motivation of some personnel creates a problem for the Sch system & its admin'ors. The response to this problem is also increased bur'cy-rules & procedures to motivate & guide teachers, & new staff people to oversee the behavior of teachers. Modified AA.

title: MODELS OF BUREAUCRACY WHICH PERMIT CONFLICT
abstract: Complex org's can be described in terms of 3 modelsWeberian, HR, &professional. The first is most efficient when dealing with uniform events & traditional areas of knowledge, the second when dealing with non-uniform events & interpersonal relations, while the third is ideal where org's are split, having some segments requiring uniformity & others not. The third model covers the great bulk of org's in contemporary society. Therefore, one of the key theoretical problems in complex org's is the study of structural procedures by which the conflicting forces are harnessed to org'al goals. AA.

title: Social Work and the New Integrative Hospital: Response to Dr. Falck
abstract: In response to Hans S. Falck's commentary on Globerman & Bogo's "Social Work and the New Integrative Hospital" (for both, see abstracts in SOPODA 18:1), it is pointed out that unequal power relations exist in both hierarchical & decentralized organizations. However, social work in health care organizations has not had power, & administrators transforming hierarchical hospital arrangements have overlooked social work. The challenge was to design alternative frameworks to house social work functions rather than to address underlying assumptions of hierarchy. V. Wagener

title: Struggles, Urban Citizenship, And Belonging: The Experience Of Undocumented Street Vendors And Food Truck Owners In Los Angeles
abstract: The study examines the experience of Latina women selling food on the streets of Los Angeles. There has been a long history of food vending since the immigration wave from Latin America to Los Angeles during the 1980s. The majority of the immigrant women who sell food are poor, without legal rights to stay in the United States, and in many instances single with children. However, the immigrant women are subject to much harassment from city officials and the police as they are forced to sell without permits, since permits are highly unaffordable and the process bureaucratic. The study examines how the women continue to work under these difficult conditions. The study also explores how the women situate themselves and the connections they make with the larger community while they sell on the street. Much of the research on Latina immigrants and informal work has been in the area of domestic work and day labor work. In examining the experience of women street vendors, the research will contribute to scholarship on undocumented immigrants, urban citizenship, and immigrants and work. Data are drawn on interviews and participation observation of women selling food in three neighborhoods in Los Angeles. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Soviet Criticism of Bureaucracy during Perestroika
abstract: A sociological analysis of Soviet literature on bureaucracy & bureaucratism is presented. Bureaucratism is defined as pathology of bureaucracy, & bureaucratization is perceived as the influence of the state on economic & social issues. It is suggested that the Soviet approach to bureaucracy neglects the particulars of modern public administration & focuses on a bureaucracy mired in economic troubles. The difference between the Western emphasis on classic problems of a bureaucratic welfare state & economic factors conditioning the Soviet response to bureaucratic changes under perestroika (restructuring) are highlighted. L. Baker

title: New Approaches to Creating Data for Economic Geographers
authors: Freedman, Matthew; Lane, Julia; Roemer, Marc
abstract: Policymakers, faced with increasing demands to make decisions at a local level, are turning to statistical agencies to provide local data. Advances in matching technology, combined with the reduced cost of archiving, indexing, storing, and curating large-scale datasets, now mean that it is technically feasible to provide information at fine levels of geographic detail by means of combining administrative and survey datasets at lower cost and with potentially greater coverage. This article describes an approach that uses administrative data from U.S. unemployment insurance records to enhance the coverage and accuracy of work location information in the American Community Survey. Adapted from the source document.

title: Reflections on ethics in public management
abstract: Dealing with ethical trends in governance leads to three directions of thought. Firstly, that in keeping with what has been called traditional public administration where public interest is interpreted by politicians and bureaucratic experts and the dominant model of accountability is formal and hierarchical. The second area deals with new public management (NPM) whose primary focus is user satisfaction; the search for public service performance and efficiency underlies such approach and involves ethical behaviour based on achieving results (i.e. compliance). The third area is based on creating public value, emphasised by public ethics grounded on the conjunction of individual and civil liberties with the state's legitimate authority which requires democratic participation, accountability and citizen participation forming key elements. This paper was aimed at analysing ethics within the context of trends in public management, implying a sense of direction for public ethics or ethics involved in policy-making and public administration. Adapted from the source document

title: Perspectives of Growth and Nongrowth among Public Officials
abstract: Data were gathered by interviews with public officials in 81% (325) of the incorporated places in Ky. Officials of metropolitan core cities were the most growth oriented, while officials of suburbs were the most nongrowth oriented. Among nonmetropolitan cities, officials of large towns were more growth oriented than those of small towns. Per capita city income was related to growth/nongrowth orientation only within suburbs, in which the higher the per capita city income, the more nongrowth oriented were the public officials. Contrary to expectations, population growth had no relationship with growth/nongrowth orientations of public officials. The theories of Molotch (1976) & Logan (1976, 1978) were only partially supported when taking into account cities of all sizes, within nonmetropolitan as well as metropolitan areas. Within both metropolitan & nonmetropolitan cities, officials of larger cities were found to be growth oriented. The theory of the predominance of the growth orientation among public officials, however, was supported only within metropolitan core cities. There was a definite residential suburban tendency toward nongrowth. A spill-in effect of growth advantages from metropolitan core cities to the suburbs, & the lack of such a spill-in in nonmetropolitan cities, is suggested by differences in growth/nongrowth orientations of city officials.

title: L'« ÉCONOMISTE » EN POLITIQUE. LES EXPERTS SOCIALISTES FRANÇAIS DES ANNÉES 1970/THE "ECONOMIST" IN POLITICS. FRENCH SOCIALISTS EXPERTS IN THE 1970s
abstract: While the issue of expertise has been massively investigated by scholars since the late 1990s, the "politically committed experts" who are active members of a party remain largely unstudied. This article, based on the quantitative and qualitative analysis of 196 economists, analyses the sociology and role of those who constructed the French Socialist Party's economic programme and discourse during the 1970s, when the party led by François Mitterrand aimed to seize power. It shows that, contrary to the clichés disseminated through the media, high-level civil servants did not have a monopoly of expertise within this organization. It also highlights that the socialist economic experts' work had to follow the strategical framework defined by the party's most prominent politicians

title: From Contradictory Intention to Contradictory Practice
abstract: The struggle over the organization of the Netherlands' Centers for Work & Income (CWIs) is taking two directions. The first leads toward decentralization; in the CWIs, parties cooperate under direction of the local governments, which, in recent years, have been given increasingly greater responsibility for social-security-related issues. The second direction, which seems to be the course the developments are taking, leads to centralization: In the CWIs, the labor market position of clients is measured in an objective, uniform way, & a national nongovernmental organization decides the allocation of the reintegration budget of the institutions in the field. It is contended here that only when the first path is followed & developed will there be a chance for CWI clients to receive appropriate attention; the new system of administration is expected to be an improvement. 2 Tables, 25 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: FRONTIERS OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND PUBLIC WELFARE
The Magic of the Populace: An Ethnography of Illegibility in the South African Immigration Bureaucracy
abstract: Recent anthropological accounts of the state have demonstrated the potential for danger or illegibility in the public's encounter with the state. Much of this work has taken the perspective of the public, however, and less has been said about how functionaries of the state perceive their interactions with the public. This perspectival bias needs to be overcome through ethnographies of the state and of state bureaucracies in everyday practice. This article examines the Immigration Services Branch of the South African Department of Home Affairs, a state bureaucracy widely deemed 'illegible' by South Africans and non-South Africans alike. It documents some of the factors that inform the actions of street-level bureaucrats, illustrating how bureaucrats develop systems of meaning to help them mitigate the challenges posed by an unpredictable populace and management hierarchy. These systems serve to stabilize these two unstable entities, but they also enable officials to act in ways that might run counter to official discourse while simultaneously upholding its legitimacy. Their stabilization efforts therefore incite a destabilization of the state, leading it to appear as 'magical' or 'illegible' to the public. Adapted from the source document.

title: Honor as Property
abstract: Ongoing research on the early-twentieth-century administration of criminal justice in the Italian countryside has found a constant overrepresentation of cases of personal insult & defamation, related to sexuality when women were involved, & to honesty & capacity to hard work in the case of men. These results are consistent with previous research in the Mediterranean area. However, other characteristics of peasant conflicts are also apparent: (1) there is often a gap between the apparently minor importance of the value at stake & the intensity of the conflict that develops; (2) many conflicts accompany diputes on a wide range of questions connected with land, & are often resolved by modalities considered by the official law to be assault & self-help. These findings raise three related questions: (A) why honor is so important in peasant society; (B) why conflicts are often so harsh, even when little of value is at stake; & (C) why offenses against honor & against land & its goods should be related to each other. Relying on criminal records from Provincial State archives for the period 1899-1914, proverbs & folklore, & unstructured interviews with old peasants (N not provided), it is argued that honor & land have constituted two fundamental goods ensuring the production & reproduction of the peasant family. Moreover, they have been viewed by peasants as parts within a system of equivalences where material & immaterial goods were considered interchangeable. Therefore, conflicts could take place in the material (land), as well as in the immaterial (honor), sphere. The choice of the arena in which the conflict should be fought depended on the degree of economic liberty enjoyed by the parties involved. 2 Tables, 57 References. Modified AA

title: New Public Management and New Professionalism across Nations and Contexts
authors: Leicht, Kevin T; Walter, Tony; Sainsaulieu, Ivan; Davies, Scott
abstract: The professions in the West are undergoing unprecedented calls for greater accountability and efficiency in service delivery. This article links these changes to recent developments in institutional theory that emphasize shifting salience of technical over symbolic organizational environments. The analysis of the adaptations to these changes in French and British healthcare, Canadian education and US managerial consulting suggest that country-specific responses to neoliberal institutional pressures are highly path dependent. The article concludes by suggesting a research program for the future study of the cross-national responses of professional groups to neoliberal economic and political ideologies. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Access to justice and social inclusion: The policy challenges in Wales
abstract: Enhancing access to legal and advice services is a central pillar of the Access to Justice Act 1999. Within the new welfare framework, employment rights come increasingly into focus as the UK government seeks to forge a link between welfare and work. Access to the labour market, and being sustained within it, are seen as major mechanisms for combating social exclusion. Discrimination at work can only thwart these ambitions. The Access to Justice reforms imply an assessment of need and a review of the ways in which individuals are negotiating the available system of redress. This article reports on a study of advice provision in employment discrimination cases in Wales, funded by the Legal Services Commission and the Equality Commissions in Wales. Drawing on the accounts of key providers, individual experiences of advice seeking and available statistical evidence, it explores the opportunities and constraints of the Welsh context and profiles many of the policy challenges posed for the devolved administration. It demonstrates that, despite advances in equalities legislation and policy directives aimed at strengthening people's employment rights, a number of critical obstacles remain for the most disadvantaged groups.

title: Assessing U.S. Strategy in the War on Terror
abstract: Al Qaeda and its jihadi allies pose a large threat to U.S. national security. Such a grave menace requires a strong response. Yet the United States has so far waged only a one-dimensional war against al Qaeda, fighting hard on one front when it should be fighting on four. Specifically, the Bush administration has focused heavily on an offensive campaign against al Qaeda overseas while neglecting three other critical fronts: bolstering homeland defense, securing weapons and materials of mass destruction from possible theft or purchase by terrorists, and winning the war of ideas. And the administration has sometimes done too little even on the offensive, instead diverting itself into a costly and counterproductive sideshow in Iraq. The public credits President Bush for toughness on terror. In fact, his administration has pursued a half-hearted war on terror, failing to devote the political and financial resources it requires. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Comparing performance: the development of police performance management in France and Britain
authors: de Maillard, Jacques; Savage, Stephen P
abstract: Performance management in some form is now a global feature of policing in both developed and developing countries. Under the steer of 'new public management', cultures of performance and the instruments of performance management are increasingly a part of the landscape of twenty-first century policing. However, there has been little by way of comparative analysis of the different regimes of police performance management, despite the wider expansion of scholarship on comparative policing. This article seeks to address this gap by comparing police performance management in Britain and France. It examines the relationship between the rise of police performance management and the wider politicisation of 'law and order' in both contexts. It then discusses police performance management in the two states in terms of comparisons of performance regimes around the themes of 'centralisation' and 'localism', the dimensions of policing which form measurements of police performance, the role of 'transparency' and exposure of data in performance management and the role of 'consumerism' the police performance regimes. It also considers the extent to which senior police representative bodies have shaped or resisted the performance agenda. In conclusion, the article locates variance in police performance management between the two states within the fundamental differences in governance, structure and ethos between the two policing systems. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Ideas that move the state: spatial imagination, Brazilian thought, and territory in Central Brazil
abstract: This article discusses the relationship between state ideas and practices based on a case study of the Fundacao Brasil Central (FBC), an agency created by the Estado Novo regime in 1943 and whose activities extended until 1967. The hypothesis is that Brazilian social thought should be analyzed as a cultural repertoire that produces effects on social life and the state. The article thus analyzes material from the FBC archives and travel records, geopolitical treatises, and other text sources published from the First Republic through the initial years of the Vargas Era. The aim is to show how narratives on Central Brazil shaped the language and practice of public administration. Adapted from the source document.

title: Two Worlds Apart in Botswana's Education System: Lessons from the 2010 Examinations Crisis
abstract: Botswana enjoys the celebratory status of a shining example of a successful democracy in Africa. As such, one expects democracy to underpin policy formulation and the running of the education system. This chapter problematizes the relationship between democracy and education in Botswana. It focuses on the Report of the Committee of Inquiry into the Conduct of the 2010 Examinations. The conduct of the examinations marked a crisis which resulted in a deadlock between the Botswana's Ministry of Education and Skills Development (MoESD), Botswana Examination's Council (BEC) on the one hand and teachers' unions-Botswana Sectors of Educators Trade Union (BOSETU) and Botswana Teacher's Union (BTU) on the other hand. Teachers' unions complained about poor conditions of service and remunerations associated with the administration of national examinations. This action triggered a national strike in the public service in general and consequently revealed Botswana Government's undemocratic response to what was a sensitive issue of national interest. When the examinations results were released, it became evident that students performed horribly BEC was persecuted for the poor performance. This chapter therefore registers that the 2010 Examinations crisis in Botswana is a classic indication that democracy and education are two worlds apart in Botswana's education system.

title: A Comparative Study of Governance in State Management: Focusing on the Roh Moo-hyun Government and the Lee Myung-bak Government
abstract: This study aims to explore development discourses of the Roh Moo-hyun and Lee Myung-bak governments and evaluate their governance in achieving their respective visions of development. The two governments advocate sustainable development and green growth, respectively, as their national development paradigms, and strategies, laws, and organizations were developed to realize their goals. This research analysis reveals that the Roh administration perceived and reflected the concept and the importance of governance into its own policy framework while the Lee administration has not. The Roh administration perceived civil society as the subject of governance and policy process whereas the Lee administration perceives it as the object. In conclusion, the Roh administration can summarily be described as non-authoritarian with civil society-centered governance that pursues sustainable development, while the Lee administration is authoritarian with token state-centered governance that pursues green growth. This difference results from the difference between the nature of development discourse, principles of government management, perception of governance, leadership style and values, and the support basis of each government. Adapted from the source document.

title: From Bottom to Top: Exploring the New Way for Women to Participate in Government's Administration
abstract: The traditional from-top-to-bottom way that women participate in governmental administration has a variety of abuses. Actually & eventually the from-bottom-to-top way is helpful for women to realize more participation in administration. Advancement of the way has the deep characteristic of time & theory basis. The essay deeply explores with a practical example the feminist slogan "personal is political," & proves the affections & meanings of self-empowering ways to participate, so as to further the sexual equality & build up a coordinated society. References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Europe -- The Soviet Administrative Elite by Kenneth C. Farmer
abstract: Review.

title: Economics -- The Struggle for Auto Safety by Jerry L. Mashua and David Harfst
abstract: Review.

title: An Economic Analysis of the In-Prison Therapeutic Community Model on Prison Management Costs
authors: Zhang, Sheldon X; Roberts, Robert E L; McCollister, Kathryn E
abstract: This study estimated the impact of an in-prison, therapeutic community (TC) substance abuse treatment program on management costs in a California prison. A deconstruction method was developed to estimate the opportunity cost of staff time & other resources involved in various prison administrative tasks. Compared to "non-treatment" yards within the facility, the TC environment generated lower administrative costs for disciplinary actions, inmate grievances, & major disruptive incidents resulting in lockdowns. These findings suggest that, in addition to their intended rehabilitative outcomes, prison-based TCs may foster institutional environments that help to control prison management costs. [Copyright Elsevier Ltd.]

title: Comunicazione pubblica e performance nella sanità digitale: trasparenza e accountability per un empowered patient (Public communication and performance in the e-Health system: transparency and accountability for an empowered patient)
abstract: Il processo di riforma e di digitalizzazione della pubblica amministrazione italiana (PA) nell’ultimo decennio prevede l’adozione di sistemi di valutazione e gestione della performance delle organizzazioni sanitarie finalizzati a migliorare trasparenza e accountability istituzionale nei confronti dei cittadini e degli stakeholders. In tali processi una comunicazione efficace riveste un ruolo fondamentale per il raggiungimento degli obiettivi che essi si prefiggono, incidendo sull’empowerment del cittadino-paziente. L’autrice riflette sulla centralità e sulle dimensioni della comunicazione pubblica in questo ambito e sulle modalità con cui le organizzazioni sanitarie italiane comunicano online la propria performance, con cenni a best practices internazionali.The recent reform and digitalization of Italian public administration in the last decade involves the assessment and management of the performance of healthcare organizations aimed at improving transparency and institutional accountability to citizens and stakeholders. In these processes, effective communication plays an important role in achieving the objectives that they are seeking, impacting on the citizen-patient’s empowerment. The authoress reflects on the centrality and on the dimensions of public communication in this area and on the way in which the Italian healthcare organizations communicate their performance online, with nods to international best practices.

title: Administrative Decentralization for Regional and Local Development in Japan
abstract: Administrative decentralization for regional & local development in Japan has, until recently, been initiated mainly by the central government. With the drafting of the Third Plan in 1978, however, the role of local governments in the formulation of national development plans was recognized. Presently, a new regional development policy of "technopolis" is being proposed to make Japanese industries' structure more knowledge-intensive, & to attain regional development objectives. The future of Japan's regional development will depend on how local governments plan & implement original & creative policies for regional & local development. HA

title: Toward a Theory of the Role of the State in Market Transition: From Bargaining to Markets in Post-Communism
abstract: Ideal-type contrasts have produced many theoretical insights regarding the differences between communist & market economies, but to really understand systemic change in the postcommunist state, markets & bureaucratic hierarchies must be examined together. Survey data collected by the Polish Academy of Sciences in 1982 (N = 3,500), 1987 (N = 5,854), & 1991 (N = 1,835) are therefore used to document changes in the structure of aggregate inequality, the distributive patterns of the state & nonstate sectors, & the relative income shares to producers & nonproducers -- the determinants of change in individual incomes during the period of market transition in Poland. 5 Tables, 111 References. M. Maguire

title: Destinations of Social Administration Graduates
abstract: The relevance to subsequent employment of a degree in social policy & administration (SPA) is assessed using statistical data from the UK & 1986 survey data gathered from 1972-1985 SPA graduates of Exeter U, England. The trends toward a multidisciplinary curricular approach & the expansion of the scope of the degree are briefly discussed. Results indicate that SPA graduates are generally successful in management & administrative fields & in a wide range of other occupations. Since many SPA graduates obtained further education that led to positions in social work, the social administration & social psychology coursework was indicated as most useful. SPA graduates appear to have a wider range of destinations than economics majors, but a narrower range of opportunities than sociology graduates. An SPA degree is most relevant to positions in the public sector, but opportunities also exist in industry & commerce. 17 Tables, 29 References. L. Goya

title: Death as an Industry
abstract: A review essay on books by (1) Robert Johnson, Death Work: A Study of the Modern Execution Process (Belmont, CA: West/Wadsworth, 1998 [1990]); & (2) Stephen Trombley, The Execution Protocol (London: Century, 1993), which examine the institutional aspects of executions in the US. Johnson presents a thorough qualitative analysis of the contemporary execution process, drawing on interviews with death row officers to uncover the human emotions behind the daily routine of the extended waiting periods & ritualistic execution days. He also analyzes the role, compulsions, & emotional turmoil of the executioners in the bureaucratic procedure behind executions. Trombley offers a historical analysis of the US execution industry, focusing on the labor, technology, & scientific management involved in the process, seeking to understand the connection between mass production, technological progress, & institutionalized killing. Like Johnson, he analyzes how the horrific act of killing can be made routine through redundancy, technology, & the bureaucratic dispensation of roles. D. Bajo

title: Competence versus care? Gender and caring work revisited
abstract: Masculinist visions gender the concepts of bureaucracy and profession, dichotomizing competence and care, and masking both the reality and the potential of public carework.  A recent campaign by the Royal College of Nursing in London England addressed the worth and value of nursing.

title: From breaking the rule to making the rules: the adoption, entrenchment, and diffusion of gender quotas in France
abstract: Once a country allergic to any type of preferential treatment or quota measure for women, France has become a country that applies gender quotas to regulate women's presence and representation in politics, the business sector, public bodies, public administration, and even some civil society organizations. While research has concentrated on the adoption of electoral gender quotas in many countries and their international diffusion, few studies focus on explaining the successful diffusion of gender quotas from politics to other domains in the same country. This paper proposes to fill this gap by studying the particularly puzzling case of a country that at one point strongly opposed the adoption of gender quotas in politics, but, in less than a decade, transformed into one of the few countries applying gender quotas across several policy domains. This paper argues that the legal entrenchment of the parity principle, the institutionalization of parity in several successive women's policy agencies, and key players in these newly created agencies are mainly responsible for this unexpected development. The diffusion of gender quotas in France thus offers an illuminating example of under which conditions women's policy agencies can act autonomously to diffuse and impose a new tool for gender equality.

title: Consumer Participation in Administrative Decision Making
abstract: The term "consumer participation" in public agencies has come to occupy an important place in discussions of administrative theory & practice without any real consensus on what such participation implies. This phenomenon is considered in the field of housing, examining the impact of tenant participation across 750 public housing projects. Analysis of data derived from a survey of housing projects conducted by the US Dept of Housing & Ur Development in 1978 supports the view that tenant organizations can be effective in increasing the level of resources & services made available to tenants, but provides no evidence that this form of consumer participation enhances the administrative process. Modified AA.

title: Bureaucracy and Development in Jordan
abstract: Bureaucracy, the major instrument of socioeconomic development in Jordan, functions within an environment of scarce resources, overpowering political leadership, & particularistic cultural habits. The progress that bureaucracy has made toward achieving the goals of national development is assessed, & obstacles that retard modernization efforts are identified. Focus is on specific bureaucratic pathologies in the political-administrative structure (eg, clerkism, centralism, nepotism, incompetence), & their negative effects on development & administrative effectiveness. It is concluded that substantive issues of reform have not been effectively articulated or managed. 24 References. Modified HA

title: SECRECY REFORM OR SECRECY REDUX? ACCESS TO INFORMATION IN THE OBAMA ADMINISTRATION
abstract: On his first full day in office, President Obama issued a Memorandum on Transparency and Open Government (White House, 2009a) committing his Administration to create an unprecedented level of openness in government and indicating his belief that government should be transparent, participatory, and collaborative. This chapter examines the Obama Administration through June 2010, and looks at how closely the administration is hewing to its promises, in the context of the legacy of secrecy it inherited. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Administrative Psychology and Sociology
abstract: At present France is running the risk of having no part in the progress of the sociol'al & psychol'al sci's. Admin, which could easily take as a model the psychol'al bureau of the army, has a tendency, in this age when indifference to human beings is disappearing, to maintain a secretive & aristocratic character. On the contrary, we need an admin'ive org which will, while maintaining secrecy in those situations demanding secrecy, allow its essential aspects to be viewed. Confidence & an atmosphere of inner security are necessary, since these play a major role in the daily existence of public services, of which the agents are at the same time the guardians of stability & the guarantors of progress. It is undoubtedly true that in practice the admin has difficulties in reconciling everyday realities & human beings with the abstractions which, in fact, make up the service. There are many who ignore the fact that a good understanding of psychol is necessary if we wish to avoid being surprised by reality. Tr by J. A. Broussard from IPSA.

title: International Institute of Administrative Science (IIAS)
abstract: The International Institute of Administrative Science and the University of Bologna are organizing the First International Regional Conference to be held in Bologna Italy June 19-22. The theme will be "Public Administration and Globalization: international and supranational administrations."

title: Introductory tenancies: A nuisance too far?
authors: Smith, Nicholas J; George, Gavin A
abstract: Part V Chapter I of the UK's Housing Act 1996 empowers local housing authorities and housing action trusts to offer introductory tenancies. Smith and George consider whether introductory tenancies are necessary to solve the "neighbor nuisance" problem by examining some of the legal and non-legal remedies currently available to local housing authorities.

title: The Landfill in the Countryside: Waste Management and Government of the Population in Campania
abstract: For the past nineteen years, much of Campania has been engulfed in a "waste emergency," with urban waste invading the region's cities (D'Alisa, Di Nola, and Giampietro 2012) and toxic waste being deposited in dumping grounds (Pasotti 2008). The waste crisis overlaps speculative socioeconomic planning, based largely on investment in the construction and waste disposal sectors, that characterizes recent economic development in the region (Pasotti 2010). This paper examines a significant but widely misconstrued piece of this complex Puzzle -- the Campanian protests against the socioeconomic transformation prompted by landfill construction during the waste crisis in 2007-2008 in Marigliano -- a town of the province of Naples -- as well as in two rural settings of Campania's inland -- Savignano Irpino and Sant'Arcangelo Trimonte. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Pacific Islanders' Fund and the Misappropriation of the Wages of Deceased Pacific Islanders by the Queensland Government
abstract: The Queensland Pacific Islanders' Fund operated between 1885 and the 1900s but is largely unknown today. It was established in the Treasury to facilitate the operation of the Pacific Island Labourers Act 1880 Amendment Act 1885 to safeguard return fares and to ensure that the money due to deceased Islanders was returned to their families. However, over time, because of the high death rates, the wages of deceased Islanders became so substantial that they were able to be used to supplement the administration of the whole labour trade. Money was drawn off to subsidize Islander hospitals and Christian missions, to an extent that in the final 1900s deportation years there was no longer enough money available to pay full fares. The Queensland government seldom returned the full wages to the families of the deceased Islanders and profited largely from their deaths. In today's money, millions of dollars were misappropriated, in similar fashion to wages misappropriated by the same government from Aborigines.

title: The Capacity of National Administrative Organizations: A Comparison of Sweden and the United States
authors: Wise, Charles R; Sinclair, Thomas; Amna, Erik
abstract: An examination of US & Swedish governments demonstrates that similar factors are influencing administrative capacity in both nations, posing important issues for policymakers. Governmental organizations operate in complex environments comprising public interest, economic, & managerial dimensions. The comprehensive nature of many social problems, as well as the limited means that governmental agencies are granted to address them, suggest that government will often lack the capacity to achieve expected levels of problem remediation regardless of its internal management capacities. Administrative problems may develop when one dimension is overemphasized to the neglect of the effects of others. 70 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Is There a Ruling Class in the USSR?
abstract: Three analyses of the USSR as a political entity hold that it is ruled by a modified form of capitalist ruling class, that it is ruled by a class of new type, & that it is ruled by a bureaucracy which does not constitute a class. The traditional Marxist theory, according to which the proletariat would be the new ruling class, is falsified by the condition of the proletariat in the USSR. The Trotskyist theory accounting for this holds that a bureaucratic apparatus, which was necessary to abolish capitalism, would itself have to be abolished in time by a second revolution, which would complete the first. However, the long duration of the bureaucracy's rule makes the claim that it does not constitute a new ruling class less plausible. What is now needed, rather than rationalizations for this hypothesis, is serious analysis of the new type of class domination that has come into being in the USSR. W. H. Stoddard.

title: Optimizing the Use of Microdata: An Overview of the Issues
abstract: It is becoming clear that advances in technology and increased use of administrative records may, at some point in the future, render our current disclosure avoidance procedures inadequate. At the same time the ? federal statistical system face[s] increasing demands for more, better and more recent data to meet critically important public policy and research needs.2 The extraordinary growth of electronic infrastructure, capacity, and use in the past decade has posed a profound new set of questions about the control, dissemination, power and use of information. On the one hand the high speed internet and the World Wide Web, email, electronic shopping, and cell-phone use have opened up extraordinary new worlds of communication and are changing the way we work, play, and learn. On the other, as the electronic world enters our daily lives, the private space untouched by the intrusions of cyberspace and information seekers shrinks for individuals, firms, and organizations? There is also another challenge. The need to build more efficient surveillance networks to combat potential terrorist attack argues for less privacy for the individual person or firm to guarantee the security of the society in general. It is in this environment that citizens, business and technology leaders, and policy makers have to figure out how to understand, manage, and regulate the new cyber world.3. Adapted from the source document.

title: Women in Public Administration in Finland
abstract: WOMEN IN THE LABOR FORCEFinnish women have a long history of participation in the labor force. In 1890, in Helsinki, about 39 percent of all working age women were in paid labor. By 1900, this figure had grown to 55 percent (Jallinoja 1983, 225). In the whole country, 32 percent Of women in the non-agricultural population participated in the labor force in 1900 and 39 percent in 1920 (Haavio-Mannila 1980, 11). In 1983, 73 percent of all working age women were in the labor force, and almost half (48 percent) of the total labor force consisted of women (Central Statistical Office 1985, 116).In 1987, one-fourth of the total Finnish labor force (over 659,000 of the 4.9 million total population) was employed by the public sector. Two-thirds of these (about 448,000) worked in the municipalities and their federations and one-third (about 211,000) worked with the state. The public sector, especially the municipalities, is a large employer of women Almost half (42 percent) of the female, but only 25 percent of the male, labor force is in the public sector The large municipal sector is dominated by women; 75 percent of its permanent monthly salaried employees are women In contrast, 60 percent of the state employees are men (Central Statistical Office 1985, 23).For a complete reprint of this article contact Haworth Press by telephone (1-800-HAWORTH) or EMail (getinfo@haworthpressinc.com) Article copyright The Haworth Press, Inc.

title: ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIETY IN ISRAEL
abstract: ISRAELI SOCIETY IS DIVIDED INTO MANY AUTONOMOUS SEGMENTS GENERATED BY THE INITIAL MATRIX OF POLITICAL PARTIES, TO WHICH THEY ARE STILL MORE OR LESS AFFILIATED. THE ABILITY OF THIS NATIONAL NETWORK TO ACT AS A WHOLE RESULTS FROM PARTY CONTROL & FROM THE ABILITY OF THEIR ELITES & VESTED INTERESTS TO COOPERATE. THE PREDOMINANCE OF THIS PATTERN THROWS SOME LIGHT ON THE CONSERVATIVE ANARCHISM OF ISRAELI SOCIETY. IN SPITE OF SOME RECENT STRUCTURAL CHANGES, THE STATE REMAINS A LIMITED & FRACTIONED REALITY WHOSE MAIN FEATURES ARE HAZY. PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION IS BY NO MEANS A BUREAUCRACY IN THE WEBERIAN SENSE. IT REMAINS A SET OF AGENCIES WHOSE MAIN FUNCTION IS TO SOCIALIZE THE CITIZENS TO THE POLITICAL SYSTEM & TO CONDITION THEM TO THE RULE OF THE POLITICAL PARTIES. THE DOMINANT STYLE OF ACTION IN PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION SEEMS TO AMOUNT TO THE INSTITUTIONALIZATION OF DEBROUILLARDISE (RESOURCEFULNESS), AN APPROACH MIXING A DEEP UNDERSTANDING OF THE NEED OF ORGANIZATIONS WITH THE REALIZATION THAT THEIR SHORT-CIRCUITING MUST ALSO BE ORGANIZED. THIS SYSTEM HAS RESULTED IN THE DWINDLING OF POLITICAL PARTIES, HIGH DEPENDENCY BY INDIVIDUALS, THE FAILURE OF NATIONAL DECISION-MAKING WITH REGARD TO LONG TERM & CROSS-SECTORAL ISSUES; THESE COSTS ARE CREATING CONDITIONS FOR ITS MODIFICATION. MODIFIED HA.

title: Science and Problem Solving: Links, Difficulties, and Paths of Progress in the Field of Administrative Science
authors: Audet, Michel; Landry, Maurice; Dery, Richard
abstract: The orthodox model of scientific problem solving is examined & critiqued to illustrate that its theoretical values are inapplicable in practice. Empiricism relies on the stability of an object's properties, the objectivity of the scientist, & the ability to predict & control the object studies, & it focuses on the study of the regularities of an object. However, the problems identified for scientific study are generally caused by transformations, or irregularities, & scientists are basically social beings. It is concluded that orthodox models must be rejected & a social theory of science developed, especially where the problem studied is a combination of people & objects, such as in administrative science. 140 References. D. Graves

title: Reviews -- The Social Production of Indifference: Exploring the Symbolic Roots of Western Bureaucracy (Global Issues) by Michael Herzfeld and edited by Bruce Kapferer and John Gledhill
abstract: Review.

title: BUREAUCRACY AND INNOVATION
abstract: The relationship between bur'tic structure & innovative behavior is examined by comparing the conditions within the bur' tic structure with the conditions found by psychol'ts to be most conducive to individual creativity. The conditions within bur'cy are found to be determined by a drive for productivity & control, & are inappropriate for creativity. Suggestions are made for alterations in bur'tic structure to increase innovativeness, such as increased professionalization, a looser & more untidy structure, decentralization, freer COMM's, project org when possible, rotation of assignments, greater reliance on group processes, attempts at continual restructuring, modification of the incentive system, & changes in many management practices. It is suggested that bur'tic org's are actually evolving in this direction. HA.

title: A Minimum Pension Guarantee Application for the Individual Pension System in Turkey: A Gendered Approach
abstract: This study examines the minimum pension guarantee (MPG), a promise by government or pension fund management that at retirement, a person's annuitized benefit will be above a prespecified minimum level. For the first time, we use an actuarial model to discuss the role of MPG in lessening the gender gaps in pension incomes in the Individual Pension System of Turkey. Our results reveal that women would be more likely than men to receive pension subsidies and would require larger pension subsidies for every combination of investment decision and years of pension participation if MPGs were implemented.

title: Publications on Public Administration in Brazil, 1938-1945
abstract: A critical and analytical bibliography of publications in public administration, issued between 1938-1945 by the Administrative Department of Public Service, an agency of the Brazilian government. L. Pap.

title: The Impact of the Public Employment Program on Sex-Related Wage Differentials
abstract: The effects of the Public Employment Program (PEP) on the wage differentials between Ms & Fs may be tested by examining the experiences of 2,289 participants in the program. Participants were interviewed in 6-month intervals beginning in June 1972, & the data provided information on pre-PEP & post-PEP employment. In general, Fs earned lower wages because of the nature of their jobs & sexual segmentation within the labor market, even within PEP. Wage differentials increased between PEP & post-PEP jobs, & it is doubtful that PEP programs can improve the labor market status of women. Programs such as PEP have the potential to ease discrimination in the labor market but are not working. 3 Tables. Modified HA.

title: Historical Evolution of Urban Social Administration in PRC
abstract: After founded in 1949, PRC's primary social institution had been keeping the civil administration in a pattern of "government-grass root unit" in a long period so as to meet the requirements of planned economy. Such a pattern was beneficial to direct social control & citizen mobilization but, on the other hand, people were therefore shackled & couldn't make fully their efforts for social development. Since the market-oriented reform, a civil administration in "government-community" pattern prevailed gradually to overcome the shortcomings of original pattern. However, it is still bureaucratic to a great extent & hard to change the slack weak in fulfilling necessary tasks for efficient social administration. In 2004, the 4th session of the 16th central committee of CPC put forward a new pattern for social administration, ie., "leading by party committee, doing duty by government, coordinating with society & increasing public awareness to participate in social activities." It is a new breakthrough in China' s urban social administration & bound to contribute to the construction of harmonious society. References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Strength of Weekly Ties: Relations of Material and Symbolic Exchange in the Conservative Movement
abstract: The current Republican ascendancy in American government has generated considerable scholarly interest in the conservative movement. Through an ethnographic study of the widely publicized but seldom-observed "Wednesday meeting" of conservative activists, this article inquires into the bases of the conservative movement's internal cohesion and successful management of alliances with state officials. I argue that the meeting functions as both an instrument of material power and a ritual of symbolic maintenance by establishing relations of reciprocal exchange and sustaining a moral community of conservative activists and their allies. More broadly, the article examines the mutual conditioning and genetic linkage of two dimensions of social reality: relations of force and relations of meaning. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Bureaucracy and Development in Saudi Arabia: The Case of Local Administration
abstract: The role of the Saudi Arabian bureaucracy in development, & shortcomings of the local administrative system are identified, including: diverse organizational structures, low educational qualifications of public officials, an imbalance between executive authority & the assigned responsibilities of local agencies, a high degree of duplication, & a lack of coordination of services. All of these constitute serious obstacles to the local administration playing an effective role in promoting socioeconomic & political development. Despite these shortcomings, the system has been active in the dynamic development of the Saudi Kingdom, a role that has been strengthened by national development plans that emphasize regional development. 8 References. Modified HA

title: Reflections on applying for NHS ethical approval and governance in a climate of rapid change: prioritising process over principles
authors: McDonach, Eileen; Barbour, Rosaline S; Williams, Brian
abstract: Ethical review and governance of health services research in the UK have undergone significant changes in recent years. Tracing this incremental development helps to understand the rationale for introducing a more standardised process. Reflecting on our experience of approval for a national, multi-centred, qualitative study provides useful insights into both the advantages and disadvantages of this new approach. Advantages include promoting awareness of ethical issues and timely review of proposals. However, excessive bureaucracy and inconsistency in obtaining local governance approvals can lead to unacceptable delays. There is also a danger that the current focus on the process of applying for ethical approval may overshadow debate about the principles of ethical research practice. Over-reliance on a checklist approach may perpetuate an erroneous notion of ethical approval being a 'hurdle' to negotiate instead of an ongoing consideration. Unanticipated theoretical and methodological implications for future health services research are critically examined. Given the continued globalisation of health services research, this discussion may help inform debates and decisions about restructuring ethical review processes in other countries. Adapted from the source document.

title: Social Work Values in Human Services Administration: Implications for Social Work Education
abstract: The perceived wisdom in the social work education community, based on an empirical research from the 1990s and the early part of this century, says that the master of social work (MSW) degree is not competitive with the master of business administration or the master of public administration to obtain top-level administration jobs in nonprofit agencies. This article reviews recent information on hiring preferences of board chairs that provides new hope that the MSW degree with a concentration in management or administration is perceived as a viable and useful degree for top-level positions in human services agencies. Thus, current board chairs are more inclined to value the MSW than administrators and academics from years past. The reason is that the values of social workers are seen as quite valuable in the current environment. Adapted from the source document.

title: Officially: The Bureaucratization of the Netherlands and the Disciplining of the Civil Servant
abstract: A review of four Dutch works addressing federal bureaucratization processes in the Netherlands in different historical eras: (1) Mario Damen's De staat van dienst: De gewestelijke ambtenaren van Holland en Zeeland in de Bourgondische periode (1425-1482) ([State of Service: Holland and Zeeland Regional Bureaucrats in the Burgundy Era (1425-1482)] Hilversum: Verloren, 2000) describes the early integration of Dutch regions into a state from a prosopographic perspective. (2) F. P. Wagenaar's "Dat de regeringe niet en bestaet by het corpus van de magistraet van den hage alleen": De societeit van 's Gravenhage (1582-1802). Een onderzoek naar bureaucratisering (["That the Government Doth Not Exist by the Corpus of the Magistry of The Hague Alone": The Society of The Hague (1582-1802). A Bureaucratization Study] Hilversum: Verloren, 2000) studies longitudinal developments in a single administrative body from a classical sociological perspective. (3) Bureaucraten betrapt: Historische Opstellen ([Bureaucrats Caught. Historical Essays] Rietbergen, P. J. A. N. [Ed], Amersfoort: Bekking, 2001) views the state & its administrative processes as cultural-historical phenomena. (4) In Paul Knevel's Het Haagse bureau: Zeventiende-eeuwse ambtenaren tussen staatsbelang en eigenbelang ([The Agencies of The Hague: 17th-Century Clerks between State Interests and Private Interests] Amsterdam: Prometheus/Bert Bakker, 2001) a culture-historical perspective is used to create a narrative microhistory of civil servants in the early modern Dutch state. The elaboration in each work of the themes of the lack of excitement in civil work & workers' personalities, the role of trust in the interpersonal networks of the early modern era, & its historiographical merits are discussed. It is concluded that each work highlights an essential moment in the development of Dutch bureaucracy, & that the heavy reliance on interpersonal relationships over time strengthened bureaucracy. 27 References. S. Paul

title: Comment on Research of Role of Local Government in Land Management in Recent Decade
abstract: The role of local government is an important factor in solving problems of land management and land use. After new Land Management Act in 1998, scholars have more and more studies on local government. At present, the studies focus on proper role and actual situation of local government, determining factors and changing mechanism of local government role. There are insufficient in study of local government's role. Adapted from the source document.

title: Land Management for Urban Development in Mexico
abstract: The new procedures for incorporating social land into the orderly growth of cities has failed to reduce its irregular occupation. This is due to two main factors: a) the State's continued overregulation of ejido & communal land owners, a practice which must be eliminated; & b) the extremely limited ability of municipal governments to arrange & plan urban development owing to the fact that the actual achievements of the 1983 municipal reform have been insufficient. The author ends by suggesting a reformulation of the notion of "territorial reserves" & pointing out the main areas of municipal administration that require attention. Tables, Figures, References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Accountability, New Public Management, and the Problems of the Child Support Agency
abstract: Evaluates the accountability of Next Steps Agencies in England through the medium of a case study of the child support agency. This agency, widely considered to offer a substandard service to its customers, was the subject of multiple reports by the House of Commons Social Services Select Committee, the Select Committee on the Parliamentary Commissioner, & the Public Accounts Committee. In addition, these committees had at their disposal internal reports from an adjudicator & the Child Support commissioner. The interlock between internal & external machinery for accountability is also considered. Adapted from the source document.

title: The coordination of the Brazilian federal public administration in the context of administrative reforms
abstract: This paper aims to discuss the coordination of the federal public administration at the time of administrative reforms, listing for this analysis the three major reforms of the twentieth century, namely: in 1938, with the creation of DASP; 1967, with the institution of the Decree-Law 200 and 1995 reform already in the democratic period. Two assumptions were considered: firstly, a pattern of continuity in the coordination of the three administrative reforms studied; secondly, the central organs of administrative coordination was strongly tied to the federal executive. The reforms were treated as critical junctures, i.e. moments in which a great discretion is shaping institutions, favoring changes in the type of coordination, whether it is more hierarchical (vertical) or more plural (horizontal). The main changes and difficulties in coordination pattern of the federal public administration in Brazil during periods of reform in screen were analyzed. Adapted from the source document.
