This was a period of increasing Dutch anxiety over weakening imperial dominion in Southeast Asia and both the colonial administration and colonial businesses feared Muslim religious networks would expose colonial subjects to anti-imperial and pan-Islamic ideas while abroad. It was vital for Dutch shipping companies to maintain segregated and highly policed spaces onboard to uphold Kongsi Tiga's monopoly over shipping between the Netherlands East Indies and Jeddah and to counter threats to Dutch hegemony more generally. Worried that "dangerous" passengers, such as Hadrami Arabs and Meccan sheikhs, would influence the general "spirit" of Indonesian pilgrims onboard by encouraging anti-colonial, nationalistic, and pan-Islamic sentiments, Kongsi Tiga systematically segregated passengers along racial, ethnic, and class lines. Racial and religious categories also informed Kongsi Tiga's reactions to indigenous shipping initiatives by Indonesian Muslims. Proposals put forth by Muslim organizations such as Muhammidiyah, were swiftly undermined by the combined forces of Dutch shipping companies and the colonial administration who worked together to maintain a Dutch monopoly over hajj shipping, not only for financial profit, but to foster Dutch control over transnationally mobile colonial subjects. This article reveals the unique and vital role shipping companies played in expanding colonial politics, culture, and society across transoceanic spaces and reconceptualizes our geographic understanding of empire as inhabiting the overlooked oceanic spaces between metropole and colony.

title: The Construction of a Market: A Frame Analysis of the Liberalization of the Electricity Market in the European Union
abstract: This article examines a specific case of policy making in the European Union, the liberalization of electricity. This case illustrates the shortcomings of traditional realist & rational choice approaches to the study of political processes. Drawing on empirical research & utilizing analytical tools from the sociological cultural institutionalism & social movements studies, the article identifies & analyses cultural frames & the transformation of these in order to interpret the changes in the European electricity policy domain, changes that traditional realist & neofunctionalist approaches could not predict. The article brings out the importance of an elite bureaucratic movement that is able to frame & reframe issues within the borders of existing cultural master frames. It is also shown how transformation of frames affects the structure of interest groups at the European level. 54 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: BUREAUCRACY AND SMALL ORGANIZATIONS
abstract: A consideration of the applicability & utility of the bur'tic model for the study of small org's. The hyp's proposed are: (1) that small org's are not signif'ly less bur'tic, & (2) that size & increasing bur'tion are not related. Using the Likert technique, scales are constructed to measure the 6 dimensions of bur'tion for org's of any size. The scales are admin'ed to S small org's. The results are tabulated using the Mann-Whitney U-Test & Rank Order Coefficient. It is found that in 4 of the 6 dimensions, the small org is not signif'ly less bur'tic than larger org's. An additional finding was that degree of bur'tion is apparently a function of factors other than size. It is suggested that the small org provides a convenient & fruitful res site in which to study the varying effects of bur'tion on both individuals & the org. AA.

title: The 'Council of Mayors' in Stockholm, and Similar Institutions in Oslo, Copenhagen and Helsinki-Some Comparative Considerations
abstract: The Scandinavian capitals have attempted to link admin'ive direction to pol'al responsibility. In Stockholm there is a council of mayors designated through pol'al election; each mayor is the head of an admin'ive service & exercises admin'ive power. These mayors prepare questions concerning local problems before transmitting them to the municipal council. Oslo has adopted a similar system in which the councilmen are functionaries who are not elected & who have only advisory powers; they are not members of the municipal council. Copenhagen has introduced a distinction between the functions of the municipal council (the executive) & that of the mayors who are only an admin'ive body. These mayors are elected for 8 yrs by the municipal council. In Helsinki the council similarly elects 9 mayors who are responsible for diff admin'ive branches, & who also are not members of the admin'ive council. (Tr by J. A. Broussard from IPSA).

title: When 'good' conflicts go bad: Testing a frame-building model on embeds' attitudes toward government news management in the Iraq War
abstract: Scholars have debated how successful the government was in managing coverage of the ground war in Iraq through the embed system, but few have surveyed the embedded journalists themselves to discover the degree they believe their press freedom was restricted. This study compares results from a survey conducted of embedded journalists in late 2005 and early 2006 to one conducted in early 2004 to examine whether embeds' opinions toward press freedom have changed over time and whether they believe government news management has increased as criticism of the Iraq War has increased and public support has declined. It also tests the hierarchy-of-influences model by examining the degree to which individual, journalism routines, external and cultural factors significantly predict attitudes toward press freedom and perceptions of censorship after controlling for demographics and political ideology. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright holder.]

title: Tax Collection in Developing Countries -- New Evidence on Semi-Autonomous Revenue Agencies (SARAs)
authors: von Haldenwang, Christian; von Schiller, Armin; Garcia, Melody
abstract: Over the last two decades, semi-autonomous revenue agencies (SARAs) have become a key element of public administration reform. They are supposed to improve revenue mobilisation and stabilise state-taxpayer relations. But do SARAs really outperform conventional tax administrations? This article argues that they do. Presenting the results of a panel analysis of local tax collection in Peru between 1998 and 2011, it shows that municipalities with SARAs collect more revenue than those with conventional tax administrations. The results also indicate that local revenue is more stable in municipalities with SARAs, which is good for budget policy and planning. Adapted from the source document.

title: Focal Point: Social and Health Administration
abstract: Since its foundation twenty-five years ago, Konstanz U (Federal Republic Germany) has offered a program of administrative science. The broad aspects covered in this interdisciplinary curriculum will become increasingly important for social & health systems in the future, as an increasing number of social services need to be administered, & as health professionals become more aware of the need for publicly administrated social & health services. The articles in this special issue are devoted to problems in this relatively new & rapidly evolving field. A. Machold

title: Politics and Management Autonomy in Cultural Services
abstract: The Italian Ministry of Labor's "Bridge" Project, which is sponsored by the EU & the European Social Fund, has a dual objective: to serve as a European initiative to look at the particular circumstances of the Italian community in Belgium, & to stimulate new management & occupational projects in the Italian cultural sphere. It is argued that in the case of the latter many cultural services are ill-suited to the type of (private sector) management reforms recommended elsewhere: self-management is difficult for institutions that rely on public moneys & hence require public oversight. Further, the nonprofit sector, which is the preeminent supplier of cultural services in Italy, is different in kind from the type of for-profit concern management that would be imported to run its affairs. A. Siegel

title: Clandestinity and 'Makwerekwere' in South Africa Post Apartheid: Category Production, Administrative Practices and Xenophobia
abstract: Based on research conducted in South Africa for over a decade, this paper assesses the current situation of irregular migrants. Despite a progressive legal dispensation and enlightened political elites, post-apartheid migration policy has continuously produced high numbers of irregular migrants that amnesties and a new asylum regime have only partly protected. The absence of migration instruments adapted to the needs of regional labor movements and cleavages between political elites and segments of the population have durably prevented the implementation of more innovative policies. Tables, References. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright.]

title: "Lick a Stamp, Lick the Kaiser": Sensing the Federal Government in Children's Lives during World War I
abstract: This article explores how the federal government mobilized American citizens during World War I by turning to their sensory experiences, particularly taste and sight. Through the Treasury Department and the United States Food Administration, as well as through state Councils of Defense and public schools, the federal government disseminated national messages surrounding food conservation and thrift. In doing so, it drew on the prior work of religious and business organizations in engaging the senses. Children stood at the center of these war mobilization strategies, representing critical targets for conservation and thrift. Relying on sources including government publications, letters, diaries, and children's poetry, this article illuminates in previously unexplored ways the extent to which federal policies infiltrated children's lives by politicizing their senses. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Maintaining the Momentum

title: Reforming Medicaid through Contracting: The Nexus of Implementation and Organizational Culture
authors: Romzek, Barbara S; Johnston, Jocelyn M
abstract: Investigates the administrative experience resulting from the intersection of two popular public management trends -- social service reform & contracting out -- offering a case study of a reform in which KS contracted with nonprofit agencies to provide Medicaid case management services. Implementation of the reforms entailed substantial changes in the roles & scope of administrative activities for the agencies involved & significant challenges to the administrative cultures of each. As a result, nonprofit agencies now play a more central role in state policy deliberations & encounter higher levels of interagency political conflict than they did prior to their contracting role. While some of the rationales for the policy reform have been realized, others have been more elusive, including cost savings & the single-point-of-entry organizing principle of the reform. Implementation challenges due to turf issues, tensions over external monitoring, & differences in administrative cultures have contributed to a lack of policy subgroup cohesiveness, which could facilitate intra- & intergovernmental relationships. 1 Exhibit, 1 Appendix, 53 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Markets, Networks and the New Welfare State: Employment Assistance Reforms in Australia
abstract: Contemporary theoretical debates point to a transformation of societies & social organizations away from universal forms of mass production & consumption, organized through mass institutions, toward smaller, diversified, entrepreneurial units linked together by new forms of market & network coordination. This greater diversity is also held to be a feature of service users who require individually fashioned solutions to nonstandard problems & tailored products for their different tastes. Applications of these accounts of social & economic transformation to the public sector propose similar patterns to those evident in private industry & in regional communities. The large, standardized bureaucracy is seen to give way to decoupled, multiple-agency models of service delivery in a new type of welfare state. Here, data obtained 1994-1996 via interviews & surveys (N = 365) with service delivery staff in the Australian employment assistance sector, where transformations of this type have recently been sponsored by government, indicate that many of the key propositions of the post-Fordist account are valid. Smaller, nonunionized units dominate the new order, & services are devolved to the local level. However, a number of the expected patterns of flexible specialization, diversity, & networking are not found, suggesting marked differences & possible tensions between public- & private-sector forms of organizational development in the new order. 6 Tables, 1 Figure, 33 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Families: Intergenerational and Generational Connections - Conceptual Approaches to Kinship and Culture
abstract: Families: Intergenerational and Generational Connections-Conceptual Approaches to Kinship and CultureThe thesis of this essay is that intergenerational rules are now changing. As a result, theories to interpret these changes need to be examined. Up to about 1960, a generation ago, self-regulating mechanisms in the private sector worked well enough to transfer resources between different generations. Since then, public bureaucracies have been more and more involved. This has happened because more citizens live longer, more households are daily empty of persons who could give services to others, and more communities lose the obligation to provide group quarters for those who cannot fully meet the normal activities of daily living. We view these changes as readjustments in the institutional framework of industrial societies as markets and government bureaucratic agencies assume obligations formerly left entirely to informal and self-regulating personal relations. We will discuss some concepts that may relate social theory to the on-going debate between the generations in modern societies.For a complete reprint of this article contact Haworth Press by telephone (1-800-HAWORTH) or EMail (getinfo@haworth.com) Article copyright The Haworth Press, Inc.

title: Between Civil Society and the State: Bureaucratic Competence and Cultural Mediation among Muslim Undertakers in Berlin
abstract: This article explores the intercultural negotiations around the death and burial of Muslims in Germany. In particular, it examines the mediating role that Muslim undertakers play between immigrant families and the German state. Drawing on an ethnographic study of Turkish funeral homes and the Islamic funeral industry in Berlin, it argues that undertakers' ability to navigate the regulatory structures of the German bureaucracy and the cultural expectations of their customers is a defining feature of their occupational identity and a principal source of their professional authority. As intermediaries between civil society and the state, undertakers guide families through the cultural, religious, political, and legal landscapes that structure the transitions from life to death. In burying the dead and tending to the living, they must reconcile competing sets of administrative and cultural norms surrounding death and interment. In doing so, the Muslim undertakers of Berlin preside not only over end-of-life decisions and their theological implications, but also over pedagogical moments in processes of political and cultural integration in contemporary Germany.

title: Through Racing Goggles: Modernity, the West, Ambiguous Siamese Alterities and the Construction of Thai Nationalism
abstract: Prince Chulachakrabongse and Prince Birabongse Bhanudej were sent to England to study at Harrow and Eton in the 1920s. They lived as Thai princes among the English upper class and indulged in the pastimes of that class, such as athletics, flying and motor car racing. Bira became a successful race car driver on the White Mouse Racing Team, managed by Chula. He even won the Gold Star, awarded to the best "British" race car driver, in three consecutive years -- 1936, 1937 and 1938. His achievements were celebrated in Siam as a sign of national greatness and of Siam's parity with the West. Racing was and still is closely associated with the nation. Bira's and Chula's story contributes to the study of the top-down construction of Thai nationalism. Thai nationalism is not about an armed struggle against colonial oppressors. It is about mastering Western civilization in attempts to appear equal. It is a nationalism closely associated with the monarchy, members of the royal family, aristocrats and bureaucratic servants of the crown.

title: Urban Planning in Nigeria: Historical and Administrative Perspectives and a Discussion of the City of Calabar
abstract: The history, organization, & policy structure of the Nigerian urban planning scene are discussed. Characteristics of colonial & postcolonial planning frameworks are identified & illustrated. It is argued that, even in the face of a very rapid urban growth & acute urban management problem, planning in Nigeria has continuously exhibited policy & institutional inconsistency, fragmentation, & an absence of demonstrable national commitment. 4 Figures, 31 References. Modified HA

title: Reconciliation of French Administrations of Social Security
abstract: A discussion of social-security programs in France & their organization under a law passed in 1974. Application of the new law covers health insurance, old-age benefits, & family assistance, while strike benefits & workers' illness & injury benefits are excluded. The law is designed to establish norms for the amount & distribution of benefits in the various categories of Social Security. Areas of inadequate coverage are noted, ie, agricultural workers & members of the "liberal professions." Discussed are means of bringing about a reconciliation between the various administrations, & problems in current methods of administration, with particular reference to retirement benefits, which should be made equivalent for all members of the society. To be enacted by Jan 1978 are specific reforms in medical insurance, family assistance, & old-age benefits, & the cost to the government for each. Proposed future reforms are considered. The present law is overly ambitious & often not specific enough. Future problems include limitations on the willingness of taxpayers to pay for such services. Structural reform is necessary, but the establishment of a single bureau to administer all aspects of Social Security is not practical. There is a general resistance to change in the present system by professional groups, who benefit most from the current situation. A distinction must be made between "social insurance" & wholesale redistribution of income. 7 Tables, 13 Appendices. B. Annesser.

title: Historic Process and Response of Administrative Area in Guangxi in the Ming and Qing Dynasties: The Evolution of Dao
abstract: It was a great change of regional administrative system that Dao as the agency of Bu Zheng Si and An Cha Si became a sub-administrative area gradually in the Ming and Qing Dynasties. The Dao of Guangxi was in keeping with the interior about the installation and evolution, and had its own characteristics. The ruler strengthened the control in Guangxi in the Ming Dynasty, The Gai Tu Gui Liu in the earlier stage and the frontier crisis in the last stage in the Qing Dynasty brought about the frequent adjustment of the installation and limits of Dao, and reflected the influence of regional historic process on the installation and evolution of administrative area. The installation and evolution of Dao played an important role in the regional historic process and the construction of frontier defense in Guangxi. Adapted from the source document.

title: Public Perceptions of Ethics in Government
authors: Frederickson, H George; Frederickson, David G
abstract: To explain negative perceptions of government ethics, particularly the ethics of public administrators, the paradox of distance & the absence of role differentiation are employed. In the paradox of distance, the public holds negative views of government generally & public administrators in the abstract, but they have favorable to very favorable views of governmental programs with which they interact & favorable views of the bureaucrats whom they encounter. Much of the negative perception of government ethics & the ethics of public officials is based on public observations of the misdeeds of those who are elected or politically appointed. These negative perceptions are well founded. Unfortunately, the public holds similarly negative views of merit civil servants, although these public officials are much less often associated with corruption or unethical behavior. It is suggested that several contemporary governmental reforms will, in the long run, result in more rather than less government corruption. Adapted from the source document.

title: The General Archive of the State of Coahuila and Transparency. "In Defense of Our Memory"
abstract: This text recounts the situation that faced the General Archive of the [Mexican] State of Coahuila as a result of a series of governmental resolutions expedited in 2005 in relation to the creation of the Coahuila Institute of Access to Information & a number of laws accompanying it. These resolutions put at risk the existence of the General Archive & its function of resolving matters of historical documentation in the public administration offices. Before these measures could be enacted, a citizen movement was organized that signaled the problems. As a result, it was agreed that the Archive's doors would remain open to the public & that this patrimonial heritage would be preserved intact. Photographs. S. Stanton

title: Administrative Procedures and Social Professions in the Transformation of Income Support Policies
abstract: The main purpose of this article is to observe two phenomena that are analytically different: the processes of the institutionalized structure of policies & of those that give structure to the problems. In this shift of focus, it is possible to access the way the combinations of such procedures produce a transformation, the alternatives left to the actors & the policy beneficiaries, & the regularities that appear to function as a condition of reproduction of policies &/or of their achievements. One of the levels of analysis for the sociological research on social policies is the erogation of services & the criteria that the local administrations use to establish their objectives & their distribution of resources, particularly the role given to the social professions in local welfare. Through the social reconstruction of such processes of mediation of meaning, it is possible to reconstruct the sociological meaning of policies within policies. It is possible to reconstruct the correlation between structures & action procedures. R. Balistreri

title: Cleansing Procedures for Overlaps and Inconsistencies in Administrative Data. The Case of German Labour Market Data
abstract: Process-generated and administrative datasets have become increasingly important for labour market research over the past ten years. Major advantages of this data are large sample sizes, absence of retrospective gaps and unit nonresponses. Nevertheless, the quality and validity of the information remain unclear. This paper contributes to this subject, focusing on the variation of research results due to alternative data cleansing procedures. In particular, the paper uses the general set up for data cleaning proposed by Wunsch/Lechner (2008) in evaluating the outcome of training programmes in Germany. First results are limited to the sensitivity of the construction of the sample populations used for the counterfactuals analysis. The results emphasize that sample construction seems to be robust to the scenario used for the data cleansing. Adapted from the source document.

title: Latin American populist regimes as authoritarian traditions players: A heterodox view on a subject still relevant
abstract: The main points of the Latin American political culture and mentality, especially in its less modernized areas (Bolivia, Ecuador, Nicaragua and Venezuela), arise from colonial times. Baroque Catholicism has been one of the major factors in this process, revitalized in the second half of the 20th century by the theology and philosophy of liberation. It most important features are authoritarianism, paternalism and centralism, on the one hand, and inefficient functioning of the state bureaucracy, on the other. Contemporary populism is nourished by the preservation of this political culture seen now as innate. Particularistic and communitarian theories tend to strengthen this situation. Populism can bring a return of nationalist and collectivist behavior patterns and political procedures characterized by caudillismo, irrationalism and authoritarian hierarchies. Adapted from the source document.

title: Innovation and Functional Aspects of Language and the Question of Genre
abstract: Considers the place of genre in a sociolinguistic approach to the history of language, offering the example of prepositional expressions such as suite a, which authors of official reports use to go from the ordinary user's story to the argumentation that bureaucracy requires. The discrepancy between the external definition of genre & formal markers (use of vulgarity or the allergy to form letters contained in the appeals the administration receives) is analyzed. In this case, receivers may consider either that such missives are only a stylistic variation, or that they belong to a different genre altogether (letters of insult/complaint). 11 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Institutional Framework for Housing Policy Administration in Cameroon
abstract: Despite efforts aimed at alleviating the housing problem in Cameroon since gaining independence in 1960, problems remain, due largely to a weak capacity for housing policy administration. Unless this capacity is strengthened, efforts to deal with the problem are unlikely to yield any significant positive results. Toward this goal, principal institutional factors constraining the performance of the country's housing delivery system are identified. 1 Table, 1 Figure, 24 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Different sources to the users' experiences of the Norwegian Welfare and Work bureaucracy (Nav) -- methodological challenges and possibilities
authors: Hansen, Hans-Tore; Lundberg, Kjetil G; Syltevik, Liv Johanne
abstract: In an article entitled 'The Coming Crisis in Empirical Sociology', Savage and Burrows have started an important debate on the challenges facing traditional sociological methods in a time of knowing capitalism. They argue that sociologists ought to reflect more on the methods they use to face this challenge, which is our aim in this article. In our work evaluating the Norwegian welfare and work reform (Nav), and work on projects exploring users' experiences with the new welfare bureaucracy, we draw mainly on surveys, interviews and fieldwork in local Nav offices. In the main part of the article we discuss the possibilities and challenges that these methods present, and in addition reflect on other sources of data (newspaper articles, internet-blogs, facebook groups and data from user organizations) and their strengths and weaknesses. Adapted from the source document.

title: Mobilization by the Administration of a "Professional World of Training"
abstract: During the 1960s, a structure was created in the French public administration to generate & guide initiatives likely to foster the provision of adult education. Given this encouragement, the professional world of training, then beginning to take shape, devised & implemented a range of different programs for both professional & continuing education. However, the broad scope of these programs was gradually narrowed to just professional education, because of economic constraints & institutional arrangements defined by the public administration. 3 Appendixes, 11 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Administrative Compensation of Medical Injuries: A Hardy Perennial Blooms Again
authors: Barringer, Paul J; Studdert, David M; Kachalia, Allen B; Mello, Michelle M
abstract: Periods in which the costs of personal injury litigation and liability insurance have risen dramatically have often provoked calls for reform of the tort system, and medical malpractice is no exception. One proposal for fundamental reform made during several of these volatile periods has been to relocate personal injury disputes from the tort system to an alternative, administrative forum. In the medical injury realm, a leading incarnation of such proposals in recent years has been the idea of establishing specialized administrative "health courts." Despite considerable stake-holder and policy-maker interest, administrative compensation proposals have tended to struggle for broad political acceptance. In this article, we consider the historical experience of administrative medical injury compensation proposals, particularly in light of comparative examples in the context of workplace injuries, automobile injuries, and vaccine injuries. We conclude by examining conditions that may facilitate or impede progress toward establishing demonstration projects of health courts. Adapted from the source document.

title: AN APPROACH TO THE STUDY OF BUREAUCRACY
authors: HININGS, C R; Pugh, D S; Hickson, D J; Turner, C
abstract: Sociol needs precise, comparative, reliable data. This requires the splitting down of unitary `grand' concepts into operationally defined variables, fashioned to attack particular problems, & amenable to multivariate statistical analysis. This approach can be exemplified in the study of bur'cy by the development of scaleable dimensions of org structure such as 'specialization.' This concept has been operationally defined, & a comparative analysis across 52 work org's of the degree of `functional specialization' & of `role specialization' within each function has yielded 17 scales on which to base a profile, characteristic of each org. An `overall specialization scale,' obtained by factor analysis, gives a range of scores in the sample from 0 (no specialists) to 87 (an extremely high degree of role specialization with the org). Using size & technology as independent variables, a prediction analysis gives a multiple r with overall role specialization of 0.81. HA.

title: Para que serve uma UOP? Algumas considerações sobre a política de ordem pública no Rio de Janeiro
abstract: The paper What is the Purpose of a UOP (Public Order Unit)? Some Reflections on Public Order Policy in Rio de Janeiro analyses the main paths and premises for the role of the Special Public Order Secretariat (Seop) in Rio de Janeiro during mayor Eduardo Paes' first administration (2009-2011), with a policy that became known as "choque de ordem" (shock and order), discussing its foundations based on the use of "broken windows" theory, which correlates disorder and criminality. It also seeks to understand how the status of public security overlapped issues of urban order, prioritizing crime as a form of government, and proposes that these actions could be perceived as being caught in a continuum between public order and public security policy.

title: FINLAND'S MANAGER PLAN
abstract: The characteristics of Finnish manager gov are collective decision-making & the institutionalization of partisan participation in municipal admin, whereas in America the system has been directed toward centralizing admin'ive authority & reducing the influence of partisan politics. Thus, Finnish managers bear little resemblance to the US counterpart in name, & these diff's can be traced in large part to diff's in att's toward admin'ive structure, & the distrust of bur'cy & partisanship. The Finnish system provides internal checks through shared pol'al responsibility in the admin'ive process. IPSA.

title: Janio Quadros, the father of the poor: tradition and paternalism in the projection of the leader (1959-1960)
abstract: In analyzing Janio Quadros' political career, historians and social scientists pointed out that he acquired political strength as a national leader by proposing a rational and impersonal State administration. He would represent the antithesis of Getulio Vargas and Adhemar de Barros, whose political actions had a remarkable paternalistic content. This, however, does not seem to be entirely correct. Through letters he received between 1959 and 1960, when disputing the presidential elections, it is possible to observe that many of his supporters considered him a politician able to defend traditional social relations. Some invoked him to fight against speculators who stored goods in an inflationary scenario, while others treated him as a paternal figure by asking him money, jobs in the public administration and other sorts of favor. In this text, the author suggests that such demands could convey political manifestations and be expressions of citizenship. Adapted from the source document.

title: O processo de construção da gestão regional da saúde no estado de São Paulo: subsídios para a análise/The process of building up regional health management in the State of São Paulo: subsidies for analysis
authors: Mendes, Áquilas; Louvison, Marília C P; Ianni, Aurea M Z; Leite, Marcel Guedes; Feuerwerker, Laura C M; Tanaka, Oswaldo Y; Duarte, Ligia; Weiller, José Alexandre Buso; Lara, Natália Carolina Cairo; Botelho, Lygia de Andrade Machado; Almeida, Cristiane A L
abstract: This article presents the main results of the survey on the regional management building process in the State of S...o Paulo, during the discussion of the COAP / Care Networks, in order to provide a basis for understanding this process of regional health pact, focusing on the metropolitan areas of Bauru, Santos, Grande ABC and the Ribeira Valley. In addition to the results presented on the health regions studied, the methodology used in the development of the construction of profiles of the regions is itself a proposal for a methodology of analyzing regional health profiles. The first section presents the general methodology for analyzing health regions. The second part covers the results and discussion of the research, organized into two items. The first refers to the analysis of the profiles of the five S...o Paulo health regions surveyed. The second item analyzes the main aspects of the process of regional health pact in S...o Paulo, highlighting strengths and limitations, based on interviews with municipal managers and supporters of the Council of Municipal Health Secretaries of S...o Paulo in these regions.

title: Organizational Response to Disaster: A Typology of Adaptation and Change
abstract: A time sequenced model of bureaucratic adaptation to a disaster episode is derived from one developed by J. R. Brouillette & E. L. Quarantelli (originally abstracted as SA D8938/ASA/1969/0187). The Brouillette & Quarantelli model does not allow analysis of dynamics of organizational change, nor does it account for planning & normative orientations of disaster subcultures. Using A. H. Barton's taxonomy of disaster phases (Communities in Disaster: A Sociological Analysis of Collective Stress Situations, Garden City, NY: Anchor Books, 1970), a typology is derived that accounts for disaster as a process & includes the expected influences of planning. With this dynamic model, short-term, particularistic, adaptations of the organization can be distinguished from long-term, universalistic, organizational change. The model is then tested on an empirical example based on a recent major flood. Results showed that the typology was applicable; however, some questions were raised as to the generalizability of Barton's typology. Recommendations are also made concerning difficulties encountered in applying the typology. 8 Figures. Modified AA.

title: Introduction; Patrimonialism, Past and Present
abstract: On January 14, 2011, thousands of protesters gathered in the Avenue Bourguiba, the main artery of Tunisia's capital city, Tunis, to demand the ouster of an authoritarian president who had been in power for 23 years. Similar demonstrations swept across Tunisia, with many galvanizing small towns throughout the country. Following Tunisia, protesters marched in the streets of Jordan, Algeria, and Yemen. On February 1 and again on February 4, 2011, hundreds of thousands of Egyptians flooded Tahrir (Liberation) Square in Cairo and other cities to demand the departure of a president who had been in power for 30 years. In Tunisia and Egypt, the popular uprisings sought to bring about a new political order and to end the influence of rulers' families in politics, the economy, and social life. They also explicitly targeted any hereditary transfer of power that would have codified, in disguise, a reversion to absolutist patrimonial monarchy.

title: Stretched but not snapped: constitutional lessons from the 2010 coalition government in Britain
abstract: Taking as its point of departure Matthews' (2011) 'Constitutional stretching: Coalition governance and the Westminster model (Commonwealth & Comparative Politics, 49(4), 486-509), this article draws on the experience of coalition government in Westminster to review, categorise and consider how power sharing has necessitated a rethink of what is the British constitution. Defining constitutional stretching as being about the sustained operation of two-party government within the Westminster model, it shows that traditional practices around manifestos, collective responsibility and the prerogative have been adjusted since 2010 in order to facilitate functioning administration. The article observes that some stretching is not entirely novel with precedents to be found in earlier single party administrations. It further argues that while conventions have been strained, the Cameron/Clegg government survived, suggesting a need to adjust our understanding of constitutional concepts. Given the likelihood of future hung parliaments, this could mean more permanent constitutional change and the article makes some modest suggestions for updating guidance.

title: Assessing the effects of neighborhood councils on urban policy and development: The example of Tacoma, Washington
abstract: Neighborhood councils form an important and sometimes problematic layer in the governance system of many cities across the USA. The literature on these institutions has focused mainly on their hypothesized role in facilitating citizen participation in neighborhood and city planning. Less work has explored the experiences of neighborhood councils as placed-based institutions theoretically embedded within, and therefore ostensibly reflective of, the overall social and political geography of the city. In particular, little research documents the actual local development priorities, fund-raising capacities, project achievements and scalar tensions associated with neighborhood councils operating in different neighborhoods of the same city. Using a perspective based on extant literatures in urban politics and public administration, this paper offers an analysis of the neighborhood council experience in Tacoma, Washington, USA. While these councils are still "segmented" from the core of urban politics, the paper argues, certain institutional reforms could unlock their long term potential as more "transformative" spaces of local governance. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Economic Policy Reform in Developing Countries: The Role and Management of Political Factors
abstract: An introduction to three papers (see abstracts in this section of SOPODA 13:1) examining the political & administrative factors that determine policy responses among different developing countries. Common themes are discussed, including: the role of political analysis & explanation; the relationship of "political will" to the reform process; & the value of the implementation phase of reform. These authors' approaches to policy making, which are critically examined, include: a taxonomy of categories for classification of political ramifications of macroeconomic policies; political variables underlying the engineering & management of change; & policy reform at the microlevel. It is concluded that policy-making styles are rooted in the interdependence of the state & society. 3 References. S. G. Yates

title: The Role of Local Public Administration Locale in Providing Social Welfare
abstract: The beginning of 90s represents the option of Romanian Government for a welfare state based on decentralization of social services delivery. This options lead to a change of relationships between public administration & citizens & to a reevaluation of the role of local government. From this perspective, this article analyze the role of local government in social services delivery. It approaches aspects like legislation, local government's relationships with central authorities, methods of local budget constitution, local authorities responsibilities in social services delivery.

title: Evaluating Child Homicide Inquests as a Learning Process: A Social Constructionist Analysis of a Canadian Experience
abstract: The death of a child known to protection agencies is perhaps the gravest critical incident affecting child welfare today. Media coverage of such tragedies has fueled public demand for solutions to this problem. In response, several countries have conducted judicial or public investigations into child homicide deaths. It is suggested here that a social constructionist understanding of organizations as cultures provides a useful perspective from which to conduct an inquest into the inquest process itself. This framework is applied to a coroner's inquest held in Ontario in 1997, & the inquest proceedings are seen to be a "storying of experience," not an impartial & comprehensive exploration of the facts. It is argued that the interpretation of the child abuse death was limited by a bureaucratic orientation. While this orientation did result in a number of promising solutions, those that were emphasized tended to reflect the paradigms, practices, & needs of the dominant stakeholders in the proceedings. The potential dangers of several of the resulting recommendations are considered. An acknowledgement of the subjectivity inherent in current inquests, coupled with a deliberate effort to integrate insights from other paradigms & perspectives, is a critical first step toward improving understanding of how to prevent child homicide deaths. Several recommendations are offered. 39 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Important but Largely Unanswered Questions about Accountability in Contracted Public Human Services
authors: Ott, J Steven; Dicke, Lisa A
abstract: Contracting-out for human services has become preferred public policy at all levels of government. This service delivery policy choice has important implications for accountability & for the ability of contracting nonprofit organizations to be flexible & innovative. Although the use of contracting has expanded dramatically in the human services since the 1970s, many important public management policy questions remain unasked & unanswered. This article raises & discusses nine largely unanswered questions that are central to the reasons why government continues to expand its dependence on contracted human services. These questions address key elements of a larger policy-of-public-management question: "Is it possible to achieve accountability & flexibility when government contracts-out for the provision of publicly funded human services?" By addressing these nine questions, we seek to determine what is known & not known about the key accountability issues in contracted public human services. We also attempt to highlight the importance of these questions & issues for public management policy, intersectorial organization theory, the practice of nonprofit & public organization management, & thus for research & theory development. 2 Figures, 100 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Myth of the M-Form? Governance, Consent, and Organizational Change
abstract: Using the textbook case of General Motors (GM), the multidivisional governance structure (M-form) is critiqued, shown to have only existed briefly, & counterpoised with an argument that emphasizes the role of consent in corporate governance. Most accounts argue that the M-form rose because of increased efficiency over earlier models of business organization. GM departed from the fundamental strategy of decentralization by intentionally introducing administrative centralization -- a development that counters the logic of transaction costs economics (TCE) as developed by Oliver Williamson (1975). Efficiency theory neither predicts nor explains this development, but GM successfully reigned for decades as one of the most powerful & profitable firms in the world. The corporation's decline began only after it implemented a classic version of the M-form, in which planning was under the control of top officers free of divisional responsibilities. The actual case of GM, however, reveals that management will institute fiat & financial control mechanisms as a substitute for decentralization in order to achieve bureaucratic compliance for short-term performance in lieu of long-term competitive advantage. 217 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Structuralism as Defense of the Bureaucratic Status Quo: A Dialectical Critique of Althusserian Theory
abstract: The writings of L. Althusser, once highly influential, may now be in decline. Interest in his work stems from 3 sources: (1) their apparent freedom from Stalinism, (2) their idealist element, & (3) the scientific character of Althusser's methodology--all of which render Althusser attractive to liberal Western intellectuals. Considering these features of his work, & its presumed post-WWII political relevance, Althusser is found wanting. His anti-Stalinism is only apparent for it hides or masks 2 central aims of his thought. Whereas he appears to reject rigid dialectical thinking in favor of criticism, Althusser in fact proposes criticism so as to maintain absolute control of the party. Any definition of revolution that removes the party, & therefore its bureaucratic apparatus from control, is not acceptable to Althusser. The 2nd aim is to remove the USSR from the functioning of dialectial laws. Because his actual intent is to maintain a bureaucratic status quo, Althusser is not able to account for either the Hungarian revolt or the 1968 French revolt. His attempt is only to remove theory from practice. F. Hydoski.

title: Mass Production of Law. Routinization in the Transposition of European Directives: A Sociological-Institutionalist Account
authors: Berglund, Sara; Gange, Ieva; van Waarden, Frans
abstract: This paper assesses the claim that there is a problem with delayed transposition of directives within the EU, using a new dataset on the transposition of directives in the fields of utilities & food safety regulation in the Netherlands, Germany, the UK, Spain & Greece. This dataset overcomes most of the problems that have plagued previous data. In 65 per cent of the cases transposition was delayed, & the average delay was seven months. There is thus indeed a problem with delayed transposition. In order to explain this problem, a sociological institutionalist approach is used. The findings point to the importance of administrative routinization. Whether or not transposition is accomplished with little delay depends on whether there are administrative departments with the explicit task to specialize in transposition, & whether they have had the time & resources to develop routines or standard operating procedures for doing so. Tables, Figures, References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Citizens and administration: dysfunctional bureaucracy and the dissemination of remedies
abstract: The concept of bureaucracy has undergone a degree of proliferation that has made it impossible to furnish a single, unequivocal definition of it common to the social sciences. The only paradigm that is commonly agreed on is Weber's definition of bureaucracy as a necessary expression of rational legal power. Nevertheless, the concept of bureaucracy conveys two explicitly negative connotations that are perceived by the general public as its two greatest problems: the inefficiency of public organisations and the arbitrary behaviour of its officials. Itemising the characteristics of the bureaucratic personality, Merton includes ritualism and deresponsibilisation. Crozier also notes that the larger and more complex that organisations become, the higher the level where responsibility for decision-making is vested, creating a decision-making bottleneck. The empirical research conducted by Jochimsen in Germany seems to confirm that an increase in an organisation's dimensions can generate significant diseconomies of scale. More recently, the theories of public choice have contested the assumption that officials interpret the public interest. Lastly, the crisis of the welfare state has led to a containment of public organisations and to the rise of the doctrine of new public management, which preaches the superiority of the private sector and suggests the introduction of the mechanisms of the market and of competition in the public sector. Despite the radical transformations wrought by new public management, scepticism towards public organisations is widespread in all Western countries, as recent surveys conducted at European level by the Eurobarometer have demonstrated. In conclusion, the article mentions the empirical research conducted to establish the effectiveness of ombudsmen in influencing the public's perception of bureaucracy and in changing its practices. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Paradox of Malevolent/Benevolent Bureaucracy
abstract: For Ralph Hummel (The Bureaucratic Experience, 3rd edition, New York: Saint Martins, 1987) bureaucracy is bad, while for Charles Goodsell (The Case for Bureaucracy, 2nd edition, Chatham, NJ: Chatham House, 1985) it is good (in the US). The professional literature is also divided between those who see bureaucratization increasing & those who see it decreasing. The paradox may be resolved if the literature is separated into works that consider bureaucracy primarily in terms of (1) individual organizations, (2) societal processes, & (3) organizational fields. Thus, bureaucracy may be receding in terms of organizational structures & fields at the same time that societal bureaucratization (rationalization) increases. Hummel & Goodsell may both be correct if the US public sector has been substantially debureaucratized (categories 1 & 3). To reduce the confusion, academics should substitute "organizational rationalization" for "societal bureaucratization.". 57 References. AA

title: Ethical Preparation and Its Importance in the Government Sector in Kuwait and Other GCC Countries
abstract: Argues that ethical preparation is needed to improve the efficiency of bureaucracies in Kuwait & other GCC countries. An investigation of bureaucratic work ethics focused on the political activities of civil servants & the conflict of interests between the private & public sectors. Ethical challenges are discussed, & government efforts to address ethical considerations are described, especially the code of ethics issued by the Zakat House. It is suggested that the development & implementation of a plan for ethical preparation should include reorientation of bureaucratic values & patterns of behavior, the creation of tools to foster ethical values, & the development of strategies for administrative supervision & monitoring. The plan should also include ways to instill public workers with a greater sense of public service. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Administrative Department of Sao Paulo State in the Institutional Engineering of the New State
abstract: Introduces & reprints a (1940) document from the Administrative Dept of Sao Paulo State, Brazil, highlighting the complexity of the institutional design of the New State, its mechanisms of representation of interests, & the ambiguous relations of the Paulista political elite to the Getulio Vargas dictatorial regime. 7 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Eminences Grise or Loyal Servants? Governmental Administrations in Processes of Political Decisions
abstract: Kai-Uwe Schnapp claims that it cannot be decided normatively if administration holds too much power. Instead their influence on political decisions must be measured & then be judged. For this reason he develops some indicators concentrating on opportunities of influence related to agenda-setting, organizational structures, & implementation. He shows, that concerning agenda-setting Germany's political system enables politicians quite well to control the administration. Problems occur related to the organizational structures & implementation. 11 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Models of disaster response: lessons learned from Filipino immigrant mobilizations for Hurricane Katrina evacuees
abstract: Hurricane Katrina forced one of the largest internal migrations of people in USA history. Among the evacuees were 28,000 Filipino Americans, many of whom fled to Houston. In a short period of time, Filipino American Houstonians relocated their co-ethnics with host families, facilitated documents needed for US federal aid (FEMA), provided material assistance, and addressed evacuee medical needs through the establishment and staffing of a crisis triage clinic. Drawing on ethnographic and survey data, we contend that two key lessons can be gained from the Filipino case that local, state, and federal agencies can draw on for future emergency preparedness and disaster management. First, federal, state, and local agencies should better implement its partnership plans with identified ethnic- and faith-based organizations in order to both network and mobilize diverse resources more efficiently. Second, this implementation should include a more effective communication plan to coordinate efforts among people of all English proficiencies and cultural backgrounds. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: BUREAUCRATIC LEADERSHIP, DIRECT ACTION AND ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE: THE ENGLISH SYNDICALIST MOVEMENT IN 1919. INTRODUCTION TO "DIRECT ACTION"
abstract: THE DILEMMA OF ELITIST LEADERSHIP WITHIN THE TRADE UNION MOVEMENT REMAINS A CURRENT PROBLEM. IT HAS CONCERNED THE WORKERS' MOVEMENT SINCE THE TURN OF THE CENTURY & GAINED NEW RELEVANCE DURING THE FRENCH STUDENT DISORDERS IN 1968. THE FUNDAMENTAL PROBLEM IS THAT THE SYNDICALIST MOVEMENT CRITICIZES ALL CONSOLIDATED ORGANISMS OF POWER, BUT TO ACHIEVE ITS GOALS, MUST ITSELF EMPLOY THE ORGANIZATIONAL WEAPON--ITS TENDENCY TO REGRESS INTO BUREAUCRATISM NOTWITHSTANDING. THESE PROBLEMS WERE DISCUSSED AT THE BEGINNING OF THE CENTURY BY R. MICHAELS (LA SOCIOLOGIA DEL PARTITO POLITICO THE SOCIOLOGY OF THE POLITICAL PARTY , BOLOGNA, ITALY: 1966) & E. BERNSTEIN (SOCIALISMO E SOCIAL DEMOCRAZIA SOCIALISM AND SOCIAL DEMOCRACY , BARI, ITALY: 1969) WHO PUT FORWARD A REVISIONIST THEORY ON THE ROLE OF THE TRADE UNION MOVEMENT & THE WC. THE PROPOSALS OF BRITISH TRADE UNION LEADERS CAMPBELL & GALLACHER, LATER CRITICIZED & CORRECTED BY LENIN, WERE TO REFORM THE SYNDICALIST STRUCTURE TO MAKE THE LEADERSHIP MORE RESPONSIVE TO THE RANK & FILE & TO FIGHT FOR WORKER CONTROL FROM WITHIN THE INDUSTRY. S. KARGANOVIC.

title: Considering risk theories in relation to a case study in the south of Brazil
authors: FIGUEIREDO, Joao Alcione Sganderla; LENZ, Catia Aguiar; NUNES, Margarete Fagundes
abstract: This survey investigates the environmental risk perception and the relationship with different actors, related to the tanning industry in the Sinos Valley region (Vale do Rio dos Sinos), Brazil. Such analysis lies in the constructivist theory, explaining how the Perceived Risk. Even though the focus of this survey focuses on a theoretical review of the theories of risk, it is based on collected data for a larger study, in which were applied 307 questionnaires and 32 interviews with different actors (workers, public administration, NGOs, neighbors and entrepreneurs). In relation to the risk perception, we will see that it is embedded in the social formation, historical and cultural community of the Sinos Valley. On the other hand, the local context emphasizes the dynamics of industrialization as the basis for progress. Thus, even identifying, in part, the risks, they are denied or silenced by the economic dependence (employment and income) of the industrial sector. Adapted from the source document.

title: Re-Enchanting Social Work? The Emerging 'Spirit' of Social Work in an Age of Economic Crisis
abstract: Luc Boltanski and Eve Chiapello's (2005) The New Spirit of Capitalism argues that capitalism has the capacity to absorb critique and become ideologically energised and discursively reinvigorated on account of this capacity. This article argues that their theorisation provides a useful theoretical lens through which to view and comprehend present attempts to re-enchant the profession and discursively infuse it with a new 'spirit', in times of 'austerity' and budget cuts: hence, the emerging emphasis on social work as a 'creative' profession needing to free itself from 'bureaucracy'. Although partly heeding the critique derived from the academic literature illuminating the constraints imposed on social work by an ever-expanding digital e-workload, this move is deeply ideological and needs to be warily regarded. Adapted from the source document.

title: Book Review: (Re)searching Women: Feminist Research Methodologies in the Social Sciences in Ireland
abstract: Byrne, Anne and Lentin, Ronit (eds.), (Re)searching Women: Feminist research methodologies in the social sciences in Ireland, Dublin: Institute for Public Administration, 2000, paper IR£16.95.

title: Muddying the Waters: Policies, Politics, Planning and Performance
abstract: A review essay on three books by: Herman L. Boschken, Strategic Design and Organizational Change: Pacific Rim Seaports in Transition (Tuscaloosa: U of Alabama Press, 1989); William T. Gormley, Jr., Taming the Bureaucracy: Muscles, Prayers, and Other Strategies (Princeton, NJ: Princeton U Press, 1989); & Carl E. Van Horn, Donald Baumer, & William T. Gormley, Jr., Politics and Public Policy (Washington, DC: Congressional Quarterly Press, 1989 [see listings in IRPSPPD No. 22]). These three books examine the relationship between politics & US public policy processes & institutions. Boschken examines six US seaports on the Pacific Rim & responses of port authorities to major policy changes affecting their transitional survival in the late twentieth century. Gormley studies institutional reform efforts in US politics during the 1970s & 1980s, using the "reform determines performance" paradigm. Van Horn, Baumer, & Gormley present an overview of US political institutions & the policy process, but do not add to a better understanding of public policy; in fact, the work muddies the water with its premise that institutions determine policies. 1 Reference. M. Malas

title: An Exploratory Study of Public Service Motivation and the Institutional-Occupational Model of the Military
authors: Taylor, Jami K; Clerkin, Richard M; Ngaruiya, Katherine M; Velez, Anne-Lise Knox
abstract: This article empirically connects Moskos' Institutional-Occupational model to the large body of cross-nationally validated research on public service motivation (PSM). We find that in our sample, the PSM construct is positively correlated with institutional motivations that reflect Moskos' insights. We also find evidence that the four dimensions of PSM (Attraction to Public Participation, Commitment to Public Values, Self-sacrifice, and Compassion) may offer a more nuanced way to assess institutional motivations. Our research suggests that those interested in military recruitment/retention/performance and public administration scholars may have much to learn from each other. We call for further research in this area.

title: The Encounter between Jews and Poles in Lublin District after Liberation, 1944-1945
abstract: In recent years, the historiography of Jewish-Polish relations after the Holocaust has often shown a marked tendency to trace the conflict between these peoples to the central role of Jews in the new communist ruling system. Poles murdered hundreds of Jews, mainly in 1944 to 1946, for various reasons--some ideological, others economic. The collective guilt that the Polish political right and some of Polish society assigned to the Jews, however, proves to be inaccurate when one examines the community of Jewish survivors who gathered in the Lublin district, the first area to be liberated from Nazi occupation (summer of 1944). Most survivors were roundly disinterested, let alone involved, in politics, and the issue of communism in Poland was totally alien to them. Their main concerns had to do with family property that had been abandoned during the deportations, an attempt to locate lost family members, and, above all, an effort to reengage with the life that the Nazi bloodbath had broken off. They were stunned to confront the intensity of Polish society's resentment and hostility toward them and the governing authorities' bureaucratic indifference. The conflation of these two factors prompted many to abandon their prior places of residence, to move to new areas of settlement, or to leave Poland forever. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Ambiguity in Law and the Marginalisation of Sedentarised Nomads of the Southern Zagros Mountains of Iran
abstract: Bureaucratic systems that do not take cultural differences into account have a tendency to marginalize non-mainstream groups & even create laws wherein their behavior is considered illegal. The impact of imposing a modern legal & bureaucratic system on traditional peoples is illustrated in this case of the sedentary Lor (Mamasani) in Iran, using fieldwork from 1977 on. In the Lor case, modern laws incompatible with the Lor's traditional justice system have created ambiguity & led to more feuding within the group. These feuds are no longer spaces of conflict where masculinities & individual capacities are at stake, but one in which weapons are used. This leads to heightened tension in the society & feeds even more irritability & feuding. 1 Figure, 16 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Academic Freedom in Sri Lanka
abstract: This contribution to a "Symposium: Academic Repression & Human Rights" contends that freedom for academics is the right to speak & teach in the classroom or in the community without censure from their institutions. This article contends that academics cannot enjoy such freedom unless others -- students, minorities, society at large -- have the same rights. The first collegiate institution in Asia was the Batticotta Seminary founded in 1823, which was soon known for its scholarly excellence. The U of Ceylon, founded in 1921, upheld this excellence. This paper, however, examines the contemporary lack of academic freedom in Sri Lanka brought about by a bureaucracy that circumscribes the activities of both teachers & students, in large part due to the struggle between the Sinhalese & the Tamils, which has constrained the administration & even provision of education. These struggles & their impact on education are described, particularly on academic freedom. References. S. Stanton

title: Mentoring and network ties
abstract: Using questionnaire data obtained from a sample of state government managers, our study examines social capital foci (network ties) of mentoring relations. Others have shown that network ties are relevant to career development and advance. We begin with the assumption that enhanced network ties are generally beneficial. We investigate variation in mentorships, which enhance network ties within the focal organization and within organizations external to the focal organization. We examine a number of factors hypothesized as shaping the relationship between mentoring and the development of network ties, including attributes of the protege and of the mentoring relationship. Our results show that the sex of the protege and of the mentor does not affect the quantity of network ties conveyed. However relationships in which protege and mentor sex is matched provide more network ties. Counter to our expectations, there is no significant difference in the amount and focus of network ties accruing from formal, organizationally sanctioned mentoring and informal mentoring. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright The Tavistock Institute.]

title: Social Administration and Its Relationship to the Sociology of Welfare
abstract: Differences beween social administrative work & the collective promotion of social welfare are discussed, arguing that sociology should contribute to the further understanding of welfare issues & in turn be incorporated into social administration. The difficulties of encompassing theoretical perspectives in social administration are outlined, & focus areas in social administration education & research are suggested, based on the work of R. M. Titmuss (Essays on the Welfare State, Allen & Unwin: London, 1958), including: policy formation & consequences, social needs & problems of access, & the role of government & the social rights of citizens. It is concluded that the sociology of welfare can make valuable contributions to social administration. 35 References. S. G. Yates

title: Complex Objectives, Decentralization, and the Decision Process of the Organization
abstract: A resource-directive model for means-ends factoring the org'al goal is developed in a way that circumvents interunit dependencies, or externalities, in decentralization. The model explicitly specializes the org's goals & decision-making activities into quasi-autonomous units, & thus imparts a well-defined org'al form. A key aspect of the model is the explicit treatment of the decision-making concept to mean a sequence of decisions by which the org makes a commitment to a tentative scheme of resource allocations & enacts exp's to gather information as a basis for future decision making. Specifically, the org is considered to act by the sequential process of decision making, operating, & then, on the basis of this experience, revising its decisions & policy goals, rather than as conventionally implied by the single-step analysis of a set of simultaneous equations. This behavior pattern specializes the firm's many-dimensional problem to a sequence of adaptive moves in fewer dimensions. Modified HA.

title: From Baghdad to the United Kingdom
abstract: This contribution to a "Symposium: Academic Repression & Human Rights" examines the efforts of the U of Wolverhampton (UK) to help their fellow academics in Iraq. In a model that incorporates personal reorientation & academic development, individuals seen as champions for "the cause" are brought together with academic leaders, decision makers, religious leaders, & social/personnel managers. The aim is for these individuals to return home & contribute to their country's future. This paper, in presenting the story of the model to date, illustrates how red tape & changing regulations constrain applications for visas, how inconsistency in the model vis-a-vis other programs creates confusion, & how the isolated academic individual deals with the risk he or she faces on returning to Iraq, where the murder of academics is not uncommon. References. S. Stanton

title: Professional training of the territorial agents. The impact of reforms of the continuous training in a sports communal service
abstract: How does evolve the professional training in the territorial public administration? Taking the example of a sports communal service, we present the new doctrine in this area (training throughout the life, the competence model) and institutional aspects (role of the National Center for Territorial Public Administration). We analyze, on one hand, the impact of reforms of the continuous training on collective representations of the training; on the other hand, the consequences of adjustment training with needs of territorial public employers. Adapted from the source document.

title: Problems in Developing a Ph.D. Program in Policy Studies for Practitioners
abstract: In Sept, 1976, Saint Louis U established a multidisciplinary PhD program in public policy analysis & administration, review of which illustrates some problems in developing such programs. Objectives included understanding of the nature of the individual & society, ethical commitment to the public good, development of analytical & decision-making methodologies, facility in multidisciplinary approaches, competence in research methods, & ability to work as a member of a decision-making team. The curriculum includes six required core courses & an area of concentration. Problems include faculty role & development, interdepartmental coordination, jurisdictional disputes between the policy program & the graduate school administration, & program identity in the University. W. H. Stoddard.

title: An Extention of Max Weber's Theory of Bureaucracy
abstract: The data were derived from both observation & participant observation of volunteer workers in a large voluntary hospital in New York City. The average age of these women was 65 years. An analysis of a structural hybrid is presented--a "rational-charismatic structure" within "bureaucratic structure," ie, a volunteer department within the bureaucratic structure of a hospital. This analysis takes issue with Max Weber's contention that there is an incongruity between charisma & bureaucracy. "Charity" or "doing good" in the bureaucratic setting of a hospital may be an object of charisma. The other basic issue addressed is the question of how nonpaid workers comply with the rules of working in a bureaucracy. Here, the "prestige of demeaning work" is involved, whereby menial tasks performed without financial recompense take on an aura of charity & are viewed as noble work; as the hospital needs the volunteer, the volunteer frequently needs the hospital, so as to feel useful by working, which is very much implicated in the Protestant Ethic. Therefore, the Protestant Ethic not only holds the seeds of Capitalism, but the seeds of voluntarism as well. AA.

title: Family Group Conference: A Bridge between Lifeworld and System
abstract: Family Group Conferencing (FGC) has been used in New Zealand since 1989. This new approach to care and protection for children and adolescents was triggered by an accusation of 'institutional racism' ( Ministerial Advisory Committee, 1988, p. 25) which denied Maori families their own ways of problem solving and decision making, thereby prolonging the process of colonisation as 'institutional decisions were being made for, rather than by, Maori people' (Ministerial Advisory Committee, 1988, p.18). FGC has been adopted in European countries for non-racist issues in response to the unwanted side effects of care and protection work. This article examines the hypothesis: what makes FGC necessary is not the issue of racism, but a more fundamental phenomenon of administration, law, professionalism and modern government. We will argue that FGC is a legal and professional procedure, needed to cure the unhelpful side effects of a legal and professional welfare state system. To explain this, we will follow Jorgen Habermas's Theory of Communicative Action (1987), which explains why system logic overpowers peoples' logic, even when this is not the intention of social work professionals.

title: Multi-level administrative structure and the distribution of social service expenditures: A Nebraska example
abstract: During the decade of the 1980s Nebraska restructured its social service (welfare) delivery system.  Prior to the change, administrative responsibility for many social service programs was shared between the state and county governments.

title: The Katrina Hurricane Spectacle and Crisis of the Bush Presidency
abstract: The August 2005 Hurricane Katrina media spectacle put on display the glaring inequities of race and class that define the United States in the new millennium. The inability of the federal government to respond to the catastrophe called attention not only to the failures and incompetence of the Bush administration but also to the crisis of neoliberalism whereby the market alone cannot provide for the needs of citizens and deal with crises. Katrina also called attention to a "politics of disposability" whereby certain people are deemed disposable and not worthy of care and help. The biopolitics of inequality and disposability was put on full display in the Katrina spectacle and may be one of the most important aftereffects of the tragic episode.

title: The Print Media in South Africa: Paving the Way for 'Privatisation'
abstract: Since the end of apartheid, national and local governments in South Africa have been involved in the commercialisation and marketisation of a wide range of public services. This article examines the responses of the mainstream media to these neo-liberal initiatives, looking specifically at English-language newspapers and their coverage of water, electricity and waste management services. We explore the extent to which the print media can be deemed to be in favour of privatisation as well as the more subtle, discursive ways in which it covers these issues. We argue that these corporate media outlets in South Africa generate and perpetuate a neo-liberal discourse on privatisation, but that this dialogue is neither omnipotent nor monolithic. Nevertheless, it is exactly this facade of objectivity which gives neo-liberalism its hegemony. By appearing to give equal space to different points of view there is a perception of balance in the press that obscures the more subtle, opinionmaking discourses that generate neo-liberal biases. We conclude with a brief discussion of what might be done to counter this neo-liberal authority. Adapted from the source document.

title: Sociology and the Swedish Model
abstract: An examination of the relationship between science & society, with focus on the Swedish case. The crisis in which sociology finds itself originates in the problematic relationship between sociology & the strong public administration characteristic of Sweden. There is a growing doubt that social methods & techniques are capable of changing society & solving social problems. At the same time, there is, even in this welfare state, an emerging cultural awareness of the hierarchy inherent in a strong society & those structures of knowledge that are related to this societal order. It is the inevitable conflict between those who administer & those administered, & between those who do research & those who are researched. It is concluded that the sociological crisis in Sweden is simultaneously a crisis of the Swedish societal order. Modified AA

title: The Rise of Indigenous Hypermarginality: Native Culture as a Neoliberal Politics of Life
abstract: Scholars have suggested that the current era of indigenous citizenship in Latin America is characterized by a postmulticultural political order that effectively reverses the historical marginality of native populations in the region. This conception, however, minimizes the established insight that the social apertures of neoliberal culturalism depend on the creation of new exclusionary regimes based on the very same mechanisms of celebrating cultural difference. Drawing on a decade of field-based inquiries into indigenous experiences of marginality in South America's Gran Chaco, this article identifies how the widespread political empowerment of an indigenous majority is structurally predicated upon the hypermarginality of a stigmatized few. I describe the general features of hypermarginality as lived experience and emergent political regime, in relation to three properties of the stratifying craft of the neoliberal state: the contraction of authorized culture, the culturalization of legitimate indigenous life, and the state management of a global economy of cultural preservation. This essay illustrates how hypermarginality is a concrete political quandary that holds significant implications for social analysis and policy, including the need to rethink the relationships between the neoliberal and the indigenous in Latin America.

title: Refuge fragments, fragmentary refuge
abstract: This experimental essay shows the ways that Somali Bantu refugees' experiences of resettlement, especially their encounters with the bureaucracy of immigration and resettlement, fragment what for the refugees are meaningful wholes (such as families), as well as the sometimes creative, though often frustrated, ways they work to re-create wholeness and meaning in their new context. Revealing cognition and feeling in the moment, these fragments challenge the conception of refuge as relief or resolution, the end of the journey. Instead they expose just how fragmentary refuge is, where the fragments, like the experience of refuge, take the form of a puzzle that shows the precarity and uncertainty of refuge. But the stories told in these fragments also push back at their fragmentation by revealing how refugees puzzle through and attempt to control fragmentation, demonstrating the strength of refugee agency and the beautiful potency of their resistances. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright holder.]

title: Local Administrative Reform
abstract: Basic forms of local administrative organization are discussed with respect to their applicability in today's Russia. Among three forms -- council-mayor-manager, commissioners' council, & mayor council -- the last is claimed to be most adequate for local administration. Results of several polls conducted among representatives of executive & legislative branches (N = 67 respondents) & residents of Bashkortostan (N = 734) show steady preference for the mayor-council form. This is explained as a reaction to a depersonified character of the local authority of the Soviet period & a strong involvement of the legislative branch in executive matters in the post-Soviet period. Prospective details of executive-legislative relationship in Russia are discussed & compared with existing forms of local administration in the West. J. Klimov

title: Perspectives on Welfare Reform Part One: Social Work -- Welfare and Work: Some Suggestions on How the Two Can Mesh, from a Public Policy Administrator
abstract: Social workers & public administrators must find common ground in revising the current welfare system in the US. In the past, the general view was that people were on welfare because they could not navigate postmodern society on their own. Recently, the common viewpoint is that many people are on welfare because it is there. There is some movement to put limits on the length of time that welfare services are available, & there is a strong push toward welfare recipients entering the job market as exemplified by recent changes in PA welfare law.
