It is recommended that the categories & methodology of the theory of administrative-state management elaborated by UN experts serve as a basis for curricula revision in Russia. 14 References. A. Devic

title: Public Administration Schools in Romania: Strategic Choices for the Future
abstract: The article addresses the topic of higher education reform process in Central and Eastern Europe in general and in Romania in special and focuses on the challenges public administration schools in this geographical area are currently facing. The author groups these challenges into five categories including students, market, community, decision-makers and academic management. The author argues that in order to develop and implement a sound reform of public administration programs one needs to take into consideration both global challenges common to all counties/programs but also features embedded in the regional context from Central and Eastern Europe. In the conclusion section the author refers to the potential competitive advantage PA programs have and to possible solutions from increasing their chances for a sound development in the future independent from other fundamental fields such as law, economics, etc. Adapted from the source document.

title: Global actors and public power
abstract: Prominent recent scholarship in global political justice has focused on creating conceptual space for international NGOs -- and sometimes also corporations and states -- as fully-fledged participants in global governance. While acknowledging the achievements of international non-state actors, I argue that core global governance tasks -- of global distribution, regulation or administration -- should not be assigned to them. Drawing from neo-republican theory, I contend that such actors fall short of the formal criteria that are necessary for constituting a global public actor, because they do not have a global function and orientation. The distinction between public and private actors matters, since it conditions our expectations for them: both categories of actors are asked to avoid dominating individuals, but public actors must, in addition, protect individuals from third-party domination. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Administrative justice - a quiet revolution
abstract: Lord Justice Carnwath first notes that the grandly titled "International Conference on Administrative Justice," organized in Nov 1997 by Martin Partington & Michael Harris, certainly lived up to its name, with 33 papers & many representatives from all over the world. He points out that the conference coincided with the 40th anniversary of the publication of the Franks report, Administrative Tribunals and Inquiries, & the 50th anniversary of "Franks" coincides with the enactment of the Tribunals, Courts & Enforcement Act 2007 & the creation of the Administrative Justice & Tribunals Council. This chain of events received no little help from Partington. This "quiet revolution" in tribunal justice, of which Partington was an early prophet, will reach fruition with implementation of the new Tribunals Service on 3 Nov 2008. References. S. Stanton

title: Informatization and Public Administration: A Political Science Perspective
abstract: Outlines three political science perspectives that might be used in analyzing informatization in the context of public administration: the policy networks approach, rational choice, & the new institutionalism. Evidence drawn from the British social security, health care, & social care sectors are related to the political science frameworks to examine their utility. These frameworks not only rightly highlight the incremental nature of change, but also help explain important variations in information & communication technologies use across the three public policy sectors. It is concluded that combining the study of informatization & political science offers a fruitful avenue for future research. 2 Tables, 82 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Governments of the Megalopolises, the Case of Brazil -- Sao Paulo: Metropolitan Administration, Decentralization and Participation as Simultaneous Challenges
authors: Pires, Valdemir; Gaeta, Antonio Carlos; Rojas Buvinich, Danitza
abstract: The government of a megalopolis, such as Sao Paulo, shows singular challenges that do not exist in less complex urban contexts. Being a city of a country with a recent industrialized economy, with an income (functional and geographical) highly concentrated, that has resumed the democracy for only one quarter of a century, this megacity lives with its own political and organizational assignments, due to the contradictory character of the political behavior of its habitants/ voters and of the traditionalist nature of populism and patronage in the relationship between the rulers and the ruled and between the Executive and Legislative powers at the local level. In such context, the difficulties to prosecute the assignments of the metropolitan organization, the decentralization and the institutionalization of citizen participatory channels in the governance and administrative activities are huge. The centrifuge forces (of the decentralization of the local government, through subprefectures), the centripetal forces ( of the metropolitan organization process) and the diffuse forces (of the claiming popular participation) act simultaneously over the deciding processes, in Sao Paulo, receiving, still, state and national political influences, since the city is a very significant historically producer of political and electoral capital. The analysis of the recent experience of the creation of the subprefectures and the representative counsels (fixed in the Municipality Organic Law of 1990) and the attempt to implement the participatory budgeting, in two occasions (1989-1992 and 2001-2004), reveal some of the social and political reasons that make difficult the establishment of a solidly democratic governance and of a more efficient public administration in the metropolitan area of Sao Paulo. Adapted from the source document.

title: Divisive 'Commonality': state and insecurity in the Democratic Republic of Congo
abstract: Northern donor policies relating to building a common future and building peaceful states and societies go to the heart of national and international security agendas. This article critiques the concept of commonality between donors and recipients and within recipient countries. It argues that the policies are problematic from the perspective of security theorising, both in their mooted 'commonality' and in terms of the political intervention that they imply. Historically security has been competitive and founded on compromise rather than commonality, and the internal legitimacy of states has been contested domestically, rather than 'built' from outside. Using the example of the Democratic Republic of Congo, the article argues that the ahistorical assumptions of these policies and the activities they license have entrenched specific forms of insecurity. There have been some returns to the donors and implementing partners but also some costs, which had not been calculated, as lessons have not been drawn from past experiences. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Similarities And Dissimilarities In Stakeholders' Perception Of Intergenerational Inheritance Of Inequalities
abstract: Decentralization of public administration, subsidiarity and delegation of considerable set of tasks (traditionally belonging to public administration) to organizations of the non-governmental sector are tendencies prevailing in most European countries and intensively promoted by the European Union as effective and socially beneficial solutions. Attitudes and actions taken by the stakeholders, active at various levels of local administration, are decisive for implementation and realization of the above mentioned recommendations. The article is based on results of focus group interviews carried out in eight towns selected for the purposes of the PROFIT project. Applying the comparative perspective and referring to the phenomenon of inheritance of social inequalities, the author discusses viewpoints of people responsible for creation and realization of social policy at the local level. Adapted from the source document.

title: Terrorized into Absurdity: The Creation of the Transportation Security Administration
abstract: Critiques the government's response to the terrorist attacks of September 11 (2001), specifically, the ambitious creation of the Transportation Security Administration (TSA). US air security called for some minor reforms rather than a dramatically more costly & less efficient overhaul. It may well be that federalized TSA personnel prove no more competent than the contract employees who performed the same security tasks pre-September 11. In fact, available performance information concerning public employees indicates that Congress may have hindered rather than bolstered airport security by establishing the TSA. The harm done to the commercial airline industry by Congress may surpass that done to the industry by the terrorists. 58 References. K. Coddon

title: The Obama Administration: Setting Up a Government
authors: Shafer, Byron E; La Raja Raymond J
abstract: This issue of The Forum brings a focus on elements shaping the new presidential administration. One cluster of articles concentrates on key influences going into the Obama Administration: Wendy Cho and James Gimpel on the differential influences from an economic meltdown; Charles O. Jones on the place of prior political experiences; Todd Estes on lessons from the beginnings of the Clinton Administration; Casey Dominquez on the mandate and the honeymoon; and Matt Grossman on the interest group environment. A second cluster of articles considers the new administration as it moves forward: Fred Greenstein on key strengths and weaknesses that Barack Obama brings to the job; Sidney Milkis and Jesse Rhodes on the interaction of this president with his own party; Dennis Thompson on the fortunes of his proposed ethics initiatives; Sheldon Goldman on his potential place in the politics of judicial selection; Steve Schier on institutional evolution, regime structure, and available skills, and David Magleby, Bradley Jones, and David Lassen on the shifting environment for campaign finance. In the book reviews, John Kenneth White asks about the current political structure as portrayed in Andrew Gelman, Red State, Blue State, Rich State, Poor State, while Bruce Oppenheimer celebrates one of the great analysts and interpreters of American politics, by way of Richard F. Fenno, Jr., Congressional Travels.

title: Principles over Prejudice: Social Dominance Theory and the Mosques' Controversy in American Cities
abstract: There are two challenges that confront elected leaders in American cities in regards the building of mosques within their precincts. The first involves Constitutional principles that ensure freedom of religion. The second is being responsive to the demands of one's constituents. These two challenges surface many issues in public administration such as representing the public interest, maintaining equality/protecting minorities and upholding the principles of the Constitution. This paper explores the relationship between mosque controversies and hate group organizations in cities in America in recent years. The social dominance theory, as propounded by Jim Sidanius and Felicia Pratto in 1999, supports the rationale behind the analysis. Following discussion and in conclusion recommendations are provided for government officials to secure religious freedom while improving governmental responsiveness, thus ensuring that principles are upheld over prejudice. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Institutional Analysis and Decentralization: Developing an Analytical Framework for Effective Third World Administrative Reform
abstract: Scholarly studies over several decades have generally concluded that the centralized, hierarchical, bureaucratic administrative model for Third World (TW) countries has failed. Research findings have stimulated efforts to change both policies & programs in these countries, including a reorientation to rural & agricultural development of the World Bank & decentralization of TW governments. It is recommended that institutional analysis be used to explore (& improve) the performance of TW administrative systems. In a proposed eight-variable analytical model, key features of given goods or services & their production processes are the level of analysis, & the individuals responsible for producing those goods or services are the unit of analysis. Also examined are variations of institutional arrangements, explaining how they neutralize or reinforce the incentives & disincentives to produce various goods & services. 73 References. S. Millett

title: Administrative Reform as Policy Change and Policy Non-Change
abstract: The literature on administrative reform shows that such efforts are quite popular but rarely have much effect. Postwar Japan is no exception. For decades, attention focused on restraining the number of civil servants across all government agencies, a "balanced" approach that was attractive because it was easy to implement. The administrative reform campaign of the early 1980s had an exceptional impact partly because Rincho was able to play a powerful "policy sponsorship" role. Despite the ironic tone of much writing about that period, many policy areas did see significant reform. Since then, however, there has been a lot of talk but little real action on administrative reform, partly owing to lack of focus -- too many ideas & too much energy. 1 Table, 54 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Between Historical Legacies and the Promise of Western Integration: Democratic Conditionality after Communism
abstract: Post-communist democracy promotion has been most important in "borderline" countries, which had less favorable structural conditions than the East-Central European frontrunners, but where a domestic democratic constituency nevertheless existed and could benefit from Western support. External democracy promotion efforts have ranged from "soft" diplomatic pressure to economic and military sanctions and have acted through a variety of channels: (1) promotion of democratic attitudes among citizens yearning for Western integration, (2) political incentives for elites (in government and in the opposition), (3) domestic power balance shifts in favor of democratic politicians, and (4) promotion of better democratic governance through incentives for public administration reform. The most effective approach to democracy promotion thus far, however, has been the combination of political conditionality with significant political/economic incentives, best exemplified by the European integration process. Furthermore, the success of any strategy hinges on its fit with the geopolitical and domestic environment of the country in question. In particular, external actors must be more sensitive to the national sovereignty implications of such interventions, which can be easily exploited by domestic antidemocratic actors to undermine democracy promotion efforts.  [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Rhetoric of Management Control in Italian Cities: Constructing New Meanings of Public Action
abstract: This article deals with Italian administrative change. The introduction of management control & evaluation systems in Italian local governments is the best example of the managerial rhetoric of administrative change in Italy. Actually, it brings new meanings of public action & suggests new identities taken from the private sphere. The authors point out some critical aspects of this local governments reform in the frame of the neo-liberal ideology. Particularly, the reductive codification of the concept of effectiveness, which the reform laws describe as a verification of organizational output, supports an auto-referential system of control & evaluation. 3 Tables, 1 Figure, 25 References. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Inc., copyright 2005.]

title: A Counter-radicalization Strategy for a New U.S. Administration
abstract: The U.S. government needs a new, two-pronged approach to counter radicalization in many parts of the world, particularly when confronting the "enabling environment." Those inhabiting this environment include potential sympathizers in the Arab and Muslim world who may not themselves use violence but either endorse the arguments and platforms of the terrorists or are intimidated into silence. This wider community needs to be won over so that they oppose terrorism in their neighborhoods, cities, and states and, critically, in the virtual world, where many of the battles are taking place. Appealing to the enabling environment may be the only way in the long term to isolate terrorists and end terrorism. This two-part approach includes (1) a prioritized development strategy (with an emphasis on good governance, anticorruption, and social service provision) and (2) innovative tools and new partners to implement and disseminate it. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Functional Autonomy: The Case of Finland with Some Notes on the Basis of International Human Rights Law and Comparisons with Other Cases
abstract: It is possible to distinguish functional autonomy, consisting of various administrative arrangement, as a specific form of autonomy on the top of territorial, cultural and personal autonomy. Functional autonomy may be understood as an organizational option for the provision of adequate linguistic services to a minority population in respect of a certain public function (such as education) by means of creating special linguistically identified administrative units at different hierarchical levels inside the general line-organization charged with the national or local administration of the public function. Language (and sometimes even religion) can be used as a divisor by which the principle of 'separate but equal' is implemented in ways that defy organizational characterizations commonly found in textbooks of administrative law or public administration. Functional autonomy is a pragmatic approach to the promotion of rights of a minority population and could be more commonly used. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Use of Social Sciences for Public Administration
abstract: One of the greatest problems of an investigation of the role of social sciences in public administration is the lack of coordinated research. Employing workers who are professionally trained in the social sciences has not been profitable; because of a lack of organization, these workers often are not properly placed, & their work cannot be translated into actual social benefit. Employment in government agencies is often seen as underemployment; the results are a lack of efficiency & little immediate public gain. The development of Italian society since World War II has created many problems for public administration. An attempt is made to characterize each type of public agency; it is concluded that the social sciences play an important role in these agencies, but that it is difficult to investigate a field of study that cannot be clearly defined. K. Shabetai.

title: Categories, Categorizations and the Political Economy of Welfare
abstract: Marxist accounts of welfare have been characterized by a critical view of social administration & an uncritical view of the concept of the welfare state. Both these views are questioned. The problems associated with basing analyses of welfare on the welfare state & the limitations of certain criticisms of the social administration tradition are explored. It is concluded that whatever the merits of the more substantive elements in Marxist accounts of welfare, there are problems associated with their assumptions about social administration & the welfare state. 64 References. HA

title: Collective Representations and Social Praxis: Local Politics in the Norwegian Welfare State
abstract: We consider an attempt -- within an economy under pressure to stay competitive in an increasingly integrated global economic system -- to reconcile the contradictory pressures of democratic values vs managerial efficiency, & of the desire for an effective social welfare safety net vs the need for budgetary responsibility, in Norway. We focus on a local welfare committee's experimental attempt to improve morale & productivity through a combination of added resources & greater autonomy. The better but more expensive service produced by the experiment triggered the paradoxical conclusion that what was needed was tighter administrative oversight. The experiment & its evaluation became a kind of self-fulfilling prophecy. We explore the conceptual, ideological, & economic factors that shape the government's reaction, & then offer a theory of word meaning, usage, & power in public discourse that accounts for the discussion & the actions that flow from it. 45 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Urban Regeneration, Governance and the State: Exploring Notions of Distance and Proximity
abstract: Recent debates over how to characterise the governance of urban regeneration are developed in this paper using a detailed case study of Attwood Green in Birmingham, UK. Specifically, the relationship between actors within governance networks and the state is critically reappraised. The case study suggests that actors tend to display highly reflexive understandings of government as multifaceted and multidimensional, simultaneously trying to establish distance and proximity from different aspects of state power. The relationship between those agents regenerating Attwood Green and local and central government is highly strategic, manipulating transfers of financial, political and legal power through new organisational configurations. Adapted from the source document.

title: Energy as a Disorganizing Concept in Policy and Administration
abstract: Energy first became widely used as an organizing concept in public policy in the 1970s. Review of past energy policies reveals confusion & disorganization in policy formation; challenges have been issued to the Federal Energy Administration, the Atomic Energy Commission, the Federal Power Commission, the system of pricing electricity, nuclear power, & petroleum policy. The growth of energy politics has challenged assumptions in all these areas. Such politics is typified by sectional conflicts & by the changing substance of energy issues over time. Three ideologies are advocated: a free market approach, central federal planning, & federal planning for decentralization. Energy policy appears likely to favor centralization, but the management of such policy may prove very difficult. W. H. Stoddard.

title: Rethinking the Relationship Among Monitoring, Evaluation, and Results-Based Management: Observations From Canada
abstract: This chapter outlines the development of performance monitoring and program evaluation at the federal level of the government of Canada. This approach stands out, as it has had a dual emphasis on both monitoring and evaluation as complementary forms of knowledge production. However, throughout its history emphases on management and accountability have shifted. The authors argue that to fulfill its potential to support results-based management the Canadian government must adopt a more stable, balanced, and strategic approach to both performance monitoring and program evaluation. Adapted from the source document.

title: Behavioral Influences of Bureaucratic Organizations and the Schumpeterian Controversy
authors: Raines, J Patrick; Leathers, Charles G
abstract: The behavioral influences of large bureaucratic organizations that were noted by Joseph A. Schumpeter would seem to weigh heavily against the plausibility of the Schumpeterian hypothesis that large corporations are more powerful engines of technological innovations than small competitive firms. But those influences also offer clues about how cultural differences between the US & Japan resulted in large Japanese corporations in the later-post-WWII era conforming closely to the Schumpeterian hypothesis. 23 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Deadly Force as a Policy Problem in Local Law Enforcement: Do Administrative Practices Make a Difference?
authors: Mays, G Larry; Taggart, William A
abstract: An examination of the impact of six administrative practices on the use of deadly force by police officers in US cities with a population of 50,000+, based on survey data published in 1981. Generally, departmental policies demonstrate little association with the f of shooting incidents per police officer, or in the number of incidents resulting in fatalities or injuries, although police departments that issue more traditional sidearms appear to experience fewer incidents than those that issue heavier firearms. The lack of association between administrative practices & the use of deadly force is discovered even when controlling for city population size & state legal codes. Notwithstanding that some of the relationships are in the expected direction, their lack of statistical significance suggests that the use of deadly force has its antecedents in sources other than the administrative policies of local police departments. 3 Tables, 21 References. HA

title: Remembering Benjamin from South of the Pyrenees: The Two-Gauge Problem
abstract: Valverde reflects on the absence of Spanish civil war refugees from the cultured public's collective memory of the place where Walter Benjamin died. Walter Benjamin died on Sept 27, 1940, in the Hotel de Francia, in the Catalan border town of Port Bou. Like many other Europeans, Benjamin had been driven away from several homes in the 1930s: from Berlin to Paris, from Paris to southern France, and from Vichy France into Spain. Having managed to hike along an unofficial route into Spain, only to encounter fresh difficulties with visas and other papers, he took an overdose of morphine. Unlike many other deaths around the same time in other corners of Europe, Benjamin's death was treated as a "normal" case by the relevant municipal bureaucracy: his name was recorded in the local archive of births and deaths, and he was given burial in the outlying and thus less Catholic part of the local cemetery.

title: Minorities in Administration: A Review of Ethnicity's Influence in Management
abstract: Theories about organizations & their management are described & placed along a continuum. A niche for the study of the influence of ethnicity in management is prescribed along this continuum. Literature is reviewed to identify distinct factors that confront minority administrators & that significantly impact management effectiveness & efficiency. Linkages between management behavior & organizational processes, & the ethnicity of administrators are exposed. Specific ethnic barriers relative to entry into management, fit in the informal organization, performance evaluations & promotions, & special role expectations are discussed. Management education that is cross-culturally sensitive is recommended. 17 References. AA.

title: Public Opinion Concerning Central and Autonomous Administrations
abstract: Examines public preferences for changing or maintaining the function of central & autonomous governments in Spain. How & to what degree these preferences are dictated by cognitive variables (eg, perceptions of resource management & government responsiveness) explored through analysis of Catalonia, the Basque Country, Galicia, & Andalusia in terms of preferences for separate or shared functions & for independent or interdependent administrations according to levels of nationalist sentiment in 1990. Variations in preferences are seen to be associated with the level of subjective nationalism, opinions on how central & autonomous government should relate, & preferences regarding the distribution of public services by each. 13 Tables, 14 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: 嘉绒藏人的房名制、内婚制与改土设屯——金川嘉绒社会的国家进程 / Familial Lineage, Endogamy and Transition from Lineage Authority to State Governance
abstract: Anthropologists agree that kinship system is the rudimentary political system prior to the emergence of state authority. Although the power of lineages was broken down by the time of Roman Empire in the West, in Max Weber's view, China remained as a country where lineages were the basic social administrative units in society. Morris Freedman suggested that the reason for familial lineages being the major social institution in southeast China was due to lack of the government power in the area. However, recently some anthropologists and historians suggest that the "lijia" system exited in Ming and Qing is an evidence indicating that familial lineages were absorbed into the state governing system to become part of local administrative structure. Confucian rituals were observed and state commended gods were worshipped, a clear acceptance of mainstream Confucianism. In ethnic southeast China, Qing first allowed the local chiefdom system continue but later implemented land and tax policies that forced changes in local social structure and culture. Chieftains were replaced with court appointed officials,and serfs and chiefs all became "equal" subjects of the emperor. Qianlong period saw the change of abolishment of chieftains, government garrison establishment and land and taxation reform in Rgyalong society in Jinchuan county of Sichuan, however, lineage system, endogamy, and conscripted labor system kept the social stratification alive. Not until the 1950s did the people gain equal status as "citizens" of the state. Nevertheless, the new state acknowledged the authority of Tibetan Buddhism in Rgyalong, which made the region unique in comparison to other south and southwestern parts of China in state authority.

title: Collective Management Strategies and Elite Resistance in Cochabamba, Bolivia
abstract: Travis Driessen examines the democratic experiment in public water management institutionalized in Cochabamba in the year 2000. By identifying specific factors that constrain the process, he reveals the challenges participatory management in public water and sanitation companies face in practice. Adapted from the source document.

title: The first peoples and the Quebec question
abstract: Hunt examines the changing political climate of Quebec Canada and shows how the indigenous peoples of northern Canada have developed and prospered in a way that opposes the large technocratic state.  Instead, they have predicated on a small and human scale of life.

title: Neo-Darwinism and Simon's Bureaucratic Antihero
abstract: Decision making, as a form of Darwinism, has reduced our sense of what it means to be a human being to the practical art of adaptation to a hostile environment. In reality, however, the practicality of decision making to the survival of the species or US culture is marginal. For economist Herbert Simon (eg, 1992) to be able to prescribe administrative behavior, which is essentially problem solving, he must also reduce the heroic nature of human beings to the dreary & uninspiring task of satisficing. Satisficing does not draw on the human capacity for proactive choice & purposeful change. It is argued that Simon bases his theories on an incomplete view of evolution -- especially human evolution. Simon's neo-Darwinism is illustrated & then compared with emerging views on the nature of evolution, the brain, & the human enterprise. It is concluded that whether or not we have bounded rationality is really a matter of the choice we make about human purpose. 60 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucracy and Social Inclusion: A Proposal for Understanding the Management of Public Organizations in Brazil
authors: Helal, Diogo Henrique; Neves, Jorge Alexandre Barbosa
abstract: This article examines the management of public organizations in Brazil, taking into account both the institutional approach & that of the economic sociology. It is a fact that the management of these organizations is affected by the actions of interest groups, especially in Brazil, which is characterized by patrimonial practices, among other things. This context forces those who work in the public sphere to constantly face the dilemma of collective action, summarized in the following question: Under such conditions, is it possible for the public organizations to act in the collective interest? To answer this question, which is related to the structure-agency debate, this work suggests two responses: One that emphasizes the agency, rationality & the formation of preferences; & another, structural, based on bureaucratic insulation & social inclusion. After such considerations, & for the purpose of illustrating the relevance of the two responses, the article discusses the case of the Bolsa Familia program (family grant), highlighting the contribution of Caixa Economica Federal & the Municipalities for the success of the program. In the end, the authors present their conclusions & recommendations for future studies. Adapted from the source document.

title: A British Bureaucratic Revolution? Uncontrolled Autonomy or "Freer Markets, More Rules"
abstract: This article originated with a puzzle: how best to account for changes in the behavior of groups, organizations & individuals in Great Britain? A detailed analysis of what Weber & Polanyi identified as interdependencies between state & market, & of the state's role in creating the market, led to the decision to adapt the notion of bureaucratic revolution put forward by Weber. We argue that the British bureaucratic revolution is reflected in the fact that the state plays an essential role in social change by creating rules & institutions that lastingly orient actors' behavior. The examples of health & local authorities are then used to identify mechanisms that were influential throughout a ten-year period; specifically the introduction of competition features (rewards & punishments) & of auditing & inspection. If our interpretation is accurate, the effects of this bureaucratic revolution may well come to be felt in contexts other than Great Britain. Tables, References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Research on Assessment Indexes of Clean Local Government Construction in China
authors: Tang, Yanwen; Jin, Yijia; Chunrong, Liu
abstract: With their deeper involvement in the development of economy and society, local governments have to explore new methods to fight against corruption. An important aspect in this endeavor is to establish assessment indexes apt to each local situation in terms of constructing a clean government based on the Central Government's document "The Implementation Plan for Establishing and Upgrading the System of Sanction and Prevention of Corruption that Equally Emphasizes Education, Rules, and Supervision." This paper analyzes and compares the domestic and international indexes of anti-corruption and pro-clean administration, describes a new theoretical framework, and then proposes an assessment index that can appropriately evaluate the actual administration of the local governments in China. This paper contends that the "involvements-outcomes" assessment method is the principle one to measure a local government's efforts and effectiveness to combat corruption. According to the current reality in China, the major method should be introspective when measuring the perception and judgment of the distribution of the value-added authority in the process of rule implementation that exists in the government's actions. This index system pays attention to the measurability of the indexes and the attainability of the data. Having such an index system may improve the effectiveness and accuracy of developing clean governments, and this index is an indispensable component of the alert mechanism in the anti-corruption combat. Adapted from the source document.

title: Middle Managers in Social Work: Professional Identity and Management in a Marketised Welfare State
authors: Shanks, Emelie; Lundström, Tommy; Wiklund, Stefan
abstract: With respect to marketisation and managerialism, the changes in the Swedish social services resemble the changes in many other countries. This article analyses how Swedish middle managers within the personal social services reason about professional identity, everyday work and leadership in the context of these changes. The study draws on four focus group interviews with a total of twenty-two managers. The results suggest a persisting social work identity among the managers, although noticeable changes have taken place within the social services. For example, the managers' budgetary and administrative responsibilities have increased, and relations to private companies in the area of residential care place new demands on their managerial skills. The managers seem to find some of the new conditions easier to integrate with their social work identity than others. The resistance to the reforms appear to be less obvious in Sweden than in, for example, the UK. There are a number of possible explanations for this. For example, it may be connected to the relatively mild implementation of marketisation and managerial strategies, a less apparent downsizing of social work and a relative lack of central state bureaucratic control.

title: Public Policies before Emergent Realities: Notes for the Discussion
abstract: This article is intended to reflect on the future of public policy in response to the challenges imposed at the global & national levels. It shows how the crisis of the welfare State represents a crisis of both its tools & the underlying concepts that prevailed in the public policy field during the second half of the 20th Century. Linked to these new conditions, the dissemination of the new public management as a set of ideas with which to address the problems of managing public institutions is examined & it is shown how the crisis demands responses that go beyond changes in the public structures. That makes it necessary to study the emerging conditions like the redefinition of the State's role or the globalization of public policy, which require the development of new approaches in the discipline. Finally, judgments are put forward to act as guides for the adoption, expansion, or radical change in public policy as a discipline that studies the available courses of action in contemporary public affairs. 81 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: First Encounters of the Bureaucratic Kind: Early Freshman Experiences with a Campus Bureaucracy
authors: Godwin, Glen J; Markham, William T
abstract: Following a review of the literature on problems with bureaucracy experienced by newcomers to organizations, nonparticipant field observations & semistructured interviews with 20 freshman students & the staff members who dealt with them at the U of North Carolina, Greensboro, are drawn on to describe new students' interpretations of & adaptations to the bureaucracy. Problems identified by all were waiting in lines, impersonality, rules, "the runaround," & paperwork. Despite its problems, bureaucracy is perceived by students & staff as a positive & efficient way of doing things, & cooperation as necessary to achieve desired results. Specific strategies for dealing with frustration are identified. 50 References. R. Green

title: Sunil Amrith, Crossing the Bay of Bengal: The Furies of Nature and Fortunes of Migrants and Mathew Hull, Government of Paper: The Materiality of Bureaucracy in Urban Pakistan
abstract: Sunil Amrith, Crossing the Bay of Bengal: The Furies of Nature and Fortunes of Migrants (2013) and Mathew Hull, Government of Paper: The Materiality of Bureaucracy in Urban Pakistan (2012).

title: "The Law Has No Feeling for Poor Folks Like Us!": Everyday Responses to Legal Compulsion in England's Working-Class Communities, 1871-1904
abstract: Here, Auberbach examines the contentious period in Victorian England when categories that state agents insisted were objectively measurable and verifiable through official documentation were instead bargained over, contested, and discursively defined through daily negotiations. In the quarter-century following the introduction of compulsory elementary education for British children in 1870, children's health, whether their working activity was "labor" according to the legal definition, the economic status of their household, and even their age were all matters to be resolved in everyday dialogues between parents and state agents. Parents efforts to mitigate or abrogate the impact of social reform were aided by strong fractures between policy and practice in the Victorian state. In addition to demonstrating the power of daily negotiations to define, refine, and alter the basic categories of children's status in Victorian England, he explores what the everyday encounters between parents and state agents reveal about the historical relationship between government authority and the working class. A closer examination of the daily negotiations over compulsion emphasizes the importance of working-class agency in setting the parameters of this relationship. It also clarifies the practical impact of the growing government bureaucracy on working-class neighborhoods and households.

title: Joseph Stiglitz: The Citizen-Bureaucrat and the Limits of Legitimate Dissent
abstract: Since being forced to resign his high-ranking post at the World Bank in 2000 for publicly dissenting from neoliberal ideas, Joseph Stiglitz has become a global policy celebrity, celebrated as the "Rebel Within." While much has been said about his neo-Keynesian policy framework, little has been done to explore the political significance of his iconic status as a renowned "citizen-bureaucrat." Yet, Stiglitz's iconic image in many ways has had a greater political impact than his policy ideas. In a world in which government and corporate bureaucracies increasingly squeeze out alternative visions, the citizen-bureaucrat suggests that space still exists within these unwieldy bureaucracies for the independent-thinker to put forward a rebellious agenda. Through an assessment of Stiglitz's policy career, this article argues that the image of the citizen-bureaucrat is, to a large extent, an ideological fantasy that masks a more uncomfortable political reality: that the available options for the "good bureaucrat" in today's neoliberal era, far from expanding, are more narrow than ever before. Adapted from the source document.

title: Why reforms fail
abstract: Police reform is risky and hard, and efforts to innovate in policing often fall short of expectations. This chapter examines sources of resistance to change in policing. Some are internal, including opposition to reform at virtually all levels of the organization and among special units. The position of unions vis-a-vis change is highly variable, particularly if proposals do not threaten working conditions and officer safety. Politicians and other potential opponents of change lurk in the vicinity of policing, and reformers need to bring them into the process as well. The public must understand how the investment they have in policing will be enhanced, and not threatened, by reform. If new strategies require the cooperation of other service agencies (as, for example, for problem-solving policing) the heads of those bureaucracies must understand they are partners in their city's program, not victims of empire building by the police. At the top, city leaders must match the commitment of chiefs and other police executives to change, if reforms are to survive leadership transition. Adapted from the source document.

title: Village, Technology, and Bureaucracy: Patterns of Irrigation Organization in Comilla District, Bangladesh
authors: Coward, E Walter, Jr; Ahmed, Badaruddin
abstract: A village-based pump irrigation system was studied to investigate patterns of articulation between an irrigation bureaucracy & a local group of water users. Data were based on field observations, a census of all heads of household, a random sample of farm units, & available secondary information. Bureaucratic tolerance was found for community variation & initiatives for organizational innovation; this led to three significant local adaptations: (1) creation of the local role of water distributor, (2) formulation of differential water use categories, & (3) the use of private mechanics for system repair. Findings suggest that effective articulation of irrigation development programs can occur when village groups are given a large amount of management responsibility, if a variety of village-developed or -originated arrangements for this management are permitted. 2 Tables. AA.

title: Government news management, bias and distortion in American press coverage of the Brazilian Coup of 1964
abstract: Using content analysis, Weis analyzes US newspaper and magazine coverage of the Brazilian Coup of 1964.  The dominant press view, that the coup occurred to thwart an imminent Communist takeover, is at odds with historical scholarship, as well as with contemporary accounts in the alternative and foreign press.

title: Family Centers in Rural Communities: Lessons for Policy, Planning, and Practice
abstract: Family centers have emerged as a focal point of considerable interest for those looking for alternatives to highly bureaucratic and residual approaches to child welfare programs and services. These centers are seen to incorporate the best elements of ecological and strengths-based family practice, bringing together professional and community members in a supportive, inclusive, and nonstigmatizing environment. However, much of the research on family centers is grounded in urban neighborhoods or has failed to distinguish between urban and rural contexts. This paper presents results from an exploratory study that highlighted issues relevant to the establishment and operation of family centers in rural communities. Implications for policy makers and planners, as well as rural family and child welfare practitioners, are discussed. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Regulation of Group Processes in Decision Making
abstract: A report on a simulation experiment, involving 30 small task-oriented work teams, comprising 5 senior officials from public administration in the Federal Republic of Germany, which investigated the effects of different task instructions & different organizational roles of participants in group decision-making processes. Four different instruction sets were applied. Each group process (eg, new beginning, sequential interdependence) was examined by time-series analysis for long- & short-term dynamic regulation patterns, & instruction effects were subjected to variance analysis. Findings reveal that different regulation patterns did depend on process variables & task instruction, & that participant roles adjusted to instructions. Regulation patterns, however, did not correlate significantly with subjective evaluations by participants. 3 Tables, 3 Graphs, 14 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Ascendance of Bureaucrat Capitalists in Malaysia
abstract: Malaysia's development of bureaucratic capitalism is traced within a review of political developments since independence from GB in 1957. Before 1969, Malaysia was ruled by an alliance of the United Malaya National Organization (UMNO), the Malayan Chinese Assoc, & the Malayan Indian Congress, with the UMNO maintaining a dominant position. After the 1969 elections, the Chinese no longer played an effective role in government; the strengthened UMNO more actively pursued capitalist policies, with the support of Malay politicians educated to serve in the British colonial administration. A "New Economic Policy" has favored Malays in comparison with other groups in its educational & employment programs, with Uc Malays benefiting the most. However, the disproportion between government work opportunities & the increasing numbers of U graduates, & the dissatisfaction of wage laborers, constitute threats to the bureaucratic capitalist government. 2 Tables. D. Dunseath.

title: Environment, Technology, and the Administrative Intensity of Manufacturing Organizations
abstract: A survey of 41 mfg establishments in a southern Calif city (pop circa 150,000) produced no support for the position that variations in admin'ive intensity can be attributed to scale factors. However, technological & environmental variables did r with admin'ive intensity. In addition, interaction effects were observed which were consistent with 5 hyp's stressing constraints on structural change imposed from outside the org & the vulnerability to environmental disruption produced by complex technologies. If org's react to environmental disturbances in diff ways depending on production technology variables, & if their reaction to most independent variables depends on the degree to which they are constrained by outside agencies, a more careful examination of these & other sources of interaction is of paramount importance. 2 Tables. Modified HA.

title: The Building Representative and the Educational Administrator: Conflicting or Cooperative Role Processes?
abstract: Research was undertaken to determine whether the interactive role functions of building-level educational administrators & local teacher union leaders are based upon conflict or upon mutual accommodation. Data were collected from teaching personnel in a large Ur school district located in the northeastern US. A ten-item questionnaire was administered to the target population. Nine items were concerned with specific demographic & professional information. The tenth, termed "proximity to position of building representative," indicated a R's level of identification with a local union leadership role. As a result of variance on that item, Ss were assigned under one of the following four population subheadings: (1) current building representatives, (2) past representatives, (3) those who aspire to the position, & (4) those with no identification whatsoever with the position. Of the 1,521 Ss asked to complete the questionnaire, 901 did so (59.24%). A level of dependence was established between the proximity variable & each of the demographic & professional items. That level was found to be significant in five cases: proximity with: (A) sex, (B) level of academic achievement, (C) earned credits in educational administration, (D) intention to apply for an administrative position, & (E) possession of certification in administration or supervision. The structure of those relationships indicated that individuals who identify rather strongly with a local union leadership role tend to aspire to administrative positions, as well as considerably invest in the compilation of administrative credentials. Based upon these factors, significant numbers of individuals with backgrounds reflecting high levels of local union leadership activity do appear to move into positions as educational administrators. Dysfunctions related to organizational inbreeding may develop as this process is perpetuated. 7 Tables. AA.

title: Involvement, Motivation, and Reorganization in a Social Services Department
abstract: Data obtained over a 2-year period via staff interviews & documentary materials are drawn on to analyze the reorganization of a local government social services department in the UK, focusing on issues of involvement, participation, & motivation. It is argued that the intention to allow greater participation foundered on the paradox that these changes lacked the explicit direction that became necessary in the context of sudden changes in the wider political & organizational environment. This case study shows a need for explicit leadership & direction if participation is to be fostered in hierarchical work organizations as a means of creating motivated staff & external contributors to the services provided. 2 Appendixes, 54 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: HUMAN RELATIONS IN CONTEXT
abstract: An attempt to deal with the combination of working conditions, logical org, & HR promoting harmonious productivity in industry. The question posed is: How shall the many detailed elements of HR be combined within the framework of the bureaucratic admin, particularly at the lower levels of the industrial org? Good physical conditions & welfare programs, clear & logical formal org, & careful selection & training of persons for positions in the formal structure are helpful procedures. These patterns are consistent with the job planning, work group formation, communication giving orientation, securing suggestions from workers, group participation in discussions & decisions, utilization of employee oriented foremen, &, provisions for residual self-determination for employee groups. But for such a combination of elements to function well, the hierarchy above the foreman should be built on similar lines, & the foreman's position should be protected from loss of prestige & authority. A relatively flat structural design may aid in this endeavor. E. H. Pfuhl, Jr.

title: Cosmopolitan and Local Orientation in the Judicial Profession
abstract: Based on its membership & authority structure, the court is viewed as a specific type of professional organization, ie, a professional bureaucracy. A structural connection between patterns of bureaucracy & profession is postulated, leading to the hypothesis that judges possess & experience a mixture of orientations classifiable as cosmopolitan or professional & local. An index of organizational identification was tested on a sample of Yugoslav judges (N = 866, or 70% of the total in the country). About 25% of the Rs showed a highly articulated professional organizational loyalty, while 75% exhibited the more intense "localistic" orientation. The professional-local orientation develops from the institutional configuration of the judicial role, the process of professional & organizational socialization, & the adaptability of bureaucracy to professional requirements & vice versa. The conflict of structure & orientation is not inherent in this profession & its organization, although sources of latent conflict may be seen in the relationship between bureaucratism & professionalism. 3 Tables, 25 References. Modified HA.

title: Social work as a bureaucratic professional labour: an empirical analysis in non-profit organizations in northern Portugal
authors: Caria, Telmo H; Pereira, Fernando A
abstract: In the last decade and a half, a new perspective on sociological analysis of professional groups has gradually emerged: professionalism and professionalization are no longer analysed as opposed to bureaucracies. In a previous article, we developed an analytical model in which we theorized a hybrid concept of Bureaucratic Professional Work (BPW), based on a theoretical hypothesis of association between various organizational forms (divisional bureaucracies, professional bureaucracies, neo-bureaucracies and post-bureaucracies) and different types of professional work in social work. Structured interviews were conducted with 63 social work professionals who work in 35 non-profit organizations of social services in northern Portugal. We questioned how these professionals perceive their own work in relation to the level of control and centralization of decisions, the routine of procedures and the predictability of results. We also study how social constraints, the tasks performed and work in multidisciplinary teams vary according to the type of BPW. This allows us to detail the modalities of the BPW and set out exploratory hypotheses for other more extensive quantitative studies as well as complementary studies of a qualitative nature.

title: Land and Work: Negev Bedouin Struggle with Israeli Bureaucracies
abstract: Since its creation the state of Israel has intended to totally monopolize the territory. As part of this project, it has expropriated the majority of the territory that used to belong to the Bedouin of the Negev. With the objective of concretizing this policy, the state has offered to each Bedouin a subsidized piece of land for the construction of a house in one of seven "new Bedouin towns." Some Bedouin have challenged the government policies & demanded land outside the towns, in large part because of the rampant unemployment among the town dwellers. 1 Appendix, 26 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Translated title not available.
abstract: Based on group interviews with five Norwegian MST-teams this article focuses the tension between demand for MST-therapists' more or less constant availability, & their need for autonomy at work. The MST-teams use working time arrangements with extraordinarily high availability on the part of the therapists organized through different shifts or through being available all day & night & all week. Team-leaders as well as therapists justified this working time arrangement with therapeutic results. The therapists did not regard this as stressful, as they experienced large degrees of autonomy & flexibility in organizing the work. They were, however, sceptical about the increased bureaucratization of routines. References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Administering Identities: State Decentralisation and Local Identification in Morocco
abstract: In Morocco, the contemporary emphasis on regionalization & increased tolerance for ethnolinguistic diversity belie state attempts to dissipate pre-Independence "tribal" allegiances among citizens for whom they hold sway. Ever-refined rural administrative boundaries & the new place names that accompany them suggest new models for group organization -- challenging indigenous understandings about the links between different locations, & about links between people & places. This article argues that Tashelhit speakers of the Souss region engage in information management by selectively revealing & concealing personal information, thus challenging state attempts to eliminate family & "tribe" from place & personal names. Civil registries, school records, & national identity cards document the discrepancies between indigenous & state naming practices, raising difficulties for citizens who must increasingly rely on documents over oral testimony to pursue legal & administrative ends. Adapted from the source document.

title: Rising Powers and Regional Orders: China's Strategy and Cross-Strait Relations
abstract: The neo-Gramscian approach has become popular within academic debates to theorize processes of global neoliberal convergence. But, it has also been challenged in the context of the ever more pronounced regionalizing tendencies of the current multipolar global order. This is especially so with the rise of China which introduces an alternative logic to regional social order formation processes from a typical neoliberal capitalist social order convergence. This paper argues, however, that a Gramscian approach can precisely account for such regional social order formation processes through the concept of regional historical blocs. This is demonstrated through a case study of the social order shaping effects that a Cross-Strait historical bloc forged between China's 'contender state'-wielding elite bureaucracy and Taiwan's ascendant social forces has had on fostering Taiwan's internationalization toward China. This illustrates that, in addition to a broader global social order convergence process, a neo-Gramscian approach is equally useful to explain similarly defined regional social order convergence.

title: Humor as a Mirror of Military Life
abstract: Humorous depictions of the hierarchical structure of the army, such as those about the Russian Army in Yaroslav Khashek's cartoon series "Adventures of the Brave Soldier Shveik," involuntarily inspired the International Sociological Conference on Armed Forces & Society. Popular images of the army necessarily ridicule its discipline & mechanical-electronic strength: without a humorous attitude, its whole structure could collapse. Popular anecdotes about the military can be used as arguments about the dynamics of subordination & solidarity in the army: (1) state loyalty can be disturbed by social & political turmoil; (2) the notion of military honor is contradicted by corruption among high-ranking officers; (3) ethnic jokes reflect & exacerbate feelings of aggressive solidarity; & (4) rationalization of army functions can bring unchecked growth of military bureaucracy. 4 Illustrations, 19 References. A. Devic

title: POLITIQUES DE L'ORGANISATION/THE POLITICS OF ORGANIZATION
abstract: This article explores how the rulers have repeatedly modified the boundaries of public bureaucracies and the division of labour within the state since the early 1980s, either by creating agencies or by promoting mergers. This transformation of the organisational forms of the state is here considered as an original and rationalised technique of governmentality through which politicians, but also top bureaucrats and experts, try to intervene on the specialization of tasks, the distribution of power and public policies. The article first offers a large state of the art about scholars on agencification and mergers, and a critique of the main theories analysing these processes. It defends a political sociology approach that emphasizes four intertwined dimensions of the politics of organization and its manipulation of state architectures.

title: The Unknown Titmuss
abstract: Recent writing in social policy on the role of agency has made important assumptions about social administration in the post-war period. In particular it is suggested that interpretations of the causes of poverty, & the thinking of Richard Titmuss, were characterised by a 'denial' of agency & almost total emphasis on structural factors. The implications were that this left the Titmuss paradigm vulnerable to more individualistic interpretations in the 1980s. In this article we look more closely at Titmuss's work & thought in the three decades of the 1940s, the 1950s, & the 1960s, aiming to produce a fuller & more nuanced analysis. We argue that the distinctive position adopted by Titmuss was in large part his response to earlier & on-going debates about social pathology. What he was trying to do was to make others aware of the broader context in which behaviour had to be analysed. But Titmuss himself became constrained by the paradigm that he did more than anyone else to create. Thus debates about behaviour, structure, & poverty have been marked as much by continuity as by change. References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Balancing Rural Poverty Reduction and Citizen Participation: The Contradictions of Uganda's Decentralization Program
abstract: Uganda's ambitious decentralization program is analyzed in terms of a "Dual-Mode" system of local governance. Under a "technocratic mode," conditional funding from the center is earmarked for particular programs but with little local participation. In contrast, the "patronage mode" is an elaborate system for local "bottom-up" planning, but with limited resources, which are largely consumed in administrative costs & political emoluments. Along with the spoils of a committee system controlling contracts & appointments, these resources provide the means for building political alliances & loyalty. In the absence of a culture of transparency & civic engagement to assure downward accountability, it remains to be seen whether decentralization can promote both efficient service delivery & local empowerment simultaneously. 3 Tables, 1 Figure, 30 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: From 'Great' Leaders to Building Networks: The Emergency of a New Urban Leadership in Southern Europe?
authors: Genieys, William; Ballart, Xavier; Pierre Valarie
abstract: This article reviews the changes that have taken place in local government leadership in France and Spain. It has been argued that political leadership in local government in Southern Europe is characterized by major political leaders who are able to obtain resources from central government through their political connections. However, both French and Spanish local governments have evolved while developing new forms of leadership that are more connected to territory, its people and local issues than to the respective administrative capitals. The article argues that the development of new policies at the local level, the opening of new avenues of citizen participation and the introduction of new methods of public management have changed the relationship between elected representatives and the people. Institutional innovations at the supra-municipal level have also created a space between regions and municipalities for local leaders to develop their capacity as project leaders and network creators. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: A SOCIOLOGICAL RESEARCH PROJECT ON THE CENTRAL BUREAUCRACY OF THE STATE
abstract: A report on a res project conducted by the Italian Instit for the Study of Public administration to determine the att's of executive functionaries in the nat'l ministries toward innovations. The scope of the res is outlined. 2 groups of variables were used: S-cul & socio-professional ones. Results in both groups of variables are presented in %'s & graphs. Factors considered in particular include: att's toward the admin'ive structure; estimation of the incentive mechanism; evaluation of COMM; att's toward the pol'al-soc competitiveness. Facts obtained bore out the hyp that the initiated process of debur'ization in the ministries has not yet led to any major rationalization of public admin in terms of specialization of duties & simplification of procedures. This is not only attributed to the insufficiency & chaotic state of the legislation, but also to a lack of application of legislative norms, eg those which pertain to training & instruction in responsibilities. But a favorable climate toward rationalization was found & functional innovations were viewed by officials positively & impartially. The implications of these findings are discussed. They are asserted to be representative of most ministries, perhaps with the exclusion of the civil administration & the financial admin, which are older instit's & closer to the public. Further, comparative res is considered necessary. M. Maxfield.

title: 'What part of illegal don't you understand?': bureaucracy and civil society in the shaping of illegality
abstract: While unauthorized immigration has existed in the USA since the inception of immigration laws in the early twentieth century, 'illegality' did not become a central concern in mainstream debate until the late 1970s. Existing scholarship has developed two lines of argument to explain the salience of illegality: a state-centred approach that sees bureaucrats pushing forth the category, and a 'bottom-up' approach that emphasizes the grass-roots activism of restrictionist organizations effectively disguising their nativism by appealing to law and order. The data collected here builds on but complicates the state-centred explanation, and points away from the 'bottom-up' approach. I locate a critical juncture in the immigration debate during the early 1970s and argue that the shift towards the focus on illegality as a point of concern was due to an alignment of interests that brought an array of civil society organizations commonly understood as progressive to coincide with sectors of the bureaucracy. Adapted from the source document.

title: Consumer Participation in Administrative Decision Making
abstract: The term "consumer participation" in public agencies has come to occupy an important place in discussions of administrative theory & practice without any real consensus on what such participation implies. This phenomenon is considered in the field of housing, examining the impact of tenant participation across 750 public housing projects. Analysis of data derived from a survey of housing projects conducted by the US Dept of Housing & Ur Development in 1978 supports the view that tenant organizations can be effective in increasing the level of resources & services made available to tenants, but provides no evidence that this form of consumer participation enhances the administrative process. Modified AA.

title: Prevention Is Better than Litigation: The Importance of Good Administration
abstract: Discusses the various ways in which ombudsmen can & do use their critical analysis of public sector performance to offer guidance on good administration. The particular focus is on the efforts of one group of ombudsmen, the Local Government Ombudsmen (LGO), since they are probably the most proactive in the area of fostering good administrative practice. Many academics have held this view for years, & the impression has been further validated by recent developments. Suggestions for improving the LGO's already strong model for enhancement of public administration are also considered, as well as the limitations on ombudsmen's capacity to perform such a function. 20 References. K. Coddon

title: The Development of Total Quality Management in the Personal Social Service: Realities, Limitations and Opportunities within the Modernising Agenda?
abstract: This paper considers the impact of quality approaches within the personal social services over the last decade. In particular, it examines how applicable private sector approaches to quality, such as Total Quality Management, are in the public & personal social services. Both the hard & soft tools of Total Quality Management are critically considered in terms of their relevance & ability to modernize service provision. In the context of the managerial discourse presently dominating the public sector, it is argued that the hard tools of Total Quality Management, such as performance measurement & review, will only add to managerial control; while the soft tools of empowerment & cultural change will lose their critical effect. It is contended that unless the current Labor government's Modernizing Services Policy succeeds in democratizing the process of developing quality then it will only add to the managerial agenda at the expense of improving service provision. 69 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Michel Crozier's Long March: The Making of The Bureaucratic Phenomenon
abstract: Hailed as a landmark in the development of both the sociology of organizations & the study of 1960s French society, Michel Crozier's The Bureaucratic Phenomenon (see SA 13:2/65B5079) is reexamined. To understand its genesis requires an exercise in the history of contemporary thought, locating Crozier's magnum opus within the context of the influence of A. Gouldner, J. March, & H. Simon. His initial intellectual interest was with the role of trade unions in the US & France during the Cold war, which led to his main cultural finding: the fear of face-to-face communication, requiring impersonal mediation to avoid confrontation with those in authority. He argued that France required a new style of authority, & her intellectuals should provide it as a way of dealing with the problem of overcoming cultural lag & changing France into a modern industrial society. Adapted from the source document.

title: Evaluating the Early Excellence Initiative: The Relationship between Evaluation, Performance Management and Practitioner Participation
authors: Owen, Jenny; Cook, Tina; Jones, Elizabeth
abstract: This article focuses on an evaluation of the pilot implementation of the UK 'Early Excellence' programme, designed to improve Early Years services & achieve national impact. As with other 'New Labour' programmes, the evaluation approach was based on addressing the relationship between 'context, process & outcome'; to facilitate this, nationally defined indicators were adopted through collaboration between a national evaluation team, local evaluators & local practitioners. This approach left considerable scope for interpretation & participation by local evaluators & practitioners, as they engaged in data collection & analysis. However, two major shifts later undermined the original scope: first, a shift from evaluation to performance management, & second, a shift from central practitioner participation to marginal practitioner involvement. In conclusion, we note the parallels & contrasts between this experience & others in UK public services, & propose some general learning points for similar evaluation initiatives. Tables, References. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright 2005.]

title: Participation and Public Policy
abstract: A description of a successful participatory social program concerning the construction of a community center which included a high school, in the Wc community of Angle Park, in Australia. A notice about the center was distributed to the 14,000 residents of the community, which included a "tear-off postage-paid card" on which the residents made comments. About 400 residents returned the card, & were subsequently contacted to join discussion groups. Of the 134 residents who joined the discussion groups, 30 went on to support a community meeting, carnival, & newsletter. The problems of participatory social programs are:(1) the unrepresented segments of the residents who do not participate, (2) the divisions between residents & officials in program goals, (3) the sublimation of residents' needs to officials needs, & (4) the assurance that the participation results in positive & not negative outcomes. The success of the Angle Park participatory program is due to "the maintenance of control by government officials, using the local residents primarily to gain acceptance for the program, & allowing planners considerable autonomy." Modified HA.

title: An Experience in "Advocacy Planning" in Mexico
abstract: As a result of the patent failure of the Ur renewal efforts in the US, a new method of assisting the residents of disadvantaged communities, advocacy planning, came into being. It consisted of efforts on the part of technocrats with connections in the bureaucracy to gain the confidence of the residents, & then mobilize them for self-help projects & political pressure. However, in most cases, instead of mobilizing the disadvantaged, advocacy planning was transformed by the power holders into a public relations effort executed by the bureaucracy itself. A similar effort of support for marginal populations had been tried in Mexico, but it also has failed. An overview of Mexican Ur sociology is given with focus on Mexico City. The capital consists of 3 basic subsystems in the popular districts: (1) the neighborhoods; (2) the popular colonies; & (3) the lost cities. The phenomenon of caciquismo or attempt by Uc demagogues to lead the public in popular districts is described. An example of the failure of advocacy planning in Mexico is given in the history of the unsuccessful attempt to clear a park in the popular colony of Olivar de Conde. The experience shows that the bureaucracy is fully impotent to improve living conditions in the popular quarters. S. Karganovic.

title: Women in Bureaucracy
abstract: If the amount of material available is any criteria, then the area of women and bureaucracy is a rich one for research. We found a sizable amount of material on women and politics, though even in this area much of the holdings of various libraries have not been cataloged. According to the librarian in the Library of Congress who is responsible for collecting material on women in general, the best holding is that of Northwestern University. A check on this source revealed that as in other libraries much of the material is in file folders and uncataloged.In terms of the available material specifically focused on career bureaucracy, the following is the overall situation:Books -- There are relatively few books. We were only able to get hold of two to annotate. The rest are book-length bibliographies. The area least covered seems to be women in state and local bureaucracies. One book is from 1915 and discusses women's role in municipalities, which at that time was mostly of a volunteer nature. The other book is an overview of women's employment in local government.For a complete reprint of this article contact Haworth Press by telephone (1-800-HAWORTH) or EMail (getinfo@haworthpressinc.com) Article copyright The Haworth Press, Inc.

title: Legal and Non-Legal Aspects of the Reform Process of the Hungarian Higher Education System
abstract: The essay surveys Hungarian higher educational reform in a historical perspective. Higher education is a special branch of public administration, where investment to human capital is of corollary importance even if the educational, research and fiscal autonomy of the given institutions is fully respected. The author investigates the legal aspects of how government oversight and supervision (as envisaged in the communist model) has been dismantled over the past 25 years in Hungary. There is no doubt: with the development of institutional autonomy, state subsidies decline and higher educational institutions need to make an increasing effort to simultaneously maintain financial stability, meet market demands and reverse the current trend of deterioration regarding the quality of education. It is for this reason that the negotiations between higher educational institutions and the state must remain within the legal framework so that government supervision will not transform into total neglection. governance. Adapted from the source document.

title: Rationality, Bureaucratic Politics and Belief System: Explaining the Chinese Policy Debate, 1964-66
abstract: An understanding of the belief systems of foreign policy elites is necessary for any meaningful application of both the rational actor & the bureaucratic politics approaches of analysis. This argument is pursued through a case study of the policy debate between Chinese leaders during 1964-1966. The analysis identifies the cognitive-analytic bases for the policy disagreements between Peking officials, thus indicating which issues seem particularly likely to generate bureaucratic politics disputes. At the same time, this effort delineates the key logics & rationales in the Peking government's policy calculation. Such clarification is necessary if rational actor models are to yield accurate & powerful predictions of government policy responses. HA.

title: THE IMPACT OF CENTRAL GOVERNMENT SERVICES ON THE SMALL COMMUNITY
abstract: How does big gov really affect the citizen of a small community? Central control has come to be on a very large scale, & rather impersonal for any small community. The latter, on the other hand, is very personal & has a purely local concern. It often cannot understand central actions. The community realizes that some services are the better for central admin, but also feels a powerlessness. One reason for this feeling is a lack of consultation of the small community in gov decisions. Is the centre fully aware of local conditions, of the fact that conditions vary enormously? Central field workers can be of great help here. They can prevent central policy from concentrating exclusively in benefits for provinces & the nation, to the detriment of the locality, & for this it is important that they should be co-ordinated at the local level. Often the public relations of the central depts are bad & justly give rise to local exasperation. IPSA.
