The mental and physical health impacts on the men and their families, of an inhumanity that beggars belief, masked under the bureaucracy of 'control orders', 'SIAC deportation bail', and torturous legal processes, is here unveiled. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Personnel Official: Now and Tomorrow
abstract: The conference of Mar 26-27, 1968, org'ed by the Dutch Society of personnel manag, was completely dedicated to the task & the training of personnel officials. E. C. Mailand, treating the 'tasks of the personnel official in a new time; described the new dimensions of the old functions (viz, advising, technical org, soc, & providing functions) of the personnel official. These new dimensions are caused by 3 factors: a general societal factor, emancipation & individualization, & the development of technology. The developments of the functions of the personnel official will demand integrated thinking on the manag of the org & real expertness on the problems of org, labor, & SR. The training of personnel officials should be on a U level. M. G. Ydo thought the source of much frustration among personnel officials in the idea that they are too little engaged in the policy of the org. To change this isolation it will be necessary that the personnel official leaves his 'ivory tower' & enter into the problems of all workers in the org. A practical training at the end of his study in the org, not in the Dept of personnel manag, & more knowledge of the possibilities of COMM, & methods to change the org will be useful. H. van de Belt.

title: THE ITALIAN BUREAUCRACY. ORIGIN AND PLACEMENT OF THE GENERAL DIRECTORS
abstract: A preliminary step in the analysis of the admin'ive behavior in Italy is the identification of basic cultural influences on the personality formation of those few people -career civil servents -who are near the top of the admin'ive org & whose duties include the management of one of the main branches of the service & the formulation of alternatives to the pol'ly appointed Head of a Ministry or Dept. Such duties are entrusted to the 96 Direttori Generali (General Directors-GD's) of the various Ministries. An attempt was made to determine the basic cultural influences on their personality using yr & place of birth data. Through their combination 3 variables were obtained: regional origin, age, & size of the township in which they were born. It was found that 46.9% of the GD's were born in southern Italy & 15.6% in Sicily & Sardinia. The GD's are, on the whole, rather old: 91.7% are 50 or older; 62.5% are 55 or older; & 18.8% are 63 or older. Diff's with the Italian managerial class as a whole (73.1% are 50 or older) & US business executives (in 1952 67.0% were 50 or older) are signif. 60.4% of the GD's were born in townships with less than 50,000 inhabitants, as compared with 72.5% of the members of the Lower House of Parliament, 34.3% of the Italian elite class as a whole, & 61.7% of the Italian pop. It is concluded that the majority of the GD's were exposed to the strong influence of the authoritarian & paternalistic culture of southern Italy during the period between the beginning of WWI &the end of the econ boom of the 20's, when fascism became firmly entrenched; they were not exposed to ideas & values basically diff from those prevailing in their native environments. The GD's are unevenly distributed among the Ministries. In general, the % of southerners, Sicilians & Sardinians seems to decrease with the increase in the degree of professionalization. Finally, a scale of 'bur'tic accessibility' was devised for members of the Lower House which showed that a member from southern Italy has 8 times as many possibilities as a northerner or central Italian to find that the GD who is handling his business is from the same part of the country. Modified AA.

title: BUREAUCRACY AND THE SOCIALLY HANDICAPPED: A STUDY OF LOWER-STATUS TENANTS IN PUBLIC HOUSING
abstract: Findings obtained in personal interviews with 452 F tenants from 25 public housing projects in a large north-eastern city suggest the influence of soc handicap or stigma on the relationship of the Ls tenant to the public housing system, a relationship not unlike that between disadvantaged groups & service bur'cy generally. Though concerned about public housing policy, these Ls tenants were less knowledgeable about bur'tic power structure & less likely to obtain adequate housing-related services than other tenants. These results may have practical implications for soc policy. The failure to provide information or to otherwise service the needs of those who are handicapped by Ls may inflame an already pervasive sense of exploitation & may lead to violent forms of protest. AA.

title: Causes and Consequences of Corruption: Mozambique in Transition
abstract: Assesses the level of corruption in Mozambique at a particularly important point during its economic transition program (1995/96) to examine what might account for the presence & the economic effect of corruption. Interview data from 30 private sector & donor representatives indicate a dramatic increase in the level of corruption in recent years. This seems attributable to a change in the basic conditions for deterrence of corruption highlighted by principal agent theory: bureaucrats retain extensive control rights over economic activity, structures for monitoring bureaucrats have been weakened during the recent political transition, & trends in wages have created incentive problems. The effects of corruption on the economy involve both a distorting effect on government trade & tax policies & a disincentive effect with regard to investment, particularly for smaller firms. Implications of poor economic reform on state performance & income, in terms of state response to expectations of democratization, are considered. 2 Tables, 3 Figures, 49 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: A threefold relationship to work: transformation of public services and occupational identity
authors: Flecker, Jorg; Krenn, Manfred; Tschernitz, Maria
abstract: During the last 2 decades the public administration and the public services have undergone far-reaching transformations that resulted in substantial changes in work and employment. This contribution discusses the question as to how workers perceive these upheavals and what consequences these have for their occupational identity. Based on empirical research on an Austrian town the authors show how local government employees, doctors and nurses at the community hospital and the post office's deliverers and counter clerks interpret the transformations in particular from the perspective of their occupational self-conception. The article makes clear that using the concept of a threefold relationship to work makes it easier to understand workers' perceptions, interpretations and reactions. Such a threefold relationship to work includes a labour power perspective, a subject perspective and the public sector ethos. Adapted from the source document.

title: Interactive Governance: A Concept of Participative Public Administration?
abstract: This article investigates possibilities for the consolidation of new forms of network based on interactive governance. Starting from theoretical considerations on the urban governance concept, it discusses innovative experiences of public participation in the cities of Santos, Porto Alegre & Curitiba. Emphasis is given to the analysis of new institutional arrangements as governmental strategies aiming at two basic objectives: first, to augment democratic legitimacy by introducing new interactive practices, & second, to improve the quality of public policies & administrative performance by means of extended participation. In spite of the general tendency of an increasingly interactive practice of local governance, differences may be identified with regard to the ideological motives that stimulate the extension of public participation, the processes of implementation of these interactive practices &, finally, the characteristics of the priority target groups of participatory arrangements. Adapted from the source document.

title: BUREAUCRATIC MAN: A PORTRAIT AND INTERPRETATION
abstract: An analysis of data from interviews with a representative sample of 3,101 M US citizens employed in civilian occup's is presented. The survey was conducted by the Nat'l Opinion Res Center in 1964 (S. Sudman & J. Feldman, "Sample Design and Field Procedures,' pp 482-485 of Appendix 1 in John W. C. Johnstone & Ramon J. Rivera, Ed's, VOLUNTEERS FOR LEARNING: A STUDY OF THE EDUCATIONAL PURSUITS OF AMERICAN ADULTS, Chicago. Ill: Aldine, 1965). It was aimed to ascertain whether ',bur'crats' really are conformist in their values & in their appraisal of soc reality, resistant to innovation & change. literalistic in their moral judgments, & inflexible in their thinking. It was also endeavored to discover how bur'tion exerts its soc psychol'al impact. Indices of values, soc orientation, & intellectual functioning are described. Contrary to general assumptions, findings show that there is a small but consistent tendency for men who work in bur'tic org's to be more intellectually flexible, more open to new experience, & more self-directed in their values than are men who work in nonbur'tic org's. This may in part result from bur'cies' drawing on a more educated LF. In larger part. though, it appears to be a consequence of occup'al conditions attendant on bur'tion-ie, far greater job protection, somewhat higher income, & substantively more complex work. Bur'tic org's have a more effectively circumscribed authority. while non-bur' tic org's do not have less authority. but personal, potentially arbitrary authority. 4 Tables. Modified HA.

title: Beyond the Organization: The Influence of Community and Personal Values on Street-Level Bureaucrats' Responsiveness
abstract: Quantifies & explains intrastate differences in Medicaid spending in MI, a state with a highly centralized program & few local discretionary decisions. The differences exist because implementation takes place in different organizational & political settings, affecting potential participants' willingness to apply for the programs & the responsiveness of social service workers to their clients. A model to predict generosity & participation in MI counties based on supply, demand, & political factors is developed & tested, focusing on participation & spending in 6 counties to understand differences in organizational, political, & task environments. It is concluded that while these factors are important, recipient behavior -- shaped in large part by the behavior of the social service office bureaucratic leadership & the policy environment of the county -- matters as well. 6, 1 Appendix, 52 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Effect of Organization Size Upon Normative Diversity
abstract: Increasing org'al size is commonly assumed to produce greater diversity of normative climates. The interactional perspective assumed here suggests that while the process of interaction is operative within any soc system, relations undergo change & become more selective & volun tary as org'al size increases. As increasing size serves to increase the number of voluntary self-selected relations, a greater range of soc perspectives & norms can find support & protection. Data from teachers in 38 public elementary Sch's gave support to the hyp that org'al size is positively related to diversity of normative climate in 3 diff specific tests. AA.

title: A Testing Case: State Incorporation of Community Work
abstract: Forms of community work that have been fostered or discouraged by the Nottingham Community Project (NCP), the largest community work project in GB, are analyzed; underlying theoretical assumptions are identified & major practice implications discussed. It is concluded that the NCP has become a massive & ineffective bureaucracy that controls, limits, institutionalizes, & incorporates residents' involvement in associated community work agencies. J. Cannon.

title: Satisfaction and Morale Among Parish Clergy: What American Catholic and Orthodox Priests Can Learn from Each Other
authors: Krindatch, Alexei D; Hoge, Dean R
abstract: The Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches share a similar theology and a hierarchical church administration. Local parish communities are organized in similar ways. However, the Roman Catholic and Orthodox Christian churches occupy different places in the context of American culture, and they have developed distinct notions of priesthood. Findings explore similarities and differences in the attitudes and experience of Catholic and Orthodox clergy. Most striking, the younger clergy (less than 45 years of age) report more conservative attitudes about the priesthood, "democracy" in church government, and empowering lay persons in the ministry. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Governmentality, Globalization, and Local Practice: Transformations of a Hegemonic Discourse
authors: Salskov-Iverson, Dorte; Hansen, Hans Krause; Bislev, Sven
abstract: Explores the relationship between local practice, governmentality, & globalization in relation to new public management (NPM) global discourse, which emphasizes business-management practices, individual rationalities, & market mechanisms for operation of the public sector. Constructivist theories are drawn on to expand the governance perspective to encompass a view of the public sector as discursively regulated, arguing that discursive moments of governance exhibit aspects of the (post)modern hegemony of management thinking. Further, local interpretations of NPM discourse follow contextually defined logics attached to discourses about projects not necessarily based on the political/ideological assumptions in NPM. An overview of the genealogy of NPM shows how it became a hegemonic discourse through the evolution of transnational discourse communities. Two cases of local government reform, in Mexico & the UK, are examined to support the argument that NPM discourse represents hegemony as an ongoing process articulated both through transnational discourse communities, & at the local level, where it is translated into arrangements relevant to political interests & power configurations. J. Lindroth

title: Un campo en construcción: Sociología de la Gerencia
abstract: El propósito de este artículo es mostrar la relevancia que en los últimos años han venido adquiriendo los estudios sociologicos de la gerencia, para desentrañar las racionalidades que subyacen en la dirección de los procesos productivos. La investigación en este campo logró demostrar que la racionalidad tecno-burocrática, impuesta con una teleología productivista, funciona bajo la lógica instrumental de una elite que impide que el proceso de trabajo se despliegue como una acción dotada de sentido humano. De allí que los estudios sociologicos de la gerencia se han planteado produncizar la perspectiva epistemológica con el interaccionismo simbólico, la etnometodología y la investigación acción participante, para la construcción una sociología de la gerencia que puenda promover el ejercicio de una racionalidad humano-productiva basada en la sensibilidad, el compromiso y la calidad de vida de los actores laborales.

title: Dual Power in the Venezuelan Revolution
abstract: Explores the rise of communal power as part of the Bolivarian Revolution in Venezuela from a Leninist perspective centered on the concept of "dual power." It is argued that communal councils are indicative of robust democratic development & reveal that state sectors are actively working to remove old state structures by devolving power to the local level where dual power is possible. Lenin's concept is defined before applying it to the Venezuelan case. In so doing, conceptual limitations are identified along with some of the challenges confronting the revolutionary process. In this context, attention is given to the establishment of the communal councils, their purpose to attack bureaucracy & corruption at other levels of governance, implications of the Leninist criterion for dual power of a directly armed populace for Venezuela, & Hugo Chavez's role as a "subversive in power.". D. Edelman

title: ON RUSSIAN NATIONAL SECURITY THROUGH THE LENSES OF THE PROBLEMS OF CONTEMPORARY LEGAL EDUCATION AND CRIMINOLOGY AS A RESEARCH AND ACADEMIC DISCIPLINE
authors: Radnayeva, Elvira L; Boskholov, Sergey S
abstract: The paper is devoted to the problems of legal science and education, viewed from the standpoint of ensuring national security. The object of the study is criminology, whose rights have been undeservingly infringed in recent years, especially after Russia joined the Bologna Process. The authors believe that this it not accidental and that such pressure on criminology, which tells the society the truth about crime and the work of criminal justice, is orchestrated. In the interests of national security and training qualified specialists in the sphere of crime counteraction it is necessary to restore the criminology's former status as one of the most important academic subjects. Diminishing its role and putting it among second-tier academic disciplines is not just erroneous, but extremely dangerous in the conditions when crime in Russia is characterized by negative trends both in its quantitative and, especially, in its qualitative side. Criminal threats' increase is a result of a lack of research-based lawmaking and the de-professionalization of the practice of fighting crime. After the enactment of the Federal Law of June 23, 2016 ? 182-?? «On the Basics of the Crime Prevention System in the Russian Federation», which is abundant in evaluative concepts, it became more urgent to train lawyers with good criminological thinking, the ability to use criminological instruments in the practice of crime prevention; another concern is the professional development of employees at police departments and other bodies involved in crime prevention at all levels. The authors mention other consequences of switching to a multilevel system: the loss of uniqueness and the mass-market character of university legal education, reduction of the study period for academic subjects, a growing number of classes given by each teacher, bureaucratization and the shrinking of academic freedom, etc. The authors suggest that the Project of the Federal Educational Standard of High Education for training in the sphere 40.04.01 Jurisprudence should include a clause that only persons with a degree in law can enroll in Mater's programs in this sphere, which will allow to improve Master's degree training level and enhance the competitiveness of Russian university law school.

title: THE RECENT DOCTRINE OF THE SCIENCE OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION IN THE UNITED STATES
abstract: A brief essay discussing the panorama of recent thought in the US on the sci of public admin, indicating the tendencies & developments & confronting them with traditional works. Instit'al studies presented in specialized professional publications such as the Public Personnel Review, &/The American City & State Government are examined & the tendency of S's to be preoccupied with dates & facts which provide a safe guide for legislators, admin'ors & voters is considered. The influence of the Public Science Quarterly & the activities of the Amer Society for Public administration are discussed. A survey of the literature in the yrs 1962 & 1963 shows a prevalence of operative models of conduct in the frame of internat'l collaboration & the fundamental problem of this comparativist direction is stated to be the development admin. M. Maxfield.

title: Autonomy and Bureaucratic Accountability in Primary Care: What English General Practitioners Say
abstract: Clinical autonomy has long been seen as conceptually central to the analysis of the occupational status of the medical profession though the implications for this of recent developments in health care managerialism have been disputed by theorists. In particular, the question has arisen as to whether "restratification," ie, the active involvement of physicians in this process, should be construed as medical elites exerting control over the rank & file in order to protect the profession as a whole, or as an incursion from outside it. This paper uses interview data from 49 general medical practitioners in northern England. It investigates their perceptions of how current government policies & the new institutions & governance arrangements that they have created impact on physicians' ability to set their own limits & to judge their own work. We found a clear acceptance by GPs of the need to discharge "bureaucratic accountability," in particular to maintain records of their clinical decisions. This provides the possibility of external surveillance of medical work, & thus implies a clear reduction in autonomy over the content of medical work on the part of rank-&-file GPs, who may regret this situation but offer little resistance to it. Our findings illustrate a form of restratification; the most frequently reported immediate source of pressure to modify casenote recording was the Primary Care Group (PCG), an organization constitutionally dominated by physicians acting in a managerial capacity. Nevertheless, the agendas of PCGs are largely driven by central government & our study thus provides further evidence of the intermediary or contingent (rather than independent) character of professional autonomy. 54 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Constructing truths in a culture of disbelief: Understanding asylum screening from within
abstract: While a multitude of immigration officers enforce the numerous laws and policies regulating the arrival of asylum seekers, their work is often hidden from the public eye and ignored by academic debate, leaving fundamental questions unanswered: Is the migration debate blinded by bureaucracy or oblivious to the complexity of the asylum screening process? This article originates from an ethnographic study, which included over 80 interviews, six months of participant observation and four years of familiarization with the main actors, framed by a triangulation scheme that allowed in-depth exploration of the field from within. The study's conclusions expose how identifying immigration officers' subculture is key to understanding asylum controls and to reach beyond the legal shield and the rhetorical concepts of political debate. Based on this empirical research, this article exposes how officers' criteria for screening individuals are not derived from regulations or laws but their own categorizations, rules and values derived from ambiguous stereotypes nurtured by officers' experiences and social prejudices. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright holder.]

title: BUREAUCRATIC SOCIALIZATION AND ORGANIZATIONAL ACCOMMODATION
abstract: Upon entering a complex org for the first time, persons unacquainted with the central 'values' of bur'tic participation must undergo a process of soc'ization with respect to these patterns. Until such learning takes place, the org may find it necessary to forego the bur'tic mode of org in favor of a form more compatible with the existing beliefs of the new entrants. These questions are considered here within the context of an Appalachian anti-poverty program employing persons native to the area. Results confirming these expectations suggest the importance of cultural & org'al compatibility. HA.

title: Running the risk: police officer discretion and family violence in New Zealand
abstract: As in other jurisdictions, the police in New Zealand have a poor record of responding to domestic violence, a category of crime widely perceived within New Zealand to be a particularly extensive problem relative to other societies. Against that background policy developments have focused on developing risk assessment techniques as a basis for identifying cases of family and domestic violence that are likely to escalate. Using interviews with frontline police officers, this article explores police officers' attitudes towards these investigating methods and their experiences of interviewing victims of family violence in order to gain information about risk. It is argued that while officer attitudes towards risk assessment in general terms might vary, in practice the majority of officers do not complete risk assessment processes in accordance with police policy, even if they support the practice in principle. The reasons for this, it is argued, have more to do with officer negotiation of the demands of routine patrol work and time-management processes that contribute to the marginalisation of bureaucratic procedures. Supervisors and managers compound the perception that these tasks are of second-order importance. In these ways there are cultural and managerial barriers to the more effective policing of family violence; however, the reduction of officer discretion through policy and procedure seems unlikely to provide a viable solution. A professional practice model might be more effective if officers can be trained and educated about the role of risk assessment in this context and the importance of their role as data collectors; although this does not fit easily with traditional concepts of 'real policework'. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Dissolving the Iron Cages? Tocqueville, Michels, Bureaucracy and the Perpetuation of Elite Power
abstract: Modern management theory often forgets more than it remembers. 'What's new'? is the refrain. Yet, we suggest, there is much that we should already know from which we might appropriately learn, 'Lest we forget'. The current paper takes its departure from two points of remembrance that bear on the sustained assaults on bureaucracy that have been unleashed by the critiques of recent years. These critiques include the new public management literature as well as its inspiration in the new literature of cultural entrepreneurialism. Both promise to dissolve bureaucracy's iron cage. We explain, using the classical political themes of oligarchy, democracy, & the production of elite power, why we should consider such transubstantiation alchemical by confronting contemporary discussions with the wisdom of an earlier, shrewder knowledge, whose insights we need to recall to understand the complexity of the hybridizations between supposedly opposite models of organizations. Tables, References. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright 2006.]

title: CONTRIBUTION TO THE DYSFUNCTIONAL CONCEPTION OF THE SOURCES OF BUREAUCRACY AND BUREAUCRATISM IN THE CAPITALIST SYSTEM
abstract: Diff ways of conceiving of bur'cy & bur'ism are discussed, proceeding from R. K. Merton's conception of org'al functions & dysfunctions. Functional conceptions of bur'cy, as seen in the works of M. Weber, F. Morstein & K. Marx are analyzed. Attention is given to the basic sources of lawful tendencies giving rise to bur'ism under the conditions of a contemporary industr society of a capitalist character. The opinions advanced are based upon A. Gramsci's view on the importance of intraorg'al needs originating from the 'iron laws of the functioning of the apparatus.' Included are Parkinson's laws re the immanent sources of excessive growth of the admin'ive personnel, the tendency toward monopolization & stereotyping of intraorg'al information, the more advanced growth of formalization as compared to the growth of org ascertained by P. Drucker, M. Dimock's developmental tendency of instit'ization toward rigidness & depersonalization, & R. Michel's law of oligarchization. The conclusion is that the 'bur'tic deformations & the dysfunction of technical & org'al relations are brought about by insufficient control of their excessive complexity, by the lag in the sci'fic & technical development behind the needs of practice, & by the fact that the various partial technical & org'al means defy their original purposefulness & liability.' To explain these processes of bur'ization, the Marxist category of alienation is recommended. Basic problems of the models of bur'tic org are also discussed: the macrosoc model, R. K. Merton's, P. Selznick's & A. Gouldner's microsoc models. An attempt is then made to construct new micro- & macrosoc models conceived from the Marxist point of view. Both these models follow 2-fold possibilities of bur'tic or democratic tendencies in the development of soc org. In conelusion, some means of eliminating bur'ism are pointed out, & it is indicated that the elimination of its deeper causes is connected with a broader soc context of the sources of org'al alienation. Modified HA.

title: Grass Roots Family Action and Military Policy Responses
authors: Stanley, Jay; Segal, Mady Wechsler; Laughton, Charlotte Jeanne
abstract: KEYWORDS: army, bureaucracy, family, family policy, formal organization, grass roots movement, military family, social change, volunteer action, work and familyINTRODUCTIONDramatic changes are occurring within the military and the military family. General changes within the American family and gender roles have encouraged policy attention from the armed forces. There is conflict between the military and the family, and the policy attention shows movement toward a more cooperative effort to accommodate the needs and interests of both.For a complete reprint of this article contact Haworth Press by telephone (1-800-HAWORTH) or EMail (getinfo@haworth.com) Article copyright The Haworth Press, Inc.

title: The Origins of the Authoritarian Welfare State in Prussia. Conservatives, Bureaucracy and the Social Question 1815-70
abstract: "The Origins of the Authoritarian Welfare State in Prussia.  Conservatives, Bureaucracy and the Social Question 1815-70," by Hermann Beck, is reviewed.

title: Franz Neumann's Theory of Modern Dictatorship
abstract: Examines the theory by a lesser-known member of the Frankfurt school, Franz Neumann (eg, Behemoth: The Structure and Practice of National Socialism, 1942), that modern dictatorship flows naturally from liberal democracy, highlighting nine major points: (1) modern dictatorships make claims to democracy; (2) all tyrannies subvert the rule of law & the independence of the judiciary; (3) all dictatorships possess their own inner logic or structure; (4) most dictatorships combine oppressive bureaucracy with powerful charisma; (5) modern dictatorships isolate individuals by eliminating institutions between the individual & the ruling class; (6) isolated individuals are more susceptible to propaganda; (7) resistance to violence alone is ineffectual; (8) racial theories provide a false enemy that aids isolated individuals in uniting & supports the material interests of the ruling class; & (9) all dictatorships are not entirely totalitarian, but possess bureaucratic politics. 21 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Political and Bureaucratic Power in Australian Government: A Weberian Approach
abstract: In one of his three theories of bureaucracy, Max Weber argued that the extent to which bureaucrats play an independent policy role depends on whether politicians exercise political leadership. Here, the historical evidence shows that the trajectory of Australian government vindicates Weber's theory. Senior officials have played an independent role in the absence of political leadership. Notwithstanding this, they have exhibited the leadership limitations that Weber ascribed to bureaucrats. Contrary to Weber's belief such limitations are not insurmountable, since the work of bureaucrats enables them to acquire leadership skills. Greater political leadership since the 1980s has curtailed the independence of bureaucrats. In Weberian terms, this may be attributed to the emergence of politicians who possess political conviction & administrative competence; one result has been the hybridization of political & bureaucratic roles. It is concluded that Weber's theory incorporates the best features of bureaucratic politics & institutionalist theory, but not their limitations. 86 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucratic Politics: Academic Windfalls and Intellectual Pitfalls
authors: Nathan, James A; Oliver, James K
abstract: The bureaucratic politics analysis of foreign & defense policy making is inadequate as a paradigm because it constricts analysis to a world hopelessly contingent on outside developments. Among these developments are presidential decisions, the activities of Congress, & such organizations as defense contractors and multinational corporations. This paradigm also requires the analysis of vast amounts of information, given the complexity of the 'bureaucratic game' to which it confines attention. These problems make it inadequate as an analysis. Modified HA.

title: Colonial Bureaucratic Culture and Development Administration: Portrait of an Old-Fashioned Indian Bureaucrat
abstract: The literature on development administration considers the ideal development administrator to be adaptable, entrepreneurial, result-oriented, tactful, freewheeling, & pragmatic. It also considers the bureaucrats bred in colonial culture as not possessing these traits & as being too rigid, procedural, hierarchical, status-oriented, & therefore less useful in a turbulent, uncertain, & highly politicized environment. It is argued through the in-depth study of the career of a colonial style Indian bureaucrat that the prescribed characteristics of the new development bureaucrats in their operational manifestation may prove to be inimical to the growth & legitimization of an administrative system aspiring to democracy & development. On the other hand, the ideology & style of the colonial bureaucrats, which emphasize respect for political masters & rule of law, & high standards of integrity, impartiality, & performance, may prove to be more effective in legitimizing & institutionalizing a democratic & developmental administrative system. AA.

title: Diaspora and Centralism: The Economy of Metropolitan Lima
abstract: Internal economic processes that regulate the district & interdistrict spaces of Lima are reviewed alongside external forces & trends. The economy of the city depends on globalization, the crisis of Lima's centralism, the city's pattern of development, diversification of the surrounding economy, financial concentration, & the persistence & aggravation of poverty. With its pronounced disarticulations, inequalities, & exclusions, Lima urgently needs a system for integrated administration, or it is in danger of becoming totally unmanageable. The administrative challenge is to move away from the concept of city-territory towards the concept of a complex & heterogeneous metropolis. Lima's development will proceed along with that of the country's interior. 19 References. M. Pflum

title: Toward Valid Computer Simulations of Bureaucratized Decisions
abstract: Simulations may be divided into 2 types: (1) those whose use aims to produce a valid human representation of the situation simulated, & (2) those whose use is founded on the assumption that such a representation already exists. Behavior based on humanly internalized norms clearly fits the 2nd category; bureaucratic decision-making is an example. The primary problem in simulation of bureaucracy is that the rules often do not actually specify what decisions should emerge precisely; however, for routinized decisions, simple linear models can yield R values of .90 in many cases. When a bureaucracy cannot be modeled in this way, it appears that either social control or improved efficiency may be needed. The exploration of this area of behavior appears naturally highly suited to computer simulation techniques of human decisions. 1 Figure. W. H. Stoddard.

title: Anti-corruption movements, mechanisms, and machines - an introduction
abstract: Anticorruption programmes, projects and campaigns have come to constitute an essential aspect of furthering good governance over the last two decades. This article provides a conceptual framework for studying anticorruption efforts and it assesses their nature and impacts across Eastern Europe by focusing on the interplay between the international and domestic domains. More precisely, it differentiates between domestic social movements, governmental political machines and international legal mechanisms. These three levels of analysis - domestic civil society, national governments and international society - provide a meaningful general basis for comparing a variety of anticorruption efforts. On all three levels, political and material interests of relevant actors are complemented by normative arguments. In assessing the case studies in this volume, this article concludes that, at the interfaces of the three levels, coincidental and spontaneous breakthroughs have largely outweighed systematic implementation of appropriate anticorruption strategies. It further stresses that broad societal support for anticorruption remains essential for the success of any international or governmental initiatives. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Multi-notability/Trajectories: Historical Reconfigurations and Social Determinants of the Political and Cultural Inscription of Brazilian Congressmen
authors: Reis, Eliana Tavares dos; Grill, Igor Gastal
abstract: This article discusses the determinants of the affirmation of congressmen, which cannot be disassociated from the realms of political power and cultural production in Brazil. In order to apprehend the logics and practices that preside over the occupations over varied and relatively well allocated positions in Parliament, universities, state bureaucracies, media, intellectual legitimation spaces and arenas in which political issues are formulated, the authors focus on the study the exemplary trajectories of Afonso Arinos and Delfim Netto. The trajectories and positions occupied by these figures are examined in light of historical conjunctures, the reconfiguration of power relations (at the national and international levels) and the transformations in the domains of university education and cultural mediation. The redefinitions and amalgamations of legitimate repertoires of interventions (erudition and technical knowledge) mobilized in the main debates concerning the nation in the twentieth century are considered. This, in turn, allows for, on one hand, the identification of processes, spaces, competences and languages that are concurrent, complementary and interdependent, and, on the other one, reflect upon the elaboration of representation of culture, politics, the economy and the State. Adapted from the source document.

title: Sociology, Political Economy and the Goals of Production Organizations
abstract: The goals of production org's represent a new subject of study. The conceptual tools accounting for the pol of large enterprises are not found in the writings of K. Marx, M. Weber or in any conventional econ theory. A critical study of both the contemporary sociol'al & econ analyses of this problem, & an attempt to determine the validity criteria of the results, show the importance of greater knowledge. In any case, the systematic study of the relationships between environment & the pol of firms & their internal power relations remains fragmentary at best. It calls for the elaboration of analytical tools (briefly described here) which are still temporary. 1 Table. Modified HA.

title: Dinâmicas do atendimento ao cidadão: estudo sobre o Disque-Câmara/Dynamics of citizen services: a study of the Dial House
abstract: This article analyzes the dynamics of reception and registration of demands from users of the free telephone answering system of the House of Representatives. The objective of the research was to delve into the workplace of the answering system operators,, in order to understand how the demands are received, recorded and processed. Priority was given to procedures relating to the interactions between clerks and citizens, which has a specific protocol regarding the language to be used on the phone. The product of this interaction is the material record of the messages in text and audio format, a bureaucratic registration device characterized by statistical rationality. In short, the Dial-Chamber is regulated by discipline, but is a functional island, disconnected from the other parliamentary social network participation tools. The theoretical framework of this work relies on sociological approaches about the mediating role of parliament and the possible uses of socio-technical networks in that process. The methodology consisted in carrying out a field survey, which combined site visits, direct observation, interviews and document analysis.

title: Jus civitas, Urban Right
abstract: This paper touches briefly on the notion of the rights of urbanism. An urban right is defined as a public right -- a matter of public function rather than of power. Such rights are recognized & enforced through public administration, according to the civil code. Several examples are provided in illustration. Adapted from the source document.

title: Intellectuals in a World Made of Knowledge
abstract: Contends that the contemporary notion of a politically concerned, socially engaged, culturally sensitive "public intellectual" has no antecedent in Hindu, Buddhist, Judaic, Greek, Christian, or Islamic traditions. Ways in which gurus, monks, rabbis, priests, mullahs, or philosophers differ from both today's intellectuals & the Confucian literati are pointed out. The Confucian literati, seen as forerunners of the modern intellectual, opted to be an integral part of the world in order to transform it from within. They were "action intellectuals" focused on "managing the world of economics, politics, & society." The Confucian literati is compared to British civil servants who were also knowledgeable generalists who had to deal with such bureaucratic details as managing budgets, handling legal cases, & supervising education. Although today's professionals & technocrats are reminiscent of both the Confucian literati & British civil servants, they have a much heavier burden of by virtue of being responsible for helping people survive & flourish in a world that is far more complex. J. Lindroth

title: Bureaucracy and Democracy: Participation and Opposition in Industrial Enterprise
abstract: The concept of industrial democracy is analyzed in the context of bureaucratic structure. Theories of democratic evolution are briefly reviewed, noting a distinction between the procedural or unitary model (in the tradition of Jean-Jacques Rousseau) & the libertarian or conflictual model (as outlined by John Locke). Comparisons between the Yugoslavian self-management industrial system & northeast Italian management structures are drawn, noting the horizontal bureaucracy prevalent in the former & its relatively high degree of democratization. The importance of participation structured around worker incentives & task individuation is stressed; participation & democracy are not seen as fully equatable, however, & areas of persistent incompatibility between democracy & bureaucracy are suggested. 2 Tables, Appendix. Modified HA.

title: Empathy and Its Importance in Long-Term Home Health Care
abstract: Describes the development & socialization of empathy, its relation to altruistic behaviors, & its role in psychotherapy & long-term home health care. The major theoretical perspectives on empathy & its antecedents are described. It is asserted that a bureaucratic health care system decreases the ability of home health care providers to respond empathetically to their patients. The bureaucracy surrounding home health care must be minimized, & health care providers must be trained to appreciate their patients' inner experience from their own frames of reference. 33 References. M. Nichols-Wagner

title: Freudenburg Beyond Borders: Recreancy, Atrophy of Vigilance, Bureaucratic Slippage, and the Tragedy of 9/11
abstract: In this chapter, I suggest three conceptual tools developed by William R. Freudenburg and colleagues that characterize the failure of institutions to carry out their duties -- recreancy, atrophy of vigilance, and bureaucratic slippage -- are of use beyond environmental sociology in the framing of the September 11, 2001 disaster. Using testimony and findings from primary materials such as the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence Joint Inquiry hearings and report (2002, 2004a, 2004b) and the National Commission on Terrorist Attacks Upon the United States (2004) alongside insider accounts, I discuss how Freudenburg's tools have the potential to theorize institutional failures that occur in national security decision making. I also suggest these tools may be of particular interest to the U.S. intelligence community in its own investigation of various types of risk and failures. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Limits of Financial Imagination: Free Investors, Efficient Markets, and Crisis
abstract: Fieldwork with a team of investment managers investing in credit derivatives in Paris in 2004 shows how the concepts of "investor" and "market efficiency" are central in the technicalities of their procedures, in diverse and contradictory ways. The employees refer to their moral and political contents, as they are articulated in liberal philosophy and in financial regulation, to make sense of their careers and of the social role of finance. "Crisis" is then defined as a deviation from market efficiency, itself expected to lead to an optimal allocation of credit. These concepts thus constitute the limited repertoire of the meaning of practical rules followed by employees for a remuneration, within a bureaucratic commercial network, in a setting very different from the utopias from which the concepts stem. Therefore, anthropologists must not use them as analytic tools; rather, such concepts should be understood as part of the object of study. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Public Management and Social Participation
abstract: This paper presents the recent changes international institutions have publicly discussed concerning the relations between economic growth & social development. In the past it was planned to grow first & then arrive at a better distribution of the benefits; today, it is agreed that it is not possible to maintain & improve higher levels of growth if one cannot achieve previously a minimum level of equity. For inducing this mental change on the public decisions it is an indispensable requisite to share a public management view, essentially different from the private activity, with a precise interest in social problems. The paper analyzes the profile of this necessary social manager & the real possibilities to develop its attributes out of academic training & participation. These initial profile attributes of the candidate's profile are basic & not easy to generate, so one can only contribute to develop some of them. Finally, as a result of the previous analysis, the paper critically analyzes the forms that are being assumed by the Latin American state reform. 27 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Exchanging Knowledge, Enhancing Capacities, Developing Mechanisms: IOM's Role in the Implementation of the EU-Russia Readmission Agreement
abstract: Research on European Union (EU)-Russia cooperation in migration issues often neglects important actors involved in these seemingly bilateral arrangements. This paper questions the role that the International Organisation for Migration (IOM) has been playing in the EU-Russia cooperation in migration management. The analysis is situated in the theoretical framework describing international organisations (IOs) as bureaucracies and within the discussions about international migration governance and migration management. The paper describes the context of the EU-Russia migration management cooperation and identifies the major activities of IOM in Russia. Treating IOs as bureaucracies that pursue their own interests, the paper argues that, far from being a mere implementing body, IOM is an actor that, to a significant extent, has shaped the outcome of EU-Russia migration dialogue. At the same time, it is the context of this bilateral cooperation that has allowed IOM to strengthen its position vis-à-vis both Russia and the EU and to be successful in the competition with other IOs.

title: Towards a Model of Philippine Bureaucracy
abstract: The Philippine civil service has attracted comparatively little scholarly attention, and such analyses as have been conducted are strongly influenced by the view that both the polity and bureaucracy lie at some distance from Weber's bureaucratic ideals. The model of an emotional bureaucracy sketched in this paper collapses a number of dichotomies (such as the impersonal versus human and social, the emotional versus rational, and the formal versus informal) in Weberian analysis. In drawing attention to, and in attempting to accommodate, the bureaucracy's emotional qualities and its dimensionality, the model may also encourage a broader and more intense debate on the Philippine civil service. The model comprises three interlocking cycles: instrumentalism and authoritarianism within organisations; a deepening affective sphere outside organisations and growing technical and emotional professionalism within organisations; and Puritanism and instrumentalism. These cycles do not describe stages of development, and they are not peculiar either to bureaucratic organisations or to the Philippines. Adapted from the source document.

title: Stable Resources of Protest Movements: The Multi-Organizational Field
authors: Curtis, Russell L, Jr; Zurcher, Louis A, Jr
abstract: The natural histories & membership characteristics of 2 protest org's, one located in a southwestern gov & educ'al center with several tertiary industries & a pop of about 250,000 & the other in a primarily indsutr city with a pop of about 100,000, both conducting anti-pornography crusades, were assembled from nonparticipant observation, document res, & structured interviews with active members & other knowledgeable individuals. The concept of a 'multi-org'al field' suggests that community org's approximate an ordered, coordinated system. Within the field, interorg'al processes can be identified on 2 levels: the org'al level, where networks are established by joint activities, staff, boards of directors, target clientele, etc, & the individual level, where networks are established by multiple affiliations of members. Multi-org'al fields should operate on both levels in the emergence & maintenance of these portest org's. The data reveal that: (1) The anti-pornography org's were enmeshed in a network of other community org's, particularly voluntary assoc's, in the larger multi-org'al field. (2) These interorg'al alignments were based on common interests, ideologies, audiences, or other shared characteristics. (3) Anti-pornography org members shared memberships in other voluntary assoc's within the milti-org'al field. (4) Diff's between the 2 protest org's in the kinds of linkages they had within the field were associated with diff's in their goals, strategies, member recruitment patterns, member characteristics, goal acievements, & life-span. The data is presented in the sequence of the historical development of the org's. 3 Tables, 1 Diagram. Modified HA.

title: CONCERNING BUREAUCRACY AS A SYSTEM OF ORGANIZATION
abstract: A paper criticizing the classical interpretations of bur'cy. M. Weber did not consider bur'cy bad in itself, nevertheless, he felt that the bur'tic org could consider the individual only as a tool. The analysis in terms of HR, the interactionist theory, & the theory of leadership concern themselves with control, but do not consider changes within the org. The decisive contributions were those of A. Gouldner & A. Tannenbaum. An analysis in terms of strategy is suggested. Power of decision will be located where stability is considered as more important than functional goals. Impersonality & rigid rules are necessary. The bur'tic system when not dysfunctional can provide the employees with a means of negotiation. The requisite for the system is that it can undergo some change until it reaches a level of fluency. Impersonality becomes a weapon & protection for the individual. Modified AA.

title: `True Stories' of Canada; Tim Hortons and the Branding of National Identity
abstract: This article discusses the connection between brands, national identity and the social and historic practices of the Canadian nation-state. Specifically, it examines the long-running `True Stories' ad campaign of Tim Hortons coffee shops, Canada's most successful quick-service restaurant chain. These ads insert Tim Hortons into customers' stories about travel, endurance and adventure, and authorize Tim Hortons itself as both the site and source of Canada's self-image.This authorization occurs in three ways: 1) by taking advantage of a space generated by overt, statist, bureaucratic management of Canadian identity and culture, 2) by locating national identity within mundane, sensual consumptive desire, and 3) by capitalizing on the ambiguities of articulating Canadian national culture, especially within the context of an officially multi-cultural project.

title: Technology Assessment and Political Decision-Making
abstract: Often technology assessments (TA) performed in the public sector serve two very different masters. As a policy assessment tool employed in a political environment, TA must make allowance for the norms, values, & sources of legitimacy for bureaucratic policy making. At the same time, TA is evaluated & legitimated according to many of the same logical & methodological criteria as the sciences & other modes of systematic inquiry. Considered are the sometimes conflicting values of rationality, political interests, & organizational routines that come into play in public sector TA. G. Allison's decision-making typology (The Essence of Decision, Boston: Little, Brown & Co, 1972) is employed to facilitate analysis of the conflicting values. Modified HA.

title: The UK Caribbean Overseas Territories: governing unruliness amidst the extra-territorial EU
abstract: This article traces the contours of the complex, often obscure administrative and governance arrangements that have framed relationships between the Caribbean Overseas Territories of the UK in recent years. Relations between the governments of Anguilla, Bermuda, British Virgin Islands (BVI), Caymans, Montserrat, and Turks and Caicos and the UK government in London have not always been smooth. From the 1970s onwards, it was assumed in Whitehall and Westminster that these territories would become independent. This absent-minded assumption reinforced a set of fragmented, and remarkably personalised, ad hoc governance arrangements, at least to the late 1990s. Little sense of post-colonial purpose or shared vision animated relations between Overseas Countries and Territories (OCT) and UK governments. The 'bias for independence' has faded, however, as opposition to sovereignty being imposed was finally acknowledged by the New Labour government's White Paper of 1999. In 2009, the UK government even imposed direct rule on the Turks and Caicos Islands, following a corruption scandal that threatened the territory's economic and political future. We reflect on lessons of the past decade or so, contrasting UK-OCT governance arrangements to those in the comparable, yet also very distinct, neighbouring Dutch and French Caribbean territories. Overall, developments in governance arrangements indicate that whilst new 'contracts' are periodically forged between the UK and its Caribbean OCTs - something that appears to be true at EU-wide level also, for the Dutch and French Caribbean territories in their relations with the 'metropolis' - reform has been insufficient and incomplete.

title: Organization Structure and Sociometric Nominations Amongst Line Managers in Three Contrasted Organizations
authors: Payne, Roy L; Pheysey, Diana C
abstract: This study contrasts the interactions & influence choices among line managers in 3 org's. The 1st Co is the large mfg division (2,912 employees) of a structurally mechanistic org, with an 8-level hierarchy, the 2nd is much smaller (350 employees) & flatter (5 levels), & the last is also small (412 employees), but it has an 8-level hierarchy. The org's were selected because of their contrasting formal structures. The relations between the sociometric indicators & the various aspects of org structure are explored across diff sub-parts of the line manag systems. The overall results are that the effects of aspects of org structure on soc processes are generally in the directions predicted, though the relationships are not large; & that the efffects of one aspect of org structure can by moderated by other structural features. Global generalizations about the effects of, for instance, bur'cy on soc behavior are therefore inadvisable. Factors such as job level, ratio of workers to supervisors, ratio of staff to direct workers, & degree of stratification are all factors which may considerably modify the effects of those aspects of bur'ization which have been defined as structuring of activities & concentration of authority. Modified HA.

title: On the Will to Ignorance in Bureaucracy
abstract: Drawing on narrative interviews with psychiatrists and health analysts in Britain, the article provides an analysis of debates over the safety of SSRI antidepressants such as Prozac and Seroxat. The focus of the article is on what I describe, drawing on Foucault, Nietzsche, Niklas Luhmann and Michael Power, as a 'will to ignorance' within regulatory bureaucracies which works to circumvent a regulator's ability to carry out its explicit aims and goals. After a description of the regulatory processes that have influenced the efforts of patients and practitioners to reach conclusions on the risks and benefits of antidepressants, I conclude by suggesting that the article's analysis of the regulation of SSRIs carries theoretical insights for the study of regulation and bureaucracy in general. Adapted from the source document.

title: Governance in the Metropolitan Area of the Valley of Mexico
abstract: This paper analyzes the Metropolitan Area of the Valley of Mexico from different perspectives. It emphasizes the urbanization process & the metropolitan government's economic & social challenges. The physical process of urbanization shows an increment of undercapitalized squatter settlements & a clear trend of metropolitan sprawl & conurbation creating a so called "megalopolis" (a metropolis of metropolis). This urbanization is in a process of covering the whole central region of Mexico which comprises 6 states & 30+ million inhabitants (2000). Finally, we argue that the public administration & governance problem faced by the ZMVM is due to the lack of political will & understanding of the problem by both the government of the Federal District & the government of the State of Mexico. These states share half the metropolitan population & urban area. 6 Tables, 1 Map, 10 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Artificial Negativity and Affirmative Action in Universities
abstract: The process by which affirmative action (AA) programs have become extensions of the very bureaucracy that administrators & faculty are trying to control is examined. Arguments against the further bureaucratization of AA programs in Paul Piccone's "The Crisis of American Conservatism" (see SA 41:1/93Z5179) are critically assessed, & examples from the U of California's AA policies are drawn on to defend minority hiring policies & to vitiate Piccone's artificial negativity thesis. In Artificial Negativity as a Bureaucratic Tool? Reply to Roe, Piccone argues that, by analyzing the dynamics of bureaucracies in terms of an uncritically accepted leftist interpretation of AA policies, Roe offers an unconvincing defense of the bureaucratic mishandling of hiring policies that could never be effectively implemented.

title: Strategies of Control and Organizational Behavior
abstract: Relationships between org'al, work role, & behavioral variables are explored in a sample of 787 senior British managers working in 78 business org's. The model of admin'ive reduction of variance in behavior developed by J.H.K. Inkson, D. J. Hickson & D. S. Pugh ("Administrative Reduction of Variance in Organization and Behavior," unpublished paper given to the British Psychol'al Society, Annual Conference, Apr 1968) is used as the framework of analysis. The model postulates that 2 main strategies of admin'ive control, structuring of activities & centralization, will give rise to conforming behavior & low levels of conflict through their prescription of roles. Structuring of activities, however, is found to be associated with higher levels of conflict & hardly at all with conforming behavior, while centralization is associated with higher levels of conforming behavior, but not with conflict. In general the pattern of relationships between the variables located at diff levels of org'al analysis is more complex than previously envisaged. Modified HA.

title: From Modernisation to Big Society: Continuity and Change in Social Work in the United Kingdom
abstract: In this paper, I will explore developments in social work in the United Kingdom since the formation of the Conservative/ Liberal Democrat Coalition Government in May 2010. I will argue that the period since then has been characterised by elements both of continuity and change: continuity in that the neoliberal assumptions which underpinned New Labour's approach to social work continue to inform the approach of the Coalition; change, in that there is evidence of a more vigorous anti-statist rhetoric, reflected both in a critique of "bureaucracy" and also in the promotion of the Big Society as an all-embracing ideological framework. Against those who see the Big Society project as providing an opportunity for the emergence of a more progressive social work, I will argue that its primary rationale is to shift responsibility from the welfare state onto individuals and communities. The final part of the paper will explore some of the implications of the Big Society approach for social work and social care, through consideration of the policies of personalisation, localism and "open public services". Adapted from the source document.

title: "I usually try to play down the official character." Emotional labor in public administration as a dimension of the transformation of statehood
abstract: In an increasingly pluralized society the public administration and its traditional inherent values like rationality, objectivity and impersonality have lost part of their legitimacy. Most citizens no longer accept an authoritarian manner or an approach in which they are subjected to bureaucratic rules and regulations. The new emphasis on customer and service orientation, which emerged in the public administration with the New Public Management reform of the last three decades, reflects the rising importance of new sources of legitimacy like proximity to citizens and procedural justice. However, empirically based research rarely addresses the issue of how this shift of sources of legitimacy affects the daily work of civil servants. This article describes, drawing on qualitative data, how emotional labor is becoming an important resource for the interaction of state and citizens. Moreover, we will show how the forms of emotional labor vary according to the interpretations of statehood and the professional identities of the civil servants. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Control of Public Faces in a Commercial Bureaucratic Work Situation
abstract: Based on extensive field research on clerical workers in a large international bank, analysis is made of how standardized public faces in the workplace are an integral part of bureaucratic rationalization. The bank examined here standardizes its workers' external behavior & demeanor, both to convey a desirable commercial image to its customers & to facilitate harmonious relationships between workers & supervisors & among workers themselves. To some extent, workers' conformance to organizational demands is negotiable; for the most part, however, conformity is experienced as being imposed. As a result, most workers feel pressured to conform; when they do wear the public faces the organization fashions for them, they feel self-artificial. The overall meaning of these experiences for workers is, however, essentially ambiguous. Workers conform not only because they must, but because it is easier; they dissemble both to do their jobs & to get along in the office. Although they feel uneasy about themselves when they act in this way, they also see no alternatives to such behavior. AA.

title: Aspects of Tokugawa Bureaucracy and Modernization
abstract: The focus is on the rapid & effective modernization in Japan in the yrs following the Meiji Restoration of 1868. 3 recurring aspects are considered important in soc change: (1) increasing econ production of the society in question with attendant 'structural diff'iation'; (2) the need for rationalism, ie, a continuous search for more efficient ways of achieving practical & understood ends; & (3) centralized control & the reintegration of values. A modernizing bur'cy seeks to gear its activities toward these goals. This conceptual outline is applied to the Tokugawa bur'cy of late 19th cent Japan. It is found that for its adoption of modernizing policies on a nat'l scale, the Meiji gov could utilize the large-scale bur'cy which already existed. The rudimentary elements of both central & regional planning, a this-worldly orientation favoring change, certain types of rationalism, esp in adoption of innovations, & the peculiar aspects of segmental emulation were already present in this bur'cy. Widespread literacy & compliance to authority also helped Japan to modernize so effectively & so fast during this period. M. Maxfield.

title: Service Users and Personal Social Services in Israel: Are We Ready to Hear What Clients Want to Tell Us?
abstract: This article presents both the perspectives of social service clients (participants) living in poverty and dependent on Israel's personal social services and the participatory research method used in this study. Discussion topics were determined by the participants, who described their experiences with personal social services providers, their perceptions and attitudes towards personal social services, and their recommendations for improvements in service concept and delivery. The participants referred to the social services as institutional bodies, and defined inadequate versus "good enough" treatment. They discussed issues such as bureaucracy, procedures relating to material assistance and the combination of material and emotional assistance. This paper discusses the implications of the participatory research method and of the findings regarding social work with people living in poverty. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Public Politics and Processes of Emancipation: Impacts of the Economical Globalization in the Brazilian Reality
abstract: This work aims to contemplate the impacts of globalization in public policies un, in Brazil & to evaluate the possibilities of construction of emancipatory policies from the analysis of in ways to the participation of citizens in public spheres. The subjects focused in those spheres are social movements & other forms of the civilian society, for example the councils & participation forums. The basic assumption is that the participation not substitute the state agents, but to increase democratization & social control of the public administration. Among the conclusions of this study, stand out the facts that movements & other social agents are knowledge sources & their practices contain possibilities of social transformations & changes, even though the participative process needs direction changes to be qualified & to happen toward the emancipation of excluded social layers. For such, the nature of public policies also has to change, to become less compensatory or assistentialist & more developmentist, in the sense of qualified economical growth & social development of the Country, with job & income generation. References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Contingent Work and Gender: A Research on Local Administrations
abstract: Public administration represents a privileged context to investigate the gendered consequences of the diffusion of contract flexibility. A research on the use of lifetime & short-term contracts in local administrations in the province of Alessandria shows the presence of different gender profiles among "flexible" workers. For most men, short-term contracts are linked to leadership positions, or they represent a transition towards a stable job, as they do for part of the younger women. There is, instead, a great number of women who seem to be trapped in a row of badly qualified, very short & often part-time contracts, with long pauses in between; a highly precarious link with the workplace seems to be their longterm condition. 3 Tables, 31 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: A Comparison of Halpin and Croft's Organizational Climates and Likert and Likert's Organizational Systems
abstract: This study is concerned with the relationship between A. W. Halpin & D. R. Croft's org'al climates as classified by the Org'al Climate Description questionnaire ("The Organizational Climate of Schools," Final Report, mimeographed, to the US Office of Educ, Aug, 1962) & R. Likert's org'al systems as classified by the teacher form of the Profile of a School questionnaire (THE HUMAN ORGANIZATION: ITS MANAGEMENT AND VALUE, New York, NY: McGraw Hill, 1967). A sample of 43 Sch's participated in the study, all within a 200 mile radius of St Lawrence U, Canton, NY. The positively signif relationship found between these 2 instruments supports the concept that the 2 models from which these instruments were developed are comparable. Modified HA.

title: New Directions in Bureaucratic Change in Southeast Asia: Selected Experiences
abstract: In most newly emerging market-centered Southeast Asian countries, the directions of bureaucratic modernization have increasingly shifted toward the promarket objectives, roles, structures, norms, & beneficiaries of public bureaucracy. These new directions in bureaucratic change have certain critical implications for the overall bureaucracy in terms of its identity, commitment, & legitimacy. The aim here is to explain the major dimensions of this recent bureaucratic change, examine its critical implications for public bureaucracy, & offer some suggestions to redress such critical consequences. 49 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Is Bureaucracy Dysfunctional for Development?
abstract: The administration of development in India calls for high standards of group performance & intergroup collaboration, good management, a high degree of achievement motivation, & continuing organizational innovation to meet environmental change & internal needs. Bureaucracy has a crucial role in development both in the capitalist & socialist systems; it is suggested that the sociopsychological attitudes of the actors in development schemes be analyzed to determine their effect on bureaucratic management. The training methodologies need to be linked with the reflection & action research. There is a need to develop an alternative to the bureaucratic model, resolving some of its dysfunctional aspects. Modified AA

title: And the crooked shall be made straight: Public road administration and the decline of localism in the rural North, 1870-1930
abstract: The history of public road administration in the rural North between 1870 and 1930 is examined in an attempt to illustrate the emergence of an organizational society in the countryside.  While this new rural perspective was a significant departure from the older, more localistic culture, it continued to form a basis for opposition to urban and industrial society.

title: THE POLITICAL ROLE OF THE COMMONWEALTH BUREAUCRACY
abstract: Australia took over from the UK the concept of the bur'cy as an impartial tool, despite the fact that certain of the fundamental assumptions on which this was based-such as the separation between policy & admin-were demonstrably invalid. Australia early developed a service-oriented bur'cy, highly pol'al in its early yrs & often making essentially pol'al decisions in spite of technically incompetent rulers. 4 periods in the growth of the commonwealth bur'cy are considered, with an emphasis on the restraints of its pol'al activities. IPSA.

title: Bureaucracy and Development in the Sudan
abstract: An analysis of the role of bureaucracy in the socioeconomic & political development of Sudan. Five distinct eras in the political & administrative history of the country since 1954 are delineated, & it is shown that all development plans have failed to achieve their goals. Despite the fact that Sudanese public servants have good educations & relatively high functional capabilities, administrative ineffiency, obsolete structures, bureaucratic infighting, & lack of coordination have caused government policies to be poorly implemented & executed. Modified HA

title: Bureaucracies and Community Planning
abstract: Personal observations made while working in several Wash, DC agencies make possible an unusual opportunity to compare some sociological concepts & theories about bureaucracies with the realities of bureaucratic life. 4 propositions about public bureaucracies can be put forth. (1) They are usually pluralistically organized, rather than monolitic. (2) Because of diffusion of power, they have greater difficulty initiating collective action & bringing it to a successful conclusion than they do preventing such action. (3) Because of their difficulties in achieving collective action, public bureaucracies are almost incapable institutionally of solving the problems of communities. (4) Major modifications must be made in the way American public bureaucracies function if comprehensive solutions to community problems are to be implemented. This latter point will not be easily or readily accomplished. One useful long-term solution might be to combine the philosophy built into the Allied Services Act with revenue sharing--with the states & local governments determining how to implement federal priorities. Modified HA.

title: The transnational track: state sponsorship and Singapore's Oxbridge elite
abstract: This paper explores the process of transnational institutional matching between elite institutions in Singapore and Great Britain, and the role of state-sponsored scholarships in enabling this process as political and administrative elites are selected and groomed. Using data gathered from in-depth interviews conducted with Singaporean undergraduates studying at Oxbridge and a dataset of the institutional origins of 580 Singaporean government scholars, the analysis illustrates how students are being matched from two Singaporean junior colleges to Oxbridge and back to the higher strata of the Singaporean Public Service. We show that the educational trajectories of these government scholars need to be addressed in relation to the informational capital acquired in specific elite schools as well as the governing roles these individuals are meant to obtain within the state upon graduation.

title: Modes of Bureaucratic Communications: Examples from Thai Local Administration
abstract: Expanding upon 'formal-informal' distinctions, 4 modes of bureaucratic communications are defined. Communications within differing bureaucracies are compared using the 4 modes. The setting associated with each mode & its effectiveness in accomplishing various tasks are explored. Illustration & descriptions of the 4 modes are given from cases of Thai local administrative behavior. A cultural explanation is sought for the choice of each mode. In the Thai situation the status of the officials determines the preferred mode of communication whereas the particular tasks determines the effectiveness of communications. 4 Tables.

title: A Program Evaluation of Los Angeles ACORN's Welfare Case Advocacy
abstract: Bureaucratic confusion & client dissatisfaction since the 1996 changes in welfare policy opened opportunities for third party advocacy on behalf of welfare clients. This paper evaluates Los Angeles ACORN's case advocacy program for welfare clients. Outcomes analyzed include client satisfaction with ACORN's advocacy & effects of the program on welfare clients who later became ACORN members. Ninety-one percent of clients surveyed (N = 99) stated they were satisfied with the resolution of their welfare case complaint. Eighty-eight percent of respondents stated ACORN did a better job resolving their problem compared to the welfare department. Unique aspects of the program include peer advocacy & opportunities for welfare recipients to join ACORN & work on welfare policy changes among other issues. Tables, References. Adapted from the source document. COPIES ARE AVAILABLE FROM: HAWORTH DOCUMENT DELIVERY CENTER, The Haworth Press, Inc., 10 Alice Street, Binghamton, NY 13904-1580

title: The new American McCarthysim: Policing thought about the Middle East
abstract: September 11 ushered in a sustained campaign by the American Right and the Bush administration to delegitimise critical thought about the Middle East, Islam and the Arab world. The Middle East Studies Association (MESA) has borne much of the brunt of this campaign, some of it conducted by think-tanks with close links to Israel's ruling circles. Such attacks on MESA date back to 1967 and the Arab-Israeli war. The role of organisations such as ADL, AIPAC, AVOT and ACTA is examined, as is Campus-Watch and the attempt to introduce legislation in 2003 to place university-level Middle East studies under much closer government control (via HR 3077). [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Role Consensus and Supervision Involvement in Small Welfare Agencies
abstract: This study focuses on the supervisor-caseworker relationship in a comparative org'al study of Public Welfare offices. It was found that the greatest role consensus on close supervision between caseworkers & their supervisors was in offices where the role specialization of the supervisor's position was low, & where the supervisor's involvement with the caseworkers was high. In addition it was found that in offices where the supervisor's span-of-control was small, the supervisor's involvement was high, & where supervisor's involvement was high, the group cohesion among caseworkers was also high. The study is based on 8 Public Welfare offices containing 42 caseworkers & 8 supervisors. The variable of close supervision was based on a 3-item index; the variable of role specialization of the supervisor's role was a dichotomous variable based on whether the supervisor carried a caseload or not; the variables of supervisor's involvement with caseworkers & group cohesion were based on sociometric questions; & the span of control consisted of the number of caseworkers supervised by each supervisor. The data was analyzed using r & partial r techniques. AA.

title: Bureaucratic Privilege as an Issue in Chinese Politics
