abstract: Since the death of Mao Zedong & the Third Plenum of the Communist Party Central Committee in Dec 1978, social policy in China has followed a more open elitist direction, with decreased attention to class struggles, than in any period since 1949. One issue, however, that continues to command Party attention is the abuse of bureaucratic privilege associated with political postion. It is argued that class conflicts, particularly over distribution of the limitied material benefits in Chinese society, have escalated in the post-Mao period, most severely between the conservative bureaucrats led by Deng Xiaoping & a group of non-Party intellectuals, scientists, Ur entrepreneurs, & politically disenchanted youth. Though sharing a hostility toward Maoist radicalism, with its demobilizing reforms & purges during the Cultural Revolution, these factions differ on the problem of bureaucratic privilege & how best to remedy its abuses. These differences are detailed & related to changes in China's economic policies, which continue to foster class conflicts, though different from those under Mao. Modified HA

title: Doing Anthropology in Yucatan: Notes from a Mexican Periphery
abstract: Gabriela Vargas-Cetina and Steffan Igor Ayora-Diaz discuss center-periphery inequities within Mexican anthropology from their position at the Autonomous University of Yucatan. Beginning with a brief review of the long history of Mexican anthropology as a globalized tradition since its origins, they trace the development of national institutions as nodes of research and advanced training. With the establishment of branches throughout the country, the institutions of the separate states have been marginalized. The disparities in access to resources and influence, along with increasing bureaucratization and an exacerbated audit culture, are certainly not unique to the research and educational system of Mexico. Adapted from the source document.

title: Change in French Society: A Critical Analysis of Crozier's Bureaucratic Model
abstract: Michel Crozier's view of how organizational & social change occurs in France (The Bureaucratic Phenomenon, London: Tavistock Publications, 1964) is examined critically. Focus is on key concepts such as change, equality, & crisis. Clarification of these concepts & examination of certain logical differences involved in their use lead to the conclusion that the Crozierian account must be rejected. It is suggested that an examination of change that would take more account of the particularities of different policy arenas would be more appropriate & more capable of elucidating the true nature of obstacles of change in French society. HA.

title: CRIME CONTROL AND DUE PROCESS IN CONFIDENCE-BUILDING STRATEGIES: A Governmentality Perspective
abstract: This article employs a governmentality framework to make sense of approaches to building public confidence, based upon a performance management regime that includes the British Crime Survey and a range of communicative technologies intended to raise public confidence. Whilst there are two discursive threads running throughout that broadly correspond with models of crime control and due process, priority has been afforded at the level of governmental 'talk' to the crime control model. Reflecting upon the strengths and limitations of the governmentality framework, the article questions the likelihood of the crime control discourse being enacted in practice, as well as the appropriateness of such a policy emphasis. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Work colonies and South African historiography
abstract: The history of work colonies enables us to plot the shifting moral and intellectual centres of gravity in white South African society, from church to state; from compassion to bureaucracy; and from theology to sociology.

title: The Perceptions of the Personal and Professional Factors Influencing Social Workers in Saudi Hospitals: A Qualitative Analysis
abstract: The perceptions of 10 social workers regarding the personal and professional characteristics influencing their practice at Saudi hospitals were examined using semi-structured interviews. A qualitative analysis employing a thematic approach informed by grounded theory was undertaken and produced three broad interrelated themes: "skills upgrading," "departmental support," and "personal experience in the workplace," which subsequently informed the development of the overarching theme of "personal and professional factors." The discussion illustrates social work practitioners are inhibited from effectively performing their roles. These include: (a) Deficiencies related to job training and professional skills updating where there is a lack of efficient and accessible inservice training programs, especially in relation to practical issues. Further, these perceptions relate to a lack of long-term educational opportunities that impact on individual practitioner's currency of skills, techniques and pedagogy enabling/disenabling him/her to excel at his/her job, (b) Obvious bureaucracy within the controlling hierarchy and difficulty with the dissemination of information between the social workers were perceived to detrimentally impact on a practitioner's ability to attend to one's work demands, and (c) Personal day to day work experiences, including counterproductive emotional feelings (high stress), increased dissatisfaction with the job, and ineffective communication within the workplace were seen as limiting the social workers' professional potential. This article will focus on how these themes were addressed in terms of qualitative interview data. Adapted from the source document.

title: Making sense of common sense: examining the decision-making of politically appointed representatives in Swedish child protection
authors: Forkby, Torbjörn; Hojer, Staffan; Liljegren, Andreas
abstract: A distinguishing feature of Swedish child protection is the direct and indirect influence on decision-making in individual cases by representatives appointed by their elected political parties. As members of local committees, they take the most interventionist and costly decisions themselves, informed by care proposals submitted by professional social workers. Other decisions are delegated to professional social workers. In direct decision-making, they are supposed to act as laypersons using their own judgement and experience, not as politicians. The aim of this paper is to describe and analyse these committees, their role and responsibilities, and possible influence of politics on child protection. A mixed method was used, with a survey sent to 467 representatives, structured interviews with 99 secretaries of local committees and data drawn from national statistics. The Swedish model is discussed as a hybrid system influenced not only by professional, bureaucratic, political and market governance logics but also by laypersons. One conclusion is that although child protection is directly influenced by politics, the reverse is also true. By exposing politicians to the difficult life circumstances and societal shortcomings experienced by vulnerable children, the system can, in turn, have an impact on politics at the municipal level.

title: Mergers and Mobility: Organizational Growth and the Origins of Career Migration at Lloyds Bank
abstract: Though organizationally driven geographic mobility is a distinguishing feature of modern careers, accounts of its origin are murky. Drawing on various theories of organization, the authors show how a merger wave exposed competing institutional logics & triggered the elaboration of the modern, mobile, bureaucratic career. Using organizational data & employment records, the authors model the association between organizational merger & the introduction of career-migration among employees at Lloyds Bank over a 45-year period. The pattern of mobility they find suggests that agency problems associated with the loyalties of newly acquired workers dominated early experiments with lateral transfers. As the merger wave matured, geographic mobility became a general feature of all bank workers' careers. The implications of this pattern of mobility for organizations, career structures, & stratification systems more generally are examined. Tables, Figures, References. Adapted from the source document.

title: THE STRUCTURE OF SMALL BUREAUCRACIES
authors: Blau, Peter M; Heydebrand, Wolf V; Stauffer, Robert E
abstract: An analysis of bur'tic structure is based on data from 156 Amer public personnel agencies. Whereas a professional staff was expected to reduce the need for many managers, the opposite is actually the case. Lack of professionalization tends to lead to the centralization of official authority in the hands of relatively few managers. The DofL, which typically accompanies growing size, promotes centralization of authority structure is well suited for the coordination of tasks diff'iated into simple routines but not for that of professional specialties. Structural complexities destroy the econ advantage that operating on a comparatively large scale otherwise has, but bur'tic mechanisms of COMM, such as a sufficient admin'ive staff, restore this advantage. HA.

title: Ethnic Identity Entrepreneurs: Their Role in Transracial and Intercountry Adoptions
abstract: Three attributes characterize ethnic identity entrepreneurs. First, ethnic identity entrepreneurs appeal to an essentialized image of identity in which ethnicity 'trumps' all other bases of affiliation and authenticity. Second, ethnic identity entrepreneurs invoke this essentialized identity and group membership to justify a claim to, or, monopolization of, scarce resources and entitlements by way of a process of social closure. Third, the activities of ethnic identity entrepreneurs which are often initially motivated by the desire to open up options and to facilitate choice among members, induce conformity and functions as a mechanism of social control. In this paper I emphasize a particular subset of ethnic identity entrepreneurs, namely, those who represent subordinate/minority groups and who work in bureaucracies -whether governmental or community based- and who have acquired a very extensive power by virtue of their office and their professional expertise, which enables them to construct and enforce their specific conceptions of what ethnic identity is and the cultural requirements this essentialized identity entails. Illustrative of these processes is the role of the social worker ethnic identity entrepreneur in formulating policies inhibiting both domestic transracial and transnational adoption which more and more frequently is involving moving children without parents or a permanent home from the Asian Pacific region to families in the United States or Britain.

title: Environmental Policy Making: From Party Competition to Bureaucratic Politics?
abstract: In this article we argue that institutionalization beginning in the 1970s has moved the most important arena for interest articulation in environmental policy away from parliament to the bureaucracy. We argue that this process can be explained by what we refer to as the sector hypothesis, which contends that institutionalization leads to the development of sectorized, institutionalized interests & patterns of cooperation with environmental interests, resulting in a higher level of conflict within bureaucracy. The "sector hypothesis" is contrasted with the "convergence hypothesis," which argues that conflicts diminish over time as a result of institutionalization. We support our argument with brief presentations of three cases & surveys carried out in 1976, 1986, & 1996 in the central administration in Norway. The article concludes that the institutionalization of environmental policy has resulted in the development of a strong sector identity & articulation of environmental interests in the Ministry of the Environment. This institutional strengthening, however, has not resulted in a stronger power base for this Ministry vis-a-vis other parts of the bureaucracy. 5 Tables, 41 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Battle of the Ms: The MBA, MPA, MPH, and MSW
abstract: An exploration of the curricular innovations that are offered in graduate study for degrees in business administration, public administration, public health, & social work. Some projections are offered as to how graduate social work education might be altered for administration students so they would be able to strengthen their competitive edge in the job marketplace & provide more effective & efficient service to clients. 4 Figures, 27 References. HA

title: Administrative Offices of Aging in State Bureaucracies: Agency Location and Organization Effectiveness
abstract: Examined here are the effects of state-level reorganization on the organizational access of Aging Units to governors & state legislatures, their ability to coordinate service delivery, their access to budgetary funds & resources, & their visibility & prestige. Data were obtained from 46 of the 50 existing Aging Units. Conclusions suggest that reorganizing an Aging Unit does have an impact on these aspects of its operation. 4 Tables, 24 References. Modified HA

title: On Being Let Loose in the Field: The Execution of Professional Ethics
abstract: In recent years concerns over litigation and the trend towards close monitoring of academic activity has seen the effective hijacking of research ethics by university managers and bureaucrats. This can effectively curtail cutting edge research as perceived 'safe' research strategies are encouraged. However, ethics is about more than research governance. Ultimately, it seeks to avoid harm and to increase benefits to society. Rural development debate is fairly quiet on the question of ethics, leaving guidance to professional bodies. This study draws on empirical research that examined the lives of migrant communities in Northern Ireland. This context of increasingly diverse rural development actors provides a backdrop for the way in which the researcher navigates through ethical issues as they unfold in the field. The analysis seeks to relocate ethics from being an annoying bureaucratic requirement to one where it is inherent to rigorous and professional research and practice. It reveals how attention to professional ethics can contribute to effective, situated and reflexive practice, thus transforming ethics to become an asset to professional researchers.   [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Care and Feeding of Defender Organizations
abstract: A review essay on a book by Lisa J. McIntyre, The Public Defender: The Practice of Law in the Shadows of Disrepute (Chicago: U of Chicago Press, 1987 [see listing in IRPS No. 49]). McIntyre's book is a sociological study of the 400-member Cook County (Illinois) Public Defenders Office, in historical context, based on interviews with & observations of public defenders. Administrative failures such as political hiring & poor supervision are well documented & are argued to stem from lack of attention by the public & by the courts. However, McIntyre does not directly address the possible effects of a more formal structure on client services & staff motivation. It is concluded that McIntyre is too pessimistic about the possibility of a well-administered public defenders office. A. Waters

title: Discourses on Modernization in the Employment Public Services: Towards a New Form of Governance?
authors: Fernandez Rodriguez, Carlos Jesus; Martin Martin, Maria Paz
abstract: The 'crisis of the social issue' in the EU has led to a certain consensus in the need to renew the organizational and institutional model of public administration. The core of the reform implies important administrative changes in most of the European welfare states. Those changes are inspired on theories such as the new public management, management by objectives or partnership. Such changes involve both semantic ('sharing responsibilities', 'effective costs', or the substitution of 'citizen under an administration' by 'consumer') and political (predominance of scattered forms of power and the individualization of responsibilities) transformations which operate in the framework of individuals and State relations. The paradigms of activation and flexicurity have been central in this public administration modernization project. This commitment with new forms of governance of social issues has important consequences for the political and moral foundations of social cohesion, and the Spanish case is not an exception. This paper aims at looking at those representations of 'modernization' (as they appear in debates about the employment services restructuring policies) in detail as well as providing references to the trajectory of such reforms of public services since the early eighties to the beginning of the crisis. Adapted from the source document.

title: Public Administration and community: how new electronic information can help a better understanding
abstract: The Albanian challenges have been insistent not just for domestic researchers, academics, or even Albanian citizens; they pique a lot of people in different geographic positions, first of all, the European ones. This brings a great necessity to watch those evolutions, processes and the impact they have in the Albanian social tissue. At the same time, it is important to understand what streamline has been followed till now by micro and macro processes. There is no sustainable change or improvement, if it is not built at the cellular level, and when we talk about the state, institutions and citizens, the way they relate, if it is standardized or not by laws or procedures, it becomes the most important reading that we must do to understand the substratum of those changes. Relations, communications and the future of the communicative situations between citizens and public operators indicate the quality and sustainability of Albanian evolutions in social view, as well as the forecasting we can do regarding their impact in the future. To increase complexity, we can add another variable to the communication's analyses in the public service, which represents an important evolution of Albania in this context, the wide introduction of the Technologies of Information and Communication (TIC) in the biggest part of public service provision. This makes us investigate about effects and impacts they have had during the service delivery. Adapted from the source document.

title: CURRENT SOVIET THINKING ON BUREAUCRACY
abstract: Current Soviet thinking on bur'cy still comprises elements of pragmatism & retardation, re real soc processes. It is concerned with the more or less peripheral & secondary sectors of SP life. Nevertheless, SP practice, ie, the measures & methods of combating bur'cy, demonstrate more boldness in the transformation of old instit's & relationships. There is greater & greater deviation from the positions assumed under Stalin. Tr from IPSA by J. Atkins.

title: THE BUREAUCRACY AND THE NAZI PARTY
abstract: 3 related problems are treated: (1) The historical: how successful was Hitler's party in eliminating the bur'cy as a counterforce & centralizing authority in Berlin? (2) The theoretical: which instit proved itself the more resilient & viable? (3) The moral: should a member of an org, the bur'crat, withdraw from the org to oppose policies which he finds improper, or hope to divert policy by remaining within? IPSA.

title: African American Students' Experiences with Special Education in Milwaukee Public Schools
authors: Obiakor, Festus; Beachum, Floyd D; Harris, Mateba K
abstract: Problems facing African American students with special needs are numerous and complex. Although processes and procedures are essentially in place to properly serve these students, far too many become ensnared in webs of bureaucracy and benign neglect. This article examines African American students' experiences with special education in Milwaukee Public Schools. In addition, it provides recommendations for those teachers and administrators willing to deconstruct the negative impact of these stark inadequacies. Adapted from the source document.

title: Suing for Justice
abstract: The scope of compensation avialable to the individual through legal claims against bureaucratic errors is discussed in an attempt to enlighten the average British citizen concerning his rights. The effects of the Crown Proceedings Act, 1947, & the Highways Act, 1961, on these rights are described. Three House of Lords cases that have extended possiblities for negligence claims against government are discussed: (1) the Dorset Yacht Co. vs. Home Office (1970) case, (2) the Hedley Byrne case, & (3) the Anns vs. Merton London Borough Council case. The investigations of complaints made by the Parliamentary Commissioner in recent years are examined. Various complaints were against officials in the Dept of Health & Social Security, or were a result of situations created by the Chronically Sick & Disabled Persons Act, 1970. Many cases reveal situations where "citizens have gone uncompensated for losses wrongfully inflicted on them by central government which ... would stand a reasonable prospect of success in the courts." G. Simpson.

title: Indian Bureaucracy in the Post-Independence Period
abstract: Covers the history of Indian Bureaucracy beginning with the mythological period of elite-controlled administration, through the Mogul occupation, and in to the British colonialist rule, showing how each successive power made its own impression upon what would become modern Indian administration. The colonialist period is expanded upon with much detail showing the great social and economic prestige that an Indian could expect if he worked in the administrative field, while the Indian bureaucratic system itself was lauded around the world. When this system was entirely turned over to the Indians, a rigid, authoritarian government became necessary given the socio-economic milieu of the time and those in charge of administering the government for the first time in memory had to relinquish their power to the politicos. With this and other factors came drastic changes ameliorating the entire economic scene, along with health and educational standards, all of which rose. Alas, the bureaucracy eventually gave way to incompetence and a lack of proper training, along with bureaucracy for its own sake, which began to weigh down the functionality of the entire system. Reminds the reader of the ideas of Max Weber on bureaucracy as well as commentators on Weber's ideas, oft in direct relation to India's administration structure. Looks at corruption, power, reduction in government, and economic liberalization and where Indian administration may be headed in the future. S. Fullmer

title: Under What Conditions Does Caseworker-Caregiver Racial/Ethnic Similarity Matter for Housing Service Provision? An Application of Representative Bureaucracy Theory
authors: McBeath, Bowen; Chuang, Emmeline; Bunger, Alicia; Blakeslee, Jennifer
abstract: In this article, we examine child welfare caseworkers' housing-related service strategies when they serve culturally similar versus culturally dissimilar clients. Testing hypotheses drawn from representative bureaucracy theory and using data from the second cohort of the National Survey of Child and Adolescent Well-Being, we find that when non-Caucasian caseworkers share the same racial/ethnic background as caregivers, caseworkers use more active strategies to connect caregivers to needed housing services. The relationship between racial/ethnic matching and frontline workers' repertoire of service strategies is most pronounced when the need for housing has been registered formally via referrals and case plans and thus legitimated institutionally. These results reinforce basic tenets of representative bureaucracy theory and provide evidence of the benefits of racial and ethnic diversity in the human service workforce. Our findings also highlight the need for research identifying institutional and frontline organizational factors that enhance the quality of service provision. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Beyond Hierarchies and Markets: Are Decentralized Schools Lifting Poor Children?
abstract: The state has experimented with a range of decentralized school organizations over the past half century, in part aiming to lift poor children. This movement stems from not only neoliberal ideology but also from the earlier "Third Way" of advancing public projects--severing local organizing from the state's bureaucratic rules, while stopping short of atomized market remedies. This article first examines the economic and institutional forces that drive civic activists to advance decentralizing remedies, especially the spread of non-government organizations (NGOs) and client choice in the education sector. We then detail the uneven empirical benefits of three decentralizing segments of the education sector: preschools, parental vouchers, and charter schools. Finally we move beneath surface-level governance changes to highlight how particular social relations found inside decentralized organizations at times do yield discernible, even sizable, benefits. Comparative cases reveal a second generation of decentralists, who build from the lessons of their policy ancestors. Second-wave decentralists are keenly focused on a social architecture that motivates poor children and educators. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: IS THERE A UNIVERSAL MODEL OF ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURES?
abstract: THE LIMITATIONS OF EMPIRICAL STUDIES OF ORGANIZATIONS ARE DEMONSTRATED. M. WEBER & EVEN F. W. TAYLOR BOTH CONSIDERED THEIR THEORIES OF ORGANIZATION AS UNIVERSAL. EMPIRICAL INVESTIGATIONS OF THE 1960'S SUPPOSEDLY DESTROYED THE UNITARY CHARACTER OF THE WEBERIAN IDEAL-TYPE OF BUREAUCRACY, WHICH WAS SHOWN TO TAKE DIFFERENT FORMS IN DIFFERENT CONTEXTS. HOWEVER, IT HAS ALSO BEEN SHOWN THAT THE LARGER AN ORGANIZATION IS, THE MORE ITS BUREAUCRACY COMES TO RESEMBLE THE IDEAL WEBERIAN TYPE; COMPLEXITY & CERTAIN TYPES OF INDUSTRY CAN ALSO HAVE THE SAME EFFECT AS SIZE. COMPARATIVE STUDIES HAVE SHOWN THAT BUREAUCRATIC POLYMORPHISM WAS CAUSED BY THE SOCIOCULTURAL ENVIRONMENT OF THE US, & THAT EVEN THOUGH THE DEGREE OF BUREAUCRATIC COMPLEXITY VARIES FROM COUNTRY TO COUNTRY, SIZE INFLUENCES IT IN THE SAME WAY IN EACH COUNTRY. ALL THESE EMPIRICAL STUDIES DEALT PRIMARILY WITH VARIABLES MEASURING THE DEGREE OF STRUCTURALIZATION OF ACTIVITIES & OF THE CONCENTRATION OF AUTHORITY--THEY ARE LIMITED ANALYSES OF ORGANIZATIONS. THE CONFIGURATION VARIABLES ARE LIMITED TO THE FORM OF THE ORGANIZATION. EXPLANATIONS ARE LIMITED TO THE DIRECT INFLUENCE OF EACH CONTEXTUAL FACTOR, TAKEN IN ISOLATION, ON STRUCTURAL VARIABLES. THE RELATIONS AMONG STRUCTURAL & CONTEXTUAL VARIABLES THEMSELVES ARE NOT TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT. A STUDY OF SALARY HIERARCHIES OF COMPARABLE FRENCH & GERMAN ENTERPRISES (J. P. DAUBIGNEY & J. J. SILVESTRE, "COMPARAISON DE LA HIERARCHIE DES SALAIRES ENTRE L'ALLEMAGNE ET LA FRANCE" COMPARISON OF SALARY HIERARCHIES IN GERMANY AND FRANCE , AIX-EN-PROVENCE, FRANCE: LABORATOIRE D'ECONOMIE ET DE SOCIOLOGIE DU TRAVAIL, 1972) REVEALS THE EXISTENCE OF 2 NATIONAL TYPES OF SALARY HIERARCHY, WHICH CAN BE EXPLAINED NOT ONLY IN RELATION TO INTERNAL STRUCTURAL VARIABLES, BUT IN RELATION TO EXTERNAL FACTORS PARTICULAR TO EACH OF THE COUNTRIES; IT DEALS WITH THE 'SOCIAL EFFECT' ON ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE. SOCIETAL VARIABLES SUCH AS LEVEL OF QUALIFICATION, SPECIALIZATION, CONTENT OF PROFESSIONAL FUNCTIONS, THE EDUCATIONAL SYSTEM, & THE SYSTEM OF PROFESSIONAL RELATIONS, ALL NEED TO BE TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT IN THE SOCIOLOGY OF ORGANIZATIONS. D. BURKENROAD.

title: 1984: Are We There?
abstract: It is possible to find a great deal of evidence in the current state of society both for & against the proposition that the US is now approaching the condition described in George Orwell's 1984. The evidence of the past thirty years casts doubt on the permanence of totalitarian regimes, & shows the necessity of charismatic leadership to preserve such regimes. The successors of Joseph Stalin & Mao Tse-tung continue to maintain authoritarian governments, but in the form of bureaucracies that no longer practice systematic terror. Orwell himself criticized the worship of power for its own sake, but his imagination has apocalyptic tendencies that support such worship; in particular, he feared the destruction of the autonomous individual. This destruction appears possible, but can perhaps be brought about as effectively through consumerism & permissiveness as through regimentation & autocracy. W. H. Stoddard

title: 'Street-Level' Bureaucracy and Political Support: Some Findings on Mexican Americans
abstract: Failure of Mexican Americans to integrate & attach themselves to United States political & social life is often attributed to bad personal experiences with political authorities. Levels of contact & satisfaction with several government agencies (immigration, police, education, employment, school, legal aid, welfare, hospitals, & courts) are correlated with measures of political participation, political efficacy, representativeness of different levels of government, & impact at different levels of living conditions among a sample of 149 Mexican Americans in Omaha, Neb, during the spring of 1973. Little evidence for support of the proposition is found. While contact with public authorities is low, satisfaction is high among the sample. Satisfaction is not, however, correlated with the different dimensions of support. 5 Tables. Modified HA.

title: Improving Quality of Life for Seniors: New Governance Tools
authors: Uryan, Yildirim; Matusitz, Jonathan; Breen, Gerald-Mark
abstract: This analysis examines new governance tools that can be applied to security issues among the aging population in the United States, particularly in Central Florida. The authors explain the problem about the structure of law enforcement agencies today. Traditional bureaucratic organizations have a hierarchical and centrally structured system, which operates with strict rules and regulations. The authors proceed to compare two models of governance: the traditional bureaucratic government and the new model governance. The latter is better in that it uses indirect methods and innovative tools. These tools are (1) grants, (2) needs assessments, (3) senior volunteers, (4) co-production, and (5) citizen participation. Adapted from the source document.

title: A Circuitous Path to Macrostructural Theory
abstract: A personal memoir of the sociologist's academic career & development of macrostructural theory. The tutelage of Robert K. Merton & Paul S. Lazarsfeld shifted his orientation to research-grounded systematic theory & set the groundwork for subsequent work on a Weberian perspective of the bureacracy, exchange theory, & a nationwide study of occupational achievement & mobility. In the latter pursuit, he was introduced & later became a convert to regression analysis. The subsequent decade produced quantitative study of various formal organizations & development of a limited organizational theory. A formal macrostructural theory of population structure's influences on intergroup relations was developed in response to organizational theory's limitations. The impact of impersonal social structure on the academic career is discussed. 29 References. D. Generoli

title: An Ontological Turn in the Debate on Buen Vivir - Sumak Kawsay in Ecuador: Ideology, Knowledge, and the Common
authors: Alonso González, Pablo; Vázquez, Alfredo Macías
abstract: Buen Vivir, a political paradigm at work in Bolivia and Ecuador that underpins the state and social regeneration after a prolonged and devastating period of neoliberalism, has become a hotly contested subject within academia and politics. Although it has been categorized as decolonial, post-neoliberal, and post-developmentalist, recent developments suggest that the Ecuadorian government is turning toward a highly extractivist and modernist model based on bureaucratic and technocratic logics. This article focuses on the debate spurred around Buen Vivir, arguing that it has been employed as a cultural representation by many academics, politicians, and social agents, thus foreclosing the possibility of engaging in more grounded and pragmatic discussions and hindering the articulation of alternative political configurations. Accordingly, it seeks to shift the debate from epistemological questions about the conditions of knowledge to thinking the nature of the world ontologically from the perspective of Buen Vivir.

title: The presence of science in Thomas Pynchon's Gravity's Rainbow
abstract: The essay describes the sociological and epistemological aspects of the presence of science in Thomas Pynchon's Gravity's rainbow, wherein the theme serves as a link to contemporary history, also having implications on the plot and on its narrative construction. A dialogue with Weber helps detect the critical component of Pynchon's approach to science, while a dialogue with contemporary epistemology locates his skepticism towards the idealization of scientific rationality and of its ordinary practice. The interconnection of the three items that compose the exposition -- "causality": "bureaucracy" and "idea" -- places science as a background for the analysis of Gravity's rainbow's understanding of the world contemporary to its release in 1973. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Use of the Code of Conduct as a Tool for Promoting Good Governance at the University of Fort Hare, South Africa
authors: Ibrahim, Seriki Idowu; Ewere, Agholor Deborah; Adu, Emmanuel O
abstract: There has been an outcry from the civil society, media and public, in conjunction with a growing demand that the provincial government of Eastern Cape Province should prevent the delusion about code of conduct by the employees from becoming an all-consuming problem. Hence, the study assesses the impact of the code of conduct on promoting good governance at the University in the Eastern Cape Province in South Africa. The study adopts a descriptive survey research design. The simple random sampling technique was used to select ninety respondents. The experts in the faculty of Business Management and Administration validated the instrument, and Cronbach's alpha was used to measure its reliability. A little above eighty-two percent of the respondents agree that the code of conduct promoted good governance and 17.7 percent were uncertain. The results showed that the seventy-six percent of the respondents were aware and used the code of conduct. In conclusion, there are some areas, which have to be improved in order for the code of conduct to yield the results, which it was intended for

title: The Dialectics of Perfection, Acceleration, and Restructuring of the Development of Contemporary Soviet Society
abstract: (The conclusion of a previously published discussion [see SA 35:5/87R9790]). Current efforts to restructure the Soviet economy are viewed as revolutionary changes leading to qualitative transformations in many areas of social development. Methods for achieving the maximum utilization of the potential & advantages of socialism are discussed. One key component in the historical dialectics of socialism is the constant struggle against bureaucracy. The perfection of socialist management combined with the acceleration of scientific-technical progress & the fruits of restructuring will help realize the full potentials of socialism. G. Prostakov

title: Judgments About Work
authors: Johnson, Monica Kirkpatrick; Mortimer, Jeylan T; Lee, Jennifer C; Stern, Michael J
abstract: The authors examine the measurement structure of individuals' orientations toward work rewards, or 'judgments about work,' a concept central to the social psychology of work. Despite extensive and sustained interest in the level of importance attached to work rewards by major markers of social location such as birth cohort, social class origins, and gender, prior studies have not examined whether the same classification schema captures the underlying variation in judgments about work across these axes of social location. Drawing on five data sets, the authors examine the fit of models corresponding to the recently revived entrepreneurial-bureaucratic classification schema with those corresponding to the dominant extrinsic-intrinsic classification schema across subgroups of the population using confirmatory factor analysis. Findings offer only limited support for reconceptualizing judgments about work along entrepreneurial-bureaucratic dimensions but call for additional research on the dimensions of judgments about work that emerge under distinct conditions and across different groups. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Inc., copyright 2007.]

title: What Is Bureaucracy?
abstract: The theory of state is analyzed through its development in the writings of 3 theorists: (1) the later writings of Marx with their emphasis on historical theory, (2) the STATE AND REVOLUTION by Lenin (no publishing information available) which closely follows Marxian principles, & (3) Trotskyist ideas of social democracy & labor aristocracy. The concept of bureaucracy in modern society is examined with reference to M. Weber's analysis of commonalities among bureaucracies, & his typification of bureaucracy based on his theory of the general nature of bureaucracy. The definitions advanced by Weber are supplemented with the ideas of other theorists such as A. Touraine, & M. Crozier. 3 examples mentioned by Weber are presented to illustrate aspects of bureaucracy. Difficulties inherent in the writing of a formal definition of bureaucracy are described; they are manifest in the imprecision & ambiguity which exists (in current literature) concerning the phenomena. Some conclusions are drawn pertaining to the bureaucrat in his functionings in the areas of administration, hierarchal power relations, exploitative SR, sphere of addressed, & principles for the guidance of discussions of bureaucracy are outlined. The described text is related to present day situations & modes of thought. C. Grindle.

title: Decision making and social work: Another look
abstract: Leadership decision making among social workers in the health care field is discussed in an editorial.  Decision making models include the rational model, the bureaucratic model and the political model.

title: United States -- America's Right Turn: From Nixon to Bush by William C. Berman / Presidency by Plebiscite: The Reagan-Bush Era in Institutional Perspective by Craig A. Rimmerman / Thatcher, Reagan, Mulroney by Donald J. Savoie
abstract: Review.

title: The Research Imperative and Bureaucratic Control: The Case of Clinical Research
abstract: The development of research ethics committees & some value & role conflicts that surround medical research are examined, focusing on medical research on children as one case that raises concerns about consent & risk/benefit analysis. Analysis of mail questionnaire data from 174 research ethics committees in GB illustrates their variety of structure & functioning. Their current practice is related to a model of bureaucratic control, considering bureaucracy both in its common-sense understanding of officious rule making & delay, & in its theoretical formulation in terms of specialization, standardization, formalization, & centralization of procedures. It is argued that the concept of bureaucracy can illuminate the problems of control over research, as well as provide a model for more informed, consistent, & open decision making. 2 Tables, 6 Figures. Adapted from the source document.

title: 'The Land that Time Forgot': Reforming Access to Social Housing in England
abstract: Despite a long period of public management reform in social housing, including shifts from state to non-profit providers & exit opportunities for tenants, access to new tenancies has until very recently continued to be mediated by bureaucratic rationing approaches. This article explores the reasons for the long dominance of rationing, & the factors that are now leading to its replacement with more consumerist approaches known as 'choice-based lettings.' Chaos & complexity theory are used to explore the role of market factors & changes in understanding in destabilising an entrenched initial attractor pattern, & the role of local experiment, policy transfer & new political agendas in establishing a new attractor pattern. 5 Tables, 2 Figures, 64 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Schengen Visa Application: Individual Experiences
abstract: Presents individual interviews recounting experiences with the Schengen visa procedure, demonstrating unwillingness on the part of European consular powers to be cooperative & helpful in the justification of their refusal of visas for applicants of non-exempt states. It is a commonplace experience for those making appeals to European consulates to encounter either unprofessional case management or administrative complications that seemingly have no justification. Individuals often remain for extensive amounts of time without replies to their requests for information concerning their own application case, & when insisting on their rights are sometimes shown a reception inconsistent with expected professional norms on behalf of the consulate. 3 References. C. Brunski

title: Presence of Government's Role in Rural Grass-Roots Public Management
abstract: The Performance of rural governance hinges on the political & social factors & their mechanism between interaction, all of which are manifested in two different public spaces: The first space is structured upon social units & aims to maintain & develop. Being intrinsic, it is self-motivated & is driven by social capital & public space; The second space is structured upon state authority & aims to exercise control over grass-roots political life. Being external, it reflects political order & is driven by political recognition & institutionalization. The two spaces, though different in function & position, are not necessarily opposed to each other. The practical way for rural grassroots political development in present China lies in the unity of the two spaces, thus achieving the unity of state guidance & social motivation. References. Adapted from the source document.

title: A Test of the Political Control of Bureaucracies Under Asymmetric Information
abstract: How does the informational role of interest groups interact with institutions when politicians seek to control the bureaucracy? In 1992, Banks and Weingast argued that bureaucrats hold an informational advantage vis-a-vis political principals concerning policy-relevant variables, and that when it is prohibitively costly to audit, the agency may over- or understate the extent of a public problem. This is less likely to happen if there is a low-cost monitoring technology and if interest groups can monitor the agency's choices. I test this hypothesis using data on bureaucratic statements that estimate the importance of a number of hazardous waste problems from a group of state-level environmental agencies. The results provide evidence for the Banks-Weingast hypothesis. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Should the nurse change the light globe?: Human service professionals managing risk on the frontline
authors: Sawyer, Anne-Maree; Green, David; Moran, Anthony; Brett, Judith
abstract: Over the last two decades New Public Management, de-institutionalization and the growth of community care have radically altered the landscape of human service delivery in Australia. As a consequence of these changes, human service agencies have been compelled to develop mechanisms for regulating and managing the risks involved in frontline community care -- and the management of risk is now pivotal to the practices of professional workers in this field. British research suggests that the emphasis on risk gives rise to greater monitoring and administrative supervision of workers and a focus on managerial rather than therapeutic skills. This article presents some early findings from an Australian study that finds a very different picture. Based on interviews with 24 social workers and nurses employed in community care, we found that these workers expressed a strong sense of agency when interpreting and negotiating the risk management policies of their respective organizations, and were focused primarily on the needs of their clients rather than bureaucratic procedures. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright The Australian Sociological Association.]

title: Power, class, and gender -- Local Merchants and the Chinese Bureaucracy, 1750-1950 by Susan Mann / Sisters and Strangers: Women in the Shanghai Cotton Mills, 1919-1949 by Emily Honig / The Workers of Tianjin, 1900-1949 by Gail Hershatter
abstract: Review.

title: The Spirit of the State. Genesis and Structure of the Bureaucratic Field
abstract: To think about the state is to take part in an exchange in which the acceptable categories of thought have already been defined by the state. The thinker often remains unaware of the state's most fundamental power: to produce & impose, notably through the schools, the categories of thought that are then applied to the analysis of the world at large & of the state itself. The state has such power to define the legitimate usages of economic, informational, physical, & symbolic capital to the extent that its role simply seems natural & its ideas universal. Sociological vision, however, ought not ignore the gap between the construction of official norms & the reality of administrative practices. M. Maguire

title: Social Welfare Interest Groups: An Underutilized Resource
abstract: Examined is the need for increased political activity by the professional social work community to enhance its status & to promote the growth of social welfare institutions required by its clientele. An attempt is made to bare the relationship between social welfare bureaucracies & the political system. A study of 19 interest groups in New York City was made between 1968 & 1972. The organizations could be categorized as civic, educational, civil rights, ethnic, religious, or economic. Four issues of broad educational & social concern were selected, & each group's action concerning the issues was analyzed. All groups emit a stronger response to economic than to educational or civil rights issues. Internal conflict over an issue severely limits an organization's ability to respond to it. Available resources have little impact on a group's decision to become involved in an issue. Degree of activity is determined by whether a group is a single- or multipurpose organization & whether it is for or against an issue. The choice of issues is determined by the organization's "operating style & its desire not to break with traditional roles$...." Social workers, as an interest group, could be more effective in advancing the goals of their profession if they better understood the political process required to do so. Appendixes. Modified HA.

title: Bureaucratization and Social Control: Historical Foundations of International Police Cooperation
abstract: I employ a theoretical framework developed on the basis of the writings of Max Weber to analyze historical developments in the formation of international police organizations. I rely on a comparative analysis of selected cases of international police networks & centrally focus on the most famous & enduring of such structures, the International Criminal Police Commission, the forerunner of the organization since 1946 known as "Interpol." Using a Weberian perspective of bureaucratization, I maintain that the formation of international police organizations was historically made possible when public police institutions were sufficiently detached from the political centers of their respective states to function autonomously as expert bureaucracies. Under such circumstances of institutional autonomy, police bureaucracies fostered practices of collaboration across the borders of their respective national jurisdiction because & when they were motivated by a professionally defined interest in the fight against international crime. In conclusion to this analysis, I argue for the value of sociological perspectives of social control that are not reductionist, but that instead bring out the specific socially & sociologically significant dimensions of control mechanisms. 103 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: THE STRUCTURE OF MODERN SOCIETY AND BUREAUCRACY
abstract: Modern society, from an historical & structural point of view, (1) may be characterized by capitalism (on its econ basis), (2) may be classed as mass society, & (3) may be described as class society. The works of M. Weber, W. Sombart, J. A. Hobson, G. Wallas, E. Fromm. K. Mannheim, K. Marx, R. Michels, R. Merton, A. W. Gouldner, P. M. Blau, R. Benedix, P. Selznick, N. Lenin, S. Tanaka, T. Gomamoto are discussed. Modern bur'cy leads to alienation of man, & makes him an impersonality, a man not able to stand by himself. The demerits of bur'cy must be considered. Modified AA.

title: Reducing Bureaucratic Inflexibility
abstract: It is generally agreed that public welfare organizations are bureaucratic. The literature dealing with bureaucratic phenomena is examined; the relevant variables are identified & hypotheses developed. The hypotheses were tested in eighteen public welfare agencies; the findings challenge the idea that large organizations are necessarily bureaucratic, suggesting that the size of an organization is not directly related to bureaucratic inflexibility, & that large organizations may reduce bureaucratic inflexibility by promoting more professionalization, higher specialization, & reduction of centralization. 4 Tables, 1 Figure. Modified HA.

title: School Bureaucratic Structure, Locus of Control and Alienation among Primary Schoolteachers
abstract: To test the hypothesis that teachers' alienation from both work & expressive relations will vary directly with the degree of centralization of the school & of formalization of school organization, data were obtained from 529 teachers in 31 Israeli primary schools via the teacher alienation inventory & a locus of control scale. The findings show that: (1) school bureaucratic structure as measured by centralization & formalization, in the subjective view of the teachers, has a greater impact than does locus of control on alienation of both types; (2) formalization has a greater impact than centralization on alienation; & (3) externally oriented teachers exhibit less alienation than do their internally oriented counterparts. 3 Tables, 40 References. Modified AA

title: Disobedient Distributors: Street-Level Bureaucrats and Would-Be Patrons in Community-Based Family Planning Programs in Rural Kenya
abstract: The implementation of social welfare programs, including family planning programs, is strongly conditioned by the needs, desires, & agendas of those who carry them out, known as "street-level bureaucrats." In this study, the strategies of CBD agents in western Kenya are examined in order to understand how they use their job as a means to achieve their own personal goals. The concept of clientelism, borrowed from the field of political science, can help to explain what the CBD agents are trying to achieve for themselves in their communities, at the same time as they promote the use of contraceptive pills & injections. CBD agents are concerned with building up their own stocks of prestige & respect from their community members, while avoiding blame for any possible negative outcomes of family planning. 47 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Cooperação internacional católica: entre a política dos movimentos sociais e o ativismo da fé em ação
abstract: The paper presents an analysis of the relations established between the Catholic Agency for Overseas Development (CAFOD), Catholic donors in the dioceses of England and Wales, and the street children movement in Brazil in the 1990s. The aim is to show that the particularity of the Catholic development chain is not expressed in the supposed existence of a bounded moral community, as suggested by Morse and McNamara (2008), but in the kinds of knowledge, techniques and language mobilized at every relation: bureaucratic knowledge with institutional donors and the Catholic doctrine among donors. Relations within the Catholic Development chain enable the practice of specific and unrelated politics, those of social movements in Brazil and of Catholic activists in the UK.

title: The State Ideal of Egalitarianism and the Bureaucratic System of Particularism: A New Model of Social Stratification Structure
abstract: Through a revisit to the concept of "redistribution," this paper overrides the overpaid attention to the differentiation of the elite from the ordinary in the previous research on social stratification in the socialist states and proposes a new model of social stratification. This paper argues that the stratification structure in socialist society is determined by the conflict between the state ideal of egalitarianism and the bureaucratic system of particularism. Redistribution itself does not generate inequality; it is the bureaucracy and the bureau-political behaviors in the process of redistribution that produce social inequality in socialism. One's distance from the center of redistribution determines not only his/her rank in the redistributive system, but also the magnitude of the bureau-political influence that he/she receives. In the transition period, the bureaucrats at the grass-roots levels will continue to have their advantages in the redistribution and the overall social stratification structure will be further differentiated apart. Adapted from the source document.

title: No Longer So Strange? (Dis)Trust in Municipality-Small Business Relationships
abstract: In this article, a trust perspective is applied to the relationship between local government and their alternative service providers in the era of new public management. The importance of category-based (dis)trust is highlighted, as well as the complications occurring when service providers belong to several categories, all of which are in some respect distrusted. More specifically, the article illustrates how gender and professional hierarchies influence municipal trust in service providers. The complexities of trust in public sector outsourcing relationships are highlighted, as the trust that citizens' show in the service providers also affects the trust of the municipality. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright holder.]

title: Bureaucracy and Ethnicity in Kenya: Some Conjectures for the Eighties
abstract: It is hypothesized: that organizations in Kenya will display increasing ethnic homogeneity over the next decade, as a response to alienation of migrant workers; that this will be greatest among segmentary lineage societies such as the Nilotes; & that ethnic homogeneity will in some circumstances produce increased organizational effectiveness. Evidence from the literature is reviewed. Tape-recorded open-ended interviews were conducted with 33 Luo watchmen employed by 2 security organizations, each employing over 90% Luo watchmen. The success of this ethnic selectivity suggests that Western norms of universalism may not be appropriate to African societies. 1 Figure. W. H. Stoddard.

title: Lost and Found
abstract: An attorney whose clients include schoolchildren & their families reflects on her path to this professional niche & the troubled educational bureaucracy in the US. Adapted from the source document.

title: Influences on Bureaucratic Policy Initiatives in the American States
authors: Schneider, Saundra K; Jacoby, William G
abstract: Develops & tests an empirical model of influences on bureaucratic policy making in state Medicaid programs. Survey data from administrators regarding adoptions of optional health care services demonstrate that interests groups, structural characteristics, & state environmental conditions all affect state policy choices. In contrast, partisan & ideological political factors have little direct impact. These findings suggested the bureaucracy's role in state Medicaid programs is politically distinct, but that bureaucrats are also rational actors who adjust to changing political settings. 3 Exhibits, 119 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Constitutionalistic Viewpoints of Public Interest in Western Public Administration Theories
abstract: In the Western Public Administration field, the controversy concerning the public interest runs through the theory developing history, the scholars have put forward various quite different defining methods & proposals. To total up, the main consensus of the constitutionalism lies in the widespread acknowledgement that public administration plays an important role & is a fundamental operating mechanism in the implementing process of public interests. According to the differences on the perspectives, they can be divided into two types: descriptive & prescriptive. However, there is a very strong tendency to try to integrate & coordinate the different values, which embodies the value integrating trend in the field. References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Motivating Military Families to Thrive
authors: Clark, Matthew G; Jordan, Jacquelynn D; Clark, Katherine L
abstract: Since 1973 excellent programs supporting military families have developed. However, a unified program across the Department of Defense (DoD) that meets family needs and connects to communities is elusive. Military Family Life Project data show that participation in many programs is limited, but when the programs are used, they often work well. The data suggest the 'coercive bureaucracy' that envelopes the military extends to the family and limits motivation to utilize programs. We propose that the military employ the Self-Determination Theory to motivate families to elevate above basic survival so they can thrive. With 73% of families living outside of military installations, their participation in programs will require community involvement because the government cannot meet the needs of most families by itself. Connecting government and community programs requires a transparent unified program structure. We propose that product life-cycle management will elucidate and integrate existing programs across the entire service life cycle and enhance community connectivity. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Inc., copyright holder.]

title: The Absorption of Orientals into Israeli Bureaucracy
abstract: Immigration patterns have changed the composition of the Israeli population. In 1948, only 9.8% of the population had immigrated from Middle East or North African countries. In 1967, 27.5% of the population had immigrated from these 'Oriental countries.' An investigation was made to determine the extent of the integration of Orientals into the civil servant market. The percent of civil servants of Oriental birth is equivalent to their proportion in the population. Only 6.6% of the highest service grades are Orientals, with 70.6% being European or United States born & 22.8% being Israeli born. 9 Tables. P. Montgomery.

title: Egalitarianism in the face of hierarchy
abstract: It is described how Sapwuahfik people handle challenges to their egalitarian ethos and how public activities, especially feasts, maintain that ethos while acknowledging the legitimacy of the regional rank system.  The linking of rank symbolism with community identity and the public management of status claims are discussed.

title: Ministerial and Parliamentary Elites in Multilevel Spain 1977-2009
abstract: In decentralized European parliamentary democracies future governing elites often acquire political experience and attain top positions by passing through sub-national political institutions. In doing so, elites circumvent and reduce the importance of national parliaments. Previous research has advanced several explanations for this pattern: Europe's tradition of bureaucratic government; parties with open methods for selecting parliamentary candidates; the "presidentialization" and Europeanization of national political systems. Since its transition to democracy in 1977, Spain has had an exceptionally small proportion of former MPs in its national cabinets. I employ data for Spanish ministers between 1977-2009 demonstrating the passage of a large proportion of cabinet ministers through local and regional government levels rather than the national parliament, the Cortes Generales. I show that multilevel rather than parliamentary political careers characterize ministerial elite recruitment, and I discuss the consequences for Spain's parliamentary democracy. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Expertise, Representation and the Common Good: Grounds for Legitimacy in the Urban Governance Network
abstract: This paper discusses the local planning of sustainable development in terms of urban governance. It is particularly interested to examine the grounds for the legitimacy of different actors and the process of legitimation in one urban network. Legitimation is understood here as a discursive process of acceptance in which the actors involved locate themselves and others in the structures of governance. The results indicate that people from the local community and local government justify their positions in the urban governance network and policy-making by means of traditional forms of authorisation-namely, in terms of expertise, representation or the common good. These characteristics have traditionally given legitimacy to the activities and decisions taken by public administration and government. In the case at hand, the traditional grounds for legitimacy are transformed into network-based practices, but those grounds are not pre-given for any of the parties involved. The future challenge in urban governance is to enable the formation of new kinds of political identities that are suitable for governance networks by reforming local discursive practices. Adapted from the source document.

title: Vive la (Sexual) Révolution: The political roots of Bourdieu's analysis of gender
abstract: This paper argues that the French Revolution constituted the basic metaphor through which Pierre Bourdieu perceived and analyzed gender hierarchies; that the class structure of the ancien regime and the mechanisms of its legitimation were the major metaphors he used through his scathing critiques on the order of the sexes; and that the ideals of liberte, egalite and fraternite were always his reformatory aims for a just, gender-neutral society. The paper shows how this preoccupation with the Revolution of 1789 structured Bourdieu's analysis of gender relations and sexual identities in contemporary society. It exposes the ways in which he identified men with the nobility and women with the third estate; it presents his analyses of the role that traditional ideologies and state bureaucracies play in legitimating this arbitrary order of masculine domination; and it analyzes his proposals for a sexual revolution while exposing the counter-revolutionary forces that persistently negate attempts to reform gender hierarchies. Fundamentally, this new reading of Bourdieu's exegeses on gender suggests that he was working with a ready-made interpretive scheme, a model of society that he was inclined to see as always reproducing itself: the ancien regime. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Hello: On Our Legacy and Possibility
abstract: As 2015 begins, there are many issues that vie for our attention and call for collective action to influence policies and treatment processes that impact those who are vulnerable and marginalized in US society as well as globally. Indifference toward other people or communities, expressed through anonymous social media outlets, fiery conversations, or brutal group action, suggest a growing culture of deepening intolerance for open, respectful dialogue about conditions and treatment of those in great need (Kolivoski, Weaver, & Constance-Huggins, 2014; Schmitz, Stakeman, & Sisneros, 2001). Finally, persistent health, mental health, and other biopsychosocial conditions that weaken individual and family strengths and capacities for growth and stability are challenged by declining funding for needed programs and service providers, onerous bureaucratic procedures, and an increased suspicion of those who carry stigmatized labels regarding their contributions to the community (Ellerbe et al., 2011).

title: Governing Police Practice: Limits of the New Accountability
abstract: The advent of public sector managerialism in Western democracies, eg, Australia & GB, has brought with it a new principle of police accountability that emphasizes managerial rather than legal or public-interest standards, favors external oversight combined with self-regulation rather than centralized control, & promotes risk management rather than rule enforcement. Here, the experience of the police force in New South Wales, Australia, is used to show that the new accountability has not been successful in holding police accountable, while elements of the old accountability have reemerged to dominate public debates. It is argued that, in police governance, the neoliberal state does not necessarily pursue a coherent strategy of "acting at a distance" (Miller, P., & Rose, N., 1990), partly because of the inability of accountability technologies to deliver the promised policy outcomes & partly because of the sensitivity of its political arm to the public's moral outrage against corruption (Garland, D., 1996). 2 Figures, 55 Appendixes. Adapted from the source document.

title: Local Institutions and the Transformation of Property Rights in Chinese Reforms: Rural Enterprises in Southern Fujian and Southern Jiangsu
abstract: An explanation is offered for regional variations in property rights transformation by examining the institutions in which local economic activities are embedded. The author argues that state bureaucracies & market mechanisms alone are insufficient for explaining institutional change in rural People's Republic of China. Only by including local institutions in any analysis of relationships among state, market, & local institutions is it possible to accurately explain paths of institutional change. Data were gathered from case studies & interviews conducted in southern Fujian & southern Jiangsu. They show that southern Fujian property rights transformation was embedded in family & clan networks, while rural enterprises in southern Jiangsu were more strongly affected by power networks among local political cadres. In terms of postreform institutional development in the late 1990s in the same regions, the author argues that institutional transformation does not necessarily lead to a convergence of global capitalism, since regional incentive structures are shaped by local institutions that serve as informal constraints affecting transformation paths originally initiated by the state. 62 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucratic aesthetics: Report writing in the Nigérien gendarmerie
abstract: Nigerien gendarmes invest considerable creative energy in their daily paperwork. I explore how the gendarmes conceive of the writing of seemingly purely bureaucratic documents, proces-verbaux, in aesthetic terms. At the same time, I ground the aesthetic appreciation of these documents in the gendarmes' socioprofessional environment. Writing an aesthetically satisfying proces-verbal is a means of gaining respect from colleagues and superiors and of justifying and actualizing gendarmes' self-perception as intellectuals in uniform. Bureaucratic work, I argue, is always also aesthetic work, and bureaucratic aesthetics is where aesthetic, pragmatic, and legal reasonings become one. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The IAS officer - predator or victim?
abstract: The Indian Administrative Service is a troubled institution - not least because of political compulsions imposed upon it. This article examines several of the more serious problems that it faces: a lack of professionalism, the creation of redundant posts, unsatisfactory structures of reward and punishment, and an inability to deliver services adequately. It then suggests steps which an increasingly proactive central government might take to address these problems at the state level in this federal system, where they are most apparent. These include a greater focus on policy outcomes; linking transfers with performance by state governments; and enhancing accountability outward to society and citizens, rather than inward and upward within the government.

title: Abstract Knowledge as a Basis of Power: The History of the Evolution of Bureaucratic Power in the Prussian Peasant State
abstract: Problems of public administration in a peasant state are examined, with peasants defined as agrarian owner-producers who partially consume their production & partially market it. The state is defined as a political body with central power & a bureaucracy. It is proposed that such peasant states pose special problems for governmental bureaucracy. These problems (as apparent in the eighteenth-century Prussian state) are due to lack of integrated markets; the peasants' defensive strategies; local pluralism in economic, social, & linguistic areas; & illiteracy. In such states, bureaucratic administration is supplemented by intermediary & despotic public servants. A case study is presented that illustrates the side-by-side existence of bureaucratic, intermediate, & despotic administration, as determined by the agrarian structure. The inroads of the bureaucracy into three areas are examined: the taxation system, military recruitment, & statistical data collection. It is shown how the collection of statistics became a tool for power & control, & how the Church, as records keeper on marriages, baptisms, & deaths, played an important role in securing bureaucratic control. AA Tr & Modified by S. Whittle.

title: Shaping Human Relations at Work: The Application to India
abstract: The superior-subordinate relationship involves both a personal & functional interdependence. Drawing heavily on Western models, particularly the Japanese example, some suggestions are provided to guide public enterprise supervisors in reconciling internal & external duties & maintaining both a people & task orientation. Personnel recruitment & training issues are discussed, along with some specific strategies for organizational team building, performance evaluation, handling organizational innovations, & successful manipulation of group processes. These ideas have been implemented in a training program for forestry administrators in India. 13 References. K. Hyatt

title: Bureaucracy, Liberalism, and Community -- American Style
abstract: The US is a bureaucracy, & US lawyers are full-time bureaucratic functionaries. In this context, Americans' passion for individualism, legal equality, & perfection has yielded a disputes orientation to US bureaucracies, along with a plague of lawyers. The legal intelligentsia, faced with this system, has offered three visions: the liberal mainstream vision, the market or law-&-economic vision, & the critical legal studies vision. Here, a communitarian vision is advanced that presents the possibility of substantially reducing large bureaucracy in favor of smaller & less bureaucratic community. This community vision harmonizes with the critical legal studies view that man must always be examined in a social setting, but rejects egocentric individualism & equality as the bases of community, locating the foundations instead in communal duties, reciprocity, & belonging. This community vision also harmonizes with the law-&-economics vision to the extent the latter leads to smallness & decentralization, but not where "efficiency" analysis leads to hedonistic markets dominated by large "private" bureaucracies. Since this community vision is half liberal, it necessarily shares the liberal vision of individual rights, but it is tripolar in that it sees the individual in community meshed with Leviathan. Hence, it demands legal recognition of community per se, not merely as derivative from individual rights. Modified AA

title: Gendered organizational dynamics: The elephant in the room for Australian allied health workforce policy and planning?
abstract: Australian governments have reported an impending 'crisis' with workforce shortages in the health sector expected to deepen over the next decade. The allied health professions, however, have barely rated a mention despite the fact their retention rates are low and they are expected to play an expanded and more preventive role in the future. This article examines current Australian public policy approaches to the allied health professions in relation to workforce shortages. It identifies the dominance of technocratic representations of the problem, noting that these have become more pervasive and robust with the New Public Management (NPM). Recent Australian sociological discussion suggests that technocratic 'framing' of allied health workforce shortages is limited by its failure to address the role of organizational and institutional dynamics. Such an analysis advances prevailing policy-based problematizations of allied health workforce shortages, but is itself constrained by the lack of acknowledgement of the gendered character of Australian health services organization and the role this may play in allied health workforce shortages. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright The Australian Sociological Association.]

title: State Intervention and Ideological Positions of Executives in Private and Public Bureaucracies
abstract: Structured questionnaires were administered to public & private executives in Quebec (N = 313, distributed in civil service, crown corporations, & private enterprise; approximately 30% English- & 70% French-speaking) to assess ideological positions in higher management on public expenditures & state intervention in industrial regulation. Major findings include: (1) a commonality of discourse & pattern of response among most Rs, with the sharpest differences between the different language groups; (2) despite widespread approval of decreased public expenditures, a generalized desire for greater state-based stimulation of enterprise; & (3) greater support for the classic liberal state model among public managers, particularly anglophones. Findings are further discussed in terms of the relations between private capital accumulation & the state in a dependent society. 14 Tables. Modified HA.

title: Beyond the Law's Ends: Files, Bureaucracy and Legal Knowledge
abstract: Files, memoranda, and paperwork in general, are seen as routine instruments of bureaucratic practice, the means for achieving an end: the legal decision. Consequently, the analysis tends to focus on the 'results' of institutional acts but not on the process of institutionalization that files entail. Therefore law is apprehended by its ends and the legal analysis is kept within the epistemological boundaries of the same ends. In this essay, I propose to bring attention to legal files as analytical objects in their own terms. To do so, I elaborate, in the ethnographic mode, on my personal file as it unfolded in my fieldwork in the Argentine Supreme Court from August 2005 to February 2007. In looking at the file as an artifact of knowledge, I seek to bring to the surface aspects of lawmaking that remain a blind spot of socio-legal studies. Adapted from the source document.

title: Public Management, Citizen Participation and Local Development. Proposals for Participative Management and Public Efficiency
abstract: Reviews current research to argue that public administration is better than the private enterprise model when it comes to managing urban development in Spain. It is contended that both public & private models use a bureaucratic hierarchy with virtually no structural difference. Public administration offers more job, salary, & job description stability. A new form of public management-administration is proposed to introduce the best elements of private enterprise into the public model, featuring worker incentives, quality control, & coordination departments. This approach, largely based on Luis Felipe Garcia Calvo's (1996) strategies for improving public management, would also seek to increase citizen participation in municipal decisions through city elections & by granting more power to elected city officials. Citizenship participation would also increase because of the proposal's distinction between social, civic, & cultural centers of administration. 2 Figures, 14 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Community Organization and Social Administration: Partnership or Irrelevance?
abstract: Three roles of community organization practice (eg, locality development, social action, & social planning) & three roles of administrative practice (eg, interpersonal, informational, & decisional activities), are explored. Special attention is given to the following questions: (1) why partnership is needed; (2) how the practice domains can be linked conceptually; (3) what some of the cognitive similarities & differences are between the two practice domains; (4) how some of the technology of macro practice can be transferred to micro practice domains; & (5) what the implications are for preparing future practitioners. 1 Figure, 18 References. Modified HA

title: Going Public: The Emergence and Effects of Soft Bureaucracy within a Knowledge-Intensive Firm
abstract: The aim of this paper is to explore & explain the emergence over time of forms of organization & governance (referred to as 'organizing templates') in a knowledge-intensive firm (KIF). A longitudinal case study tracks the ways in which this firm has evolved from its inception in 1986 through to 2001. The analysis emphasizes, in particular, the strategic role of power politics in shaping organizing templates following firm success & expansion. The paper focuses on the shift away from adhocracy as the (ideological) organizing template & towards a new form of governance within the firm, characterized as soft bureaucracy. It shows how this shift coincides with economic, technological, & cultural imperatives imposed by the increased sovereignty of the market. A multilevel analytical model of organizational change processes is outlined in which shifting dominant management logics are aligned with firm level innovations through organizing templates. This framework is used to structure our narrative historical account of the various phases of restructuring throughout the period. The paper attempts to inform existing understanding of soft bureaucracy by showing how this particular form of governance emerges in a KIF through the interplay between macro-level sectoral change & micro-political processes. It concludes by considering first the implications of this shift for firm level knowledge work processes, & second, the politics of organizational change more generally in the knowledge-intensive sector at the start of the 21st century. 1 Table, 1 Figure, 32 References. [Copyright 2004 Sage Publications Ltd.]

title: Domination, Mobilization and Chaos: The State and the School in Quebec
