abstract: Analyzes the political structuration of socialization in schools, starting from acknowledgement of the present disorder in schools & the positive or negative roles taken by social actors in this regard. Socialization is thus argued from the perspective of political ordering. It is contended that state domination & bureaucratic expansion have generated the chaos in schools, & only local disciplinary mobilization will resolve the disorder. 66 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Birth Certificate Program: Politics and Pragmatic of the Reform
abstract: Since the mid 2000's medical help to expectant mothers has been one of the key issues in Russian social policy. The birth certificate program is one of the most significant policy innovations introduced in the sphere in order to ameliorate healthcare services and increase their availability to different categories of pregnant women. This paper considers the reform from a social science perspective and studies how the program is actually implemented, i.e., how innovations of social policy are 'translated' into the pragmatic language of the everyday professional practice of Russian obstetricians. The results of case studies conducted in four state-funded maternity clinics show that the reform has different effects on the actors involved in the process of medical care for pregnant women. On the level of the everyday practices this expectedly liberal political measure has unexpectedly led to more bureaucratization of doctors' work as well as to increased responsibility for each pregnancy case. Adapted from the source document

title: Fiction and Social Consciousness in Interwar Siam: Thai Elite Culture in Crisis and Transition
abstract: This article examines representations of Thai society in fiction during the 1920s and 1930s. Initially the hobby of palace writers and readers, by the 1930s the evolving form had come to be widely popular with middle-class commoners. The rise of middle-class society was of profound importance in the interwar period: far beyond constituting a new reading and writing public, social and economic change undermined the political power of the old elite, and in 1932 a bureaucratic coup toppled the absolute monarchy. But the 'revolution', as it came to be known, was incomplete; the growth of new social classes and democratic ideas did not produce a new society. Nor, as this article demonstrates, did it destroy the cultural power of the old elite. The royal-aristocratic class remained cultural icons, and this is clearly shown in the new genre of realistic fiction that appeared. Royalist culture, an enduring aspect of twentieth century Thai history, maintained its power through a period of crisis largely because of its adaptation to changed circumstances.

title: Enterprising States: The Public Management of Welfare-to-Work
abstract: "Enterprising States: The Public Management of Welfare-to-Work" by Mark Considine is reviewed.

title: THE OFFENCE OF NEGOTIATIONS PROHIBITED TO PUBLIC OFFICIALS AFTER 5/2010
abstract: This study aims to assess the criminal concept of negotiations and activities prohibited to public officials as it is established in article 439 of the Spanish Criminal Code. It constitutes a criminal offence against the public administration that has hardly been investigated by the doctrine and upon which our courts have not ruled on. This contrasts with the usualness of these behaviours in practice, as the media often reports on the economic improvement experienced by certain family-owned businesses whose shareholders include elected representatives (mayors, town councillors...) or other types of abuse of office that could easily fit into this offence. That is why we will analyse its characteristics in depth and will give special attention to the recent reforms passed in 2010, in order to provide interpretative and criminal justice policy answers that can solve the problem. Adapted from the source document.

title: A HALF-CENTURY OF MUNICIPAL REFORM
abstract: In the 1890's there was a mighty citizens effort in many cities to turn the rascals out of municipal gov's by straight frontal attacks. With the founding of the Nat'l Municipal League in 1894, new principles of strategy began to appear. These had to do with improving visibility for the voters. In 1909, W. Wilson spoke out for the short ballot. The Galveston-Des Moines Plan spread to a hundred cities & towns by 1909. It cracked the assumption that the mayor & council plan was the only structure conceivable for a municipal gov. By December, 1914, there were 17 city managers in office and 8 of them formed the City Managers Association. The selection of city managers freely from out of town, essential if city management was to become a profession, proved acceptable from the start. The march of the city management movement set up hundreds of new civil service systems, nonpartisan elections, centralized purchasing, orderly budgeting procedure, & short ballots. The list of council-manager cities totals nearly 1,400 in communities of all sizes in the US & Canada. Management has become a career. This marks a real advance over the earlier municipal misgovernment and ramshackle amateur service. Moreover, citizens find it relatively easy to survey the candidates listed on the ballot & pick 5. Municipal reform makes practical workable mechanisims of democracy universal. J. E. Jacobi.

title: New Public Management, care and struggles about recognition
abstract: New Public Management (NPM) is usually perceived as a homogeneous discourse. However, when we examine it by looking at micro-politics in municipalities and understand its consequences drawing on the voices of home helpers, the picture is more complex and ambiguous. NPM is seen as disciplining paid public elderly care by limiting and forming the understandings applied through two combined but different logics: a usually dominant logic of details and a usually minor logic of self-governance. The bottom-up study presented here investigates the translation -- the understanding and application -- of these two logics in two different Danish municipalities that are strategically chosen to illustrate differences along the continuum of NPM translations. It asks which logic the home helpers feel is most dominant and relates the results to feelings of recognition and misrecognition as well as to strategies of resistance. The analysis applies feminist theories of recognition and care, and its findings are based on focus group interviews and feminist discourse analysis. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright holder.]

title: Computerizing the Welfare State: An International Comparison of Computerization in Social Security
abstract: Although computer technology is central to the operation of the modern welfare state, there has been little analysis of its role or of the factors shaping the way in which it is used. Using data generated by expert informants from 13 OECD countries, this paper provides an indicative comparison of the aims of computerization in national social security systems over a 15-year period from 1985 to 2000. The paper seeks to identify & explain patterns in the data & outlines & examines four hypotheses. Building on social constructivist accounts of technology, the first three hypotheses attribute variations in the aims of computerization to different welfare state regimes, forms of capitalism, & structures of public administration. The fourth hypothesis, which plays down the importance of social factors, assumes that computerization is adopted as a means of improving operational efficiency & generating expenditure savings. The findings suggest that, in all 13 countries, computerization was adopted in the expectation that it would lead to increased productivity & higher standards of performance, thus providing most support for the fourth hypothesis. However, variations between countries suggest that the sociopolitical values associated with different welfare state regimes have also had some effect in shaping the ways in which computer technology has been used in national social security systems. Tables, Appendixes, References. Adapted from the source document.

title: "Men who smell of fear": The Menzies Government and Rhodesia's Unilateral Declaration of Independence
abstract: This article uses international archival sources to examine Australian policy on the problem of Rhodesian independence during the 1960s. It demonstrates that until November 1965 the Australian government led by Sir Robert Menzies followed a finely balanced policy that was broadly supportive of Britain but also sympathetic to the Rhodesian Front. However, the Australian response to Rhodesia's Unilateral Declaration of Independence (UDI) revealed increasing bureaucratic conflict in Australian policy-making and exposed the limits of Australian support for Britain in dealing with the international consequences of the UDI. Analysis of Australia's decision to not attend the Lagos Conference in January 1966 demonstrates the Menzies government's anxiety about the implications of racial issues for Australian domestic and foreign policies. This suggests that historians should pay more attention to the significance of Africa in Australian foreign relations during the Menzies era.

title: An American Reading of Portuguese Corporativism
abstract: Howard G. Wiarda's Corporativism and Development: The Portuguese Experience (Amherst: U of Massachusetts Press, 1977) is reviewed. Wiarda places Portuguese Salazarist corporativism in the larger framework of a tradition of bureaucracy, clientele, & mercantilism that has existed for centuries in Iberia & Latin America. The course of the overthrown regime is traced from its advent in the 1930s to its fall in 1974. Wiarda's work connects the analysis of the new state with the general theory of corporativism, explains the passage from Salazarism to Marcelism by presenting the latter as a renewal in continuity, & discusses the destiny of corporativist organization after 1974. Modified HA

title: Power System and Field of Resocialization
abstract: Systems of power are examined in two sets of people: (1) administrators & management personnel, & (2) persons in charge of individual & group-level social services. The locus of the research was Belgian reception centers for socially handicapped adults. The structuration of the resocialization process is considered in light of the existing power patterns. These two factors, power & structuration, are analyzed in direct relation to the social characteristics of the users of the reception centers. The principal questions were: (A) How does power gain collective recognition in the field of resocialization? (B) How could its legitimacy be enhanced & efficiency increased? Leaders should be specially trained to participate in collective strategies. Efficiency will be increased when leaders regain their self-confidence, which will happen simultaneously with the enhanced legitimation of their authority. 7 Tables. HA Tr & Modified by S. Karganovic.

title: The Theoretical Concept of Administration
abstract: A historical sketch of administration from 17th-century England to present-day Europe presents a variety of political & legal viewpoints, emphasizing responsibility, public interest, balance of power, & efficiency. More modern approaches concentrate on a complex, dynamic system of social regulation. Aggregate socioeconomic development demonstrates the inadequacy of viewing the management of administrative systems primarily as a marginal social activity based on a legalistic paradigm. In this light, administrative social regulations are examined as prerequisites for economic efficiency, cultural development, & general social welfare in advanced industrial & urban environments. The concept of public administration then becomes an integral part of the political system, oriented toward problem resolution. 13 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Team Nursing: Professional Coordination or Bureaucratic Control?
authors: Bloom, Joan R; Alexander, Jeffrey A
abstract: Nursing teams are conceptualized as coordination mechanisms that respond to task interdependence within the hospital unit. The form of coordination is predicted to result from organizational decisionmakers' conceptions of the work to be performed as well as the more objective characteristics of the work. The effects of these technological variables on coordination are mediated by the size of the unit & the degree of professionalism exhibited by the nursing staff. A path model was constructed & tested using a sample of 146 patient care units from a national sample of 17 hospitals. Three sources of data were utilized: (1) a questionnaire administered to 1,230 registered nurses in the sample units; (2) a structured interview with the head nurse on each unit; & (3) a questionnaire completed by the director of nursing at each hospital. In general, the results were supportive of the model: both conceptions of a task & task predictability (or known technology) appeared to affect coordination through other structural characteristics of the unit. On larger units the nursing team provides a hierarchical control mechanism, whereas teaming in units characterized by greater staff professionalism provides a means of lateral coordination as well as hierarchical control. 2 Tables, 2 Figures. Modified HA.

title: Problems of Controlling the Efficiency of Bureaucratic Behavior
abstract: Problems of controlling the efficiency of bureaucratic behavior are discussed. Two broad approaches to the topic are taken: (1) a general discussion of systemic complications that mitigate against efficiency; & (2) a study of productivity & efforts at instituting program changes that result in more efficient operations. The former is by nature a more theoretical &, unfortunately, less positive statement, & the latter is more practical & optimistic; taken together, however, the two approaches provide a balanced overview of efficiency as it relates to bureaucratic behavior. 1 Table, 27 References. HA

title: The Enduring Nightmare: The 1984 Bureaucracy
abstract: The power of George Orwell's 1984 lies in the depiction of an authority capable of manipulating the general culture while the "masses" remain apathetic; eg, Winston Smith's crime is not the act of writing a diary, but his belief in an ultimate sense of decency. Orwell elaborates a bureaucratic theory of a totalitarian society, & describes the functions of falsification of the past, maintenance of continuous warfare, & preservation of the Inner Party's power. The question Orwell presents is whether a complex society can prevent its bureaucratic government from becoming a "system of organized lying" by those who love power. K. Carande

title: Parkinson's Law and the United States Bureau of Prisons
abstract: Parkinson's Law (C. Parkinson, Parkinson's Law, Boston: Houghton-Mifflin, 1957) states that the number of workers in any public bureau will tend to rise, at an annual rate of about 6%, irrespective of the amount of work to be done--or whether any work is done at all. A look at the history of the US Bureau of Prisons (BOP) would suggest that this bureau follows Parkinson's Law, & may be the "ultimate bureaucracy." Formed in 1930, the BOP was designed to make uniform the treatment of prisoners in all federal prisons. In its forty-seven years of operation, the number of prisoners has increased 93.76% & the number of BOP employees has increased 874%. From 1970 to 1975, inmate population increased 21.24% & employees increased 82.57%. The average increase annually for the latter was 12.81%. At the Federal Correctional Institution, this was caused in part by a "unit management" concept which added twelve personnel for inmate casework between 1967 & 1975. The number of inmates increased from 400 to 500 in this same period. There has been a great increase in the amount of paperwork, but how has it helped the inmates? "Not in any way that can be determined." The trend continues--increased staff & no visible increase in the quantity or quality of work being done regarding the stated purpose of the institution. BOP would seem to be a prime illustration of Parkinson's Law. 2 Figures, 1 Table. B. Hubinger.

title: Public Administration and the Third Sector. Analytical Proposal and Study of the Andalucian Case
authors: Navarro Yanez, Clemente J; Rodriguez Garcia, Maria Jesus
abstract: It is a commonplace argument that the benefits of nonprofit inclusion in the provision of public services reduce the welfare-state crisis. Therefore, there are many few studies about the quality of relationships between the nonprofit sector & governmental agencies. This article presents an analytical proposal & its application by a case study. The main argument is that the quality of relations between the nonprofit sector & the government depends on governmental agencies' information about nonprofit entities. 3 Tables, 2 Graphs, 24 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Gender and leadership in South African educational administration
abstract: Between 1994 and 1999, new discourses of social justice and gender equity in South Africa enabled the entry of significant numbers of women in the previously all-male educational bureaucracy. At the time, women in one bureaucracy were leaving as fast as they were entering. Chisholm probes this phenomenon of the simultaneous transformation of the educational administration and the apparent consolidation of earlier patriarchal forms of control, albeit on a non-racial basis.

title: Debating the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit
abstract: In Feeding the Sparrows by Feeding the Horses, Chester Hartman argues that the low-income housing tax credit is an indirect tax-break route that most advantages upper-income investors & big corporations (ie, community-based housing developers) who avoid paying parts of their income taxes by offsetting these obligations via investment in low-income housing. A significant amount of money is wasted in the process by paying middlemen lawyers, syndicators, & accountants to structure complicated deals. Furthermore, the packaging process is disempowering at the community level, & the system tends to replicate the "expiring use restriction" with respect to projects built in the 1960s & 1970s. In Good Policy, Good Politics, Paul S. Grogan & Benson F. Roberts argue that the credit act is not redistributably unjust, & that the true distributional beneficiaries are low-income tenants & communities. The program's involvement of private investors also brings vigor to the development & management of the housing that direct government subsidies fail to provide. This rigor is combined with flexibility in which communities, not federal bureaucracies, decide how to use the credits. In addition, the credit is not qualitatively more complicated than other federal housing programs, & empowers community groups by providing them resources to bring to the negotiating table. It is agreed that direct, cost-effective subsidies are needed to complement the program. S. Millett

title: Fraud and Bureaucrats: Tobacco and Paraguay, 1789-1790
abstract: The events leading up to a cancellation of orders for Paraguayan tobacco by the Spanish government in 1789, & the consequences of the cancellation, are examined. After the cancellation, with large quantities of less than high quality tobacco in inventory, the tobacco growers had three options: to suspend planting, continue planting only high quality tobacco, or sell the harvest to contraband players in the internal market. Many opted to sell the tobacco internally. After Spain resumed ordering in 1792, shortages plagued the tobacco business throughout the 1790s. This chain of events is blamed on the bureaucracy of the tobacco monopoly -- its bad judgment, poor planning, mistakes in simple calculations, & inability to admit errors. In addition, bureaucrats in Buenos Aires (Argentina) made decisions affecting the local growing area of Asuncion without knowing local conditions. As a result, the tobacco bureau was discredited, contraband flourished for the rest of the colonial era, & the monopoly over tobacco in Paraguay was broken. M. Pflum

title: Enclaves of inequality: Brasiguaios and the transformation of the Brazil-Paraguay borderlands
abstract: This contribution traces the history of Brazilian immigration to Paraguay and the emergence of 'Brasiguaio' communities, arguing that the enclaves are products of the development policies of each country's military dictatorship. Although Brasiguaios are currently associated with wealthy Brazilian agriculturalists in Paraguay, the majority of these immigrants have been poor workers who face constant marginalization from state bureaucracies and unequal access to land. Paraguay's eastern border region is among the most complex spaces in Latin America of cultural, economic and national hybridity. The transformation of this borderland is predicated on a highly unequal social hierarchy that resulted largely from the evolution of Brasiguaio immigration.

title: Ministerial and Parliamentary Elites in an Executive-Dominated System: Post-Soviet Russia 1991-2009
abstract: This article analyzes the recruitment and circulation of ministerial and parliamentary elites in Russia from the Soviet Union's collapse in 1991 until 2009. The social backgrounds and careers of all ministers in 13 cabinets (1991-2009) and all members of the State Duma during its five terms after 1993 are studied. Especially during Vladimir Putin's presidency (2000-2008), a shift toward super-presidentialism altered the circulation and composition of ministerial and parliamentary elites. Cabinets in Moscow consisted increasingly of ministers recruited from state bureaucracies, while the State Duma more and more contained businessmen, party politicians, and celebrities who appeared to treat MP service as simply an episode in their wider careers. Adapted from the source document.

title: Education of the countryside at a crossroads: rural social movements and national policy reform in Brazil
abstract: This contribution explores the strategies used by popular movements seeking to advance social reforms, and the challenges once they succeed. It analyzes how a strategic alliance between the Brazilian Landless Workers Movement (MST) and the National Confederation of Agricultural Workers (CONTAG) transformed the Ministry of Education's official approach to rural schooling. This success illustrates the critical role of international allies, political openings, framing, coalitions and state-society alliances in national policy reforms. The paper also shows that once movements succeed in advancing social reforms, bureaucratic tendencies such as internal hierarchy, rapid expansion and 'best practices' -- in addition to the constant threat of cooptation -- can prevent their implementation.

title: Book Review: The Government of Mistrust: Illegibility and Bureaucratic Power in Socialist Vietnam
abstract: MacLean, Ken , The Government of Mistrust: Illegibility and Bureaucratic Power in Socialist Vietnam is reviewed.

title: Character, civil society and prospects for democracy
abstract: In this article a framework is developed for comparing a number of present-day societies in terms of their ability to produce social order and moral character. America is compared with Europe, and then, in less detail, to Latin America and the Islamic world. Reference is also made to Alain Touraine's What is democracy? to show a present-day French perspective on democracy. The place of the middle class in America and in Europe in providing compromise solutions for their societies is noted, together with the possible relationship between social and political democracy, and how they may converge and diverge. Cultural elements involved in the production of social order are taken into account. Reference is made to the different checks and balances in different societies between the central and local government and local communities, as well as between elites and the masses. This reflects the cultural factors as well as the degree of bureaucratisation of these societies. Finally, there is a summary of various principles of honour governing differing structures of political power derived from the Baron de Montesquieu's The spirit of the laws. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Competence versus Care? Gender and Caring Work Revisited
abstract: Argues that masculinist visions serve to gender the concepts of bureaucracy & profession, dichotomizing competence & care & masking both the reality & the potential of public carework. A distinction is proposed among caregiving, carework, & professional care. An analysis of professional care is developed by reference to a recent campaign by the leading nurses' organization in the UK, seeking to highlight the worth of nursing work. The carework discussion has barely any echo in the debate about the "new managerialism" in the public sector; it is argued that a critical understanding of the centrality of binary gendered thought is crucial to a constructive critique of today's emphasis on bringing health care into the marketplace. 66 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Study of Public Administration in Times of Global Interpenetration: A Historical Rationale for a Theoretical Model
abstract: In a historical interpretation of the role of the administrative state in the construction of social order, a theoretical model for the study of the relationship between globalization & public administration is articulated. To actively participate in building the new structures of social relations that globalization is bringing about, the discipline of public administration must develop its theoretical capacity to transcend the ahistorical, voluntaristic, instrumental, parochial, & state-centered nature of its approaches & explanations. 88 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Restructuring neoliberalism at the World Health Organization
abstract: Most descriptions of the spread of neoliberal economic policies since the 1980s overlook the significant contribution of international organizations not only to the dissemination of these policies, but also to their making. The scholarship often regards international organizations as passive transmission belts that merely comply with the demands of their member-states. Scholars who do identify the constitutive role of international organizations consider them to be enthusiastic supporters of the neoliberal project. There were cases, however, when international organizations were opposed to neoliberal reforms imposed from above. This paper draws on the experience of the World Health Organization (WHO) to show that in the process of adapting to the emerging neoliberal regime, international bureaucracies actively restructured this regime in accordance with their own institutional cultures. Some neoliberal prescriptions were successfully transmitted, but others were transformed, with the result that the global regime was hardly monolithic and included elements that were introduced by the international bureaucracies themselves. In developing this argument, the paper identifies the adaptive strategies that allow international bureaucracies, in spite of their vulnerability to external forces, to incorporate their own organizational agendas into what has consequently become a more heterogeneous global neoliberal regime. Adapted from the source document.

title: Wrapped in the Flag of Israel: Mizrahi Single Mothers and Bureaucratic Torture
abstract: First and foremost, it is a book about understanding the grip of state violence on its defenseless subjects - poor women of color-through the notion of bureaucracy as a form of torture: from everyday humiliation and powerlessness to the paralyzing impact of all-encompassing webs of procedures to debilitating and long-term scarring of women's bodies, minds, and souls.

title: Systems Engineering and Contractual Individualism: Linking Engineering Processes to Macro Social Values
abstract: After eminent thinkers in the 1960s submitted critical views on technology, some philosophers of technology extended their macro perspectives. Since then, many historians and sociologists of technology steadily marginalized their general claims through richly empirical, constructivist case studies of concrete engineering processes. Some recent efforts have begun to bridge these two diverging orientations. This paper participates in such efforts with a case study of relationships between macro cultures and engineering processes. It shows that behind the adoption of systems engineering by engineers and managers who led the Apollo programme was a macro current of social values in the USA. Post-war American society saw the rise of highly individualistic social norms that valued mobility, meritocracy and clear-cut contractual working relationships. Such norms triumphed most conspicuously in the federal government during the 1960s. Engineers and managers at the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) headquarters, who tended to share such values, refined the formalized, depersonalized methods of systems engineering, which enabled them to perfect space technology. In order to show such a correlation between macro values and micro practices, this paper draws a comparison between engineering communities in different cultural settings in the USA and Japan. This paper thus explores the macro social environment that gave rise to systems engineering, which, in turn, continues to function as a skeletal structure for our technological society today. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Civil Servant: From Serving the State to Serving Society
abstract: An English translation of a debate originally published in Russian in Obshchestvenniye nauki i sovremennost, 2002, 4.

title: 在理念与现实之间——当代中国法治化进程中体制内法治工作者职业倦怠研究 / Caught between Ideal and Reality:A Study on Occupational Burnout among Legal Professionals under the Rule by Law Reform in China
abstract: This paper analyzes job burnout of legal professionals under the rule by law reform in China and its possible causes. Social cognitive theory, including cognitive dissonance, expectancy theory and social comparison theory, provides the analytic framework for this study. The conclusion reveals a high level job burnout among the legal professionals in China. Further analysis indicates that one's commitment to the rule by law, confidence about the reform, and difficulties experienced at daily work are influential factors affecting his/her job stress levels. Importantly, the interaction coefficients between these variables are statistically significant, clearly demonstrating that the discrepancy between expectation and disappointing reality is one of the root causes of job burnout in legal profession. The discrepancy causes cognitive dissonance and psychological imbalance. At theoretical level, this finding opens a new way of examining a particular occupational burnout. It shows that under the rule by law reform, the Chinese legal workers exhibit cognitive discord between ideal and reality, which can constitute a micro-political psychological basis of organizational change as speculated by Neo-institutionalism and in turn reveals some insights for us to understand the reform process within the bureaucratic system.

title: On the Administrative Sector of Social Systems: An Analysis of the Size and Complexity of Government Bureaucracies in the American States
abstract: 4 hypotheses were formulated & tested: (1) the size of the 50 state governmental bureaucracies will decrease as the size of the population of the states increases: (II) the size & the complexity of the government bureaus are positively related to the complexity of the social structures of the states; (III) the size & the complexity of the governmental bureaucracies are positively related to the wealth of the population of the states; & (IV) the size of government bureaucracies will increase as land area increases; complexity will decrease as land area increases. In measuring the dependent variables, data on the size & complexity of governmental bureaucracies was drawn from the "Census of Governments: 1962" (Bureau of the Census, 1963); the relative size of governmental bureaucracies was operationalized as the number of bureaucrats per 10.010 people in the state. To measure the complexity of the governmental bureaus, the distribution of personnel among a limited number of categories (social roles or functions) into which the more detailed DofL has been divided was calculated. The independent variables were: the size of the population, the wealth of the population, the land area of the state, & the complexity of the social structure. In general, results supported all 4 hypotheses. To test the stability of these findings, a path analytic model was set up, & expected path coefficients were found for every hypothesized relationship. Results were interpreted as supporting a systems perspective in the analysis of social structure. 3 Tables, 1 Figure. Modified HA.

title: Development through Positive Deviance and its Implications for Economic Policy Making and Public Administration in Africa: The Case of Kenyan Agricultural Development, 1930-2005
abstract: Positive internal innovation has long been a central element of African agricultural development, even if modern efforts to stimulate technical, institutional, and policy innovations in African agriculture have tended to look outwards. This paper examines the role of positive deviance in Kenyan agriculture over the last 75 years to cast doubt on the alleged authoritative sources of policy advice and mandates from the outside. Positive deviance and appreciative inquiry are suggested as organizing frameworks for identifying and amplifying the generation and uptake of internal African innovations. [Copyright 2006 Elsevier Ltd.]

title: A Study of the Advancement of Women in Municipal Government Bureaucracies: Persistence of Glass Ceilings?
authors: Reid, Margaret; Kerr, Brinck; Miller, William H
abstract: If women's advancement to the highest-level decision-making positions in governmental bureaucracies is to be enhanced, a better understanding of the continued impediments to such progress is essential. This study employs a large, previously underutilized national data set obtained from the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) to answer two questions. To what extent are women represented in the top-level administrative positions in municipal governments? And, are the impediments to women reaching the highest-level administrative posts in municipal governments related to the policy outputs and/or organizational cultures of these agencies? We find that (1) the underrepresentation of women in top-level administrative positions in distributive and regulatory agencies is pervasive across cities, suggesting that women continue to be confronted by the presence of glass ceilings in such agencies; and (2) even though women are well-represented among administrative cadres in redistributive agencies in many cities, their full representation at the uppermost administrative levels is still an elusive goal.For a complete reprint of this article contact Haworth Press by telephone (1-800-HAWORTH) or EMail (getinfo@haworthpressinc.com) Copies are available from: Haworth Document Delivery Center, The Haworth Press, Inc., 10 Alice Street, Binghamton, NY 13904-1580. Article copyright The Haworth Press, Inc.

title: Book Review: Encounters with Modern Ireland: A Sociological Chronicle 1995-1996
abstract: Peillon, Michel and Slater, Eamon (eds.), Encounters with Modern Ireland: A Sociological Chronicle 1995-1996, Dublin: Institute of Public Administration, 1998, x + 183 pp., paper IR£12.00.

title: CO-OPERATION AND COMPETITION IN A BUREAUCRACY
abstract: A study of productivity of individuals and groups related to an index of competition and co-operation, based on the performance of 12 interviewers in 2 small sections of a public employment agency. 'The extent to which an interviewer filled the vacancies he had received over the phone with his own clients in excess of chance expectations furnishes an index of competiveness'. Members of Section A were more competitive than those of B. The 2 groups differed with respect to 3 conditions: (1) security of employment, (2) opportunity for the development of a common professional orientation, and, (3) the evaluation practice of the supervisor. Most members of Section A had temporary civil service appointments. They were evaluated primarily on the number of placements made, and the Section did not develop a common professional code by which their behavior was governed. Section B tended toward the reverse of A in the above characteristics. Findings indicate that, though the competitive individuals have the highest productivity, the group with the greatest social cohesion and cooperation had the highest productivity record. The greater social cohesiveness reduced status anxiety, and increased productivity in Section B. 'In the absence of social cohesion, competitive striving for outstanding performance is an alternative way of relieving anxiety over status. This explains the paradox that competitiveness and productivity are inversely related for groups, but directly related for individuals in the competitive group'. D. E. Roos.

title: EQUALITARIANISM AND BUREAUCRATIC RECRUITMENT
abstract: Western society is distinguished by the convergence of 2 themes, equalitarianism (EQU) & bureaucracy (BUR), which appear in the practice of BUR'ic recruitment, according to classical org theory. This classical theory is challenged by empirical studies pointing up the limited scope, limited efficiency, & ambiguous goals of BUR'ic org. BUR'ic recruitment in thus seen as subject to non-EQU'ian, non-BUR'ic influences. Such influences are suggested in 2 forms: (1) EQU takes diff forms based on the SS of its advocates, & any given form is likely to reflect some advantage on those who support it. The, ideal of BUR'ic recruitment is of advantage to the Mc elements in society who have access & orientation to specialized training & credentials. (2) The efficiency of BUR'ic performance depends on common understandings & commitments which are inculcated by training agencies. These agencies are disposed to reward & encourage only certain types of individuals, once again those of the Mc. A soc structure which bases recruitment on skills alone is contemplated. 3 circumstances might give rise to it: (i) cultural homogeneity in the class structure, (ii) greater role for communal socializing agents (Sch system), & (iii) tolerance of greater strain within occup'al & professional systems. B. Beck.

title: The Political Role of the Judiciary: The Belgian Case
abstract: Traces the political vicissitudes of the administration of justice in Belgium & their connections with a range of phenomena: neglect by politicians; reactions of the judicial apparatus to a series of events & scandals; & several ineffective parliamentary investigation commissions. Partisan politicization of the magistrature is critiqued, finding that many contextual factors hinder a normal, acceptable process of politicization, eg, over- & underregulation, bad legislation, misconceived administration of justice & over judges, nondemocratic decision making, poor relationships. Recent governmental proposals are assessed, eg, improvement of criminal & judicial inquiries, foundation of a national advisory body for the magistrature, simplification of the legislation, & modernization of court activities. Whether it suffices to tinker with the system of the administration of justice alone is considered. The Belgian & Italian situations are compared. Adapted from the source document.

title: Selling the Unemployed: The Performance of Bureaucracies, Firms and Non-Profits in the New Australian "Market" for Unemployment Assistance
abstract: Major changes to the organization of welfare programs indicate the emergence of a new welfare state (NWS) model which claims to put an end to the traditional "one size fits all" ideal of universality & standardization. The stated aim of such arrangements is to improve service for the client, reduce costs for the taxpayer, & lift the performance of the system as a whole. The Labour government reform of the Australian employment assistance system between 1994 & 1996, & the Coalition's first modifications of this scheme in 1997, provide a means to investigate the performance of a NWS system which uses private & public agencies to provide a basic, mandatory employment assistance service. Using verified data on the comparative performance of public, private, & nonprofit agencies & qualitative data on a study of Best Practice among high-performing agencies, the study shows that this system produces greater service variation than the previous universal service system. Overall, the system also does better in achieving employment & education outcomes with long-term unemployed clients. However, the study shows that such outcomes differ between different classes of client & between different types of service provider. In particular, outcomes are lower for the more disadvantaged, & are higher for those who have training programs available to support them. 6 Figures, 41 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Looking Anew at Organizations and other Forms of Associations: Implications for Educational Leadership and Schools
abstract: This article reports out the results of employing a different lens through which to view common organizational forms, from bureaucracies to learning communities. Structural and processual aspects of the most common organizational forms are discussed. The article draws upon recent advances in the fields of primatology and neuro-psychology in its illumination of the characteristics and, especially, the hindrances of, for example, dominance and social status hierarchies. These different views of organizations and their forms hold immediate relevance for, especially, education, and for other forms of human association as well. Adapted from the source document.

title: Social Work -- A Profession?
abstract: In the context of external bureaucratization of British social work, evidenced by a loss of professional identity, particularly in terms of an inhibition of individual judgment & loss of the sense of possession of an inherited body of knowledge, it is argued that, among relevant models of social work intervention, the place of the treatment model has to be restored. Perhaps, ultimately, only professional self-regulation may restore the necessary conditions for offering effective professional service. Meanwhile, the endeavor to negotiate greater autonomy at a local level, & the recovery of a sense of professional history & inherited knowledge, could contribute much to restore the sense of professional identity essential to responsible practice. 34 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Canoe Racing Ritual of Luang Prabang
abstract: This article presents an analysis of the canoe racing ritual conducted in the Mekong and Nam Khan rivers bordering the town of Luang Prabang in North Laos as part of an annual ritual cycle. It focuses upon the ways in which the socio-political order, articulated in the ritual, is valorized in reference to a model of cosmological sovereignty that is manifested in offerings brought to aquatic spirit manifestations of a primordial King and his Queen-Consorts. It identifies the present-day changes in the ritual that have been implemented by the socialist Lao state as part of an endeavor to replace the principle of monarchic sovereignty with the authority of the state and to supplant the socio-cosmological understanding of society with a corporate model of bureaucracy and market economy variables. Adapted from the source document.

title: Political and Administrative Conditions in the Governors Office in Zulia State in Relation to Social Control
authors: Henriquez, Deyanira; Montes de Oca, Yorberth; Boscan, Elizabeth
abstract: In 1999 in Venezuela constitutional & legal bases were promoted for the purpose of contributing to a deepening of democracy & social justice. Among the transformations proposed were the incorporation of a social accounting of public management. The state governments in this process continue to be key elements for the national government in social, economic & political development in the country. The purpose of this paper is to explore the conditions of the Zulia State Governors office in the exercise of social accounting. The methodology was based the analysis of theoretical & judicial documents, as well as semi-structured interviews of officials in said governors offices. The results indicate that: 1) there is widespread incorporation of citizen rights & obligations in social control in the new legal framework, 2) citizens have rights to receive information in order to exert social control, 3) there is little action on the part of the regional governmental apparatus to apply this institutional framework due to political differences with the national government, 4) there is a lack of transparency on the part of state governors offices, which places obstacles in social accounting, & 5) there is an absence of training of government officials in the area of social control. The conclusion is that legal national & state conditions favor social control but Governors offices do not undertake actions that promote this practice. References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Rethinking "make do": Action "from the side" and the politics of segmentation in the Republic of Macedonia
abstract: In this article, I examine the social performance of bodily movement "from the side" in bureaucratic institutions in Macedonia, specifically, how locals use their bodies to weave their way in and out of insider outsider classifications that shape bureaucratic organization. Additionally, I explore how Macedonians and Albanians use, in common parlance, bodily movement "from the side" as a metaphor to lend different meanings to a new sociopolitical order wrought by the collapse of socialism. The case study of Macedonia helps refine theories of "make do" by pointing to the shifting degrees of insiderhood and outsiderhood within the body of insiders. Adapted from the source document.

title: Citizenship and Government: The Challenge for Management in the Public Domain
abstract: The domains of the public & private are different. Analysis of management that obscures their distinctive characteristics will miss the significance of each domain. Here, in an analysis of the values, institutional conditions, & management tasks unique to the public domain, it is argued that the distinctive challenge for this domain derives from the duality of publicness: the need to enable citizens in their plurality to express their contribution to the life of the community &, out of that plurality, to enable a process of collective choice & a government of action in the public interest. HA

title: Bureaucracy and Underdevelopment in Developing Societies: A Critical Review
abstract: In opposition to the dominant tendency in the current literature to highlight the favorable role of state bureaucracy in socioeconomic development, the adverse implications of such bureaucracy are examined here. The prevalent advocacy of privatization as a panacea to resolve bureaucratic problems is rejected, & alternative policy measures to transform this antidevelopmental state bureaucracy into an effective institution of development are prescribed. 101 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: New Experiences in the Labor Market Administrative Organizations. The Case of the Work Office
abstract: As part of the 1994 reforms of the Italian Labor Ministry for dealing with the multitude of regionally differentiated job markets, the market's diversification in both employment supply & demand, the availability of various job training programs, & the lack of regional uniformity in trade union-worker relations, state employment offices adopted greater organizational flexibility. In an effort to coordinate a national plan for guaranteeing impartial labor-market interventions, the restructuring of the employment office function introduces participatory management, & qualitative improvement of services offered. Drawing on their diversified backgrounds, the office's staff pools its efforts to build a clearinghouse of employment information from the contributions of a variety of professional & skilled work associations. The representative case of the Work Office in Ivrea, in the Piedmont region, is reviewed. J. Sadler

title: Constructing truths in a culture of disbelief: Understanding asylum screening from within
abstract: While a multitude of immigration officers enforce the numerous laws and policies regulating the arrival of asylum seekers, their work is often hidden from the public eye and ignored by academic debate, leaving fundamental questions unanswered: Is the migration debate blinded by bureaucracy or oblivious to the complexity of the asylum screening process? This article originates from an ethnographic study, which included over 80 interviews, six months of participant observation and four years of familiarization with the main actors, framed by a triangulation scheme that allowed in-depth exploration of the field from within. The study's conclusions expose how identifying immigration officers' subculture is key to understanding asylum controls and to reach beyond the legal shield and the rhetorical concepts of political debate. Based on this empirical research, this article exposes how officers' criteria for screening individuals are not derived from regulations or laws but their own categorizations, rules and values derived from ambiguous stereotypes nurtured by officers' experiences and social prejudices. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Chiefs in South Africa: law, power and culture in the post-apartheid era
abstract: Chapters 2 and 3 eloquently show how legal recognition of traditional leaders emerged not from one single factor, but from an interplay between global discourses on cultural diversity and decentralization, national party political interests, bureaucratic legacies, and the search for an African identity, made possible by the openings, and institutional and legal insecurities, of the democratic dispensation.

title: Spanish Coordination in the European Union: The Case of the Habitats Directive
abstract: Spain's successful negotiation of the habitats directive can be explained by the political salience of this particular issue (the priority attached to the strategy whereby the EU had to be convinced of the need to link environmental protection to the provision of special funds) & by the nature of the domestic political system, characterized by its powerful & autonomous executive & by the noncooperative system of interest intermediation. Above all, the triumph of the Spanish strategy is due to the ability of successive heads of government to tightly control leading EU issues by not allowing a highly departmentalized state administration & the regional governments to be too closely involved in community negotiations. The absence of formal mechanisms that would allow contending interest groups to partake in the decision process, thereby reducing time-consuming procedures & administrative costs, must also be taken into account. As a result, Europeanization has scarcely made any progress in Spain. 14 References. [Copyright 2003 Sage Publications, Inc.]

title: THE PHYSICIAN'S CHANGING HOSPITAL ROLE
abstract: Trends in the org'al structure of hosp's are changing the MD's role from unchallenged, charismatic master to some type of bur'tic function. The MD's previously commanding posture, the traditionally sanctuary & paternal nature of the hospital & the concept of the independent liberal professional are discussed. Following Weber's thesis that there must be a 'routinization of charisma,' the bur'tic route is seen as medicine's only possibility. Specialization, involving the concept of limited performance, is a major force promoting the MD's role shift. Another is the increasingly complex org'al nature of the hosp. The med practitioner must be subjected to 'labor disciplines.' Regulation stems from the hospital administrator, enjoying a growth of stature. Rational planning & control has also created new high-level admin'ive roles. Evidences of encroachment on the MD's power are the very existence of a 'problem' in authority relationships & the administrator's increased status. Also, the enhanced status of other specialists points to medicine as a team activity. Finally, Med sophistication & the routine use of hosp's by the public diminishes the MD's charisma. One locus of strain inheres in the diffusion & formalization of authority. Among probable new definitions of the MD, he is seen as becoming a team member in the hosp. Hughes notes the lack of congruence between the older image & the accepted model of other persons who work in largescale org's. Compensating for a presumed loss of therapeutic function, Galdston & others foresee the doctor developing as life counselor or generalist in psycho-social medicine outside the hosp. In the long-run the re-shaping of the MD's hospital role may afford a test of the limits in the bur'ization of the free professional. J. Field.

title: Customer Oriented Bureaucracy & Flexibility: Interactions & Implications in the Services Industry Context
abstract: Customer oriented bureaucracy is the creation of a fragile social order with dual imperatives of efficiency and customer focus. Human capital flexibility and flexible people management system are critical in the service industry due to the features of simultaneity, variability and intangibility. This paper emphasizes the need for flexibility as opposed to fit in handling the issues related to CoB (customer oriented bureaucracy). Together human capital flexibility and flexible people management practices can mitigate the ensuing tensions related to CoB and in turn have a positive effect on the firm performance. The paper also highlights that the dichotomy of customer oriented bureaucracy is experienced at both organizational and individual levels. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Current Relevance of Raymundo Faoro's Work
abstract: Raymundo Faoro, deceased in 2003, was one of the pioneers in the use of Max Weber's sociology for interpreting the formation of the Brazilian political system. In Os donos do poder (The Owners of Power), first published in 1958, Faoro launched the thesis that ever since its colonial period Brazil has always been dominated by a "bureaucratic stratum" with its origins in the peculiar characteristics of the Portuguese state, thus contradicting the previously dominant view that Brazil had experienced a feudal past dominated by traditional rural power. He thus opened the way for the Brazilian political system to be studied & interpreted in terms of its own political & institutional variables & no longer merely in terms of class interests & conflicts. However, according to Faoro, this domination by the bureaucratic stratum was a perennial, immutable characteristic of Brazil, a view that ended up limiting his analyses, even as he became an activist against all forms of Brazilian authoritarianism. 7 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Industrial Bureaucracy and Scientism. On the Relationship Between Administrative and Expertise Authority in Economic Enterprises
abstract: The diff's between expertise & admin'ive authority often lead to conflict & have a series of other disadvantages (eg, COMM barriers between experts & managers). It is hyp'ed that experts & specialists can be trained to make admin'ive decisions if admin itself is presented to them as a kind of expertise. 3 areas of decision-making in the econ enterprise are distinguished: manag, expertise areas, & the rank-&-file of workers & office employees. An analysis of aspects of bur'tic knowledge & expertise is offered, under reference to structural conditions. Sci'fic experts could be drawn into formulating alternative goals or define the goals of the enterprise, design long-term action-chains from the plans, & predict the possible consequences of certain goal constellations (risk & success probabilities, etc). Enterprises will increasingly become sci'ly run; the degree to which manag can preserve its decision-making power will depend on the lines it draws vs the experts & specialists. M. Maxfield.

title: Government and Urban Management in Morocco
abstract: Analyzes official state statistics, international funding group data, & recent studies to discuss the problem of urban management throughout Morocco due to decentralization & an increasingly transnational economy. Since the 1980s, Morocco has experienced a massive rural exodus to the cities as a result of economic & agricultural restructuring. But as the cities have grown larger, local & state governments have ignored expansion & refused to manage growth areas. In the case of Temara, an urban setting has evolved that has not even been granted the status of municipality, spurring a political battle between state & local authorities as the federal government becomes more & more decentralized & the urban poor are left socioeconomically marginalized. With the brunt of political management fragmented into local governments in the 1990s, Morocco stood unprepared for transnational economic assistance from international funding sources. Currently, it is up to local authorities, private sector investors, public action committees, & nongovernmental organizations to manage urban development & its international funding. 8 Tables, 1 Figure. Adapted from the source document.

title: Covering whoever is eligible? An exploratory study on the eligibility of the Urban Minimum Living Standard Guarantee in China
abstract: This article puts the policy goal of the Urban Minimum Living Standard Guarantee (UMLSG) in China into question and it aims to expose the assertion 'covering whoever is eligible' as a myth. An exploratory study of the implementation of the UMLSG eligibility criteria was launched in Guangzhou. Interviews were conducted with twenty-five poor people and local bureaucrats. In addition to people's meeting the income requirement, it was discovered that there were three unwritten principles flexibly used by local bureaucrats in assessment: the ability to work, the family unit and clientelism. The prevalence of street-level bureaucracy in the UMLSG administration not only hampered state resources from reaching the families living in urban poverty, but also seriously contradicted the reformulated ideologies and undermined the party's legitimacy. The findings of this study suggest that variations in UMLSG eligibility, which are causing a serious problem of under-coverage, should attract immediate attention from both officials and academics. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright holder.]

title: BRAZILIAN SENATE TRANSPARENCY: STRATEGIC ACTION AND INSTITUTIONAL JUSTIFICATIONS﻿
abstract: The present article analyzes the Brazilian Senate's digital transparency project, focusing on relationships between official policy, practical logic and justifications, and contextual factors that favor political debate over transparency and its respective strategic-institutional action project. The methodology employed combines in-depth interviews, document research and the analysis of information available on the Senate Transparency Website (http://www.senado.gov/transparencia). Theoretically embedded in political sociology, the research presented here reveals the existence of two rhetorical universes and a series of controversies sparked by polarization between the institution's president and the institutional-bureaucratic functionaries who are responsible for managing the institution's digital tools. The results reveal two principal functions of the Senate's transparency project: accountability and political propaganda. The first of these functions seeks to propagate political and administrative information while the second tries to promote the public reputation of the institution and its leaders.

title: BUREAUCRATIC MASS MEDIA: A STUDY IN ROLE DEFINITIONS
authors: Lystad, Mary H; Stone, Robert C
abstract: A study concerned with the characteristics of & importance attached to written documents in a bur as they are related to employees' role definitions. The res was undertaken in one city office of a state employment agency, which secures jobs for the unemployed & dispenses unemployment compensation. There is a discussion of content analysis of agency documents; employees' att's toward procedure, service & personalization; employee perceptions of daily tasks; & soc judgments of daily tasks. The official literature shows a dominant emphasis upon procedure & upon impersonality in soc relations. Employees' role definitions are weighted toward the norm of service & toward personalization of relations. Clerks manifest less emphasis on service & personalization in their roles than do supervisors & interviewers. 'It was concluded that the presence of clients serves to reinforce among employees an ideology of service which may conflict with procedural norms.' P. Widem.

title: Droit et cultures en sol français: Récits de femmes juives et musulmanes à l'aube et au crépuscule du divorce
abstract: This article is part of the existential questioning that every secular society is now undertaking to consolidate a harmonious living together. More specifically, it focuses on the normative role of civil law systems in relation to religious law and the impact of religious rules on women in the context of French society. The adepts of strict secularism in the French generally link these two premises by the following correlation: religious rules oppress women and must consequently be removed from the administration of civil justice. In order to provide a critical analysis of this position, this article is based on field research among French Jewish and Muslim women who have navigated through civil and religious legal systems in divorce proceedings. Interviews with the women involved in this debate, although not an exhaustive sample, suggest that the total evacuation of all religious rights is based on an inadequate and inadequate understanding of the actual scope of religious rules. The testimonies reported in this article evoke a counter narrative relevant to pro-secular republican discourse and demonstrate that religious norms can be used, manipulated and reappropriated by women for emancipatory purposes that civil law does not necessarily allow. This observation does not affect the normative objectives of secularism. However, he warns against the excessive simplification of the relationship between women and religion and advocates an understanding.

title: Sociology -- Mayors and Money: Fiscal Policy in New York and Chicago by Ester R. Fuchs / Holding Bureaucrats Accountable: Politicians and Professionals in St. Louis by Lana Stein
abstract: Review.

title: Overview of tertiary public policy training in South Africa
abstract: This article deals with the contents and delivery of public policy education and training programmes at South African higher education institutions. It first conceptualises public policy, then identifies the prevailing best practices in public policy training internationally to establish benchmarks against which the South African situation can be assessed. The contents and delivery of public policy training programmes in South Africa are then summarised and assessed against these benchmarks. Public policy programmes are presented in various faculties, not only in public administration or public management departments, but in many political science departments, as well as specialised sectoral programmes. Training programmes normally consist of academic education programmes for full-time students at undergraduate and postgraduate level, as well as short in-service executive training programmes for mid-career professionals in public sector agencies and organisations. These are presented part time or in the form of a block release programme, through face-to-face residential teaching or distance learning modes. The contents of policy curricula are normally constructed around one or more international texts or domestically published texts, mostly following a policy procedural approach that conceives, describes, analyses and assesses the public policy process as consecutive, but inter-linked stages. These curricula are sometimes purely theoretical and in other cases are illustrated with practical examples. The nature, focus and contents of South African public policy programmes are generally in line with international standards. Local programmes are diverse and heterogeneous, although the policy process or sectoral policy foci are always the hub. A better balance between content and procedure should be established for a more accurate perspective on public policy. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Political Management of Change in Urban Retailing
abstract: This article deals with changing relations between retailing & the town. It focuses on the implications of changes that have arisen over the last 30 years & on the processes that have generated such transformations -- or, to be more precise, on the role that policies may have played in the way change is conducted. The analysis examines the trend toward homogenization, on the world scale, of the way towns are being reconfigured: the development that locates large stores in distended, mono-functional, off-center zones; the reshaping of neighborhoods, which now tend to be defined solely by the notion of accessibility; town-center crisis & the selective rehabilitation of some town centers; & the decay of public spaces. It goes on to express reservations about the use of the term "Americanization" to describe this movement, & then attempts to evaluate how far national laws & local administrations are likely to produce significant spatial, social, & cultural differences. To achieve these aims, it adopts an approach that compares situations & practices from one country to another (in Europe & in North America), as well as from one town to another. 4 Tables, 4 Figures, 2 Appendixes, 87 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucratic Effects: 'Weberian' State Agencies and Poverty Reduction
authors: Henderson, Jeffrey; Hulme, David; Jalilian, Hossein; Phillips, Richard
abstract: Evans and Rauch (1999) have demonstrated that there is a strong relationship between the `Weberianness' of a national state's bureaucratic capacities and its record on economic growth. Using their data set and the best available data sets on the incidence of income poverty, this article investigates whether there is a relationship between a Weberian notion of effective bureaucratic capacities and the state's ability to reduce poverty. Using the same time frame as Evans and Rauch (1970-90) and analysing data for 29 developing and middle income countries, the article concludes that, in general, there does indeed seem to be a relationship between states with effective `Weberian' public institutions and their ability to reduce poverty. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright 2007 BSA Publications Ltd.]

title: Health Care and Cancer Screening Experience of Chinese Immigrants in New York City: A Qualitative Study
abstract: The purpose of this exploratory study was to assess the health care and cancer screening experience of Chinese immigrants in New York City and identify health care delivery system barriers to cancer education and screening activities. A qualitative, exploratory research methodology based on a grounded theory approach was used. Thirty-nine low-income and medically underserved Chinese men and women participated in 4 focus group sessions and 14 in-depth interviews. Findings revealed numerous barriers experienced by participants: red tape and bureaucracy in the health care system, provider insensitivity to their concerns, lack of availability in doctor schedule, long waiting time in clinics, and fragmentation of the medical care system. This study highlighted the importance of cultural relevancy and appropriateness in the design and implementation of effective cancer screening programs for this population. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Articulation of Labor Logics and Domestic Logics in an Employment Policy for Young People in Argentina. Individual Autonomy and Personal Ties in the World of Work
abstract: This paper analyzes the main youth employment policy in Argentina: the youth with more and better work program. Based on the paradigm of active employment policies, this program illustrates a new form of management and state regulation regarding the problematic question of employment among the poorer sectors of the population. For the analysis, the authors begin by exploring the theoretical possibilities opened up by Foucault's notion of the 'device,' and then point out some disarray concerning the logics, the division between 'domestic' and 'work' areas, and models of person (individual or linked) that this policy seeks to impose in the labor practices and trajectories of young people in low-income sectors. Finally, they note the need to incorporate the notion of instruments of reproduction and social capital to account for the singular character of the practical logic these young people apply in order to enter into and to be in the world of work. Adapted from the source document.

title: THE ARMY AND BUROCRACY
abstract: An examination is made of the relations between the army & bur'cy-first offered as a paper at the 6th Congress of the Internat'l Sociol'al Assoc at Evian in 1966. The starting point is a contention that the phenomenon of technology affects bur'cy not only in the sphere of business & industry but also in other areas, such as the military. A number of definitions of bur'cy are quoted, & it is concluded that the bur'tic phenomenon is linked with the structure of org's. Bur'cy operates in functional & dysfunctional ways. The process of technologizations of bur'cies has some dysfunctional aspects, notably its favoring of a bur'tic monopoly. Military bur'cy shares certain characteristics with other types of bur'cy, eg secrecy & conservatism. One of its distinctive features is a special kind of discipline. Technologization has produced a harmonization between the army & other types of bur'cy, eg the armed forces of the US are increasingly run along 'business' lines. The effects of technologization of military bur'cy are judged to be positive, inasmuch as they tend to lower its aggressive tensions. I. Langnas.

title: Max Weber and the Complexity of Parliamentary Democracy: Applying Formal and Substantive Rationality to the English and Welsh Education Policy-Making Process
abstract: This article illustrates the importance of Max Weber's attitude to both bureaucratic & political functions. Formal & substantive rational concepts are applied to distinguish the actions of education civil servants & politicians in relation to education policy making. Evidence is taken from English & Welsh Educational & Public Administration Parliamentary Select Committees of the 1970s & the present day. We gain from Weber's ideas a relevant framework to critique the relationship & the significantly historical & contemporary roles of education civil servants & politicians. The article demonstrates that a change has occurred with more substantive inputs visible within both the education relationship & general policy-making processes. The article further argues that Parliamentary Select Committees are crucial in questioning both formal & substantive influences within parliamentary democracy. Adapted from the source document.

title: Differential Treatment and Communicative Interactions: Why the Character of Social Interaction is Important
abstract: Regulatory studies have traditionally focused on external political and administrative factors when explaining the behavior of regulatory inspectors. This is, however, only one part of the story about regulatory behavior. To understand the behavior of street-level bureaucrats such as regulatory inspectors, it is essential to look not only at external political and administrative factors but also at the very interaction between the bureaucrat and the client. By focusing on differential treatment of regulated firms by inspectors and the explanatory power of the interaction between inspector and firm, the article shows that variation in the level of communication between inspector and regulatee helps to explain variation in regulatory leniency. The higher the level of communication, the more lenient is the inspector. Tables, Figures, References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Government and Governability in the Public Universities. Concepts, Problems and an Agenda for Investigation
abstract: Analyzes a 1992 law in Colombia designed to standardize the governing structure of the country's public universities while increasing the diversity of their governmental aims & decisions. The general condition of public university administrations prior to 1992 is described, highlighting the clientelism, inefficiency, & corruption that plagued higher education in Colombia. Problems after the law was initiated centered on rectorship elections marked by coercion, character attacks, economic extortion, favoritism, & even threats of violence. Nonetheless, the law is perceived as a way toward vast improvement once institutional development is established as a force able to promote a culture of innovation within Colombian academia. An agenda for investigating ways to improve governability is outlined, featuring means for refining decision-making councils, procedures, elections, & links between students & community support. D. Bajo

title: Urban Management, Local Government Reform and the Democratisation Process in Mozambique: Maputo City 1975-1990
abstract: The urban management of Mozambique's capital was reorganized at independence to reflect the priorities of the ruling Frelimo Party. Heralded as constituting a radical break with the past, many of the new structures & practices of local management demonstrated striking continuities with the colonial corporatist political culture inherited from the Portuguese administration. The highly centralized structures & complicated lines of responsibility introduced by the new administration proved unworkable in the face of generalized economic collapse & war. The agenda for the current reconstruction of city administration is being set largely by the international community & is aimed at more effective management practices. It is unclear whether the outcome will bring greater local accountability. Adapted from the source document.

title: Participatory Management and Evaluation of Social Policies
abstract: The article reviews the concepts, speeches & practices related to social participation from international organizations, governments, & the organized society in Latin America & Mexico. It looks at relevant participation experiences developed in other countries. It also contributes with a synthesis of the latest developments in the Canadian case in order to through light to the alternatives to be considered while designing national strategies. Adapted from the source document.

title: Performance measurement and the informatisation of services in judiciary systems. An assessment from Europe to Italy
abstract: At the end of the Nineties, policies and projects aimed at improving the quality of justice in the name of efficiency and accountability were introduced within many European national judicial systems. This happened with a decade of delay in respect to other sectors of the public administration. These types of policies were mainly focused on the one hand, on the evaluation of judges and courts performances and, on the other hand, on the introduction of ICTs in the judicial systems. Nowadays, after a decade from the introduction of these innovations, the available data and studies show that, only in a few cases, these policies were successful in introducing significant changes and quality improvements. Moreover, in many cases, these expensive projects were interrupted, during the implementation stage, without any result. On the basis of these assumptions, this article aims to present some examples of projects and policies introduced in some European countries. These examples have been selected as they allow to underline both critical and positive factors that influenced the policies implementation processes and, consequently, their results. The overall aim of the article is to emphasize that, also in the justice sector, as well as in other public administration sectors, the introduction of managerial tools and paradigms did not always provide the expected results. In many cases, during formulation and in the implementation stages, the peculiar organizational characteristics of the judicial sector were overlooked, opting for a standardized managerial approach, with the consequent lower results. Adapted from the source document.

title: Administrative Responsiveness to the Disadvantaged: The Case of Children's Health Insurance
abstract: Issues of administrative responsiveness to the disadvantaged (as distinct from formal policy responsiveness) possess important implications for American democracy. In this regard, the administrative practices that facilitate or impede enrollment, or take-up, in social programs deserve attention. This study focuses on two means-tested programs in the context of American federalism, Medicaid & the State Children's Health Insurance Program. Based on an in-depth analysis of seventeen states, we develop an index of administrative responsiveness to the disadvantaged related to take-up. We then explore some possible sources of variation in responsiveness rooted in the task environment, political ideology, good government culture & practice, & signals from political principals. Our findings point to the need to refine & expand upon existing explanations of state variation in social programs. Among other things, this study suggests the political importance of international (not interstate) population mobility & gubernatorial leadership (rather than bureaucratic autonomy) in shaping administrative responsiveness to the disadvantaged. It also points to the need for a contingent approach in examining whether the greater presence of racial minorities tends to depress such responsiveness. Tables, References. Adapted from the source document.

title: A Profile of the Higher Public Servant in the Nigerian Government
abstract: Results of a questionnaire survey conducted in 1982 in 4 Nigerian states are used to compile a profile of a high-level bureaucrat (N = 44 federal & state bureaucrats). The sample responded to questions addressing issues of education, religious affiliation, social behavior, mobility, & how they view their roles in decision & policy making. The findings indicate that the higher public servant is predominantly: male, Christian, well-educated, religious but not dogmatic or fanatical, & a community leader.
