Results indicated that formal hierarchical decision making & affective responses were significantly related to various stages in the innovation process. Participation by all physicians in strategic decisions was negatively related to each phase in the innovation process. By contrast, organization size, complexity, formalization, & person specialization were not related to innovation activity. It is speculated that minimal bureaucratization may be necessary to move the innovation process in differentiated professional groups. 3 Tables. Modified HA.

title: In search of the glass ceiling: gender and recruitment to management in Norway's state bureaucracy
abstract: There are still fewer female than male managers in Norway's state bureaucracy. This article asks if there are organizational barriers which prevent women from entering these positions. Is there really a glass ceiling, or must one look outside the organizational environment to find an explanation? Is it rather the case that the scarcity of female managers is caused by women's own preferences or their life situations outside work? Or do both contribute to the situation? The study shows that female managers are treated just as well as male managers in central parts of the state bureaucracy. Employers give equal shares of respect and attention to both genders. Female managers are encouraged to apply for the same number of jobs as men and are offered an equal number of jobs as men when they apply; in fact, women are offered more jobs than men, when one controls for the number of job applications. This indicates that organizational barriers are not the problem. The study also shows that there are no differences in work orientation between male and female managers. Female managers are just as ambitious as male managers. Nor do female managers find it more difficult than male managers to combine work and family life. So, how can one explain the low number of female managers? The study shows that one reason can be that female managers apply for management jobs less often than in their male colleagues. The cause of this seems to be anticipated discrimination rather than lack of ambition or self-confidence. However, this slows down women's movement into higher management positions in the state bureaucracy. Adapted from the source document.

title: Writing against identity politics: An essay on gender, race, and bureaucratic pain
abstract: Equating bureaucratic entanglements with pain -- or what, arguably, can be seen as torture -- might seem strange. But for single Mizrahi welfare mothers in Israel, somatization of bureaucratic logic as physical pain precludes the agency of identity politics. This essay elaborates on Don Handelman's scholarship on bureaucratic logic as divine cosmology and posits that Israel's bureaucracy is based on a theological essence that amalgamates gender and race. The essay employs a world anthropologies' theoretical toolkit to represent bureaucratic torture in multiple narrative modes, including anger, irony, and humor, as a counterexample to dominant U.S.-U.K. formulae for writing and theorizing culture. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Organizational Environments and Organizational Discourse: Bureaucracy between Two Worlds
abstract: Contends that differences in European & US organizational discourses result from differences in the institutional & cultural conditions under which formal organizations emerged. In Europe, conditions favored a centralized, hierarchical, obedience-based organizational form. The US, which was characterized by large businesses operating in volatile markets under a cultural imperative of equality, developed organizations that were flatter, less hierarchical, & based on temporary contract. This explains why Max Weber's theory of bureaucracy (which was based on European observations) was often rejected by US researchers, who developed a distinct organizational discourse. Implications for comparative research are discussed. 78 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Splintering urbanism: Networked infrastructures, technological mobilities and the urban condition
abstract: Coutard reviews "Splintering urbanism:  Networked infrastructures, technological mobilities and the urban condition" by Stephen Graham and Simon Marvin.

title: Information Systems and Organizational Changes in a Large Metallurgical Enterprise
authors: Baldissera, Alberto; Bravo, Gian Luigi; Luciano, Adriana; Pichierri, Angelo; Saccomani, Edda
abstract: An extensive study is presented of the relationship between the technological system--means of production, production technology, products, etc--& the org, authority structure & power of a large metallurgical Co. A Foreword by Gian Luigi explains that the analysis is based on general systems theory applied to decision-making processes. The study is presented in V Parts: (1) Introduction--explains res subject & scope, the basic structure of the Co examined, & the Co's plans for setting up a new information system. (2) The Information System--discusses the present state of these plans, the innovations already introduced, their effect, & the shifts in power, decision-making & worker participation in manag which have resulted. A conflict situation exists at present between workers & manag re the validity of the innovations adopted. General manag has adopted an att of restraint. (3) Supplies--deals with the org'al levels in the Co (the plant, top manag, section heads, middle & low manag), & how they cope with the supply situation & policy. All levels have expressed criticism of the present supply situation; it has been felt that the policies adopted have made the Co more vulnerable to changed market conditions, introduced irrationality into purchasing procedures, & had negative effects on the quality of purchases. The perceptions of & att's toward the use of sci'fic information systems of the diff manag levels are discussed. (4) Personnel--analyzes the increasing marginality of the personnel office of the plant. This part of the Co structure was marginal to begin with, but became more so as the planning & partial realization of the new information systems progressed. Its intervention in various decision areas has decreased as a result of its limited awareness of the implications of the new systems. (5) Conclusions--indicates that the introduction of the new information systems represents a global response on the part of the org to the growing complexity of Co operations & control. The Co is in a phase of transition to modernization which contains certain risks, eg, the risk of too rigid a centralization, putting limits on the exp'ing & learning possible for local units. Modified Author's Summary.

title: What Went Wrong? Lessons Learned from a Failed Group Intervention at a Family Company
abstract: This article analyses the failure of an intervention made by a group in the management team of a family company to improve its workplace relations. The concepts discussed in this article include regression and paranoia genesis, fantasies of personality dissolution, imbalance between constructive and destructive forces, an illusory sense of equality and the anti-group. For the analysis, the author considers ideology, bureaucratization and characteristics of the setting, as well as the conductors' focus and verbal interventions. The analysis reveals that the conductors failed to create a safe atmosphere that could contain destructive emotions and impulses. The conductors did not sufficiently stimulate or reinforce connections among the participants, positively connote the processes observed or formulate appropriate interpretations. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright The Group-Analytic Society.]

title: Enchanting bureaucracy: Symbolic violence and the (re)production of charismatic authority in a police apparatus
abstract: This article dissects the role of culture in securing authority relations within a militarized police apparatus. Adding structure and power to the symbolic interactionist approach to organizational culture and interests and positionality to the structural functionalist perspective on militarized organizations, the author examines how, through the preservation and imposition of a sacralized worldview and morality (symbolic violence), police officers -- the commanding caste of a two-tiered type of police organization -- manage to charismatically legitimate the internal distribution of authority and its exercise in the relations between commanding officers and the non-commissioned officers, turning sheer bureaucratic authority into charismatic power (symbolic power). The author draws on ethnographic observations, interview data, and a structural-semantic analysis to reconstruct the system of beliefs involved and to describe the practices and mechanisms through which intra-bureaucratic domination is charismatically legitimated and made effective. These processes are examined both in everyday relations of command and in the extraordinary event of a police mutiny. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Bureaucrats and Politicians: A Case Study of the Determinants of Perceptions of Conflict and Patronage in the Greek Bureaucracy under PASOK Rule, 1981-1989
abstract: Interview data are used to compare the influence of organizational & sociopolitical factors on the perceptions of 152 Greek top civil servants & political appointees of the PASOK party, governing in Greece 1981-1989. The modern Greek bureaucracy is placed in historical perspective & described as a case of politicized bureaucracy, ridden by party patronage. Multivariate logistic regression analysis reveals that organizational role is the main predictor of perceptions of consensus or conflict in intrabureaucratic relations, & political party affiliation is the main predictor of perceptions of patronage in the bureaucracy. 5 Tables, 31 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Role of Text in the Processing of People in Organizations
abstract: An examination of the micro processes that comprise the daily operations of formal organizations charged with processing people, with attention to the role of bureaucratic texts. The background knowledge & information that personnel possess are treated as resources upon which personnel can selectively draw to accomplish their processing of cases. Examining the presentence reports filed by probation officers in a county probation department, it is shown that the structure & content of these reports are explained by various formal & informal protocols possessed by officers; officers selectively use this knowledge in order to accomplish their work. Also important are the roles that officers play within the justice system & the position they occupy vis-a-vis judges. It is argued that the analysis presented here can be used to examine bureaucratic texts produced by other personnel in other kinds of people-processing organizations. Such an analysis allows the researcher to discover important information about the routine social action of personnel as well as the knowledge that makes possible & constrains these actions. 2 Figures, 18 References. Modified HA

title: Passive and Active Representation in the Federal Service: A Comparison of Blacks and Whites
authors: Rosenbloom, David H; Featherstonhaugh, Jeannette G
abstract: Sociological representation in a bureaucracy can serve as a prerequisite to greater representation in an active sense of the social groups from which the bureaucrats come. Regardless of rank & seniority in the federal bureaucracy, black bureaucrats differ in their attitudes toward politics from white bureaucrats. Moreover, there is a marked congruence between the attitudinal patterns of black bureaucrats & blacks in the society as a whole. The study is based on 1969 data. 2 Tables. AA.

title: Thinking about Ecology: Cognition of Pacific Northwest Forest Managers across Diverse Institutions
authors: Richardson, Catherine Woods; Lee, Robert G; Miller, Marc L
abstract: Analysis of interview data from 48 forest managers in the Dungeness River watershed (WA) revealed four main cognitive models of its forest ecology. Organizing principles for the four models were the wilderness concept, timber management, forests as habitat or home for humans & animals, & a bureaucratic orientation incorporating forest regulation & policy. Managers' ecological cognitions varied with multiple personal, institutional, & cultural influences. Managers with a wilderness orientation represented a common wilderness-civilization dichotomy in US thought, while cognition of managers with a timber orientation appeared to be largely a product of professional training. Habitat orientation coincided with a close economic relationship to the land, ie, direct use of land for subsistence of income as a farmer or logger. Bureaucractic orientation appeared to develop with experience as a middle or upper manager in public agencies. Considerable diversity in ecological cognition appeared within forest management institutions. This contradicts previous research suggesting that managers in the same institutions become homogenized in their thought. 1 Table, 5 Figures, 34 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: North Korea in the World: Plus Ca Change?
abstract: While North Korea remains an Orwellian nightmare, the impact of cell phones and greater access to computers and other information sources can only erode the regime's centralized controls. Dynasties, bureaucracies, and political systems may hold fast, but surely the personality of the central dynasty is an important variable -- one that can change the game in fundamental ways. Thus, Kim Jong-il seemed introverted but calculated in his decision-making. His son appears far more extroverted and -- at least to some outsiders -- reckless in both internal and foreign affairs. If pushed too far, its leaders might try to oust the last remnant of the Kim dynasty and introduce a more sober form of governance. While most of the work reviewed in this article looks at North Korea from the top down, the unfailingly brilliant essays in Non-Traditional Security examine the linkages between state-centric security and human security issues such as gender, energy, and food. Adapted from the source document.

title: ESSENTIAL PROBLEMS IN THE FUNCTIONING OF THE PRISON AS A FORMAL-BUREAUCRATIC ORGANIZATION
abstract: THE BASIC PRINCIPLES OF BUREAUCRACY (ACCORDING TO M. WEBER) ARE GUIDELINES TO THE STRUCTURE & FUNCTIONING OF ALL THE VARIOUS FORMAL SOCIAL ORGANIZATIONS. THE PRISON, AS A COERCIVE TOTAL INSTITUTION, IS ANALYZED IN THE LIGHT OF THESE PRINCIPLES. AMONG OTHER THINGS, SPECIAL ATTENTION IS PAID TO THE FOLLOWING ASPECTS: THE PROBLEM OF POWER & LEADERSHIP INSIDE THE PRISON, THE INMATES' WORLD & THEIR ADJUSTMENT, THE ROLE OF THE DIFFERENT GROUPS OF WORKERS IN THE PRISON, & THE STAFF IN THIS SPECIAL SETTING. ONLY A SMALL PART OF THE BUREAUCRATIC PRINCIPLES CAN BE STRICTLY FULFILLED IN PRISON. THE BUREAUCRATIC PATTERNS ARE EFFICIENT ONLY TO A CERTAIN EXTENT BEYOND WHICH IT IS THE DEVIATION FROM THESE PRINCIPLES WHICH CONTRIBUTES TO THE PROPER FUNCTIONING OF THE PRISON. SOME DATA ON THE PRISONS IN ISRAEL ARE PRESENTED & THE NEED FOR RESEARCH ON THIS TOPIC IN ISRAEL IS EMPHASIZED. 1 TABLE. MODIFIED HA.

title: 'Rights' in the grey area: undocumented border crossers on Lesvos
abstract: The Aegean island of Lesvos is one of the gateways that refugees and undocumented border crossers use for entering European territory. This study deals with two phenomena related to border crossings on Lesvos: first, the efforts of those arriving to be placed in the status of 'administrative detention' in order to receive an expulsion order and then be able to continue their journey; and, second, the activity of the local solidarity network, which initially established an open reception centre for refugees and undocumented immigrants under the umbrella of the civil society, until some activists agreed to put this project under the jurisdiction of the state authorities. In reflecting on these developments, the author addresses two major issues: first, immigration imprisonment as a facet of 'positive power' in the Foucauldian sense, and the possible relationship of the latter to grassroots humanitarian commitment; and, second, specific facets of the current paradigm of immigration imprisonment that can help explain why detention may be interpreted as a right by refugees and immigrants. The author argues that the humanitarianism that arises in the interface of surveillance and the provision of care demonstrates post-bureaucratic features; and further, that the strategy pursued by refugees and undocumented immigrants shows how limited their scope is for asserting any rights, given the intensified augmentation of border surveillance worldwide.

title: The Bureaucracy of Race: Enforcement of Civil Rights Laws and Its Impact on People, Process and Organization
abstract: A study of bur'cy, race & civil rights in the "racial bur'cy," the municipal, county, state, & federal civil rights agencies. The internal HR of the racial bur'cy is studied, ie, to what extent is it diff from the general bur'cy in US gov, & what kinds of interpersonal, racial, & programmatic conflict & strain occur in civil rights agencies peculiar to the racial bur'cy. The racial bur'cy is defined: it usually attempts to maintain a 50-50 black white ratio, & it is exclusively concerned with race, or aimed at improving race relations; many have a law enforcement function, & many have been involved in intense debate, conflict & racial disagreement in the community. It is pointed out that given a deep-rooted problem, & the impressive & seemingly vigorous mandate, racial bur'cies never get the kind of resources to carry out an adequate, vigorous program. The problem of affirmative action & the "hidden program" is discussed. The status of black bur'crats within the agencies is also treated. It is felt that there are 2 major consequences of the racial strain & conflict: (1) Bur'crats become more militant, more disillusioned, angrier than the black pop at large as a result of the frustration, the failure, & the rhetoric of their work experience. (2) Bur'crats deal with the hostility & frustration by a process of intense self-flagellation, & a continual testing of their bur'cies. E. Weiman.

title: A NOTE ON THE APPEARANCE OF WISDOM IN LARGE BUREAUCRATIC ORGANIZATIONS
authors: Deutsch, Karl W; Madow, William A
abstract: An important test for the promotion of an individual to higher rank in a large bur'tic org, civilian or military, is often his record of `wisdom,' that is, of having chosen repeatedly the correct alternative in a series of relevant decisions. A calculation of mathematical probabilities shows that for a small number of decisions of over-riding importance, any large bur'tic org should be expected to have in its ranks at any time several officials with an unbroken record of correct judgments for this limited series of decisions. Thus if there are 8 important decisions, each consisting of a single yes or no choice, & if there are more than 28 or 256 officials in this org, & if the effects of statistical variation are disregarded, then at least one official is likely to obtain a perfect record of wise choices on these 8 decisions by pure chance. Formulas are given connecting the number of relevant decisions, officials, relevant alternatives in each decision & the expectable numbar of spurious wise men in the org. Slightly more detailed computations of the expectable number of such men are then given for diff assumptions, taking into account the effects of statistical variation. The actual excellence or inferiority of the decision record of the aggregate staff of a large org can then be found by subtracting the expectable number of correct decisions produced by chance from the number of correct decisions made on the same issues by the officials of the org. Genuinely correct decisions, based on some relatively permanent personal quality of the decision-maker, are thus inevitably contaminated by an appreciable amount of spurious correct decisions based on chance. Promotion policies based on successful answers to a small number of overridingly important tests may thus result in the preferment of mediocrities or incompetents. This contamination effect of the high ranks of any large & long-established bur will be higher if the number of test decisions relevant for preferment are not numerous & are very diff in kind from the ordinary run of decisions in routine practice. Increasing the number of test situations will reduce the contamination effect but if the additional test situations are not relevant for the chief interests of the org they will introduce another type of contamination, since preferment would now go more often to those of tested competence in trivia or routine matters. Personnel policies based on performance in crisis decisions thus carry a signif & measurable margin of error. AA.

title: The Politics of Bureaucratization and the U.S. Bureau of Corporations
abstract: The US Bureau of Corporations, which existed from 1903 to 1914, is examined in the context of the transition from an electoral to a bureaucratic mode of politics. The rise of the Bureau is explained, in part, by conflict within the capitalist class over the relationship between the state & the economy, resulting in a protobureaucratic organization incapable of solving the problem it was mandated to address. It lacked the antitrust power desired by small businessmen but failed to rationalize the economy as desired by corporate capitalists. Its incomplete bureaucratization was a result of this conflict, but also sustained the level of conflict. By the second decade of the century, the early supporters of the Bureau had abandoned it in favor of creating the Federal Trade Commission, which was vested with more formal authority than the Bureau, but, because of its more bureaucratic structure, was endowed with greater autonomy from instrumental political influence. The result was to depoliticize the antitrust impulse. The relationship between SC conflict & the historical construction of state autonomy is also discussed. HA.

title: Administration, Sociology, Law
authors: Pavlov, I V; Kazimirchuk, V P; Bobotov, S V; Zavadsky, S; Lebedev, M P; Safarov, R A; Seyukov, F T; Shneyder, Kh Kh
abstract: A Vol in 5 Chpts, with an Introduction & a Conclusion, on the ways & means of conducting many-faceted res on the socio-legal forms of admin'ive activities, with special attention paid to gov. (1) "Gosudarstvennoye upravleniye kak sotsiologicheskaya problema" (Government as a Sociological Problem)--examines the specific features of the sociol'al study of gov, the role of prediction in gov, the methodology of studying problems of gov. (2) "Pravovye faktory upravleniya" (Legal Factors in Government)--examines laws & legal acts in their capacity as gov decisions, sfa of state decisions, the role of the legal factor in the org of gov. (3) "Sotsialno-psikhologicheskiye faktory upravleniya" (Socio-Psychological Factors of Administration)--discusses the signif of socio-psychol'al factors in executive work, & the role of socio-psychol'al interests in the admin of production collectives. (4) "Deputatskaya deyatelnost v sisteme upravleniya gosudarstvom" (The Work of Elected Members of Legislative Bodies in Government)--examines the sociol'al aspects of the work of elected members of legislative bodies & the sociol'al study of the functional problems of local elected gov bodies. (5) "Kollektiv i problemy upravleniya" (The Collective and Management Problems)-- examines the soc-legal aspects of the manag of production collectives & the sociol'al study of forms of manag in collective farms. 20 Tables, No Index. M. Mackler.

title: REACTIONS TO A STUDY OF BUREAUCRACY AND ALIENATION
abstract: A critique of C. M. Bonjean & M. D. Grimes, see SA 0312/ E0856. An attempt is made to show that the non-signif findings of the study of bur'cy & alienation are largely due to inadequacies of res design, instrumentation, theoretical direction, & methods of statistical analysis. An alternate mode of data analysis is suggested for the Bonjean-Grimes data as a guide to other res'ers seeking more powerful means of investigating the effects of org'al structures on individuals. AA.

title: How agrarian cooperatives fail: Lessons from 1970s Peru
abstract: Given current interest in the agrarian cooperative as an egalitarian institutional form to counter the economic effects of neoliberalism, considered here is how class divisions/distinctions operated inside one such unit in the 1970s. Of particular interest is the way idioms and forms of struggle used by bureaucrats, peasants and agricultural labourers in a Peruvian agrarian cooperative during that decade challenge one of the enduring myths of development theory. The latter invokes a familiar dichotomy to explain the failure of rural cooperatives: a powerful state bureaucracy imposing inappropriate policy on an undifferentiated and uniformly powerless peasantry. The case study presented here suggests that, on a number of crucial issues (privatization of co-owned means of production, the employment of labour-power that was unfree), it was much rather better-off peasants who overruled bureaucrats and imposed their own accumulation project. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Ethnicity, Bureaucracy and State-Building in Africa and Latin America
abstract: To understand the state-building process, ethnicity must be explicitly considered. In Africa & Latin America, state-builders, regardless of the level of statism on which the polity currently operates, use ethnicity to promote their political objectives. To understand the expansion & centralization of state institutions, the linkage between ethnic groups & political change must be examined. Although ethnicity may be discussed in terms of the rationalist-functional & representative models of state bureaucracy, this is not satisfactory. A more appropriate model needs to stress the power & systemic dimensions of bureaucracies. M. Migalski.

title: THE INDIGENOUS NONPROFESSIONAL IN THE SOCIAL SERVICE BUREAUCRACY: A CRITICAL EXAMINATION
abstract: A major conceptual reason for the use of indigenous or lowincome nonprofessionals in soc service agencies is that they bring an authority or expertise by virtue of their indigenous skills & characteristics not ordinarily present in agencies which will improve the scope & quality of agency service delivery. However, aside from some questionable assumptions regarding the genotypical characteristics of the poor, an analysis of the selection & training processes & methods used by agencies to structurally integrate the nonprofessional into the agency indicates that such methods generally should result in a loss of the valued indigenous skills. The article addresses 2 modalities for maintaining the indigenous characteristics: (1) the team approach, & (2) compartmentalization; & concludes that compartmentalization offers a more viable shortrun approach to the maintenance of indigenous skills. AA.

title: Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Policies -- The Relevance of a Dead German
abstract: Places affirmative action & equal opportunity policies in the context of organization theory by relating these policies to the ideal type of bureaucracy as described by Max Weber as well as his conception of rational action. A main argument is that affirmative action & equal opportunity policies have contradictory implications for the ideal type of bureaucracy. Further, acceptance of affirmative action, in particular, may require transcending Weber's conceptual scheme. These ideas are illustrated by means of a consideration of the South African Employment Equity Act (1998). 1 Table, 26 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Nature and Role of Bureaucracy in Bangladesh during the Mujib Regime
abstract: An in-depth chronicle of the role of the Bangladeshi bureaucracy during the regime of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman (Mujib) & his political party, the Awami League, 1971-1975, following years of colonial British rule. After reviewing Max Weber's theory of bureaucracy, & noting basic continuity of personnel & structure between British & Bangladeshi bureaucracies, events leading to the coup d'etat that deposed Mujib are sketched. Mujib failed both to exert political control through the Awami League & to control the bureaucracy. He prioritized the party & created a personalistic patronage system. Demonstrating an openly hostile attitude toward, but begrudging dependence on, the bureaucracy, Mujib's actions created internal ruptures. 6 Tables, 75 References. J. Sadler

title: 7 The reign of terror of the big cat: bureaucracy and the mediation of social times in the Indian Himalaya
abstract: This paper describes the arrival of a man-eating leopard in a small Himalayan town in India and the local state's subsequent struggle to control the big cat. By focusing on what went on within the apparatus of the state during this period, this paper attempts to contribute to the study of modern time in bureaucracy. It argues that the startling inefficiencies in the effective governance and regulation of the big cat stemmed from a clash of various social times that were unfolding simultaneously. It outlines five distinct forms of social time that were in play during this period, which led to long periods of waiting and allowed for the articulation of a searing critique of the Indian state by town residents. Ultimately this paper contributes a rethinking of current theories of bureaucratic time that focus on the production of disempowered waiting, risk analysis, and anticipation. Instead it argues that a study of low-level bureaucrats and citizens shows that a central task of bureaucracy is to attempt to mediate conflicting forms of social time. Moving away from accounts of bureaucratic indifference, this paper depicts failure as an impasse arising out of attempts to bring incommensurable forms and representations of time into congruence. These failures importantly imperil the legitimacy of bureaucrats and can lead to a radical critique of the state. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Enduring Nightmare: The 1984 Bureaucracy
abstract: The power of George Orwell's 1984 lies in the depiction of an authority capable of manipulating the general culture while the "masses" remain apathetic; eg, Winston Smith's crime is not the act of writing a diary, but his belief in an ultimate sense of decency. Orwell elaborates a bureaucratic theory of a totalitarian society, & describes the functions of falsification of the past, maintenance of continuous warfare, & preservation of the Inner Party's power. The question Orwell presents is whether a complex society can prevent its bureaucratic government from becoming a "system of organized lying" by those who love power. K. Carande

title: "E-Government" and Society. Comparative Analysis of Global and Russian Realities.
abstract: Examines the concept of electronic government (e-government) & its origins. Traces the importance of the Internet in the business world & Russia's involvement in its development. States that due to the major reforms taking place in Russian healthcare, education, & government, the role of e-government will increase considerably. Examines the issues of information safety. Concludes that the key approach to understanding modern government is Weber's classical theory of bureaucracy complemented by e-government. Tables, References. K. Duft

title: Cooperation and Conflict in the Factory: Some Observations and Questions regarding Conceptualization of Intergroup Relations within Bureaucratic Social Structures
abstract: This article is an examination of intergroup relations in a factory setting, drawn from participant observation research over eleven months of employment as a radial drill operator on the drill line of a piecework machine shop. Drawing upon a daily diary of observed interactions, the writer came to the following three conclusions: while a main axis of interaction in labor-management conflict exists, this is one feature in a larger web of relationships; the nature or quality of group connections in an industrial establishment fluctuates; &, the various members of the interacting groups participated in the interactions in different manner & degrees, suggesting that the boundaries of cooperation are oscillating. It is concluded that the social groups have shifting boundaries & may vary from what are described as consensus in thought, feeling, & action representing group behavior & intergroup relations of a cooperative type. R. Prince

title: Falling Outside: Excavating the History of Central American Asylum Seekers
abstract: This article takes a retrospective look at legal advocacy on behalf of Central American asylum seekers, which has been influential in the development of US asylum law and in the creation of an infrastructure to address immigrants' needs. The article considers three time periods when Central Americans have been deemed to fall outside of the category of refugee: (1) the 1980s, when US administrations argued that Central Americans were economic immigrants; (2) the 1990s, when civil wars in El Salvador and Guatemala came to an end; and (3) the 2000s, when some Salvadoran youths in removal proceedings have argued that they faced persecution as perceived or actual gang members. This retrospective analysis highlights the ways in which law can be creatively reinterpreted by legal actors, as well as how legal innovations carry forward traces of prior historical moments. Adapted from the source document.

title: An Almost Universal Scheme of National Service in Australia in the 1950s*
abstract: While the Australian Government partly justified the introduction of a universal National Service Training Scheme for eighteen-year old males in 1951 by highlighting the threat of imminent war and the consequent need for military preparedness, advocates also believed that national service encouraged the development of a sense of civil responsibility. Its confidence in the potential of national service to promote citizenship explains why the government was so strongly committed to the scheme's universality. Nonetheless, although the government went to great lengths to enforce compliance, Aborigines and those from other "non-white" backgrounds were actively discouraged from participation and women were only reluctantly admitted to the professional army. As would be expected in this period, they were never considered for national service. An examination of the rationale for national service and the associated discourse for inclusion and exclusion not only indicates the social assumptions shaping policy-making by government and bureaucratic elites in 1950s Australia, but also reveals their wider social aspirations. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Bureaucracy in Bourgeois Sociology [A Critical Analysis of Concepts]
abstract: The conceptual confusion surrounding the term bureaucracy in the Western sociological literature is discussed. The views of Western scholars such as M. Albrow & F. Riggs are contrasted to Karl Marx's treatment of the phenomenon, which gives a more adequate account of its complexity & the sociopolitical processes that generate it. Presented also is a critique of Western scholars' efforts to formulate a scheme for reconciling effective bureaucratic management with democratic values. S. Karganovic

title: Connecticut's Hybrid Culture: Its Politics, Issues, and Future
abstract: With its mixture of traditional, individualistic, and moralistic cultures, Connecticut remains a hybrid state. Political parties are strong because they control decision making in the General Assembly and place candidates directly on ballots in local partisan elections. One of the central issues in Connecticut's current politics is this state's continuing efforts to deal with metastasized corruption in its state and local government. Central to this issue was the resignation of Republican Governor John Rowland, who was under federal court indictment and investigation by a state legislative impeachment committee. Two of his key staff members were found guilty or running a major operation of bribes for contracts out of the governor's office. Related to personal corruption by state and local officials is the failed administrative policies of the Connecticut Department of Transportation. Also part of Connecticut's corruption problem is the issue of state ethics reform. The author also provides some forecast for Connecticut's political future. Connecticut's battle with state and local corruption will not end for two main reasons. First, corruption has become ingrained in this state's ethics. Second, this state's leading newspaper have so deeply cut their state and local reporters that there are few talented and well-placed journalists to investigate and report wrongdoing by Connecticut public officials. These factors and conditions mean that Connecticut likely will remain a 'hybrid' state with its mixture of individualistic, moralistic, and traditional culture. Adapted from the source document.

title: Sexual Harassment Policy, Bureaucratic Audit Culture, and Women's Studies
abstract: In an era of waning public funding and growing assumptions within the academy that gender has been integrated into curricula, Women's Studies Programs work under the monitoring eye of a corporate model of budget-slicing, bureaucratic, audit-culture accountability. Programs come under increasing assault on the grounds of obsolescence and cost-effectiveness. This article documents the institutional setting of a Women's Studies Program under threat and traces how program faculty have attempted to counter antifeminist obsolescence and individualist rhetoric, using as an example the struggle over institutional sexual harassment policy and its successor at the authors' state university. In participating in re-writing policy, the authors discovered possibilities and blockades in professors' and students' attempts to position the Program as more than a curricular remedy. We reveal the limitations of valuing departments solely on quantitative grounds and insist that feminist work in transforming academic culture is far from complete. Adapted from the source document.

title: Changing Urban Spaces: Mobile Phones on Trains
abstract: Mobility is changing the ways people routinely behave in public places. Since the appearance of digital mobile phone networks, mobile phones have become part of suburban and urban landscapes globally. Both the use of public transport and mobile telecommunications are integral for daily life and self-presentation in most large cities such as London and Tokyo. Public places and spaces are being transformed into hybrid geographies through the introduction of new spatial infrastructure. In this paper, we present our analysis of the responses of our survey sample of commuters concerning their use of mobile phones on trains. Adapted from the source document.

title: Use and Abuse of Power: Evaluation in a State Education Agency
abstract: A historical view is provided of national & local influences on internal evaluation within a state education agency. The impact of the increased acceptance of qualitative approaches for evaluation practice is discussed. 11 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: BUREAUCRACY: A SOCIOLOGICAL STUDY OF IMPERSONAL ORIENTATION AMONG SUBORDINATES (CLERICAL STAFF)
abstract: A sample survey among 62 subordinate admin'ive officers in 6 district level state gov offices in Varansi is reported. 38 were junior & 24 were senior clerks. Att's of impersonality as defined by M. Weber were measured along a range containing 3 categories: low, medium, & high. 4 hyp's were established. No statistically signif is were found between level of impersonality & age, educ, & father's occup, nor between impersonality & Ru/Ur background, seniority in service, job tenure, & incumbency. This leads to the rejection of 3 hyp's. The qualitative analysis of the data re dislikes about gov service, types of officers preferred, & att's toward personal favors, however, confirms the hypothesis that admin'ive subordinates (clerks) in Indian gov offices are not highly oriented towards impersonality & prefer personal considerations in following bur'tic norms. It was found that bur'tic norms are followed when they fall into the clerks' 'zone of indifference.' But their orientations & bur'tic behavior are strongly influenced by caste, kin & friendship loyalties. Rules are often sacrificed in favor of the clerks' own interests. An overconformity to authority, based on fear, was also noted. Similar studies at diff levels of bur'cy are proposed. Such studies may help in evaluating the role played by S-cul factors in accelerating or retarding effective functioning of bur'cy. M. Maxfield.

title: The Glass Ceiling Revisited: Determinants of Federal Job Advancement
abstract: Using the results of a recent survey of federal employees & focus groups of the same population, previous research on the existence of a glass ceiling in the federal bureaucracy is extended. Even when controlling for differences between the sexes in human capital factors, work habits, work opportunities, & personal circumstances, women who have been in the federal bureaucracy from 0-10 years & 20-30 years have not advanced in their professions as successfully as have men. In contrast to & departing from previous research, there is little evidence that a glass ceiling has been experienced among women who have worked in the bureaucracy 10-20 years. Additional findings consistent with past literature include the fact that among women who have faced gender-based barriers, those who chose to have children during their careers have been especially disadvantaged. It is concluded that the glass ceiling on the federal level, where apparent, has been multidimensional & quite subtle. 3 Tables, 31 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Global Labor: Algocratic Modes of Organization
abstract: This study investigates a practice that allows workers based in India to work online on projects for corporations in the United States, representing a new mode of labor integration. In the absence of direct bureaucratic control across continents, the question arises how this rapidly growing labor practice is organized. The riddle of organizational governance is solved through an analysis of software programming schemes, which are presented as the key to organizing globally dispersed labor through data servers. This labor integration through programming code is distinguished from two other systems of organization--bureaucracy and the market--while bringing out the salient features of each system in terms of its ruling principle: bureaucracy (legal-rational), the market (price), and algocracy (programming or algorithm). The logic of algocratic systems is explored methodically to analyze global work.

title: The Defeat of the Golden Gate Authority
abstract: In 1958, John F. McCarthy and Edgar F. Kaiser proposed the Golden Gate Authority to coordinate, plan for, and develop regional transportation in the San Francisco Bay Area. This agency would have incorporated all Bay Area bridges, seaports, and airports and would have provided the foundation for general regional planning and metropolitan area government, with capacity to expand its jurisdiction and functions. As such, the proposal threatened the autonomy of local governments, whose officials rallied against it, evoking the principle of federalism under the rubric of 'home rule.' In accounting for the defeat of the authority, this article describes local government officials as an independent interest group engaged in the decision-making process. It also considers some of the long-term implications of the defeat, including the reinforcement of a fragmented, federalist governmental structure at the local level. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Inc., copyright 2008.]

title: Effetti perversi della valutazione ed equità sociale: riflessioni sul Sistema Nazionale di Valutazione
abstract: The essay focuses on the National Evaluation System, discussing about its possible effects on the school community's subjects and on the governance of the educational system. After critically reviewing the concept of social equity in relation to education, the paper presents three different ...logics... of the National Evaluation System, underlying for each of them the possible unforeseen and unintended effects. The aim is to consider whether and under what conditions such evaluation system could increase social equity and reduce social inequalities or could reproduce or even intensify them. The authors outline some perverse effects linked to its implementation, in particular related to the typically bureaucratic formal adaptation to the assessment requirements by teachers and headmasters. On the other hand, the use of the evaluation as a leverage for improving the active participation of school stakeholders could pave the way that leads from school evaluation to school improvement.

title: The Health Care Bureaucracy: Small Changes, Big Consequences
abstract: Administrative changes that have reshaped health policy over the past decade have resulted in a more constrained medical profession, & a more powerful health care bureaucracy. Most industrialized nations have called on democratic principles to balance profesional norms; in contrast, Americans are developing a distinctly bureaucratic health care regime. Explored here are the ramifications for both the politics of health care & the practice of medicine. 49 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Effects of school restructuring on the achievement and engagement of middle-grade students
authors: Lee, Valerie E; Smith, Julia B
abstract: A study of the impact of attending restructured schools on the achievement and engagement of young adolescents is examined in a conceptual framework favoring the development of more communally organized schools and away from a bureaucratic organization.  Modest but consistently positive effects of restructuring were found on both achievement and engagement.

title: Localism, Cosmopolitanism, and Faculty Response
abstract: A case study of Leyden U was carried out between 1969-1971 via participant observation on determinants of participation in policy-making. The conceptual framework used distinguished between localism & cosmopolitanism & a progressive vs conservative stance re issues concerning student & staff power. Both localism & cosmopolitanism proved to promote better participation in policy-making &--in contrast to findings in the US--a progressive rather than a conservative position. Results point to the importance of the macro-soc context as conditioning not only the degree but sometimes even the direction of relationships at the mesoor micro-level. A tendency of Dutch admin'ors to avoid open conflict & bring things to a head may also be involved. An interpretation of results in terms of a typology of the following combinations of localism/cosmopolitanism is offered: (1) general local-cosmopolitan orientation (senior professors); (2) partial cosmopolitanism with a local touch (young faculty members in the humanities, theology & soc sci's); (3) the pure res orientation (found esp in law & medicine); (4) micro-localism (rather old, senior faculty members with a meager professional record). These types represent clusters of characteristics of professors. Res is proposed on the dynamics of career patterns in relation to the soc & disciplinary origins of the profession. 5 Tables, 1 Diagram. Modified HA.

title: State and Capital in Late Colonial Indonesia: The Sugar Industry Braakhuur and the Colonial Bureaucracy in North Central Java
authors: Knight, G Roger; Van Schaik, Arthur
abstract: The relationships between state bureaucracy & the sugar industry in late-19th- & early-20th-century colonial Indonesia are surveyed, using developments in the practice of braakhuur, 'fallow rental', as an illustration. Instead of renting land after local peasants have harvested their maincrop, rice, in braakhuur, the sugar companies rent the land before rice planting takes place, which assures a head start on the sugar cane planting season; the land lies fallow until cane can be planted, thus depriving local farmers of their main food crop but guaranteeing cheap cane labor. Braakhuur was almost exclusively conducted in climatically favorable regions of north central Java between the 1890s & the early 1920s. Because braakhuur weakened the farming element integral to this agrarian society, some colonial officials & elements of the colonial bureaucracy quickly realized its long-term disadvantage, especially when importation of rice became necessary. The different factors & individual efforts by residents & other colonial officials involved in its demise are described in detail, highlighting main areas of economic vs ecological & local vs global conflict. 38 References. J. Paul

title: Black Power and the Rise of Bureaucratic Autonomy in New York City Politics: The Case of Harlem Hospital, 1917-1931
abstract: Reviewed is the gradual emergence of bureaucratic autonomy in New York City politics, a result of late-nineteenth/early twentieth-century reforms against political corruption in city administration. One effect of municipal reform was to make policy the specific province of certain ethnic & professional interests. As a consequence, blacks fared particularly badly, since they were prevented from advancement as policemen, firemen, & physicians by bureaucratic self-government. The years after World War I saw blacks & party politicians unite against city bureaucrats. This trend is analyzed through study of the drive to hire black physicians at Harlem Hospital. The campaign, which lasted through the 1920s, involved a concerted effort by the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People, the National urban League, the Citizens' Welfare Council, & the Manhattan & North Harlem medical societies, among others. However, the social changes finally effected by 1930 were due more to the Democratic Party than to this coalition of organizations for racial justice. D. Dunseath.

title: Public Bureaucracies and Policy Implementation
abstract: As agents of policy implementation, public bureaucracies have significant margins for discretionary action in fulfilling their tasks. This raises problems of efficiency & effectiveness. The latter is focused on & attitudinal & structural determinants of agency behavior in policy implementation are analyzed. AA.

title: The Role of Automobilization and "Destructive Competitiveness" between Slovenian Cities and the Hinterland
abstract: The article analyses the development of traffic infrastructure in Slovenia & its influence on spatial & socio-economic development. The analysis is based on various theoretical & conception elements that deal with the "spatio-temporal organization of the living environment." The unilateral modernization of specific traffic infrastructures leads to non-productive, destructive competitiveness between cities & the hinterland & influences the degradation of less "networked" spaces. Special attention is paid to the analysis of automobilization in Slovenia which in the period since 1991 became the dominant mode of transport, with effects on the economic & social systems of Slovenia. The article concludes by considering orientations to reduce the role of automobilization & expand the role of public transport so as to enable the more complementary development of settlements in Slovenia. Adapted from the source document.

title: Identity papers, lamas' books, and the magical essays of Lenin: literacies of desire and exclusion in Nepal
abstract: Attempting to harness the powers of literacy to improve his standing and opportunities in rapidly developing Nepal, Dil Bahadur Tamang, an ambitious uneducated man of the hill village of Charigaon, instead encounters a most unexpected book of power and magic. This article tells the story of his encounter and of my own attempts to understand it. What is it about a book of essays by Lenin that makes it magic? Village resources for interpreting the significance of written materials include secular, Nepali-language schooling with its contexts of development, bureaucracy and state power; Tibetan Buddhist textuality with its ritual and lamaic authority; and the seemingly effortless literacy of foreigners -- as well as a variety of less obviously related domains such as street magic, love curses and possession. In the end, however, the major power that literacy carries into Dil Bahadur's life is its power to exclude him. Adapted from the source document.

title: Gender, Bureaucracy, & Democracy: Careers and Equal Opportunity in the Public Sector
abstract: Set in a theoretical context of fostering representative bureaucracy and equal opportunity for women, this work "seeks to identify key factors that act as barriers and facilitators to career advancement at the state and local levels of government" (p. 13). Research at the sub-national level provides a superior barometer of progress towards democratic ends through bureaucratic representation because of the number of employees involved, their distribution and visibility, and the opportunity for comparison. Through a skillful combination of literature and empirical analysis, the editors offer scholars and policy-makers a wealth of information about the current status of women as public administrators and the effects of gender on public sector employment.For a complete reprint of this article contact Haworth Press by telephone (1-800-HAWORTH) or EMail (getinfo@haworthpressinc.com) Article copyright The Haworth Press, Inc.

title: Justice Through Bureaucracy: The Ukrainian Model
abstract: This paper examines legal proceedings in the court of first instance for civil cases in Ukraine. Using ethnographic methodology, it demonstrates that a large part of a court judgement is predetermined by the institutional infrastructure and by practices established more widely in Ukrainian society. By observing case hearings and interviewing litigants and judges, the paper reveals that an unbridgeable gap separates a legal case, as constructed through documentary files, from the reality of life. This affects the very meaning of 'evidence' and the way that judicial decisions are made. The paper also illustrates the benefits of viewing a lower-level civil courtroom as a microcosm of a society, demonstrating that it provides rich insights into different layers of that society. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright holder.]

title: Productivist Welfare Capitalism: Social Policy in East Asia
abstract: The article engages with the literature on the "East Asian welfare model" by using Esping-Andersen's "worlds of welfare capitalism" approach to analyze social policy in the region. It describes the main features of a productivist world of welfare capitalism that stands alongside Esping-Andersen's conservative, liberal, & social democratic worlds. It then shows that Japan, Hong Kong, Singapore, South Korea, & Taiwan are all part of this world, though they divide into subgroups within it. To account for productivist welfare capitalism in East Asia, the article focuses particularly on bureaucratic politics at the unit level & on a range of key shaping factors at the system level. It closes by considering the implications of East Asian experience for comparative social policy analysis. 2 Tables, 39 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: THE MALAYAN CIVIL SERVICE, 1874-1941: COLONIAL BUREAUCRACY/MALAYAN ELITE
abstract: As it grew & developed, the Malayan Civil Service (MCS) faced a dilemma between becoming a Malayan soc elite, the cream of the 'British Malayan' community, & remaining a loyal overseas extension of British bur'cy. This dilemma is observable in its relations with other races: it spontaneously created the Malay Admin'ive Service to facilitate Malay participation in gov & then systematically frustrated its functioning. The main variable at any given time was its relations with the unofficial British community. The paper is based on a set of index-cards, one for each member of the MCS in the period (about 1100) showing educ'al background, career, etc. Some evidence is adduced from Colonial Office Files, literature, etc. Special attention is paid to the effect of the growth of numbers & gradual predominance of those with a I Public Sch/Oxford or Cambridge educ'al background. Disputes with London & other bur'tic instit's are also traced. Gayl D. Ness (U of Michigan, Ann Arbor), THE MALAYAN BUREAUCRACY AND ITS OCCUPATIONAL COMMUNITIES: A COMMENT ON JAMES DE VERE ALLEN'S 'MALAYAN CIVIL SERVICE, 1874-1941'-expresses praise & agreement re Allen's analysis of the Malayan civil service. It is possible to extend Allen's boundaries to observe other situations in the Malayan bur'cy in which occup'al communities developed to varying degrees. The ambivalence he noted in the British MCS is brought into sharper relief by reference to the postwar period. Study of the groups of indigenous civil servants & officials which arose is suggested. Res should examine how these groups react when their loyalty to their bur'tic roles comes into conflict with their loyalty to their subcultural role as a Malayan elite group. 'Allen's analysis provides a useful model for additional individual & comparative studies that can contribute to our understanding of the colonial process.' Modified AA.

title: Development and the State in Post-Colonial Algeria
abstract: After briefly reviewing four stages of state formation in Algeria, the role of the bureaucracy in development is assessed. It is shown that the state owns the significant means of production & has used the bureaucracy to implement its statist model of development. In so doing, it has emphasized the development of heavy industry & the use of the most advanced technology to promote it. Despite initial high hopes, this model has failed to create jobs for the bulk of the population, led to a heavy reliance on foreign capital, & created large pools of un- & underemployed. Though these problems were staved off for two decades when high oil prices shaped the relationship between bureaucracy & development, the decline of oil prices in the 1980s caused major unrest & turmoil, creating an economic crisis that the state & its bureaucracy are still trying to manage. Modified HA

title: Training and Mobility among Mexican Public Administration Officials
abstract: Attempts to disprove the hypothesis that access to the highest positions in Mexican bureaucracy depends on personal relations rather than on professional capacity. Analysis of the curricula of general directors & undersecretaries during the administrations of presidents De la Madrid, & Salinas de Gortari concludes that experience within the different levels of the bureaucracy serves as a mechanism of training & testing the abilities of public servants. An average of ten years of service in hierarchically inferior posts typically proceeds accession to a general directorship, & fourteen years to an undersecretary. In addition, while electoral training & party involvement are expected of undersecretaries, they are not necessary for a general director. The idea of a controlled mobility within the Mexican high-level bureaucracy is thus identified as a mechanism to assure competence in high-level officials. 13 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucratic Manipulation of Physical Symbols: An Empirical Study
abstract: Hypothesized is that an organization's use of service symbols will vary with the discretion available to its clients, while its use of authority symbols will vary with the resistance to be expected from its clients. Empirical observations were made in 122 government offices within Ill: 31 Drivers License Examining Stations, 38 municipal police departments, 29 county public health departments, & 24 Armed Forces Recruiting Stations. The data obtained support both the hypotheses proposed & reveal marked differences in the ways the agencies manipulate symbols. 4 Tables, 1 Figure. Modified HA.

title: The Dual State: The Unruly "Subordinate", Caste, Community And Civil Service Recruitment In North India, 1930-1955
abstract: This paper explores the nature of the everyday state in historical perspective in colonial and postcolonial Uttar Pradesh, north India, through the lens of civil service recruitment. It argues that social relationships between different cadres of the revenue and police services effectively created a bureaucratic space in which citizens' approaches to the state recreated forms of ambiguity in the reach and authority of state power. In this sense, it provides a deeper historical basis for anthropological and sociological work on the nature of the "fuzzy" everyday state in postcolonial India. But it develops this literature further, arguing that important structural changes over independence in 1947, also transformed the ways in which caste and community lobby groups represented their corporate interests through bureaucratic recruitment. These lobby groups, as a result of disjunctions in state power and discourses, between centre, province and locality, were often able to subvert systems of caste and community reservation. In the process, their actions emphasized the inability of the state at central and provincial levels to adjust to local political identities that depended on hybridity. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Are We There Yet? A Roadmap to Understanding National Park Service Rulemaking
abstract: The preproposal stage of the rulemaking process is notoriously understudied, but enormously important in determining regulatory outputs. Recently, Rinfret (2011c) analyzed the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) rulemaking process and developed a frame analysis model to interpret stakeholder influence during the preproposal stage. Rinfret argues that stakeholders use three frames to influence agency rulemaking, including an expertise, a fiscal feasibility, and an information frame. This article tests this model to determine whether it is applicable to other federal agencies such as the National Park Service (NPS). Through an analysis of stakeholder framing within the 2012 NPS Yellowstone Winter Use Rule, this research confirms that Rinfret's model is indeed applicable to the NPS process. Therefore, this research suggests that this theoretical model examining stakeholder influence is applicable to other public land agencies, and arguably can be applied across the bureaucracy. Adapted from the source document.

title: When Local Models Fail
abstract: Models treating the simple properties of social groups have a common shortcoming. Typically, they focus on the local properties of group members and the features of the world with which group members interact. I consider economic models of bureaucratic corruption, to show that (a) simple properties of groups are often constituted by the properties of the wider population, and (b) even sophisticated models are commonly inadequate to account for many simple social properties. Adequate models and social policies must treat certain factors that are not local to individual members of the group, even if those factors are not causally connected to those individuals.

title: Has Transport Infrastructure Promoted Regional Economic Growth? -- With an Analysis of the Spatial Spillover Effects of Transport Infrastructure
abstract: Taking full account of the synergistic effects of multidimensional factors on regional economic growth in China, this paper constructs a model of the spatial spillover effects of transport infrastructure on regional economic growth. Using provincial panel data from 1993 to 2009 and employing spatial econometric techniques, our empirical analysis comes to the following conclusions. (1) The total output elasticity of transport infrastructure for regional economic growth varies between 0.05 and 0.07, indicating its important role in such growth. (2) Transport infrastructure has very clear spatial spillover effects on regional economic growth; its role in regional economic growth will be overestimated if these are neglected. (3) For a specific region, transport infrastructure in other regions has mainly positive spillover effects on economic growth, but there is also evidence of negative spillover effects. (4) Among multidimensional factors contributing to regional economic growth, labor plus capital stock from other parts of the public sector make the greatest contribution to regional economic growth in China, followed by the new economic growth factors and new economic geography. Adapted from the source document.

title: Security above all else? The gradual securitization of German development policy
abstract: In current development debates it has become a staple for policymakers to see development policy through a security lens. Whether or not official German development efforts confirm this assessment, however, is debatable. In this article, recent dynamics and trends in German development cooperation are analyzed from the perspective of such an alleged "securitization". The focus is on five dimensions of securitization and its effects: 1. shifts in developmental discourse; 2. local patterns of the allocation of development funds; 3. sectoral patterns of resource allocation; 4. eventual security-related implications of institutional reforms in the development sector; and, 5. authority shifts among agencies and bureaucracies. That is, the concept of securitization has been broadened to encompass changes in political action and, at the structural level, shifts in thinking. In the German case, the results indicate that securitization taking the form of "militarization" has, so far, been sporadic at most. This is likely because of the long-term and incremental nature of shifts in perception, which have preceded (and enabled) forms of civil-military cooperation in the development sector, however, future developments will have to be watched closely. The current experiences in Afghanistan will help decide the contours of future official development policy in this regard. Adapted from the source document.

title: Administrative Oversight and Control
abstract: In discussing accountability, one must ask to whom, by what standards, & by what means is one made accountable. With regard to administrative control within bureaucracies, the ability of the administrator to control the actions of subordinates is shown to depend on certain factors, & it is noted that the greater the effort made by higher officials to control the behavior of subordinates, the greater the efforts made by the latter to evade control. Initial steps toward control (agency goals & rules), the problem of information, & determinants of bureau behavior & strategies for change are considered with precautionary comments added. The important variables include: (1) recruitment & selection, (2) training within the agency, & (3) the culture of the bureau (values & standards of performance). Despite noted constraints, the aggressive administrator can find levers to modify dysfunctional aspects of a bureau. Sensitivity, sophistication, & systematic analysis are required of the successful administrator. B. Hubinger.

title: THE LANGUAGE OF PERSUASION IN BUREAUCRACY: 'MODERN' AND 'TRADITIONAL' APPEALS TO THE ISRAEL CUSTOMS AUTHORITIES
Lenin and Revolutionary Democracy
abstract: Lenin is the obvious keystone of what can be called 'the Bolshevik tradition'. There has been considerable confusion over the meaning of this term, with frequent identification of it with the murderously bureaucratic phenomenon that in fact strangled it (for example, J. Arch Getty's description of Stalin's 1930s purges as 'the self-destruction of the Bolsheviks'). To the contrary -- Lenin and the Bolshevik tradition he represents are inseparable from the revolutionary, anti-dogmatic, profoundly democratic perspectives of Karl Marx. While rooted in problems and contradictions arising within 'Leninism' and Bolshevism in the difficult years of 1918-1924, Stalinism represents a qualitative divergence. In fact, Bolshevism is a tradition that is essential to the best and most activist elements associated with 'Western Marxism' -- particularly as represented by its foundational figures of the 1920s, Lukacs and Gramsci -- and with currents influenced by Trotsky. It is likely that a resurgence of left-wing activism will cause renewed scholarly debate on the issue of Lenin and revolutionary democracy. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: NAFTA: The governance of economic openness
abstract: Although the rule-based regime of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) has instituted the empowerment of private actors vis-a-vis government bureaucracies, and of transstate institutions at the regional level, it is contended in this article that NAFTA should be envisioned as a hybrid model of economic governance.

title: Tradition and Ritual in the Everyday Life of Judges
abstract: Although German judges consider themselves more modern than tradition-bound in the British sense, their professional structure rests on the most highly bureaucratic system in Western Europe, with roots going back 250 years. This system is so strong that laws & constitutional principles are sometimes overridden, & it has given rise to meaningless rituals criticized yet still practiced by the judges. Chances for improvement are assessed. 6 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Cultural Change and Training in Public Organizations
abstract: The distinction between public & private organizations has become less clear, because of two opposing trends: the growth of the public sector beyond its original purpose, & the process of privatization. The influence of market-associated values has structurally & culturally transformed public organizations since the 1980s. Private management values, eg, competition & productivity, are not always compatible, though, with bureaucratic ethos, eg, justice, integrity, & objectivity. Efficiency in the public sector does not necessarily serve the general interests of the population nor ensure equal application of the law. The future training of civil servants should try to resolve these incompatibilities by establishing a new code of public service. 69 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Usurping Social Policy: Neoliberalism and Economic Governance in Hungary
authors: Phillips, Richard; Henderson, Jeffrey; Andor, Laszlo; Hulme, David
abstract: This paper takes issue with arguments emanating from the global social policy literature that neoliberal policy agendas have been largely a consequence of the interplay of international agencies with indigenous reform interests. While relevant, such arguments grasp only part of the story of social policy change. By means of a case study of Hungary between 1990 & 2002, this article emphasises the role played by the bureaucratic reconstitution of the state & changing forms of national economic governance in the explanation of social policy change. We show how the bureaucratic redesign of the Hungarian state generated a 'finance-driven' form of economic governance with the state bureaucracy reconfigured around the fiscal control of the Finance Ministry. These changes had significant implications, not simply for social expenditure, but for the intellectual nature & bureaucratic space for social policy-making. Whereas critiques of neoliberal social policy reform tend to focus on the ideological nature of the projects, this analysis highlights the need to develop visions of, & arguments for, an alternative to the finance-driven forms of economic governance that have become the de facto bureaucratic archetype for re-designing welfare states. Tables, Figures, Appendixes, References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Schooling, Socialization, and Group Boundaries: A Study of Informal Social Relations in the Public Domain
abstract: Pupil socialization is examined by comparing the bureaucratic structures of three elementary schools (public, Catholic, & Episcopal) serving Chestnut Heights, New York City. The data were collected from June 1972 to Sept 1973. Bureaucratic role differences (particularly occupations) are seen as the most important factor in the establishment of the different group & boundary identities of the area. Demonstrated is how these group boundaries are transferred to the elementary school environment through the establishment of schools & classrooms which are group-homogeneous. The various socializations received by the children in group-specific bureaucratic behavior prepare them to assume the roles exhibited by their parents. Methodological concerns regarding the research are discussed. 5 Tables. A. Rubins.

title: THE RISE OF THE BUREAUCRATIC STATE
abstract: BUREAUCRACY AS AN UNACCOUNTABLE CENTER OF POLITICAL AUTHORITY IS USUALLY UNDERSTOOD TO BE A FUNCTION OF THE SIZE & COMPLEXITY OF MODERN GOVERNMENT, IN EFFECT A CONCOMITANT OF MODERNITY. AGENCY HISTORY & BEHAVIOR IN THE US, HOWEVER, SHOWS SUCH FACTORS TO BE INADEQUATE IN EXPLAINING THE GROWTH OF BUREAUCRATIC POWER. RATHER, THE DECISIVE FACTORS WOULD SEEM TO BE THE TASKS PERFORMED BY AGENCIES, THE CONSTITUTIONAL & POLITICAL ENVIRONMENT, & THE PREFERENCES, DESIRES, & DECISIONS OF CITIZENS & LEGISLATORS WITH WHOM, & FOR WHOM, AGENCIES WORK. THE POST OFFICE & THE DEFENSE DEPT, 2 OF THE LARGEST BUREAUCRACIES, ARE THE DIRECT RESULT OF POLITICAL DECISIONS & THE NATURE OF THEIR TASKS. THE CLIENTISM OF REGULATORY AGENCIES IS LARGELY THE RESULT OF THE SYSTEM OF SEPARATION OF POWERS & FEDERALISM PROVIDED FOR IN THE CONSTITUTION, & THE NATURE OF THE TASKS STIPULATED IN LEGISLATION & DEMANDED BY SPECIAL PUBLIC & PRIVATE INTEREST GROUPS. BUREAUCRATIC INERTIA CAN ALSO BE ATTRIBUTED TO THE CONSTITUTIONAL SYSTEM. ALL OF THESE FACTORS COMBINE TO SUGGEST THAT BUREAUCRATIC AUTHORITY IS NOT A NECESSARY FEATURE OF GOVERNMENT & COULD BE OVERTURNED BY LEGISLATIVE DECISION. F. HYDOSKI.

title: Grass-Roots Participation and Bureaucratic Interfaces: The Case of Mexico -- Introduction
abstract: An introduction to a special issue, "Grass-Roots Participation and Bureaucratic Interfaces: The Case of Mexico," focuses on similarities between notions of "participation" & past patronizing ideas about modernization. Michel Foucault's (1980) distinction between monarchical power & modern power is drawn on to discuss power relations associated with the changing nature of both capitalist production/circulation & socialist politics. Attention is called to the way in which public discourses about "participation" are set in forms of domination/governmentality as well as in potential forms of subversion/resistance. Although the articles focus on the Mexican reality, they shed light on neoliberal governance & new forms of direct democracy elsewhere. Topics covered include the blurred line between the world of the entrepreneurial subject & that of new social movements seeking "empowerment"; participation as a tool of vertical relations of power; the effect of combining participation with aid targeted at selected recipients; dangers involved in removing specific experiences from their specific contexts; hidden dimensions of local organizing practices; & interfaces between organizational, cultural, & institutional settings. 7 References. J. Lindroth

title: Bureaucracy and Ecopolitics in the Third World: Environmental Policy Formation in Brazil
abstract: A study of the bureaucratic politics of environmental policy formation in Brazil. The social & political conditions that favored the creation of a specialized environmental agency are identified, as well as the extent to which these conditions have determined its perceived missions & its ability to translate environmental concerns into coherent public policies. Also analyzed is the bureaucratic politics of ecopolitics, understood both as pollution control & abatement, & as conservation & management of natural resources. 39 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: PUBLIC BUREAUCRACY, RESOURCE STRUCTURE, AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT: A NOTE
abstract: Due to the necessity of managerial & entrepreneurial skill to the econ development of relatively backward countries, economy in the allocation & use of this skill is of the greatest importance. Expansion of the public sector of an underdeveloped economy at the expense of its private sector may intensify the effective scarcity of utilizable entrepreneurial & managerial skill. In general, misuse of scarce entrepreneurial skill through excessive expansion of the public sector tends to aggravate the extent to which a shortage of qualified public bur'crats always operates to slow down the rate of econ development. Evidence is presented to support the view that this shortage is very pronounced, in terms of both numbers & quality. A solution is not to be sought in exempting from civilservice requirements individuals selected to administer econ activities in the public sector. Such exemption might retard the development of a highly qualified & morally responsible public bur'cy. At the same time private entrepreneurs cannot be counted on to initiate some of the undertakings essential to a country's econ development. An appropriate division of functions between the state, on the one hand, & private enterprise, on the other, must be made. Modified AA.

title: Determining the identity of 'black Africans' in UK population and health policy contexts: ethical issues and challenges
abstract: In everyday settings in the UK the self-determination of identity has been taken for granted. In the decennial census and the bureaucratic practices of modern governance, the ascription of ethnicity is in the hands of the subject who is the final arbiter, even if this sometimes breaks down by default. However, for some minority ethnic groups, notably 'black Africans', a group 'created' by the decennial census, observer-led approaches to determining identity have insinuated themselves into some policy contexts in the UK. The targeting by HIV/AIDS workers of 'black Africans' in mundane public settings based on such signalling devices as appearance and language or accent has been endorsed as a modus operandi in preventative care. For around a decade the UK Border Agency has made use of linguistic analysis and other forensic methods to establish the nationality of Somali-origin asylum seekers as against claims from other East Africans. Its latest Human Provenance Pilot Project - the use of isotope analysis and DNA ancestry testing to establish nationality - again places 'black Africans' on the front line. These external processes of identification raise important ethical challenges, given the potential for harm when assignment is incorrect.

title: Sources of Citizens' Bureaucratic Contacts: A Multivariate Analysis
abstract: Among variables generally reported to predict individuals' bureaucratic contacts are need, awareness of programs, socioeconomic status, political orientation, social involvement, & political participation. Here, a multivariate analysis of the predictors of bureaucratic contact was undertaken, using interview data from a sample of 456 older Americans.
