abstract: Triggered by the recent inquiries into the Fukushima nuclear disaster, this article reflects on the challenges of developing and operating risk regulation and crisis management regimes in an era of highly complex and tightly interconnected socio-technical systems. These challenges are not just technical and professional but fundamentally institutional and cultural. The article identifies three key paradoxes and challenges of contemporary risk and crisis management, signals a range of recurrent problems in governments' efforts to cope with these challenges, problematizes current patterns of societal learning from crises, and sketches an agenda for public administration research in this area. Adapted from the source document.

title: Liberation Theology, Sustainable Development, and Postmodern Public Administration
abstract: Examines the prospects for integrating liberation theology, a postmodern public administration perspective, & sustainable development in response to the avid neoliberal pursuit of growth regardless of consequences. Such liberation theologians as Gustavo Gutierrez offer an alternative framework for development that entails nurturing the economic & environmental prosperity of communities without compromising sustainability. A postmodern public administration approach based on extrastate activist collaborations with nongovernmental & nonprofit organizations may prove more effective than conventional forms of political struggle. The continuing dialogue between liberation theology & leftist activism & scholarship has created a strategy that has produced results against poverty & oppression in Latin America. 85 References. K. Coddon

title: European Bureaucracy
abstract: International bureaucracy is a phenomenon peculiar to our time, but it is difficult to study: From the outside, studies remain superficial; from the inside, they can become biased. However, certain qualities of this bur'cy appear when we study the civil servants (CS's) of the various European states. Characteristic (1) is the diversity of the various groups of CS's. Each org acts independently; some CS's like those of the CECA, have legal status, while others are hired on a contractual basis. There is also diversity in treatment, in pensions, in conditions of service, & it is impossible to move from one org to another. Characteristic (2) is the uncertainty of the recruitment process: some subordinate positions & important posts are filled in advance; there is also direct recruitment at every level of employment with a consequent risk of cooptation. Furthermore, these civil servants must belong, in a predetermined proportion, to the countries of the various member nations, which of course creates difficulties of all kinds. Finally, it must be recognised that the role of this bur'cy is ill-defined. Psychol'ly, European CS's are in a difficult situation. They feel that they are uprooted, far from the country of their origin, and not part of an established hierarchical framework. Tr by J. A. Broussard from IPSA.

title: Quality of Life and Living Conditions in the Netherlands
abstract: The four planning offices in the Netherlands form a network that covers all areas of government. This network matches with the policy structure in Dutch administration. One of the planning offices, the Social & Cultural Planning Office (SCP), studies social & cultural aspects. Most of the SCP publications deal with several different aspects of living conditions. As an integrative tool, the SCP developed an overall monitoring instrument: the living conditions index (LCI). The LCI measures aspects of individual living conditions & is composed of indicators from eight areas: housing, health, leisure activity, ownership of consumer durables, sport activity, vacation, social participation, & mobility. Education, income, & paid employment are considered as resources & are used to describe the backgrounds of living conditions. Developments in living conditions for the Netherlands are monitored not only overall, but for various groups in society as well. Asked in conclusion is whether the LCI is useful for policy(makers). 1 Table, 7 Figures, 11 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: SOCIAL STRATIFICATION AND ASPECTS OF PERSONNEL MANAGEMENT IN THE CHINESE COMMUNIST BUREAUCRACY
abstract: One signif trend in the Chinese pol'al system in recent yrs has been the growth of complex bur'tic patterns of soc stratification, even within the ranks of the Party cadres in Communist China. The Party has tried in many ways to resist these trends, but as the egalitarian heritage of active revolutionary struggle recedes into the background, deep-rooted authoritarian & bur'tic predispositions have reasserted themselves. Both the trends towards complex stratification within the bur'tic elite & the regime's highly developed techniques for personnel management deserve increased attention. These trends & techniques are discussed on the basis of data concerning one particular Chinese Communist ministry. IPSA.

title: The Road not Taken: international aid's choice of Copenhagen over Beijing
abstract: A decade after the United Nations conferences on gender equality and social development, this paper explores their policy origins and discusses their differential impact on international aid since 1995. The author draws on her direct experience to consider why Copenhagen led to Poverty Reduction Strategies and the first Millennium Development Goal, whereas Beijing has become largely invisible in the mainstream world of aid. She argues that the powerful influence of economic rational choice theory associated with bureaucratic modes of thought has meant that the central debate in development policy has remained that of growth versus equity. Beijing's agenda of societal transformation offered another paradigm of development that has remained marginal. The paper concludes with a proposal. If international aid policy could handle more than one paradigm and thus be more open to different ways of thinking about economy, society and politics, aid agencies would be better able to support transformative processes for social justice. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: "A knock on the door": Managing death in the Israeli defense forces
abstract: This paper discusses death that occurs within organizations through an analysis of how deaths of soldiers are handled by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF). While such deaths challenge the military's organizational order and legitimacy, the IDF handles them through the institution of a "moving bureaucracy": a combination of fixed administrative procedures and intense emotional work carried out by liminal military personnel (reserve officers).

title: WHO WRITES WHAT IN THE BUREAUCRATIC UNIVERSITY?
abstract: The phenomenon of ghost-writing & split authorship within the academic context is examined. Particular attention is directed to ghost-written proposals by 'principal investigators' in res org's attached to U's. It is stated that 'it is possible for quasi-illiterates to become the authors of innumerable speeches, papers, monographs, articles, & books, written by variegated specialists whose only relationship to each other is that they are financed by the same agency.' The anxieties which beset the putative author are discussed. He needs to validate & advance himself through authorial credits & must justify his claims for authorship. He can do this by editing the manuscript, making suggestions & possibly rewriting some of the original material. The actual author may fight for credit to the work & for what he regards as the integrity of the manuscript. If he is intractible, he will resign. In that case the problem is solved. However, in most cases the issue will be resolved by splitting authorship among a handful of co-authors, all under the senior authorship of the illiterate or non-writing senior conventional author. But even in this case much bitterness may result. All of these complexities are generally known & understood by the participants, by U admin'ors, by res sponsors, & by faculty not engaged in project res. The net result is to devalue res authorship, since no one knows who actually wrote what. Editorship for the man who aims to also be an author is fraught with even more anxiety, since he is expected to be impartial & self-effacing in accepting or editing a manuscript for a publisher. M. Maxfield.

title: Fragmented Bureaucracies in Built Heritage Conservation: The Case of Shamian Island, Guangzhou
abstract: Located in Guangzhou, Shamian Island was leased as a foreign concession to the British and French forces in the mid-nineteenth century. The island has been granted the highest heritage protection status. Through the lens of the Fragmented Authoritarianism framework, this paper examines the bureaucratic structure of the Chinese state, bargaining activities, and policy outcomes related to conserving Shamian Island. The following conclusions are drawn: first, coordinated conservation efforts have been hamstrung by the fragmented heritage management system that is tier-differentiated and jurisdiction-based; and second, the two most concerned agencies - the Planning Bureau and the Cultural Bureau - have not been able to agree on the appropriate approach to conserving heritage and historic buildings on the site. Deadlock has resulted, as no agency can really push for better, and more compatible, policies. Nor have sustained conservation practices for the site been viewed as politically significant enough to prompt higher-level government officials to step in and end the bureaucratic squabbling.

title: Public Management of Basic Needs and Local Social Actors in the Epoch of Structural Adjustment: A Reflection on Mexico
abstract: This paper analyzes the relation between the level of organization of the civil society & the nature of local public policies related to the satisfaction of basic needs in the Mexican context during the 1980s. It postulates that an associative community experience (in wards, urban zones, & municipalities) is an key element in the making of such policies. The strength of the collective spaces must be well established to confront the problems resulting from the growing socioeconomic inequality in Mexico. 13 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Governing of French-Speaking Communities in a Minority Situation and State Partnership
abstract: In this article, we turn to the issues that stem from the partnership between Francophone community organizations in a minority setting & the Canadian federal state. While it seems to respond to the communities' will of taking charge of their own development, by promoting notably a process based on the principle of shared governance, this partnership nevertheless has administrative requirements that appear to weaken autonomy & the free governance of Francophone communities in a minority setting. The participation of Francophone organizations in elaborating & implementing public policies comes with the bureaucratization of their community activities & a re-assessment of their representative structures. Because they must more formally represent the community's general interest & must directly collaborate with the state in order to attain their objectives, they are compelled to act in a way that, we note, clashes with new legitimacy imperatives. These have the effect of questioning the corporatist arrangement that has formed between them & the state. It is this legitimacy issue that weighs on the new world of governance among FSMC that we wish to reveal in our research, a few elements of which we present in this article. Adapted from the source document.

title: Organizational and Individual Responses to External Stress
abstract: Org'al & individual changes resulting from severe environmental stress in 3 R&D org's were studied at the beginning & the end of a 20-month period. The changes were examined with both longitudinal & independent sample data. 3 Conn R&D org's of similar size were studied in Aut 1967 & Spr 1969. Half-hour group interviews were conducted with professional members of the res staff, each of whom then completed an individual questionnaire. In 1967, the res'ers responding were a small random sample of those in the org. In 1969, as many of the R's in the 1st study as possible were seen, resulting in a matched-pairs sample of 31 res'ers. The greatest changes occurred in the way res'ers perceived their jobs & their org's rather than their self-perceptions or att's to ward work. Despite the greatly decreased satisfactions experienced by the res'ers, their job involvement & aspiration levels did not change greatly, & their intrinsic motivation decreased in one of the 2 samples studied. It was concluded that this lack of expected individual coping behavior might be associated with high levels of internal strain for the res'ers, although some strain was probably reduced by becoming alienated from the org. Modified HA.

title: Public Finances in 1985
abstract: Examined is the evolution of public financing in France between 1963 & 1978, as compared to the provisions contained in two government reports of 1963 & 1970. Based on this analysis, future developments are predicted. Discussed are changes within administrative, local, & military sectors, as well as in methods of financing. Maintaining the progress of real value of social benefits in relation to any of the other economic sectors entails a growing need for financing of public administration. While there are no official projections for 1985, proposed are two possible solutions to the crisis caused by slower economic growth: increase in compulsory taxation, & reduction of spending in certain sectors. Discussed are four main tasks of public financing: securing services not otherwise provided by private enterprise, substituting public choice in the matter of national resources, securing national solidarity in the realm of redistribution, & regulating economic activity. 5 Tables, 5 Figures. I. Irwin-Zarecka.

title: Methodological Issues in the Study of Bureaucratic Elites: A Case Study of West Point
Professionals, Managers and Discretion: Critiquing Street-Level Bureaucracy
abstract: Social workers are classic street-level bureaucrats. This article provides a critical examination of Michael Lipsky's account of discretion within street-level bureaucracies. While concurring with the main thrust of Lipsky's critique of management control of discretion, I argue that he gives insufficient attention to the role of professionalism in his analysis and the impact this has on the relationship between front line managers and workers and the nature of discretion. I employ a qualitative case study of adult social work within a local authority to illustrate and develop this argument. The study, which draws primarily on interviews with local managers and practitioners, suggests that the professional status of social workers influences both the nature of their discretion and the way in which this is managed. I conclude that Lipsky's work needs to be augmented by an understanding of the role of other perspectives, such as professionalism, in examining manager-worker relations and discretion in the street-level bureaucracies within which social workers practise. Adapted from the source document.

title: Architectures of incarceration: The spatial pains of imprisonment
abstract: This article considers the contribution that physical environment makes to the pains of imprisonment. Synthesizing concepts and theories from critical organization studies with those that have informed criminological studies of prison design and the lived experience of imprisonment, the article discusses the ways in which the architecture and aesthetics of penal environments might be better understood with reference to the restricted economies of space found in industrial and bureaucratic organizations. It is argued that a grasp of the limits historically placed on the subjective growth of individual workers (workspaces frequently being characterized as 'iron cages' or 'psychic prisons') can enhance our understanding of the physical and psychological confinement of those in custody. Moreover, critical organization studies can inform emerging debates about what future prisons should look like and alert us to the potential fallacy in assuming that 'modern' equates to 'better'. While clean, humane and safe environments are unquestionably desirable for both prisoners and prison staff, and considerations such as natural daylight, access to outside space and aesthetic stimuli are increasingly being incorporated into penal environments around the world, this article will critically interrogate the value of such initiatives arguing that they may, in fact, represent a new and potentially more insidious form of control that bring their own distinctive 'pains'. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright holder.]

title: The Evaporation of Gender Policies in the Patriarchal Cooking Pot
abstract: Presents an analogy between the dissipation of gender issues in international development organizations & the evaporation of water. It is asserted that women's development have made little progress in international agencies since the 1985 Nairobi (Kenya) World Conference on Women. This neglect contradicts the underlying Weberian ideology of bureaucracy. Patriarchal dimensions of a government agency in the Republic of Snowdia, South Africa, are demonstrated in a case study. It is concluded that feminism must be incorporated into the patriarchal bureaucratic structure if true change is to be made. 1 Table. Adapted from the source document.

title: Social Commitment and Efficiency Measurement in Indian Public Enterprises
abstract: The pattern of capital & recurring expenditure on social overheads in 25 Indian central government enterprises is examined, using data from annual accounts for 1984/85. Results show that removal of social burden from the enterprises has a favorable effect on the rate of return. Modified HA

title: State Functions and Media Politics: Case Study on Print Media in Slovenia
abstract: What is specific in the efforts of the Slovenian state institutions to handle the current economic, political, and cultural crisis in the country? The answer is searched for in the media representations of the building of a new government in February 2012. The analysis is focused on five major functions of modern states: security provision, regulation of macro-economy, administration, reproduction of human resources, and environmental protection. The source of primary information for the analysis and argumentation is the daily newspaper Delo (Labor). Relevant publications in the newspaper were differentiated by applying two criteria: first, predominant reference to one of the five functions of the state; second, if the article contains no alternative (1) or presents a strong alternative to a given situation, event or opinion related to the state functions (5) on a 5-point scale. The analysis identifies a large share of publications focusing on the administrative function of the state and rather limited share of publications on security issues and environmental protection. The analyzed publications contain only modest efforts to present and discuss alternatives to political situations and opinions. The hypothesis about alleged colonization of politics by mass media is falsified. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Gender and Style in Bureaucracy
abstract: Using data from a questionnaire completed by Wisc professional & executive civil servants (N = 389), the gendered nature of Weberian bureaucracy is examined. Analysis of respondents' behavioral styles & views of the ideal bureaucrat shows that the preferred style is gender neutral with equal value placed on feminine & masculine characteristics. Both sexes cross gender stereotypes in their behavioral styles, as well as in their perceptions of good administrators & colleagues. Women shun traits with negative connotations, while endorsing those important for achieving results in an agreeable manner. Men, in contrast, adopt more traits of both genders with potentially negative connotations, attending more to hierarchy, competition, opportunism, & power games. Adapted from the source document.

title: Administration's Moral Hemophilia: Its Eroding Legitimacy
authors: Mitchell, Terence R; Scott, William G
abstract: The US public's increasing distrust & lack of confidence in their administrative leadership is documented using data from empirical studies & the popular press, & linked to the concept of legitimacy. It is argued that US administrators in both government & business have failed to demonstrate the characteristics on which legitimacy is based: expertise, visionary entrepreneurship, & stewardship or trustworthiness. A distinction is made between confidence in institutions & confidence in those institutions' leadership, though they are related in that circumstances which weaken administrative legitimacy can jeopardize institutional structure. Implications for administrative practice are discussed. Modified HA

title: The African National Congress (ANC) and the Cadre Deployment Policy in the Post-Apartheid South Africa: A Product of Democratic Centralisation or a Recipe for a Constitutional Crisis?
abstract: The cadre deployment policy has been implemented by the African National Congress (ANC) and its alliance partners in pursuit of its avowed intention to have loyal party hands on all the levers of power in government. The present paper finds out that although the policy is justified by the ANC, it has attracted criticism from those who believe that its implementation has been exposed to abuse by some ANC officials. While certain deployed cadres in public administration are able to function at an acceptable level, it is argued that in some instances far too many are there to do the bidding of the cadre deployment committee that appointed them to national, provincial or local-level positions. However, it is worth noting that historians and political scientists alike contend that this undermines the accountability structures in the public service. Further, this paper avers that deployed cadres who succeed do so despite their deployment, not because of it. There are a number of arguments stating that the implementation of a cadre deployment policy by the ANC is an attempt to centralise democratic powers within the ruling party. In conclusion, the paper attempts to provide a historical analysis of this policy in the 20-year rule of the ANC in South Africa.

title: Management Paradigm Change in the United States: A Professional Autonomy Perspective
authors: Skaggs, Bruce C; Leicht, Kevin T
abstract: The social organization of work has become more entrepreneurial & less bureaucratic over the past 20 years. How is this development consistent with managerial control over the labor process? This paper develops a professional autonomy perspective to explain the acceptance of new management ideas in the United States, including the recent turn away from bureaucratic organizational forms. The focus on professional autonomy helps to create a theoretical link between past & current managerial practices, including the latest anti-bureaucratic phase that we label neoentrepreneurialism. We conclude by exploring future research implications of studying managerial practice from a professional autonomy perspective. 1 Table, 1 Figure, 43 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Policy Lessons of the East Asian Demographic Transition
abstract: The usual lessons drawn from East Asia's striking experience of health and fertility transition concern the efficacy of well-designed government programs catering to an existing or ideationally stimulated demand. An alternative interpretation sees the demographic change--and the uptake of services--as a byproduct of social and economic development together with, in some cases, strong government pressures. This article probes more deeply into this experience, seeking to identify common features of development design and administration that underlay it. The broad sequence entailed, initially, establishment of an effective, typically authoritarian, system of local administration, providing (sometimes incidentally) a framework for promotion and service delivery in health, education, and family planning. Subsequent economic liberalization offered new opportunities for upward mobility--and greater risks of backsliding--but along with erosion of social capital and the breakdown or privatization of service programs. The study is mainly focused on seven countries: Taiwan and South Korea ("tiger" economies), Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia ("second wave" countries), and China and Vietnam ("market-Leninist" economies). The period is roughly from the 1960s to the 1990s. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Narrative and Identity: Storytelling in Bureaucracy
abstract: The relationship between bureaucracy & identity is discussed in an examination of the narratives of clients, students, & professionals in the medical & legal fields. It is argued that the legal & medical professions, as well as most other institutions & informal sites of identity creation, attempt to maintain community & solidarity through proceduralism, conformity, & objectivity. However, individuals at all levels of bureaucracy seek to assert their own identity through resistance to conformity. Therefore, individuals in these settings must simultaneously conform to succeed & communicate, while they rebel to maintain personal identity. The bureaucratic demand to eliminate subjectivity & individuality actually undermines the productivity of institutions. By creating boundaries between the institution & outside influences, the institution loses touch with the individuals who are both the subjects & objects of institutionalized professions. Individuals enlist a variety of strategies to maintain personal autonomy, & it is concluded that behaviors deemed incompetent by institutions may represent individuals' attempts to escape bureaucratic confines. 45 References. T. Sevier

title: Standardising Cornish: The politics of a new minority language
abstract: The last recorded native speaker of the Cornish language died in 1777. Since the nineteenth century, amateur scholars have made separate attempts to reconstruct its written remains, each creating a different orthography. Later, following recognition under the European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages in 2002, Cornish gained new status. However, with government support came the governmental framework of “New Public Management”, which emphasises quantifiable outcomes to measure performance. This built implicit pressure towards finding a single standard orthography, for greatest efficiency. There followed a six-year debate among supporters of the different orthographies, usually quite heated, about which should prevail. This debate exemplified the importance of standardisation for minority languages, but its ultimate conclusion saw all sides giving way, and expediency, not ideology, prevailing. It also showed that standardisation was not imposed explicitly within language policy, but emerged during the language planning process.

title: PROFESSIONALS IN ORGANIZATIONS: A NEOTERIC MODEL
abstract: The efficiency & rationality of bur'tic methods of org, often assumed in the literature, are held not to obtain in many bur'cies staffed with professional employees, eg, academies, res instit's, legal firms, hosp's. Where the demands placed upon an org are non-routine, where innovation & professional skills are required, & where org'al goals are somewhat abstract, traditional bur'tic forms often inhibit org'al goal-attainment. Such org's are referred to as neoteric org's, & the neoteric model stipulates the conditions required for the optimal structure & operation of such org's. Internal conditions include the absence of (1) general rules, (2) hierarchy, (3) over-professionalization, (4) hyper-impersonality, (5) material props, & (6) role-strains; the presence of (7) an appropriate professional myth & (8) professional evaluation of professional problems. Environmentally, the model requires (9) societal norms conducive to professional autonomy, (10) high SS for the professions, (11) unprogrammed resources flowing into the org, & (12) pol'ly relevant horizontal professional links. These 12 factors are functionally related so that the modification of any factor will produce changes in all the other variables of the model. The variable of hyper-impersonality is selected arbitrarily, & its impact upon the other elements in the system is shown in hyp'al form through its analytical manipulation. AA.

title: A reappraisal of the rank-and-file versus bureaucracy debate
abstract: This paper celebrates some of the considerable strengths of Hyman's 1970s/early 1980s analysis of unions in general and bureaucracy specifically, and reapplies it to more recent developments within British unions, while at the same time providing a critique of Hyman's refutation of the 'rank-and-file' versus 'union bureaucracy' conception of intra-union relations. It argues that the wider set of implications Hyman drew from the accentuated pressures towards the bureaucratisation of workplace unionism that he identified 'bent the stick' too far in the opposite direction. In attempting to defend and refine the classical revolutionary Marxist analytical framework, the paper maintains that the conflict of interest that exists between full-time officials and rank-and-file members is a meaningful generalisation of a real contradiction within trade unionism, notwithstanding the variations and complexities involved. It examines the nature and social dynamics of full-time union officialdom, shop stewards and workplace unionism, and the relationship between the two. In the process, the limits and potential of both Hyman's 'earlier' and 'later' writings are highlighted and some broader generalisations are drawn with relevance to current dilemmas for trade unionism. Adapted from the source document.

title: Stressing Academe: The Wear and Tear of the New Public Management
authors: Chandler, John; Barry, Jim; Clark, Heather
abstract: In recent years academic commentators have born witness to the emergence of what has been called a New Public Management, or NPM, evident in a number of countries around the world. While the literature has sought to document its appearance & attempt to assess its impact, this article considers an aspect of the NPM which has been little explored: the human cost associated with its introduction. In examining higher education in England, one of the countries where the NPM is thought to have been embraced at least relatively enthusiastically, the article explores research on the experiences & reactions of those working in academe to recent attempts to change working practices through an analysis of the stresses & strains experienced by those subjected to the processes of managerialism. In drawing on published sources & the authors' own empirical work it is argued that the NPM, not least in intensifying the labour of academics as intellectual workers, has provoked a range of responses which include collusion, resentment & resistance. The consequences of the NPM, it is argued, include blaming of the victim & diverting attention away from processes of control & the action of human agents who initiate stressful conditions of work by implementing the NPM in particularly harsh ways. It is further contended that attempts to encroach on professional autonomy, & operationalize the NPM in English universities in harsh ways, are being mediated by those subjected to the changes who are seeking to preserve elements of collegiality. 60 References. [Copyright 2002 Sage Publications Ltd.]

title: Understanding Bureaucratic Centralism
abstract: Discussed is the failure of classical Marxist social theory to explain bureaucratic centralist societies. The following components of classical theory are analyzed in this regard: (1) the concept of critique, (2) the theory of history, (3) the theory of the state, (4) the theory of capitalism, & (5) class theory & the theory of revolution. A formal & comparative sketch is provided of the main features of bureaucratic centralism, focusing on the following: (A) the organizing principle, (B) the question of control, (C) the legitimation problem, (D) the primacy crisis tendency, & (E) the spcificity of rational crises. The limits & merits of a political crisis model of bureaucratic centralism are discussed. A. Rubins.

title: Knowledge of Sexually Transmitted Diseases among Secondary School Adolescents in Asa Local Government Area of Kwara State Nigeria
authors: Oluyemi, Joseph A; Yinusa, Muhammed A; Abdullateef, Raji; Sunday, Akoh; Kehinde, Kadiri
abstract: The adolescent age is the period of sexual identity when adolescents make sense of their feeling and turn them into actions. This stage requires adequate knowledge of sexual behaviours so that adolescents will not rely on peer group for information. This is because of the far reaching effects it may have on them and the society at large due to misinformation and the consequences of the high risk sexual behaviours they may engage in like sexually transmitted diseases. This study therefore aims at accessing the knowledge and sources of information of STDs among adolescents in the Asa local government area of Kwara State, north central region of Nigeria. The study was carried out in three public secondary schools in Ogbondoroko and Laduba towns, suburbs of the capital city, Ilorin. Information was gathered through questionnaire administration. A total of 240 questionnaires were administered to (SS1), (SS2) and (SS3) students in the study area and in all 210 were retrieved representing 88% return rate.

title: The methodological and thematic impacts of the American social science approach on social science disciplines in Turkey in the 1950s
abstract: By the end of the Second World War, the German emigre scholars, who had undertaken important roles in Turkish academia, left Turkey. During the 1950s they were replaced by Americans. In the meantime, the American social science approach, dominated by behavioralism and empiricism, was heralded as the "universal science" in the world. Being influential especially on sociology, psychology and public administration, the American approach played a constitutive role for the newly developing political science discipline as well. Through scrutinizing the methodological and thematic impact of the American approach and American scholars in Turkey, this research argues that social science disciplines were almost reestablished or exposed to a fundamental change under these circumstances. Although anti-Americanism started to shake Turkish university campuses and became popular among the academics in the following decade, the American impact on social sciences has not been seriously discussed. Adapted from the source document.

title: Loneliness and the Aging Homosexual: Is Pet Therapy an Answer?
abstract: Loneliness is not only a matter of being alone. Solitude need not be equated with loneliness; the latter can be experienced in a crowd. Loneliness is, rather, a deep awareness of isolation from other caring persons. It is, of course, not exclusively a condition of the old; it can occur at any age and is more likely the result of loss -- desolation -- rather than isolation. The National Center for Health Statistics tells us that, of the 26.3 million Americans over the age of 65 who are not in hospitals or nursing homes, almost a third (8 million) live alone. According to the current estimate, 10% are homosexual.Human consciousness exists reflexively, and the lonely, in order to fill the void of their desolation, traditionally created a caring God as the perfect companion. In the last half of the 20th century, space exploration and the vision of an infinite universe, along with a turning away from the traditional concept of deity as the omnipresent and caring "other," leave us apprehensive and intrinsically isolated on our blue-marble planet. The explosion of technology, with our lives directed by the computer and menaced by a Star Wars bureaucracy, brings us to the edge of recognition of our irredeemable insignificance and impotence. We are no longer the center of the universe or even of an extended, loving and supportive family.

title: Professionals from China: Entrepreneurship and Social Resources in a Strange Land
authors: Salaff, Janet; Greve, Arent; Wong, Siu-Lun
abstract: New skilled immigrants may have a hard time getting jobs. Among other reasons, local employers may not value their foreign-earned credentials. This could prompt professional and technical immigrants to start a business instead. In this paper, we examined how educated immigrants from the People's Republic of China avoid underemployment in Canada by setting up their own businesses. We found that many immigrants brought entrepreneurial backgrounds with them. However, their entrepreneurial experience was linked to their human capital, which was dynamically related with the organizational needs of large, complex bureaucracies back home. Once in Canada, where their social resources are diminished, few could reestablish enterprises. Without these supporting relations, skilled immigrants are not prime candidates for entrepreneurship.

title: On Appropriate Application of Qualitative Research in Public Administration
abstract: The research method is crucial to high quality research in public administration. Compared with quantitative research methodology, qualitative method has its special potential in knowledge growth in China. Therefore, the author argues that public administration scholars should pay more attention to its appropriate application in empirical research. Tables, References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucracies in Retrenchment: Vulnerability Theory and the Case of U.K. Central Government Departments 1975-85
authors: Hood, Christopher; Dunsire, Andrew; Huby, Meg
abstract: Using official data drawn from UK central government departments over the period 1975-1985, bureaucratic vulnerability to cutbacks is examined at three levels: programs, groups within the bureaucracy, & the department. Results indicate that party-political influences & prior history seem to have low power in predicting vulnerability to cutbacks. Bureaucratic process influences have some predictive power for these data, particularly at the group & departmental level of vulnerability. 7 Tables, 2 Figures, 27 References. Modified HA

title: Citizen-Initiated Contact and Satisfaction with Bureaucracy: A Multivariate Analysis
abstract: Multivariate probit models are used to integrate the overall factors that contribute both to individuals' contacts with unelected officials & to their satisfaction with that contact. Analysis of data obtained via telephone interviews with 821 citizens whose names were obtained from a congressional office indicates that of 6 key independent variables purported to affect citizens' encounters with government agencies, awareness of programs & social involvement are the most important. The 2 most potent shapers of citizens' satisfaction with bureucracy are their assessments of the process that the agency went through (promptness, efficiency, & fairness) & their assessments of the behavior of street-level bureaucrats with whom they personally interacted -- in terms of knowledgeableness, courtesy, & openness to criticism. 2 Figures, 42 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Clinical Governance and Governmentality
abstract: The introduction of Clinical Governance into the National Health Service in England represents a fundamental shift in the regulatory relationship between the state & medical professionals. This paper critically examines the underlying assumptions of Clinical Governance, & discusses them in relation to Foucauldian concepts of "governmentality." First, official definitions of Clinical Governance are reviewed in the context of other policies to apply increased control & surveillance to medical professionals & linkages between this & wider tends in public sector managerialism & governance. The paper then briefly considers these developments in relation to theoretical accounts of bureaucracy, professionalism, risk, & trust. It is argued that at the organizational level, Clinical Governance can be usefully analyzed as involving a move toward "encoded knowledge" through the use of "soft bureaucracy.". 2 Figures, 83 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Government and Bureaucracy Still Have Not Been Able to Accept Unions
abstract: Unions in Turkey are pressured by the government & other unions to change their opinions & stance. Preferences are made among unions & government workers are pressured to change their opinions. The educational non-governmental organization (NGO) called Turkish Education-You maintains that other NGOs provide educational seminars with money they received from the West, thus, influencing their opinions while their seminars are uninfluenced from the outside. It also works to improve citizens working conditions & holds symposiums, panels, & conferences to disseminate knowledge on civil society. Problems will continue to increase within the Turkish education system unless something is done about it through using knowledge & consulting fellow coworkers to make improvements. D. Jones

title: A Competitive Model of Local Government Organization: Implications for the Process of Community Formation within Metropolitan Regions
abstract: While the proliferation of local governments is commonly viewed as inefficient, a public choice perspective suggests that it may contribute to efficiency by allowing competitive pressures on jurisdictions. A model of competitive local public service provision is developed for the case in which local governments consume but do not produce a single public service without interarea spillovers. Analysis of this model shows that competition does yield efficient results. Extensions to more complex cases are considered. Consideration of the migration rates resulting from differential public goods provision rates provides criteria for determining the optimal number of communities & jurisdictions in a county. Consideration of the economics of community formation suggests that population mobility is likely to produce greater than optimum numbers of communities; the formation of isolated outlying suburbs partially resolves this problem. 5 Figures. W. H. Stoddard.

title: Public administration in the imperatives of democratic governance
abstract: The article aims to analyze the conditions, processes and implications of contemporary public administration based on democratic governance, as it has been the most important concern, considering that the actors and times in the civil society of the twenty-first century increase the complexity of associated life, which responds to the force of public spaces, the requirement that administrative institutions to be more responsible, that managerial and operational performance have better development and that groups of society multiplied their presence in the formulation and definition of public policies, to structure in an articulated and consensual way, collective goals to be processed with the intervention of a skilled and efficient public management by the governing structure, as well as executive and operational areas which are in charge of nurturing the responsiveness of the contemporary State. Adapted from the source document.

title: Managing the Living through the Dead: Colonial Governmentality and the 1912 Burial Rules in Colonial Korea
abstract: This article investigates how the Japanese colonial state's new governmental rationality was deployed and how these technologies of rule sought to regulate Koreans. Using the theory of colonial governmentality, it examines the 1912 burial rules that transformed Koreans' social norms on death and the dead. In order to achieve efficient state management of burial customs, the Japanese colonial government applied laws pertaining to burials, and the disciplinary technologies of policing and punishment. In so doing, the colonial government disciplined the individual Korean body and enforced conformity to colonial institutions. Adapted from the source document.

title: New Concepts of Management in Cultural Establishments: Experiences of Experts in the Field
authors: Mader, Sabine; Mields, Just; Volmerg, Birgit
abstract: New Public Management is being introduced in Germany as Contract Management -- a management strategy that is characterized by extended flexibility in work performance & objectives. Control of processes is replaced by control of results with increased responsibility of the individuals for fulfilling the aims in the contracted area. In cultural establishments, contract management is implemented with the aim to create commitment not only within the public administration but also between the administrative body & the newly founded, independent enterprises of the communities. In reality, however, many of the processes carried out do not correspond to the theoretical requirements. In order to explore the structural level of the process of contracting in cultural establishments in Germany, we conducted expert interviews in three establishments selected from within the cultural sector. A total of 11 experts were asked for their personal evaluation of the following topics: purpose of contract management & particular effects; processes of negotiations relating to reform; consequences for employees; consequences for organizational structure & management. The picture that emerged was manifold. The experts elaborated the new options theoretically associated with contract management. However, they complained that they could not make efficient use of these due to a number of structural shortcomings while administrative tasks have increased considerably. In particular, the level of trust essential for the proper implementation of this leadership strategy has not yet been established. The consequences of the results for the ongoing processes of negotiation are discussed. Figures, References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Moral Discrepancy and Political Discourse: Accountability and the Allocation of Blame in a Political News Interview
abstract: During the course of this article we intend to explore some issues surrounding government policy and actions and the moral organisation of political discourse surrounding the recent enquiry into the BSE crisis and the publication of the Phillips Report in the UK. More specifically, we wish to develop the concept of moral discrepancy and it's use in politically accountable settings, in this case the political interview. The paper, through the use of membership categorisation analysis, explores issues surrounding the social organisation of interview settings, the discursive management of policy decisions and 'bureaucratic mistakes' and the allocation of blame in situated media/political formats. The paper then relates these issues to notions of democracy-in-action, public ethics and the respecification of structure and agency as a members phenomenon.

title: Governmental Retreat and the Politics of African-American Self-Reliant Development: Public Discourse and Social Policy
abstract: The concept of African-Americans helping themselves is addressed in light of the Reagan Administration's rhetoric about reducing the federal government's role in providing social welfare.

title: Det muliges kunst. Om betingelserne for det tværsektorielle samarbejde i et New Public Management orienteret sundhedsvæsen / The conditions for cross-sectoral collaboration in a New Public Management oriented health care in Denmark
abstract: Despite the current idea of collaboration and communication as crucial in creating a coherent and holistic healthcare system in Denmark it seems as if the institutional framework and conditions today counteract such co-work. A strong discourse on the necessity of well-functioning cross-sectoral collaboration is isolated from and challenged by the logics of ´New Public Management', which characterize the past decades of management and organization of healthcare services. Based on two analytical examples of an action research project, I show how tensions and paradoxes in cross-sectoral cooperation affect the healthcare professionals working conditions and their possibilities for cooperating on the discharge of elderly patients.

title: Politics, Bureaucracy, and Worker Participation: The Swedish Case
abstract: Sweden, over the past twenty years, has developed toward a conflict between politics & bureaucracy. This conflict is examined for the specific area of worker participation. Recently, the revisionist democratic theory that most citizens cannot & should not participate has been challenged by participatory democrats. In this challenge, the call to develop responsible participatory capacity has been extended to all areas of life, including work. Demands for participation emerged in Sweden in the 1960s from many groups. In the late 1960s & early 1970s, this led to concern for worker participation & then to new legislation favoring such participation. One controversial proposal, by Rudolf Meidner, adopted in 1971 by the Swedish Confederation of Trade Unions, calls for accumulation of funds out of corporate profits, which would be used to purchase stock to be managed by labor organizations. This has been supported strongly by socialists, while bourgeois parties have opposed it. Its resolution in the 1980s will be a major factor in determining events in Sweden in the 1980s. W. H. Stoddard.

title: Development and Development Administration in the UAE: A Case Study
abstract: Data were collected via field visits, interviews conducted Jan-Feb 1988 of United Arab Emirates (UAE) public administration officials & other informed individuals, & official documents concerning development administration in the UAE, as part of a series of studies evaluating the role of administrative reform agencies in member states of the Gulf Cooperation Council. Focus was on: development challenges in the UAE; the UAE administrative system, problems facing it, & efforts to overcome these problems; & the contribution being made by agencies for administrative development toward solving these problems. It is concluded that development suffers due to poor definition of development objectives & policies, & inadequacy of goals, organization, functions, & resources of administrative development agencies. The role of each emirate in national development should be reviewed as a key to finding solutions to the problem of unbalanced national development. A thorough review of planning strategies is recommended to formulate a comprehensive new plan for administrative development. 22 Tables. Adapted from the source document.

title: Is Bureaucracy Inevitable? The Chinese Experience
abstract: The possibility of the existence of an organization without such features of bureaucracy as a specialized DofL & multiple rules is explored through a review of the Chinese attempt to eliminate bureaucracy, especially during the Cultural Revolution. Confucian ideology opposed specialization & elaborate rules in administration; Maoist ideology took a somewhat similar position. The consequences of the Cultural Revolution & its aftermath suggest that bureaucracy is inevitable, & that efforts should be made not to eliminate but to improve it. 71 References. Modified HA.

title: Nuclear new build in the United States 1990-2010: A three state analysis
abstract: This research examines nuclear energy policy across three states in the United States (US) - Georgia, Pennsylvania, and Texas - from 1990 to 2010. Therefore, the nuclear energy crisis at Fukushima in Japan March 2011 is beyond the scope of this paper. Nevertheless, the fundamental conclusions of this research remain valid, as the impact of Fukushima is not yet known and in addition the US has experienced its own crisis in Three Mile Island, which has shaped its own nuclear industry to an extent already. Interviews are at the core of the research methodology employed, which is similar to other in-depth studies on nuclear new build. The aim of this paper is to identify and clarify those aspects of the legal, economic, and political requirements of the US that affect prospects for nuclear new build but which, so far, have not been well understood by experts. The research provides these new insights through a unique comparison of US states which have deregulated, regulated and 'hybrid' electricity markets. It is evident that law can play a central role in the nuclear energy sector, and the role of state-driven policy in the nuclear energy sector is also demonstrated. Further, the methodology identifies key assumptions within the nuclear sector in the US that are contested, and delivers lessons on how these contested issues may be resolved. The paper adds to the literature in public administration, legal development and nuclear energy policy, and in particular nuclear new build. [Copyright Elsevier Inc.]

title: The Map of Social Exclusion in Belo Horizonte: A Methodology for Construction of an Urban Management Instrument
authors: Nahas, Maria Ines Pedrosa; Ribeiro, Carla Andrea; Esteves, Otavio de Avelar; Moscovitch, Samy Kopit; Martins, Vera Lucia Alves Batista
abstract: Constructs a model for urban management to overcome social vulnerability in the municipality of Belo Horizonte, Brazil, based on a 1998 official diagnostic that followed Aldaiza Sposatti's 1996 map of social exclusion in Sao Paulo. The map for Belo Horizonte is drawn according to an index of social vulnerability determined by access to several public services & economic opportunities, & according to five dimensions of citizenship: environmental, cultural, economic, juridical, & public. The map is intended to help direct public resources to where they are needed most. 4 Tables, 6 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Assessing the influence of regional Environmental Protection Agency offices on state hazardous waste enforcement decisions
abstract: In assessing the influence of regional Environmental Protection Agency EPA offices on the state management of hazardous waste programs, we focused on the extent to which federal administrative decisions affect levels of enforcement activity by state environmental agencies and whether these effects vary overtime. Our results indicated that state enforcement actions were affected by state program capacity variables such as primacy and the strength of existing hazardous waste policies as well as one federal-level factor-the distribution of grant monies. The impact of federal oversight decisions was minimal. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Administrative Construction of Cultural Reality in Spain
authors: Fernandez Sobrado, Jose M; Antolin Iria, Jose E
abstract: The authors analyze the role that public administration plays in the construction -- definition, shaping, & changing -- of social reality. They contend that there are three different logics underlying its performance: bureaucratic, political, & market rationality. The main purpose is to study the grasp, effects, & failings of those different rationalities within a certain boundary: public policies on cultural resources. As the construction of large cultural resources is in vogue in many Spanish & other European cities, it becomes a main object in the study of the role of public administration in planning & constructing social reality. 29 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The "Minimum Standard of Living" between Administration and Legislation
abstract: The decision-making process in the evaluation of the needs & rights of welfare recipients is investigated in the analysis of 775 cases in Catania, Italy, to determine how social workers interpret the existing law of financial assistance to the poor. Application of legal norms in a specific context of action & the mutual interdependence of social problems & policy are the specific objectives. The former pertains to the sociology of law & its field of research, whereas the latter addresses the mechanics & processes underlying changes in public administration as it enforces & targets welfare laws. 2 Figures, 139 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucrats and Politicians in Botswana's Policy-Making Process: A Re-Interpretation
abstract: Interpretations of the relationship between bureaucrats & politicians within Botswana's policy-making process have consistently presented the former as the policy-dominating group throughout the postindependence period. An alternative to this depiction of Botswana as an essentially administrative state is presented, centered on the choices & political strategies of senior ruling party politicians operating within a political context whose domestic parameters have been variously defined by the demands of the economic planning cycle & the requirements of the electoral cycle. Contrary to conventional views, the electoral cycle is found not to be subservient to the planning cycle. In practice, regularly held competitive elections are central to the maintenance of a politician-defined politico-economic strategy of paternalistic developmentalism. Although the division of labor between politicians & bureaucrats allows the latter considerable latitude & influence within the policy process, it is the former who have defined & who ultimately control the current system. AA

title: Governmental Institutions as Agents of Change: Rethinking American Political Development in the Early Republic, 1787-1835
abstract: Discusses recent historiography on law, public policy, & public administration in the US, 1787-1835. While an earlier generation of revisionist scholars minimized the impact of governmental institutions during this period, new institutionalist historians are focusing on institutional themes (eg, national public administration, state & local government, federalism, & the separation of powers) & reevaluating governmental institutions as agents of change in US society. New institutionalism, grounded in the view that politics & governmental institutions have a substantial effect on large-scale social processes, contests three assertions about US political development: (1) US government of the 1780s had little lasting impact on society; (2) politics were dominated by courts & political parties; & (3) political developments in the early US republic can be understood as responses to earlier social causes. Areas for future research are suggested, & it is concluded that, by incorporating knowledge from social & local historiography into the study of political history, the new institutionalist historiography may provide a more complete understanding of the cultural & institutional development of the early US. J. Ferrari

title: BEYOND THE NORM: COGNITIVE BIASES AND THE BEHAVIORAL UNDERPINNINGS OF US FEDERAL AGENCY MACROECONOMIC FORECASTS
abstract: US federal agency macroeconomic forecasts are generally made in a manner consistent with the unbiasedness-forecast rationality (UFR) hypothesis. While this inference may be valid under normal policy conditions, cognitive biases can make ex ante policy analysis more difficult when macroeconomic circumstances deviate from the  norm. I test whether policy forecasting under abnormal macroeconomic conditions generates predictions that exhibit cognitive biases (uncertainty-induced bias). Moreover, I investigate whether government agencies will either overstate (availability bias)or understate (mean anchoring bias) true conditions during both good and bad times. These three behavioral hypotheses are examined by performing simultaneous quantile regression analysis on a pooled dataset on US macroeconomic  forecasts by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Congressional Budget Office (CBO), and Social Security Administration (SSA) for the 1976- 2002 period. The statistical evidence provides unequivocal support for the uncertainty bias hypothesis as well as strong support for the availability bias hypothesis.  Specifically, deviations from frequently occurring (normal) policy conditions are positively related to cognitive bias involving ex ante policy decisions, and such  biases tend to overstate abnormal policy conditions. These empirical findings highlight the power of cognitive psychology for explaining departures from classical  rationality with respect to government agency forecasting under atypical macroeconomic conditions. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Evaluation in Italy: Experience and Prospects
abstract: The management of public affairs in Italy today is characterized by a demand for transparency & accountability, & by a desire to learn to manage the available instruments of intervention. These emphases highlight the need to evaluate the effectiveness & results of policies & programs, which is not, however, matched by adequate knowledge of the methods or by sufficiently creative approaches. This social deficit in evaluation has both a cultural & an organizational origin, discussed here. 9 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Helio Oiticica: unfoldings of the body in space
abstract: Looking at the work of artist Helio Oiticica, this paper is intended to analyze the crisis of the modern city, to revisit and revise the ideas of bureaucracy and efficiency, and to analyze the role of urban experience, with all its political, social, economic and aesthetic complexities, in the disintegration of the work of art as a thing to be owned and as a rigid support of representation. In this case, the body becomes the basis of a new paradigm, that of the aesthetic participation, in detriment of the passivity of contemplation, becoming capable of constructing new powerful and ephemeral spaces. Adapted from the source document.

title: School Bureaucratic Structure, Locus of Control and Alienation among Primary Schoolteachers
abstract: To test the hypothesis that teachers' alienation from both work & expressive relations will vary directly with the degree of centralization of the school & of formalization of school organization, data were obtained from 529 teachers in 31 Israeli primary schools via the teacher alienation inventory & a locus of control scale. The findings show that: (1) school bureaucratic structure as measured by centralization & formalization, in the subjective view of the teachers, has a greater impact than does locus of control on alienation of both types; (2) formalization has a greater impact than centralization on alienation; & (3) externally oriented teachers exhibit less alienation than do their internally oriented counterparts. 3 Tables, 40 References. Modified AA

title: Bureaucarcy and Centralization: An Examination of Organizational Structure
abstract: The Aston group's contention that M. Weber's concept of the bureaucratic type is no longer useful (see SA 18:4/70E3036) is considered. The relationship of bureaucracy to centralization of decision-making was examined based on results from 2 empirical studies, the Aston group's & its replication by J. Child (see SA 20:7/72F9957). Both studies investigated various types of organizations & used the same methodology, however, they came to different conclusions. In reviewing the group's methodology, it is concluded that the main variables in their research are scalar quantities, not vector quantities as they suggest. A number of reinterpretations of the Aston variables are presented & the abandonment of bureaucratic type is found to be premature. The results suggest "that the characteristics of Weberian bureaucracy, operationalized by the Aston group, namely standardization & formalization, pattern sensibly with other variables, & do this in a way which is not incompatible with Weber's reasoning." 3 Tables. Modified HA.

title: European Policies: The Impact of National Administrative Traditions
abstract: Argues that a central problem for effective implementation of European legislation is the impact of national administrative traditions, since the formal & practical transformation of European Union (EU) law rests mainly at the national level. The interplay of national administrative traditions & EU policy implementation is described, noting that national administrative traditions prevalent in a policy field may differ from country to country. It is argued that implementation effectiveness depends on the "institutional scope" of EU adaptation pressure, which is not only affected by broad European requirements, but also by the embeddedness of the respective administrative traditions & national capacities for administrative reform. According to the degrees of adaptation pressure, different paths are distinguished, suggesting more or less effective implementation. 1 Table, 44 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Women and Public Administration: A Comparative Perspective -- Conclusion
abstract: A conclusion to a symposium on women in public administration (see related abstracts in this section of SA 40:5) that compares the results of questionnaire & interview data gathered 1985-1987 in six different countries: India, the People's Republic of Bulgaria, the Netherlands, the Federal Republic of Germany, Finland, & the US. Women were present in limited numbers in the top levels of the bureaucracies in all countries, ranging from 1% to 11%. All had high levels of education. All reported experiencing discrimination & gender-related barriers to advancement, as well as the heavy burden of family, marriage, & child care. The top female (F) administrators tend to adapt to the existing (often male [M]) norms of the organizations that they work in rather than confronting or rebelling against such norms. The social origins of top F administrators varied: in India, they came primarily from upper-income groups; in the US, from all social class backgrounds; & in Bulgaria, primarily from non-college-educated parents. Marital status varied from country to country. While similarities may exist between top women administrators in different countries, the different histories, economies, labor markets, governments, cultures, religions, & political ideologies of these countries differ significantly & obviate simple correlational explanations for why or how women have been able to obtain positions in higher administration. 2 Tables, 10 References. AA

title: BUREAUCRACY IN TRANSITION: INDEPENDENT NIGERIA
abstract: Public employees in Nigeria number more than 300,000. Of these nearly 33(- work for the 4 public corporations, which have been hived off in recent yrs from the civil service. Only about 50,000 work for the Federal Gov & 70,000 for the 3 Regional admin's. Grades follow the British pattern, but the Executive Class was started late & has so far been little more than a channel of rapid promotion from clerical to admin'ive work. There are 3 substantial unions among civil servants, most of whom have the right to strike. Whitley Councils appear to be ineffective except for the clerical officers. A system in which several professional Departments dealt direct with a Minister is giving way to unified Ministries co-ordinated by Permanent Secretaries. This has been said to delay Nigerianization. The Gov, leaning heavily on the Northern People's Party, is less in a hurry with Nigerianization than with Northernization, & the Northern Region recruits expatriates freely to avoid Southerners. IPSA.

title: Performing 'Legitimate' Torture: Towards a Cultural Pragmatics of Atrocity
abstract: Scholars have traditionally explained away torture as an act of monstrosity. Hannah Arendt has proposed instead a socio-cultural explanation of the phenomenon. Modern rationality, she suggests, constitutes the legitimacy principle that grounds the bureaucracy of repression and that perpetrators can ultimately tap into for the purpose of justifying their deeds. I will suggest, instead, that modern technical rationality is per se not sufficient to justify torture. Rather, to do so, it must undergo a profound transformation as a result of its being linked to deeper moral logics. Linkage, in turn, is a matter of cultural performance. To tackle the question of legitimacy in torture, it is therefore necessary to address its cultural pragmatics. Jeffrey Alexander's latest work on social performance can help in this respect.

title: Bureaucracy and Development in Syria: The Case of Agriculture
abstract: The Syrian bureaucracy is examined through a case study of its role in agricultural development. Discussion centers on: (1) the degree of technocratic rationality imparted to agrarian policy; (2) the effectiveness of the bureaucracy in carrying out its agricultural policy; (3) the beneficial role of the bureaucracy for the agrarian economy & the peasantry; & (4) the political consequences of the bureaucracy's role in agriculture. It is shown that, while senior public officials play a role in shaping agrarian policy, this role is in turn shaped by Ba'thist ideology & a political structure that vests control over high policy in the presidency & the ruling party rather than in the ministerial bureaucracy. Implications for agricultural planning, administrative leadership, & patronage politics are discussed, & it is concluded that the bureaucracy has implemented development programs that have greatly benefited agriculture. 17 References. Modified HA

title: Reforming Leviathan: The Public Administration
abstract: In Spain, the state & public administration sector have lost their inherent legitimacy & are called on daily to more efficiently provide services. Values & ideologies required for efficiency have been lost, & the highest administrative officials, charged with the public trust & democratically elected, have been discredited as public managers. Public services administration should follow a double model -- that of administration & the market -- moving toward privatization & demonopolization. A change in administrative culture in the political class & the public sector is needed to achieve the new dialectic between authority & services, & consequently, in administration. Adapted from the source document.

title: Managing the Renewal Process: The Case of Vietnam
abstract: The postwar renewal process for Vietnam's economy has been relatively more successful than in other developing Asian countries, because of its more flexible public administration culture & its strong human capital. However, the prospect of more rapid growth in the booming Asian region has led the Vietnamese government to explore changes in public administration policy. After the war, Vietnam experimented briefly with central planning (1976-1980) & then instituted the doi moi reform after Western & Chinese aid were discontinued. In the next stage of reforms, where the goal is macroeconomic stabilization, international assistance may be needed to change the legal & institutional framework of the market economy, to reform government administration, & to improve enterprise management. In the reform of government administration, the size & staffing of civil service, salaries, human resource management, systems & procedures, reform of state enterprises, & management skills development are at issue. Two multilateral assistance projects, the UN Management Development Program on training in economic management & support for development of the legal system & a successor project for elaboration of reforms, are described. 11 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Organizational Learning, Bureaucratic Control, Preservation of Form
authors: Lovell, Rickie D; Turner, Billy M
abstract: Research utilization refers to a phenomenon or set of phenomena inseparable from the complicated context in which use is to occur. The notion is proposed that preservation of form is a subtle bureaucratic imperative that influences research use at the levels of the single organization & of the organizational sector. It is suggested that the metaphor of organizational learning provides a rich set of possibilities for conceptual development, & that examination of characteristic orientations & features of decision systems, combined with examination of bureaucratic control of the decision system, results in important possibilities for refining the essential foundation for understanding & investigating research utilization in complex public organizations. 24 References. Modified HA

title: Employment relations and unions in public administration in Portugal and Spain: From reform to austerity
abstract: This article examines trade union responses to the transformation of employment relations in the public administration in Portugal throughout the Reform programmes launched after 2002 and the more recent austerity measures. It examines the relationship between conflict and concertation and analyses the perspectives and practices of the sector's ideologically divided trade unions. It finally considers comparative issues emerging from the application of similar austerity packages in Portugal and Spain and contrasts their paths of employment relations and union action in public administration. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Gérer l’école d’aujourd’hui : compétences actuelles et souhaitées chez les nouveaux directeurs au Canada/Administrar la escuela hoy día: competencias actuales y deseadas en los nuevos directores en Canadá/Managing Schools Today: The Skills Required for new Principals in Canada
authors: Isabelle, Claire; Gélinas-Proulx, Andréanne; Meunier, Hélène
abstract: In North America and Europe, whilst demographics have accelerated the renewal of school principals, schools are experiencing a structural shift characterised by a more decentralised public management, an autonomy of schools leading to profound changes without always guaranteeing an improvement in the teaching of students. What are the current skills required by new principals? How to identify those who need to develop their skills and know-how in order to better manage their schools? 101 actors in French-speaking education in Canada were questioned - experienced principals, new school managers and others actors in education. The results show that more new school principals state believe that they have the required skills, attitude and knowledge compared to those who believe they need to develop them, whereas more experienced directors and other educational actors consider that the new principals need to consolidate their administrative management skills and their attitudes compared to those who believe they already have them. Thus, the survey highlights potential training themes.

title: AUTONOMY IN BUREAUCRACIES
abstract: Data are presented in which the managerial & supervisory orientations to bur'tic procedures in 9 bur'tic org's are compared. The Yale Technology Project Files (F. L. W. Richardson, Jr. & Charles R. Walker, HUMAN RELATIONS IN AN EXPANDING COMPANY, New Haven, Conn: Labor & Mang Center, Yale U, 1948) were used as the main data source. A negative orientation in bur'cy, called autonomy, was found to typify middle managers more than other positions. It was also found to characterize banks more than production org's, & unprofitable more than profitable production org's. It is argued that the orientation to autonomy is a symbolic expression of frustrated mobility needs characteristic of those who perceive an unlikeliness that they will continue to advance within their org. 4 Tables. Modified HA.

title: Shorter reviews -- The Changing Organisation and Management of Local Government by S. Leach, J. Stewart, and K. Walsh
abstract: Review.

title: Why Have We Made Neglect So Complicated? Taking a Fresh Look at Noticing and Helping the Neglected Child
abstract: The experience of chronic neglect is extremely harmful to children's physical, emotional, cognitive and behavioural development. As an area of research it has been traditionally described as neglected, and as an arena of practice it is viewed as complex and intractable. Over the last few decades, however, there has been a body of evidence building up to help with the understanding of the impact of neglect upon children and to guide intervention. This paper draws on experience as a researcher in the field to present some thoughts on our current understanding of neglect, and how we can move forward with more appropriate responses. It argues that existing evidence is not being used to best effect and that current protective systems, like those in the UK, are still struggling to provide an effective response to neglected children. The language of neglect has become over-complicated and the systems and processes for assessment, planning and intervention are mired in bureaucracy. Some of these complexities are explored in more detail and a model is proposed that would support a more direct and straightforward response to children whose needs are not being met. [Copyright John Wiley and Sons, Ltd.]

title: Sensing locality in Yura: Rituals of carnival and of the Bolivian state
abstract: In this article, I discuss how an indigenous population in highland Bolivia established a sense of locality through participation in two different rituals: the musically based rituals of carnival and the bureaucratic practices of rituals of state that resulted from the initial implementation of a decentralizing law. Through a privileging of visually perceived representations, the logic behind the new law assumed populations were attached to contiguous territories within a national grid.

title: Women's agency across cultures: Conceptualizing strengths and boundaries
abstract: Synopsis The authors in this special issue discuss how women's voices are excluded, silenced and marginalized in settings and processes such as war, displacement, democratization, labor market, judicial system, state bureaucracy, nonprofit organizations and national debates on citizenship. They also discover how women found their voices, channeled them, modified them, and gained a measure of empowerment. They examine women's agency across cultures by focusing on countries as diverse as Turkey, Portugal, Lebanon, Mexico and the US. Each article is concerned with particular transformations in social, economic and political systems that in turn shape women's social, economic and political ability or lack thereof to make their voices heard. All articles are engaged with identifying structural problems that limit women's personal, social and political capacity to maneuver for their own interests. Then again, each piece analyzes a particular form of women's agency or efforts to change their circumstances according to their interests and concerns. [Copyright Elsevier Ltd.]

title: GOVERNING THROUGH UNCERTAINTY: Experiences of Being a Refugee in Turkey as a Country for Temporary Asylum
abstract: This article addresses the question of how to theorize the relation between uncertainty and governmentality with regard to displacement and its consequences. It explores the experiences of asylum seekers in Turkey and the bureaucratic processes of refugee status determination, local dispersal, and third country resettlement, illustrating two main points throughout.
