First, 'protracted uncertainty', characterized by indefinite waiting, limited knowledge, and unpredictable legal status, is a central element of the experience of being an asylum seeker in Turkey. Second, this uncertainty serves to demobilize, contain, and criminalize asylum seekers through the production of protracted uncertainty, which in turn is normalized as a necessity of bureaucracy and/or security. The article invites readers to question the governmentalities of asylum and border regimes that not only discipline refugees' everyday movements but also determine the uncertainty of 'refugeeness'. Adapted from the source document.

title: Teaching Biopolitics in a Professional Curriculum
abstract: The ways in which teachers of public administration can address biopolitical issues within an established professional curriculum are considered. The teleological & instrumental aspects of a belief system are distinguished, & it is argued that biobehavioral explanation can be pedagogically useful & can provide public administrators with a model for assessing & responding to workplace phenomena. It is proposed that undergraduate & graduate teaching impose different standards on an instructor seeking to introduce biobehavioral & biostructural concepts. The different standards arise out of the explicit & focused career instrumentality of graduate study in public administration, as well as age graded differences in receptivity to particular propositions about human nature. Ways are detailed in which biobehavioral explanation can be introduced in organizational behavior classes & in classes that consider the structure of public organizations & their decision-making processes. 32 References. HA

title: That's not fair!: The social construction of organizational (in)justice among professionals
abstract: Mitrano attempted to come to a greater understanding of the social construction of perceived injustice among professionals employed in large, bureaucratic organizational structures.

title: THE SOCIAL BASIS OF THE FRENCH CENTRAL BUREAUCRACY UNDER THE DIRECTORY 1795-1799
abstract: There being no satisfactory general picture of the French bur'cy in the crucial period of French admin'ive history formed by the French Revolution, this paper attempts to fill the gap by a detailed soc examination of some 4,300 ministerial clerks employed during the Directorial regime (1794-99) based on ministerial personnel archives. Res revealed a distinct admin'ive hierarchy roughly categorized as executives, middlegrade employees, & assistant personnel. This hierarchy was paralleled by definite soc divisions, although the majority of clerks came from sound Mc backgrounds. Clerks were drawn mainly from the better educated North Eastern region of France. The personnel were not mere sinecure seekers but were a blend of youth & experience; the latter was gained in various branches of administration both before & during the Revolution. In addition the majority served nearly 7 yrs in ministerial employment. Although conditions, security & prospects were limited, there was no shortage of recruits, as admin'ive employment did offer some shelter during the revolutionary yrs when-rather than under Napoleon as is often stated-a Weberian burley was first created in France. AA.

title: When Torture is a Duty: The Murder of Imam Yapa Kaseng and the Challenge of Accountability in Thailand
abstract: On 19 March 2008, Imam Yapa Kaseng was arrested in Narathiwat in southern Thailand and detained as a suspected insurgent by Special Task Force 39 under the provisions of martial law and the Emergency Decree on Public Administration in an Emergency Situation (hereafter Emergency Decree). Two days after his arrest, he died in the custody of the army. On 25 December 2008, the Narathiwat Provincial Court ruled that "the cause of death is that the deceased was physically assaulted by state officials ... while he was in the custody of soldiers who were performing their civil service duties". This ruling is paradoxical: Thai state officials are named as responsible for a death in custody, yet torture is categorised as a "duty". Since the ruling, Imam Yapa's family has pursued criminal, civil and internal state methods of redress, but the case has been stalled and the responsible state officials have not been held accountable. In response, I challenge this paradox by reading the inquest decision in light of both relevant national and international legal instruments and the testimonies given during the hearings. Drawing on the testimonies given during the inquest hearings, I construct an alternative narrative of suffering and state accountability.

title: Institutional Arrangements and the Measurement of Policy Consequences: Applications to Evaluating Policy Performance
abstract: A model of the policy process is presented in order to explore the relationship among instit'al arrangements, individual inter-actions & the problem of measuring performance of Ur public policies. The model includes reference to: individual interactions, the production of consequences, data recordation, data interpretation & the role of policy makers. A particular focus is placed on sources of error in the policy process. The policy process in regard to a competitive market is compared to the vicious circles described by A. Gouldner (see SA 894) & P. Blau (see SA 0624/A8842). The existing measures for evaluating policy consequences in the provision of police services are then examined so as to ascertain when this policy process is self-correcting or error amplifying. In particular, the adequacy & reliability of the FBI Index of Crime is examined. The problem of assessing the consequences of aggressive patrol is discussed in some detail. The need for new indicators for the evaluation of police performance is posed & several possible measures are discussed & evaluated for their consequences in producing error correction policy processes & adequate data for policy evaluation. AA.

title: Power, Knowledge and Organizational Transformation: Administration as Depoliticization
abstract: The use of power & knowledge to transform organizational practices in various public service organizations & institutions is examined. An overview of the transfer of private sector knowledge to the public sector in the contemporary UK is presented to account for the rise of new organizational practices. Differences between the way professionals & administrators interpret knowledge are discussed; in addition, the problems professionals-turned-administrators of public service organizations face when attempting to implement a corporate sector understanding of knowledge are addressed. The effects of the dominant position maintained by the corporate sector's understanding of knowledge on the practices of public service organizations are also considered. It is then contended that the implementation of novel surveillance methods for assessing performance standards in public service institutions serve to increase tension between individuals. Moreover, it is asserted that the corporate sector's profit-driven practices are not in accordance with the ethos of many public service organizations. It is concluded that such administrative practices are essentially de-politicizing public service institutions. 1 Table, 61 References. J. W. Parker

title: Public Decisions, Private Profits. Theoretical Considerations On Corruption
abstract: Motivated by two scandals of corruption (CCSS-Fischel and ICE-Alcatel), this article studies some theoretical approaches that may contribute to our understanding of corruption in the contracts between the State and private sector. First, some conceptual precisions are made. Then, socio-institutional conditions that facilitates corruption are analyzed. Finally, there are some reflections about the political implications of corruption, and some suggestions of measures in order to reduce our social vulnerability to this phenomenon. Adapted from the source document.

title: Governance and Participation in Local Welfare: The Case of the Italian Piani di Zona
abstract: This article analyses four cases of governance in Italian local welfare systems. Following Law 328/2000, the design and management of the social services system in Italy involve different public responsibility levels, mainly regional and municipal. In order to manage social policies, Italian municipalities have to join in new inter-municipal groupings called 'Piani di Zona' (Area Plans). Moreover, the law provides for engaging in these Plans even local third-sector organizations and citizens. The article attempts to highlight the implications of this complex system that is leading local authorities to open new governance arenas. We hereby present the results of a research project on two Piani di Zona in the Region of Lombardy (Northern Italy) and on two in the Region of Campania (Southern Italy), carried out by means of institutional analysis. We particularly focus on the dynamics of participation triggered by the Piani di Zona. Our hypothesis is that the role of public administration is a fundamental variable to understand the different ways of participating. In this sense, we discuss the dynamics of local governance by relaying them to four main questions: who participates in what, where and how?. Adapted from the source document.

title: Urban Theory and the Treatment of Differences: Administrative Practices, Social Sciences and the Difficulties of Specifics
abstract: In developing categories to address urban problems & social needs, the administrative approach has had difficulty handling the specifics of social groups & places. In this approach, generalizing/unitary attitudes have historical links with the centralist & self-referential quality of the systems for addressing needs that are typical of the administrative tradition, similar to the structuralist-institutional perspectives of the sociological tradition. However, with the changes in cultural attitudes accompanying recent trends in the industrialized world, there has been a trend toward recognition of local diversity & a need for treating social & territorial variances. This trend creates new opportunities for representations of nonunitary approaches to needs, in which social science & administration can interact. Local administrations have not taken practical advantage of the trend, which would involve restructuring. In dealing jointly with diversity & systemic connections, present theory on relationships between groups, places, & actions is inadequate & must be broadened. New convergences are needed between the social scientific & administrative approaches. 68 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Governing Gaza
abstract: A review essay on a book by Ilana Feldman, Governing Gaza: Bureaucracy, Authority, and the Work of Rule 19171967 (Durham: Duke University Press, 2008).

title: The Individual and Bureaucracy: An Alternative Meadian Interpretation
abstract: The dominant Western moral orientation of individualism, which views organizations as morally unaccountable, is challenged. Proceeding from George Herbert Mead's concept of the social mind & its unique process of reflectivity in "The Genesis of the Self and Social Control" (Reck, A. [Ed], Mead: Selected Writings, Indianapolis: Bobbs-Merrill, 1964), attention is focused on how organizations constrain human thought & how individuals, as reflective agents, invent means to protect themselves. Crucial to this position is the idea that a dialectical tension exists between organizations & individuals that is neither artificial nor reducible. As such, organizations must be viewed as morally accountable. The sound use of sociological theory to discuss moral issues has deep implications for scholars, practitioners, & citizens. 39 References. Modified HA.

title: Ideal types in public service television: Paternalists and bureaucrats, charismatic and avant-gardists
abstract: Over time, the broadcast media develop conventions of self-presentation that are formulated more or less explicitly by academics and media professionals as ideal types. The article discusses four such ideal types of self-presentation in television: paternalists and bureaucrats, charismatics and avant-gardists. It demonstrates how they have been formulated and evaluated by researchers and media professionals. Following Raymond Williams's notion of 'dominant', 'residual' and 'emergent' forms, the article also discusses the historical interactions and contests between them. Examples are drawn from Nordic and British public service broadcasting. A case is made for acknowledging the coexistence of several ideal types, rather than taking at face value notions of some general 'slide' from a paternalist past to a charismatic present. The article draws particular attention to the importance of bureaucratic modes of self-presentation for understanding early public service television, and of avant-gardist modes for understanding more recent developments.

title: Validating Health Insurance Coverage Survey Estimates: A Comparison of Self-Reported Coverage and Administrative Data Records
authors: Davern, Michael; Thiede Call, Kathleen; Ziegenfuss, Jeanette; Davidson, Gestur; Beebe, Timothy J; Blewett, Lynn
abstract: We administered a health insurance coverage survey module to a sample of 4,575 adult Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Minnesota (BCBS) members to examine if people who have health insurance coverage self-report that they are uninsured. We were also interested in whether respondents correctly classify themselves as having commercial, Medicare, MinnesotaCare, and/or Medicaid coverage (the four sample strata). The BCBS of Minnesota sample is drawn from both public and commercial health insurance coverage strata that are important to policy research involving survey data. Our findings support the validity of our health insurance module for determining whether someone who has health insurance is correctly coded as having health insurance coverage, as only 0.4 percent of the BCBS members answered the survey as though they were uninsured. However, we find problems for researchers interested in using survey responses to specific types of public coverage. For example, 21 percent of the Medicaid self-reported coverage came from known enrollees and only 67 percent of the MinnesotaCare self-reported count came from known enrollees. We conclude with a discussion of the study's implications for understanding the Medicaid "undercount" and the validity of self-reported health insurance coverage. Adapted from the source document.

title: On the Federal Scene
abstract: Four significant US federal-level activities in 1989 that are expected to impact future mental health administration are examined: (1) the State Comprehensive Mental Health Services Plan Act requires the provision of case management services & outreach to seriously mentally ill individuals receiving public funds or services, social services to homeless mentally ill, & rehabilitation, employment, housing, medical, & other support to the severely mentally ill. (2) The National Instit of Mental Health (NIMH) initiated five new research centers to investigate the organization & financing of care for the severely mentally ill, with the goal of improving long-term care in the public sector. (3) The Nursing Home Reform Act requires states to divert mentally ill persons from nursing homes to community residential care & treatment. (4) The NIMH established a program for in-service training in mental health administration. 6 References. S. G. Yates

title: Professionalism and Bureaucracy: English Doctors and the Victorian Public Health Administration
abstract: Exception is taken with O. MacDonagh's thesis that bur'tic growth is composed of a 5-stage process which underlay all of English centralization ("The Ninetheenth-Century Revolution in Government: A Reappraisal," The Historical Journal, 1958, 1, 52-67). This conception is seen as saying the bur'tic growth is continuous, almost inevitable, follows its own internal logic, that all bur'cies are essentally the same, & that bur'crats are passive agents of the process of bur'ization. A historical survey is undertaken to determine the motivations involved in the Med profession's atempts at greater involvement in Victorian England's public health admin. Through this it is hoped to discover the impact of professionalism on the course of bur'tic growth & to test the applicability of MacDonagh's model. It is emphasized here that MD's were interested in the civil service because they believed that state employment would raise the SS of the entire Med profession. F Nalitt.

title: The Ethnographer and the IRB: Comment on Kevin D. Haggerty, "Ethics Creep: Governing Social Science Research in the Name of Ethics"
abstract: Comments on Haggerty's "Ethics Creep Governing Social Science Research in the Name of Ethics" in Qualitative Sociology, 2004, 27, 4, 391-414.

title: Liberal Democracy and National Security: Continuities in the Bush and Obama Administrations
abstract: The antiterrorist policy of the George W. Bush Administration established a relationship between democracy and security that implied the limitation of the former as a necessary condition for the achievement of the latter. This strategy led to the diminishing of the basic liberties promoted by liberal democracy through legal means with the putative objective of guaranteeing the 'security' of American citizens. A key starting point of these policies can be found in undercover operations carried out abroad by the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and the Department of State at the beginning of the Cold War. This article focuses on the continuities and ruptures between the official discourse of the G. W. Bush Administration and that of the first years of the Cold War, focusing on the realist and liberal patterns present in those discourses. This leads to an analysis of the relationship between democracy and national security under the antiterrorist policy implemented by the G. W. Bush government, approached from a power elite perspective. The aggressive foreign and homeland policies of the US government were based upon a booming military-industrial pole, closely bound to free market expansionism and liberal democracy as key dimensions in the reproduction of capitalism. Included in this consideration are the 2002 and 2006 National Security Strategies, the Patriot Act (2001), and the Domestic Security Enhancement Act (2003) (or 'Patriot Act II') put in place by the G.W. Bush Administration, as well as the National Security Strategy (2009) established by President Obama. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Internationalization of Public Administration Schools in Brazil
abstract: Public administration studies programs in Brazil have always possessed a distinctive international flavor. A survey of the short history of such Brazilian schools shows that their curricula follow leading schools in the US. An arrangement between Rio de Janeiro's Fondation Getulio Vargas (established 1944) & Michigan State U, 1952-1965, provided international experience for students. A similar arrangement continues today with some 30 foreign institutions. A second, competing strand of public administration pedagogy developed in Brazil's universities also reflects international trends, eg, the program at the U of Sao Paulo. A 1998 study shows that 60% of graduates from such programs obtain employment in large, private firms that do business internationally. Many other graduates work at smaller firms in the fields of information science or telecommunications. 4 Tables, 1 Figure. L. Brentlinger

title: Conceptual Notes on the Public Interest for Public Administration and Policy Analysts
abstract: An argument is made for critical evaluation in public administration & political science. The current lack of publicly acknowledged standards of judgment results in poor direction provided to policy & research sciences. It is argued that the appropriate standard of evaluation is public interest, arising from interactions among private parties. The consequences of public interest can be assessed through projection & evaluation of agreed-upon values in "reasoned argument." Drawing on examples from twentieth-century US politics, the process of policy appraisal vis-a-vis public interest is described, with emphasis on the need for tests of generalizability & affordability. 14 References. C. Grindle

title: Local Autonomy: Urban Management in Indonesia
authors: Malo, Manasse; Nas, Peter J M
abstract: The structure of the Indonesian administrative system is both decentralized & deconcentrated, & is characterized by pluriformity, a two-tiered system, & a dual function -- national security & national development of the military. The most salient feature of the urban management system is the kotamadya, an urban municipality that serves the people living in the locality. It has no sovereignty, but cannot merely be considered as a lower rung of government subordinate to higher & more central levels. Each level of the administrative system has it own responsibilities & resources, & the independence to carry them out. The functions of the urban municipalities can be roughly divided into planning the layout & design of cities & city administration. Financial resources come largely from the central government, but are supplemented by the municipalities' own resources & private investment. Urban managerial resources consist of personnel, organization, & legal infrastructure, but each of these has constraints, eg, a shortage of officials with middle-level education, conflicts between decentralization & deconcentration, & the absence of a single & comprehensive law on urban management. 2 Tables, 2 Figures, 18 References. D. Generoli

title: Selection of Major Planning Issues
abstract: A feature of government departments is the continuous stream of policy issues which arise & require some response. Research has been undertaken, with particular reference to health services, to develop an approach to planning & policy making which would filter issues in order that those requiring an analytical rather than an administrative approach may be identified & their relative importance decided. In this way, issues of major importance could be selected for detailed planning attention, & the limited planning skills available could be used to the greatest advantage. Proposals for this process of selection are suggested, & a set of criteria is described which may be used in a procedure which is systematic yet retains political realism. 6 Figures. Modified HA.

title: Outsourced Responsibilities and New Public Management: The Context of Swedish Crisis Management As Seen From County Administration Boards
abstract: In this article, a storm named Hilde is the entry point for an exploration and analysis of the consequences of public sector reforms on the crisis management system in Sweden. The researchers are particularly interested in reforms of decentralization, privatization, and the adoption of New Public Management (NPM) mechanisms. Empirically, they study the views of Civil Defence Directors at County Administration Boards (CAB). The 21 CABs represent the central government at the regional level and are required by law to coordinate crisis management between national agencies, municipalities, and private interests. Their empirical investigations indicate that the Defence Directors perceive and adapt to reforms differently depending on the size of CABs, thereby bringing to the fore critical matters of equivalence. It also appears as if the discretion that the reforms were supposed to provide for crisis management actors is severely hampered by NPM inspired regulations, competitive features, and instruments of control.

title: Inter-Bureaucratic Civil-Military Relations in Israel: The Case of Planning Post-Peace Military Redeployment
abstract: The social impact on Israel of the redeployment of the Israeli Defense Forces in the Negev region following the Israeli-Egyptian peace agreement is examined. The military & civilian bureaucracies faced the problem of redeploying the army in a way that would yield maximum benefits with minimum damage to civilian objectives. The structure of civilian-military relations in Israel worked against the solution of this problem; the military sector's objectives were largely met, while little development took place in the civilian sector. The usual "nation-in-arms" model of civil-military relations does not appear to be valid for this situation; an alternative model is needed, the "garrison state" model of Dan Horowitz ("Is Israel a Garrison State," Jerusalem Quarterly, 1977, 4, 58-75) being one possibility. Modified HA.

title: Russia and China: Similar Past, Different Present
abstract: Kiva compares the economic and social development of Russia and China and explores the similarities in their intellectual and cultural backgrounds. Stable economic growth will require the protection of private property, controlled rule of state bureaucracy and the creation of a competitive environment. Adapted from the source document.

title: Autonomia e politização nas elites administrativas portuguesas, 1999-2009/Autonomy and politicization of the Portuguese administrative elites, 1999-2009
abstract: What is the position of the Portuguese administrative elites in the confrontation between professional autonomy and their politicization? In Portugal a pattern of professional autonomy within central government prevails. While keeping certain clientelistic traits at the local level, the Portuguese case reveals a new kind of politicization in public administration - in line with what is happening in other Western democracies. In sum, Portugal has an hybrid administrative elite recruitment pattern, containing predominant elements of professional autonomy within the central government, combined with elements of political control at agencies' level, and even clientelistic elements in the state's local branches.

title: Public-Private Partnerships for Social and Human Services: A Case Study of Nonprofit Organizations in Alabama
abstract: This paper seeks to provide an integrated theoretical framework for public-private partnership (PPPs) via the incorporation of network and collaboration perspectives, the examination of past empirical research in PPPs, and the findings in research conducted on PPPs. The authors argue that this integrated framework can contribute to the literature on PPPs and lead to a deeper understanding of the concepts involved. Applying the framework, the case study of Alabama PPPs in area of social and human services confirms some of the empirical findings from other research but also exhibits a certain variation. Adapted from the source document.

title: Dealing with child sexual assault: Recent developments
abstract: In light of the growing evidence of significant levels of child sexual abuse, bureaucracies and researchers have been recommending and producing change.  The recent developments in psychological research on child memory, in the law relating to child victims and in the management of allegations of abuseare examined.

title: A Unified Public Administration? Revisiting the Prospects of Constructing a Grand Theory for the Field 1
abstract: Since the early origins of Public Administration, scholars bemoan the absence of a grand, unifying theory for this applied, social science as a discipline. From their arguments it seems that the absence of a unified theory is largely to be blamed for the identity, existential and academic crisis which the discipline arguably experiences. If such a unified theory does not exist, and there is a general consensus that it could add value by focusing research and generally facilitating a sharper demarcation of the study field, the appropriate question is: Why not simply attempt to construct one? The purpose of this paper is to reflect on the feasibility of designing a unified theory as a coherent framework for the study of Public Administration. The reflection will include a deliberation on the desirability of such a unifying theory, contemplation on the possible methodology to pursue such a theory, as well as an exploration of the potential challenges which theorists will face in their attempts to design such an integrated and comprehensive foundational framework.

title: WHO GETS THE DADDY BONUS? Organizational Hegemonic Masculinity and the Impact of Fatherhood on Earnings
authors: Hodges, Melissa J; Budig, Michelle J
abstract: Using the 1979-2006 waves of the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth, we investigate how the earnings bonus for fatherhood varies by characteristics associated with hegemonic masculinity in the American workplace: heterosexual marital status, professional/managerial status, educational attainment, skill demands of jobs, and race/ethnicity. We find the earnings bonus for fatherhood persists after controlling for an array of differences, including human capital, labor supply, family structure, and wives' employment status. Moreover, consistent with predictions from the theory pf hegemonic masculinity within bureaucratic organizations, the fatherhood bonus is significantly larger for men with other markers of workplace hegemonic masculinity. Men who are white, married, in households with a traditional gender division of labor, college graduates, professional/managerial workers and whose jobs emphasize cognitive skills and deemphasize physical strength receive the largest fatherhood earnings bonuses. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: La dimensión relacional del gobierno abierto y el liderazgo colaborativo/The relational dimension of open government and collaborative leadership
abstract: This article explain the rational dimension of open government, which implicates governmental innovation sustained with civic knowledge and the development of public policies in favor of this governance as a new form of governing. It concludes that public management is derived from the compromise of public officials and citizens with the government, facilitating civic intelligence, management control via the social controller, as well as a shared conception of what is public, and that the collaborative, interactive, and entrepreneur competences are fundamental for public management.

title: Criminal Due Process in the Administrative State
abstract: A discussion of the due process revolution of the 1960s & devolution that helped legitimize the expansion of the administrative state, with attention to impact on the US system of criminal procedure. It is argued that the very procedures that were introduced as extensions of due process have become mechanisms for circumventing & diminishing due process rights. Further, there has been an erosion of the distinction between criminal & administrative procedure that is on the verge of transforming the criminal process into a species of the new administrative process. It is argued that criminal laws are applied & criminal punishments enacted through procedures that were once labeled illegal, but are now labeled administrative & thus are hidden in the different legality of the administrative state. It is concluded that the discourse & methodology of administrative due process lead to very different outcomes (marked by less protection of the individual) than those of criminal due process. 70 References. D. Schwartz

title: Administrative Compensation of Medical Injuries: A Hardy Perennial Blooms Again
authors: Barringer, Paul J; Studdert, David M; Kachalia, Allen B; Mello, Michelle M
abstract: Periods in which the costs of personal injury litigation and liability insurance have risen dramatically have often provoked calls for reform of the tort system, and medical malpractice is no exception. One proposal for fundamental reform made during several of these volatile periods has been to relocate personal injury disputes from the tort system to an alternative, administrative forum. In the medical injury realm, a leading incarnation of such proposals in recent years has been the idea of establishing specialized administrative "health courts." Despite considerable stake-holder and policy-maker interest, administrative compensation proposals have tended to struggle for broad political acceptance. In this article, we consider the historical experience of administrative medical injury compensation proposals, particularly in light of comparative examples in the context of workplace injuries, automobile injuries, and vaccine injuries. We conclude by examining conditions that may facilitate or impede progress toward establishing demonstration projects of health courts. Adapted from the source document.

title: Muslim Representation in the Three Ottoman vilayets of Macedonia: Administration and Military Power (1878-1908)
abstract: Within the frame of the late Ottoman Empire the historical region of Macedonia was divided into three vilayets. The Ottomans were represented by "the two pillars" of the regime: the administration and the army. This paper presents the link between Muslims and Ottomans within the turbulent Macedonian context of the rise of nationalism. In the three vilayets, the central power took the form of a pyramidal organization topped by a local governor (vali). The paper studies the administration with an emphasis on portraits of several valis and their links with the central authority under Sultan Abdulhamit II's rule. It also discusses the relationships between the non-Muslim population and symbolic representations of the Ottoman order such as the local police and the judiciary. Further, the urban landscape as a reflection of the tanzimat spirit is also analyzed. Military power is presented via a comparative study of the three garrisons in Selanik, Manastir and Uskub, which emphasizes the everyday life of the soldiers and the implementation of the reforms imposed by the Great Powers following the Murzsteg Agreement of 1903. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Gentrification of Public Welfare
abstract: Public welfare agencies are assuming responsibility for the problems of an increasing number of middle-class Americans. Six factors contributing to this gentrification of public welfare agencies are discussed: (1) growing demands for services from nontraditional clients, (2) restructuring of public welfare's service delivery system, (3) declining resources, (4) increasing emphasis on child protective services, (5) expanding child support enforcement efforts, & (6) social work's diminishing role in public welfare. Strategies are presented for ensuring that the needs of traditional public welfare clients -- ie, poorer people -- are met. 2 Figures, 51 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The institutional dimension to urban governance and territorial management in the Lisbon metropolitan area
abstract: Approaches to governance have been influential in the design and implementation of urban policies. The state and public administration no longer play the exclusive role, focusing now on the coordination of interests for achieving collective goals. The organisational capacities of the central/regional and local powers are, therefore, critical to urban management efficiency. The article analyses the Lisbon metropolitan area, looking into practices of planning and governance in terms of (i) the role of municipalities determining patterns of development relative to the central state and public companies; (ii) the emergence of municipal and inter-municipal institutions and companies in the management and provision of services. Adapted from the source document.

title: 中国传统社会的双轨治理体系——封建与郡县之辨 / The Double-Track Governance in Chinese Traditional Society: Dialectics between System of Enfeoffment and System of Prefectures & Counties
abstract: Since Yin-Zhou and Qin-Han, the development of Chinese imperial system revolved around the dialectical tension between the feudal system of fiefdom (封建制) and the bureaucratic prefectural system (郡县制). In Fei Xiaotong's words, it is a dual-track politics of "Power of Monarch" and "Power of Gentry." Under fiefdom, the relationship between monarch and his kinship was governed by the Confucian hierarchical principle of favoring the intimate (qin-qin) and respecting the superior (zun-zun), and ritualized by the patriarchal order of clan, mourning rites and ancestral worship. In addition, "Mandate of Heaven" solidified an organic relationship between the emperor and his subjects and became the foundation for the monarchical rule. The prefectural system highlighted the historical change since the Warring States that had abolished the feudal fiefdom system and gave the birth of an "All under the Heaven" (公天下). Thinkers like Wang Fuzi and Gu yanwu place emphasis on fiefdom as a counterpart of the prefectural system to break up the centralization of power and renew the debate on the dialectic between "public" and "private." In sum, the feudal system of Fiefdom in China still needs to be clarified through reexamining the classical texts.

title: The Market Form in United Kingdom Education: Information, Values and Political Control
abstract: It is argued that the British educational system is overly bureaucratic, & that its schools are overdetermined by the UK's policy decisions. National curricula that have been established are described, & continual government intervention into the educational arena is discussed. It is held that the result of this tight regulation is a highly organized "loose-tight" market, & the emergence of the market form in the public sector is examined. The resource of "performance formation" is addressed, & attention is given to fabrications & the role of teaching in the education market. The way management approaches have overtaken & dismissed the "service ethic" previously existent in the British educational system is reviewed, & the underlying social category shift that has allowed these transformations is considered. 25 References. D. Weibel

title: Sex and Power in the Federal Bureaucracy: A Comparative Analysis of Male and Female Supervisors
authors: South, Scott J; Bonjean, Charles M; Corder, Judy; Markham, William T
abstract: Questionnaire data from 152 F employees & 46 supervisors in a large federal bureaucracy are used to test R. M. Kanter's hypothesis that sex differences in supervisory behavior result from sex differences in organizational power (Men and Women of the Corporation, New York: Basic Books, 1977). F subordinates of F supervisors, compared to F subordinates of M supervisors, reported less job satisfaction & lower group morale & were more likely to describe their supervisor's behavior as controlling & particularistic. However, when differences in organizational power (as measured by an index comprising supervisor's job status, the amount of voice they believe they have in their superior's decisions, & the amount of autonomy they feel they have with respect to their superior) are controlled, differences between M & F supervisors on all of these variables are significantly reduced. The results are interpreted as providing support for Kanter's theory. HA.

title: When Clients Complain: Bureaucratic Responsiveness in Large Federal Agencies
abstract: High error rates in entitlements & slow responses to client complaints by federal agencies are analyzed from a market-power frame of reference, focusing on the relative powerlessness of agency clients in relation to the agencies themselves, which hold monopolies of life-sustaining benefits. Data from a survey of 125 members of the US Congress are presented to provide an estimate of error rates. Three alternative structural solutions to the problem of unresponsiveness are assessed, including increased congressional casework service, ombudsmen services, & the use of federal information centers to aid clients. Necessary quality control procedures to facilitate each solution are described. 2 Tables. Modified HA.

title: Democratic Inclusion and the Governance of Immigration
abstract: The standard view that democratic governance of immigration amounts to the self-rule of citizens to the exclusion of migrants stands in tension with the democratic logic of political inclusion suggested by the all-affected interests principle. However, while all who are affected by immigration and border control must be included in their governance, such inclusion claims must be differentiated according to the kinds of interests at stake if this principle is to preserve the democratic ideal of self-rule. In contrast to those who argue that the principle either requires a global demos or threatens to undermine stable democratic states, this article argues that the principle requires recognizing the interest people have in a viable democratic political order, and that territorial states are the contingent vehicle for this interest in contemporary circumstances. This insight provides a principled basis for differentiating the inclusion claims of citizens and potential immigrants. As members of democratic states, citizens are responsible for the decisions and actions of their state and hence for authorizing policies on immigration and border control, but they must do so via institutions that ensure accountability to potential immigrants on the basis of their affected interests.

title: Worker Administration in the Mexican National Railways
abstract: The term of Mexican president Lazaro Cardenas del Rio was characterized by an economic policy promoting capitalism. A key aspect of his program was the expropriation of various industries of public interest & the promotion of cooperatives & worker administrations to manage them, including the Mexican National Railways, supervised by a worker administration from 1938 to 1940. An examination of the worker administration's founding, management of labor unions, & motives for reorganization shows that persistent problems with unions led the government to withhold financial support &, ultimately, to disband the worker administration. 3 Tables. M. Meeks

title: On the Organizational Question
abstract: I agree with the claim that there is no such thing as a structureless group that persists for any length of time. There is also no such thing as a protest movement that masters the basic tasks of communication and coordination, and that is nevertheless literally unorganized. So, finally, let us put those canards aside, and then maybe we can go on to consider the advantages and disadvantages to the movement of different kinds of structure or organization. And here there are real disagreements, not about organization per se, but about kinds of organization, and specifically about vertical and horizontal organization, or bureaucratic hierarchical organization and looser modes of collaboration that permit internal democracy and a good deal of autonomy to the collaborators. The socialist, social democratic, and labor movements of the past did create top-down bureaucracies. But more recent movements have struggled to create alternative forms of organization, sometimes called anarchist, emphasizing internal direct democracy. We can see the beginning of this trend in the civil rights movement's Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee and the antiwar movement of the 1960s. It emerged again in the Clamshell Alliance, and in the environmental protest groups of the '70s and '80s. It was a major preoccupation of the Global Justice movement. And now this vision of a movement organized horizontally and democratically has sprung up again in the Occupy movement. Immanuel Wallerstein (2012) describes this tendency as a revolt against the verticalism of the Old Left, against the view that there should be one controlling movement in each country. The horizontalists think instead that since there are multiple kinds of injustice, there should be multiple justice movements, but that the movements should speak to each other and legitimate each other (Wallerstein 2012). Adapted from the source document.

title: Organizational Responsibility and Local Administration: The Case of Melfi
abstract: During the 1990s, major efforts have been underway to orient Italian public administration toward granting greater autonomy to local publicly owned companies. Law 142, passed in June 1990, recognized the comune (municipality) as the primary promoter of economic development on the local level. The 1970s & 1980s saw a loss of public confidence in government administration due to bureaucratic ineptitude. Proceeding from Max Weber's definition of governmental responsibility, three levels of responsibility identified in James D. Thompson's L'azione organizzativa ([Organizational Action] Turin: Isedi, 1988) are applied to the problematic building of a new Fiat automotive plant in the small community of Melfi in southern Italy. Considerable discrepancies are noticed between theory & practice. 1 Table, 1 Figure, 43 References. M. Meeks

title: Political Corruption in a Thai Province
abstract: Data were gathered from 50 leading figures in the province who were administered a questionnaire containing a series of questions related to corruption. Data analysis leads to the conclusion that (1) Thai officials attempt to maximize their own interests in terms of financial rewards & sociopolitical status. The evaluation of the best methods to achieve one's goals 'is a function of the expectations of others as well as one's particular role orientations.' (2) In the province under study, relationships are based on a superior-subordinate model, & stem from persons seeking advantageous ties to assure goal satisfaction. 5 Tables, 1 Figure. M. Cain.

title: Ministerial and Parliamentary Elites in an Executive-Dominated System: Post-Soviet Russia 1991-2009
abstract: This article analyzes the recruitment and circulation of ministerial and parliamentary elites in Russia from the Soviet Union's collapse in 1991 until 2009. The social backgrounds and careers of all ministers in 13 cabinets (1991-2009) and all members of the State Duma during its five terms after 1993 are studied. Especially during Vladimir Putin's presidency (2000-2008), a shift toward super-presidentialism altered the circulation and composition of ministerial and parliamentary elites. Cabinets in Moscow consisted increasingly of ministers recruited from state bureaucracies, while the State Duma more and more contained businessmen, party politicians, and celebrities who appeared to treat MP service as simply an episode in their wider careers. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Effects of Bureaucratic Versus Familistic Environment on the Role Definition of Chronic Mental
abstract: With reference to current literature, role definition within mental hospital life is contrasted to role definition during family-care. Clarification & redefinition is needed of the claim that primary group associations within the hospital & family-care home should be encouraged because they are paramount toward a treatment-oriented "socialization" of the patient & are a motivational factor for self-help. The present bureaucratic nature of the mental hospital tends to deter the goals that the medical model strives to achieve. By fostering feelings of dependency, subordination, & submissiveness, mental hospitals tend to inhibit the patient from developing a healthy give-&-take emotional response to others. Primary face-to-face associations, when fostered, could better meet emotional needs, & could become a determining & contributing part of the crucial environment inputs. These associations would help encourage the patient to respond more independently to his milieu. Modified HA.

title: Perspectives on Policy, Planning and Administration Tasks in Spain and the United States
abstract: Scale data are used to compare preparation for roles in policy, planning, & administration among 82 graduate social work students in the US & 23 social service managers in Madrid, Spain. Special attention is given to tasks & activities emphasized by both groups. 5 References. Modified AA

title: The class-origin wage gap: heterogeneity in education and variations across market segments
abstract: This paper uses unique population-level matched employer-employee data on monthly wages to analyse class-origin wage gaps in the Swedish labour market. Education is the primary mediator of class origin advantages in the labour market, but mobility research often only considers the vertical dimension of education. When one uses an unusually detailed measure of education in a horizontal dimension, the wage gap between individuals of advantaged and disadvantaged class origin is found to be substantial (4-5 per cent), yet considerably smaller than when measures are used which only control for level of education and field of study. This is also the case for models with class or occupation as outcome. The class-origin wage gap varies considerably across labour market segments, such as those defined by educational levels, fields of education, industries and occupations in both seemingly unsystematic and conspicuous ways. The gap is small in the public sector, suggesting that bureaucracy may act as a leveller. Adapted from the source document.

title: Personal Rule in Africa: The Case of Eritrea
abstract: Notwithstanding the on-going struggles for democratic transformation, many African countries still lack rudimentary principles of the rule of law and legitimate political institutions. Contemporary Eritrea exemplifies this type of situation in which personal rule is the embodiment of the political system. The article argues that the perpetuation of personal rule in Eritrea is explained by the political strategy of unleashing sheer coercive force against citizens by the military whose loyalty is bought off by providing its top echelons control over substantial state economic resources. This is facilitated by a culture of impunity fostered by a legacy of three decades of guerrilla conflict, and by deliberately keeping the rest of society off-balance in an economic situation characterized by rampant poverty. The regimenting of civil-society institutions within the power structures and chapters of party-controlled organizations has reduced them into instruments of social control in order to diffuse any form of organized resistance. Finally, the party and the bureaucracy as agents of the state function to accentuate the symbolic dimensions of socio-economic activities to which the entire society is mobilized in order to wedge the immense legitimacy gap and make the system appear popular. Adapted from the source document.

title: Covering whoever is eligible? An exploratory study on the eligibility of the Urban Minimum Living Standard Guarantee in China
abstract: This article puts the policy goal of the Urban Minimum Living Standard Guarantee (UMLSG) in China into question and it aims to expose the assertion 'covering whoever is eligible' as a myth. An exploratory study of the implementation of the UMLSG eligibility criteria was launched in Guangzhou. Interviews were conducted with twenty-five poor people and local bureaucrats. In addition to people's meeting the income requirement, it was discovered that there were three unwritten principles flexibly used by local bureaucrats in assessment: the ability to work, the family unit and clientelism. The prevalence of street-level bureaucracy in the UMLSG administration not only hampered state resources from reaching the families living in urban poverty, but also seriously contradicted the reformulated ideologies and undermined the party's legitimacy. The findings of this study suggest that variations in UMLSG eligibility, which are causing a serious problem of under-coverage, should attract immediate attention from both officials and academics. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright holder.]

title: Managerial Discourse and the Restructuring of a District Authority
abstract: A case study of a district authority in GB highlights the complex nature of managerial discourse in its relation to both central & local government. This relation is above all mediated by shifting conceptions of public service on the part of managers & those in nonmanagerial positions. It is concluded that, due to the structural constraints under which local authorities operate directly, managerial discourse is becoming increasingly significant in the reconstitution of professional & semiprofessional identities. 49 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Old wine in new bottles: Democratic peace as empowerment of states in conflict resolution
abstract: This article examines the capacities of various regimes to master conflicts. The capacities of regimes are measured by an empowerment index that reflects more accurately the capacity of states to manage conflicts than measures of democracy. The study draws from a wide range of indicators to calculate values of the independent variables 'challenges' and 'support' for each existing state. In addition to these explanatory factors, regime factors are calculated independently. The dependent variable 'conflict' draws on the data set by Kosimo (http://www.kosimo.de) and is based on the number of conflicts occurring between 1945 and 2000. These conflicts are then considered in relation to the management capacities of each state. The analysis shows that the empowerment indicator is a better predictor of conflict involvement than the regime indicator. Cross-calculations also show that, not surprisingly, on the whole, democracies have had a better record in the management of conflicts than other regimes. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: From Voluntary Association to Welfare State: The Illinois Immigrants' Protective League, 1908-1926
abstract: The History of the Illinois Immigrant League from 1908 to 1926 raises the possibility of a model which both historians & soc sci'ts might use to explain the development of US public bur'cies in general. The people who founded the League's work were primarily from the professions. Enough biographical data was available for 40 out of 60 trustees, officers, & executive committee members between 1908 & 1917 to construct a collective biography which confirms that pattern. 20% were lawyers, 22.5% were Coll professors, 12.5% were career soc workers, 7.5% were MD's, 15% were other professionals, & 22.5% were businessmen. All of the businessmen were high level managers in large Corp's as opposed to entrepreneurs, inheritors of fam concers, or self-employed owners of small enterprises. Business manag was itself becoming a profession in those yrs, & the predominance of the managerial type among the League's directors may in fact be further evidence of its professional base. A more general model of bur'tic development in the US context could be formulated as follows. In a country where decison-making has been highly decentralized & where the natural impulse was always toward local autonomy & a suspicion of gov, the voluntary assoc assumed a crucial role in developing the expertise & the org necessary to manage soc problems. When the state finally acted, the minimum requirements of knowledge, personnel, & procedure were already available in the experience of private assoc's org'ed by professional experts in related fields. Modified AA.

title: The Public-Private Relationship in Social Services: The Role of the Third Sector
abstract: The strategic alliance between public administration and the Third Sector is key for the development of a management model for social services in general in the future, and specifically for the externalized management of services in which it acts as a protagonist, given the social solvency of the Third Sector and its ability to multiply public funds. The Third Sector is an emerging player and contributes efficiency and social cohesion. We should move forward in measuring its impact and specific value added by identifying the social clauses which are used in public procurement, in the strengthening and structuring of the sector as well as in the capitalization and professionalization of social entities. Some of the principal challenges of the public-private relationship are identified and some proposals for the future are put forth. Adapted from the source document.

title: State Management of Careers Workplace Conflict, and Regime Legitimacy in Socialist China
abstract: Recent research indicates that career mobility under Chinese Communist rule has been shaped by state political screening & shifts in official ideology. Drawing on Weber's concept of modern bureaucracy & a study of schoolteachers in the Mao era (1949 1976), this article suggests that within the workplace official control of careers engendered an inferior & heterogeneous corps of management personnel, a deep schism between management & the staff, & a fractured division of labor. The antitheses of the rational features of modern bureaucracy, these arrangements fostered workplace friction & political resentment that precipitated post-Mao reforms. Primary evidence comes from recently declassified government documents & firsthand interviews with retired teachers. 2 Tables, 71 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: State Business Relations and Economic Growth in Sub-Saharan Africa
authors: Sen, Kunal; Velde, Dirk Willem Te
abstract: This paper contributes to the literature on the determinants of economic growth in sub-Saharan Africa by examining the effect of effective state-business relations on economic growth for a panel of 19 sub-Saharan African countries for the period 1970-2004. We propose a measure that we argue captures the various dimensions of effective state-business relations in sub-Saharan Africa. We then estimate standard growth regressions using dynamic panel data methods with this measure, along with the more conventionally used measures of institutional quality such as degree of executive constraints, the rule of law, the degree of corruption and the quality of the bureaucracy. Our results show that effective state-business relations contribute significantly to economic growth - countries which have shown improvements in state-business relations have witnessed higher economic growth, controlling for other determinants of economic growth and independent of other measures of institutional quality. Adapted from the source document.

title: Law-Making as Administrative Behaviour: The Case of Investment Regulation in Hungary
abstract: Lawmaking -- legal norm creation -- is analyzed as an organizational reaction to uncertainty, based on participant observation of 29 regulatory processes between 1974 & 1979 in Hungarian public bureaucracies. Public agencies in Hungary are responsible for government (public) investment & for the gross national investment, as realized by autonomous state-owned enterprises. The data reveal that the authorities were unable to cope with the problems of high investment outlays, & reacted in a way that resembles J. G. March's & J. P. Olsen's ' 'garbage-can" model (Ambiguity and Choice in Organizations, Universitetsforlaget: Bergen, 1976). A standard reaction to uncertainty is recurrent lawmaking; eg, the duration of life of all the relevant rules & regulations observed was about 13 months. Case studies of 50 Hungarian investment regulation projects indicate that lawmaking & its qualitative deterioration can be explained in terms of administrative behavior. It is concluded that the inclination, especially in Eastern-Central Europe, toward the selective use of law & lawmaking as legal regulation is cheap & has sufficient publicity & weight to appease the public. 12 References. Modified AA

title: Max Weber's Charisma
abstract: Scholars have concentrated on Max Weber's notions of traditional and                 bureaucratic authority because these figure prominently in his lifelong concern with                 the rise of Western rationality. However, Weber himself often characterized what                 something is by showing what it is not. In his discussions of the third type of                 authority, charisma, he demonstrates what charisma is not then what it                 is. He contrasts the permanence, rules and impartiality of bureaucratic                 authority with the changing, arbitrary and personal characteristics of charismatic                 leadership. Weber also opposes the 'everydayness' and economic                 concerns of the bureaucratic and traditional authorities with the                 'extraordinary' feature and otherworldly indifference of the                 revolutionary nature of the charismatic leader. I contend that his examination of                 charisma is not merely another of his important sociological studies; in addition,                 it has far-ranging implications for showing the strengths and weaknesses of the                 religious and especially of the politically charismatic leader.

title: The childcatchers: An exploration of the representations and discourses of social work in UK film and television drama from the 1960s to the present day
abstract: SummaryThis article reports on research undertaken to critically examine portrayals, representations and discourses of social work and social workers in UK film and television drama from the 1960s to the present day. The research analysed four film and television dramas where social work and social workers were featured: Cathy Come Home (1966), Ladybird Ladybird (1994), Happy Go Lucky (2008) and Oranges and Sunshine (2010). The research aimed to examine portrayals and representations of social work and social workers in UK film and television drama; inform and develop an understanding of contemporary narratives and discourses about social work and contribute to debates about the purpose and future of social work.FindingsPortrayals and representations of social work in UK film and television drama often encourage and reinforce an overly simplistic, hostile and negative impression of the profession, work which is presented as predominantly focused on child protection and the removal of children from families. Social workers are typically characterised as incompetent, bureaucratic, well-meaning but misguided. This potentially endorses neo-liberal ideologies and discourses about welfare, welfare recipients, welfare provision and social service.ApplicationsThis approach to the topic offers an accessible and interesting platform for research, teaching and policy development, which has the potential to critically inform debates about the future and purpose of social work and welfare in the United Kingdom.

title: BUREAUCRACY AND PRESENT SOCIETY
abstract: The systematic study of bur'cy goes back to the 1st quarter of the 20th cent, with M. Weber & R. Michels. Weber distinguished 3 fundamental types of pol'al domination: charismatic, traditional, & legal-rational. The purest legal-rational type is that which is exercised by the interpreter of a bur'tic structure. It rests essentially on a preliminary distribution of tasks, a hierarchy of fuctions, the establishment of abstract standards, a formal impersonality, a stress on technical qualification & an org oriented exclusively toward res of efficiency. The conception of Weber, very close to that of the pioneers of the sci'fic org of labor, is strongly criticized by the HR specialists, who reproach him for his overly formal principles, or his mechanicalism. However, this 2nd group is losing force today, because it is appearing more & more that the faults of the bur'tic org require an increase in org. It is important, above all, to consider the bur as an instrument, & not as end, & to distinguish bur'cy from tur'tion. Tr by E. Weiman from IPSA.

title: Speaking Precision to Power: The Modern Political Role of Social Science
abstract: The distancing from politics by social science is threatened by the current flourishing of partisan think tanks & the campaign for "sound science." The impulse to social quantification traces its roots from Weber & Condorcet, through the aristocratic Victorian National Association for the Promotion of Social Science, & the Statistical Society of London. Social science is characterized as public & administrative deliberation until the late 19th century, and has grown as an alliance of rationalized bureaucracy that has made precise measurement central in response to political demands. The rise of decision technologies to focus on precision in measuring the value of human life has evolved into the image of scientific knowledge as strict, controlled reason, governed by experimental & mathematical demonstration. The critique of precision as public reason is concluded to be creating a critical shift, away from the 20th century idealization of disciplinary autonomy & rigorous objectivity. Scientific practices are attempting to deal with complexity particularly in modeling local climate change, but the uncertainties of drawing conclusions about the reality of rising global temperatures must involve diverse communities of researchers to reveal the structure & outcome of an immensely complex process, & reason discussion within & outside disciplinary communities to interpret the results. References. J. Harwell

title: Illusions of Affection: Bureaucratic Ritualization's Relation to Emotional Abuse and Neglect in Nursing Homes
authors: Ulsperger, Jason S; Knottnerus, J David
abstract: This research uses 40 ethnographies, biographies, and autobiographies to explore various symbolic themes expressed through everyday interaction in nursing homes. The themes involve bureaucratic concepts such as staff separation, rules, documentation, and efficiency. They also involve ideas of emotional abuse and neglect, like objectification, compassion transgressions, and spiritual negligence. Relying on structural ritualization theory, we argue ritualized symbolic practices of bureaucracy unintentionally facilitate attitudes and acts of emotional neglect in both for-profit and nonprofit nursing homes. This assists in the development of rituals facilitating the poor treatment of residents. Overall, we propose that if society is going to have humane care for nursing home residents, it must first understand the ritual dynamics that lead to employees viewing and treating those they care for with a lack of dignity. Adapted from the source document.

title: Professions in Policy and Knowledge Transfer: Adaptations of Lean Management, and Jurisdictional Conflict in a Reform of the French Public Service
abstract: The question of how lean management has been transferred to public services and adapted in differing professional and international contexts, though important, is underresearched in sociology and political science. This article addresses one main issue concerning lean: what role do professions play in the transfer and implementation of policy and knowledge? This article draws on policy transfer theories and the sociology of professions to examine how consultants and the French state agency in charge of "modernizing the administration" worked to implement lean management within national and local French public services, including the judicial system. This led them to take principles and methods developed in the private and corporate sectors and translate them to public, professional, and state rationales. Lean is a multipurpose management tool, and so easier for professionals to appropriate despite "jurisdictional conflicts" (Abbott 1988), either with consultants or else between professional groups. The article shows how the transfer of managerial instruments, rationale, and know-how can, in many cases, challenge professionalism and generate resistance.

title: Administrative Issues in Substitute Care
abstract: An examination of whether local administrative systems are currently consistent with 1980 federal legislation mandates (US Public Law 96-272) & whether they implement the legislation's general philosophy -- permanency planning -- in the administrative system. Data from mail/telephone surveys with a child welfare supervisor in each of 69 Wisc counties & from state records reveal that most Wisc counties have made significant administrative changes, some of which have successfully reduced the time children spend in substitute care & the proportion of children in long-term care. Research in other states is needed to more completely assess the efficacy of permanency planning measures. 5 Tables. Modified HA

title: THE PHILADELPHIA EXPERIENCE
abstract: In a historic US city, pol'al reform elevated recreation to an equal position among 10 services reporting to the Managing Director. By the implementation of a broad philosophy of recreation through efficient management practices, Philadelphia has developed a program which sets a high standard for US cities. To cope with increasing quantities of leisure & new areas of service, imaginative planning, programming, personnel admin, & enlarged facilities are necessary. Further, coordination & correlation of community efforts must be achieved. AAAPSS.

title: Speaking Seriously: Part II
abstract: A continuation of a paper published in Theory and Society, 1974, 1, 1, 1-15 is presented. "Bureaucratic" speakers conceal their own authoritative claims. While sociological phenomenology & ethnomethodology make their topic the rules employed by laymen in assembling (through their accounts) the recognizable character of their world, observers' accounts of members' usage, by grounding themselves in correspondence theories of truth, have tended to assimilate themselves to this bureaucratic usage. As an alternative to accounts which ask to be taken seriously as an adequate description of members' usage, it is suggested, following Wittgenstein, that accounts (both lay & sociological) necessarily exemplify forms of life. More specifically, both the grading of the promotion review panel (discussed in Part I) & de-authored accounts of that grading are addressed as expressing the form of life of alienated labor. The commitment of such usage to a concealment behind "technique" serves to efface the mode of production. An attempt is made to clarify this assertion by reference to Marx's early view of writing as "confession" & Heidegger's notion of "dialogue." A provisional version of writing & reading as activities that circle around their mode of production is offered as an alternative to the "functionary" mode of existence that is proposed as the character of "bureaucratic" speech. AA.

title: Bureaucrats versus the State in Capitalist and Socialist Regimes
abstract: Failure to maintain a sharp analytical distinction between the state & its bureaucrats has led to unnecessary confusion in studies of capitalist & socialist political systems. The state is an arena of conflict, while bureaucrats are one group participating in conflict. Liberal & Marxist traditions of scholarship have contributed in different ways to blurring the distinction between states & bureaucrats. 1 Table. AA

title: Seventeen Years of Judicializing Politics
authors: Vianna, Luiz Werneck; Burgos, Marcelo Baumann; Salles, Paula Martins
abstract: This article studies the judicialization of politics in Brazil, based on an analysis of a database containing 3.648 ADINs filed between 1988 & 2005. Examining this data, the overall impression gained is that ADINs are now a normal part of the everyday running of the modern Brazilian democracy, their institutional presence consolidated over almost two decades through successive & different governments -- & even more firmly in the current Lula government. Over this time, they have functioned as a channel for the conflicts between society & the State, as well as conflicts within the Public Administration & the Federation. Hence, as well as being an instrument for the defense of minorities, their original constitutional function, the research shows that the ADINs are also a strategic institutional resource for government, turning the Federal Supreme Court in practice into a kind of Council of State prevalent in countries with unitary governments. Tables, Graphs, References. Adapted from the source document.

title: THE POLITICS OF CHINA'S DEATH PENALTY REFORM IN THE CONTEXT OF GLOBAL ABOLITIONISM
abstract: This paper explores the influences of worldwide anti-death penalty campaigns in the local institutional environment in China and its implications for China's capital punishment reforms in recent years. It found a 'concentric pattern' of the dissemination of human rights values and anti-death penalty activisms may explain the varying attitudes towards human rights and international activism among different social groups across the Chinese society. Divergent interests of and perceptions held by national-level and lower-level legal elites are likely to be one of the causes for China to adopt an incremental reformist stance. Further, this study shows that the Chinese legal elites were poorly informed of the current status of public opinion on capital punishment. A populist-sentiment-driven administration of capital punishment is closely tied to reliance on capital punishment. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: University-Industry Linkages and Economic Development: The Case of Thailand
abstract: This article analyzes university-industry linkages (UILs) in Thailand at the national level and in four sectors (automotive, textiles-garments, agro-industry, and electronics). Public officials and firm managers recognize the importance of UILs for meeting challenges facing Thai producers. But with interesting exceptions, Thai UILs are frail. This is due to protection and low levels of innovation resulting in few private sector efforts to link up with universities; rigid structures and weak incentives in the Thai universities discouraging ties with business; and generally fragmented Thai bureaucracy. Underlying these obstacles is inconsistent support for UILs on the part of political leaders. [Copyright 2007 Elsevier Ltd.]

title: 'As Unremarkable as the Air They Breathe'? Reforming Police Management in South Africa
abstract: With the transition to democratic governance in South Africa in 1994, the public service was identified as the key sector requiring transformation. This involved refashioning the types of delivery offered to the public & a complete renovation of labour relations practices & institutions within public service organizations. The police were expected to dramatically change their labour relations framework & practices to allow for increased 'worker' participation in decision-making processes & enhanced performance management. This article examines attempts at transforming police labour relations in one unit of the South African Police Service. Existing legacies of authoritarianism & police disciplinary customs & a lack of directive leadership from management have seriously limited this attempt at transforming police labour relations. This, in turn, has hampered the unit's transition towards operating in accordance with the community policing framework that is supposed to guide the practice of the 'new' South African Police Service. 74 References. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright 2004.]

title: Book Review: Sociology for Health Professionals in Ireland
abstract: Hyde, Abbey, Lohan, Maria and McDonnell, Orla, Sociology for Health Professionals in Ireland. Dublin, Institute of Public Administration, 2004, paperback [euro]29.00, 384 pp.

title: Everyday Government in Extraordinary Times: Persistence and Authority in Gaza's Civil Service, 1917-1967
abstract: Examines how the mandate system, developed in the aftermath of WWI, shaped the relationship between former colonial governments & emerging nation-states, focusing on the case of the Gaza Strip & the relationship between Israel & Egypt. Data drawn from ethnographic & archival research on the civil service in Gaza during the British Mandate (1917-1948) & the Egyptian Administration (1948-1967) demonstrate the workings of the Gaza government through the eyes & activities of everyday workers. Though it lacked stability & clarity, it is shown that the Gaza civil service was able to create "bureaucratic authority without authenticity" & to maintain this through its everyday practices of "repetitive bureaucracy.". K. Hyatt Stewart

title: S. N. Eisenstadt's Concept of Political Systems of Bureaucratic Societies
abstract: A review of S. N. Eisenstadt's The Political System of Empires (New York: Free Press of Glencoe, 1963 [see IRPS No. 28/85a37015]). After presenting Eisenstadt's theoretical & methodological approach, considered are his views on the conditions necessary for establishing centralized political systems, the role of the bureaucracy in political processes, & the functioning & self-preservation of the political systems of historical bureaucratic societies. A particular advantage of Eisenstadt's theory is the successful sociological analysis of the formation of the bureaucracy, its self-perpetuation, & its motives & goals. S. Karganovic.

title: Policing's Productive Folds: Secretism and Authenticity in Brazilian Cultural Heritage
abstract: Social scientists typically treat policing as repressive and historical centers as impoverished imitations of unmarked social relations. Yet in Salvador, Brazil's Pelourinho Historical Center, police attempts to discipline both tourists and working-class residents, together with these officers' violent support of attempts to separate people from their practices memorialized as public culture, generate perforations or folds in the musealized landscape. These structures of feeling support the neighborhood's aura of rooted authenticity. In this way they punctuate, and thus veil, the heritage zone's fraught construction and support the ideological goals of Bahia's cultural heritage bureaucracy that claims to safeguard humankind's shared legacies. This emphasis on the productivity of policing is not to argue that such spaces are bona fide tokens of Brazilian pasts or popular vitality, but to suggest the importance of policing in animating supposedly homogeneous spaces. Adapted from the source document.

title: An Exploratory Study of Public Service Motivation and the Institutional-Occupational Model of the Military
authors: Taylor, Jami K; Clerkin, Richard M; Ngaruiya, Katherine M; Velez, Anne-Lise Knox
abstract: This article empirically connects Moskos' Institutional-Occupational model to the large body of cross-nationally validated research on public service motivation (PSM). We find that in our sample, the PSM construct is positively correlated with institutional motivations that reflect Moskos' insights. We also find evidence that the four dimensions of PSM (Attraction to Public Participation, Commitment to Public Values, Self-sacrifice, and Compassion) may offer a more nuanced way to assess institutional motivations. Our research suggests that those interested in military recruitment/retention/performance and public administration scholars may have much to learn from each other. We call for further research in this area. [Reprinted by permission; copyright Inter-University Seminar on Armed Forces and Society/Sage Publications Inc.]

title: Obituary: Peter Kragh Jespersen (1946-2010)
abstract: Obituary is presented for public administration and organization professor Peter Kragh Jespersen.

title: Public Service Accountability and Development in the Arab World: The Case of Saudi Arabia
abstract: Examines obstacles to accountability & development, showing how they impose a heavy financial burden on the Arab countries & hinder political & socioeconomic development.
