Bureaucracy is commonly depicted as detrimental to rural development, a perception attributed to various circumstances: limitations of the central planning process, a legacy of suspicion regarding bureaucratic mechanisms in colonized nations, lack of coordination between state & local government, & the tendency for bureaucratic institutions & officers to favor state dictates over local needs. However, it is argued that effective rural development demands the expansion of bureaucracy to the local level. This form of bureaucracy is characterized by local leadership with real power, decentralization, & improved coordination & cooperation between & among the higher & lower echelons of society & government. The success of such a system relies on the ability of local leaders to challenge & reject politically motivated decisions by national ministers, politicians, & administrators. 1 Figure, 16 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Police Organization Continuity and Change: Into the Twenty-first Century
authors: Mastrofski, Stephen D; Willis, James J
abstract: American policing demonstrates both continuity and change. A high degree of decentralization persists, as do bureaucratic structures of larger police agencies. The structures and practices of the nation's numerous small agencies remain underexamined. The potential growth of professional structures inside and outside the police organization is largely unexplored. The core police patrol technology has remained essentially unchanged for decades, and early police adaptations to information technology have not yet profoundly altered policing structures and processes in easily observable ways. The demography and education levels of police workers are changing, but the consequences are not obvious. Police culture has long been under siege. Current reforms attempt to reduce the occupation's isolation from the communities it serves and the scientific community that presumably serves it. Mechanisms and styles for governing police retain considerable variation, but the growing role of grassroots community groups and police professional associations remains underexplored. The complexity of the dynamics of change manifests itself in the reaction of American police organizations to two consequential reform movements: community policing and terrorist-oriented policing. American police agencies have shown a remarkable capacity to absorb these reforms while buffering core structures and practices from change. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Fixers in Motion. A Conversation
authors: Jeffrey, Craig; Philliou, Christine; Rogers, Douglas; Shryock, Andrew
abstract: A discussion between Craig Jeffrey, Christine Philliou, Douglas Rogers, and Andrew Shryock on the topic of "fixers," that widespread class of political operators and go-betweens who proliferate in state bureaucracies and at the margins of state control, where they solve problems, channel resources, and specialize in activity that looks like naked corruption to some, savvy facilitation to others. Fixers play a key role in recent books by the participants, and their discussion is enlivened not only by reference to this fresh work, but by the many links they draw between Ottoman, Russian, and Indian settings and new scenarios created by the Arab Uprisings, a chain reaction of political revolts that erupted during the exchange. Adapted from the source document.

title: Revolution and State Structure: The Bureaucratization of Tax Administration in Early Modern England and France
abstract: This article explores the relationship between revolution & the bureaucratization of tax administration in early modern England & France. Revolution produces bureaucratization only when the monitoring capacity of states is developed enough to make bureaucratic organization more efficient than alternatives such as tax farming & collection by local notables. As monitoring capacity varies across types of taxes & levels of administration, states also bureaucratize at different paces & are differentially affected by revolution. This explains why the revolutions in England & France had greater effects on indirect taxes than on direct taxes & at top levels of tax administration compared to lower levels. Thus, revolution is neither a necessary nor a sufficient condition for bureaucratization, but it contributes to the process by sweeping away impediments to reform. 2 Tables, 81 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Book Review: Criminal Justice in Ireland
abstract: O'Mahony, Paul (ed.) Criminal Justice in Ireland. Dublin: Institute of Public Administration, 2002, paperback [euro]30.00, 818 pages.

title: Being a Participant in School Bureaucracy: On the Limitations and Freedom of Action of the School Administrator
abstract: This article discusses school administrators scope for action in the school system. The school administrator is often described as the middle manager of the school hierarchy, creating an impression of limited authority. Taking our lead from the philosopher Hans Skjervheim's conception of freedom of action as a potential realizable only through practice, we discuss the administrator's scope for action in terms not only of contextual constraints, but the administrator's cognitive transformation of the constraints of the organisational system. References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Homophobic Violence, Cultural Essentialism and Shifting Sexual Identities
abstract: Contemporary researchers have gathered widespread evidence of same-sex practice and desire with no implications for identity, across a range of historical and social settings. Paradoxically, models of understanding hate crime and homophobic violence that incline towards sexual essentialism have emerged in the same period. Categorizing perpetrators and victims as distinct groups of dangerous heterosexuals and vulnerable 'sexual minorities' is a politically seductive position in the media, public bureaucracies and criminal justice systems of contemporary liberal states. Fatal attacks are regarded as extreme expressions of homophobia that encapsulate this group division. But the author's study of anti-homosexual killings in New South Wales, and related criminal trials, signals the frequent significance of same-sex activity that is not accompanied by homosexual/gay identity among perpetrators and victims, and the relation to perpetrators' reasoned concerns about masculinity. Expert discourse and legal findings have typically viewed non-gay same-sex activity (by either victims or perpetrators) as the marker of an unresolved struggle for homosexual identity. But more recently, this is interpreted as signalling a lesser mental pathology or problematic male risk taking for pleasure. These shifts have had unexpected negative outcomes for victims without a gay social identity, and some perpetrators in 'homosexual advance' cases now derive a benefit from the newer cultural understanding of gay and straight categories.  [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Living Independently as an Ethnic Minority Elder: A Relational Perspective on the Issues of Aging and Ethnic Minorities
abstract: This study examines the residential experiences of Korean ethnic elders in affordable housing in the greater Chicago area, focusing on how patterns of social relationships that evolved around a geographical location and its urban infrastructure enabled the elders to achieve their desire for residential independence. Based on the theoretical concept of activity settings and social capital, the study suggests an integrated theoretical model where social capital is understood as an embedded asset of an activity setting. Methodologically, this study uses a combined method of qualitative interviews with 138 Korean elders in affordable housing in the greater Chicago area and a geographic analysis of their social relationships in order to present associations among social relationships, urban infrastructures, and the shared value of independence within their residential communities. The study findings indicate that the elders mobilized ethnic businesses, urban infrastructures, and the collective efficacy of groups to achieve the shared goal of maintaining residential independence. In each community, a cultural broker acted as an important bridge between the community of ethnic minorities and the larger social networks coexisting within the community boundary. The relational perspective as a potent ground for understanding and further solving the issues of aging and ethnicity is highlighted. Adapted from the source document.

title: Counterbureaucracies in Theory and Practice
abstract: Several theoretical propositions concerning counterbureaucracies are developed & tested in terms of how they actually behave, drawing on real-life exemplars. Focus is on their goals, resources, discretion, & culture, & how these differ from those of other US bureaucracies. Despite negative goals & a self-reliant culture, counterbureaucracies have generally flourished in recent years. It is argued that public relations, a service orientation, & professionalism have helped them to generate vital political support. 1 Table, 45 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucracy, Liberalism, and Community -- American Style
abstract: The US is a bureaucracy, & US lawyers are full-time bureaucratic functionaries. In this context, Americans' passion for individualism, legal equality, & perfection has yielded a disputes orientation to US bureaucracies, along with a plague of lawyers. The legal intelligentsia, faced with this system, has offered three visions: the liberal mainstream vision, the market or law-&-economic vision, & the critical legal studies vision. Here, a communitarian vision is advanced that presents the possibility of substantially reducing large bureaucracy in favor of smaller & less bureaucratic community. This community vision harmonizes with the critical legal studies view that man must always be examined in a social setting, but rejects egocentric individualism & equality as the bases of community, locating the foundations instead in communal duties, reciprocity, & belonging. This community vision also harmonizes with the law-&-economics vision to the extent the latter leads to smallness & decentralization, but not where "efficiency" analysis leads to hedonistic markets dominated by large "private" bureaucracies. Since this community vision is half liberal, it necessarily shares the liberal vision of individual rights, but it is tripolar in that it sees the individual in community meshed with Leviathan. Hence, it demands legal recognition of community per se, not merely as derivative from individual rights. Modified AA

title: Cultural Patterns and Competence in Slovenian Public Administration
abstract: The article deals with the cultural profile of Slovenian public administration and the mode of its transformation. Its main aim is to analyse prevailing cultural patterns and the situation regarding competences and efficiency of this segment of the government as well as its 'europeisation', i.e. transmitting of knowledge, skills, norms and values from the Western European environment into Slovenian context during the process of the country's accession to the European Union. The author claims that, despite the fact that one can not speak about some wide cultural gap and even less about incompatibility between Slovenian and European administrative culture as well mentality and political culture in general, there are evident deficiencies that have to be redressed in order to achieve higher level of performance in its conduct. Adapted from the source document.

title: Uloga i izdaci socijalne zastite u gospodarskoj krizi/The Role of Social Protection and Social Expenditure Developments in the Economic Crisis
abstract: The paper examines the role of social protection and social expenditure in the financial and economic crises. Accordingly, the objective of the paper was to analyse the trends in social expenditure developments in EU countries since the beginning of the last economic crisis (2008), examine changes in the composition of social protection spending during and following the crisis, and analyse the effectiveness of social protection schemes during and following the crisis in terms of poverty rate reduction. The paper confirmed that social protection expenditure has increased in almost all EU countries since the beginning of the crisis and that in the crisis most countries rely on redistributive effects of the so-called automatic stabilizers. Social expenditure developments during and following the crisis and the effectiveness of social protection in alleviating consequences of the crisis are related to the features of social protection models (regimes). Countries with larger social sectors are coping with the crisis more successfully. Economic, financial and social crises may induce changes in the social protection system. The crisis is an opportunity for countries with low social expenditure to widen the coverage of social schemes, set up new schemes or increase the level of benefits. As inappropriate crises management models fuel poverty and unemployment, and decrease economic growth, it is important to define the role of social protection/welfare state in a crisis management strategy. Among other things, a solution is to strengthen an approach where social expenditure is seen as social investments which may revitalize the role of social protection in the economic development.

title: MARXISM AND SYSTEMS THEORY IN A BUREAUCRATIC SOCIETY
abstract: A SERIES OF PROBLEMS ENDEMIC TO THE CONFRONTATION OF MARXISM WITH SYSTEMS THEORY IS UNFOLDED AS THESE PROBLEMS EMERGED IN THE RECENT SOCIAL, POLITICAL, & IDEOLOGICAL HISTORY OF EAST GERMANY (GDR). A CRITICAL ANALYSIS IS MADE OF A MAJOR ASPECT OF ITS IDEOLOGICAL & POLITICAL SYSTEM & OF PROBLEMS WITHIN THE METHODOLOGIES OF MARXISM & COMTEMPORARY SOCIAL SCIENCE. THE GDR DISPLAYS TENDENCIES TOWARD AN OPEN SOCIETY, YET CAN EQUALLY BE DESCRIBED AS A CLOSED SYSTEM--BY VIRTUE ON THE COMMANDING & DETERMINING ROLES PLAYED BY A SERIES OF BUREAUCRACIES IN THE DAILY LIVES OF THE PEOPLE. THE BASIC OFFICIAL IDEOLOGY OF THE ENTIRE SYSTEM SERVES THE COMMUNIST PARTY AS AN INSTRUMENT FOR MAINTAINING ITS POWER. IN BECOMING THIS INSTRUMENT, THE CLASSICAL CATEGORIES OF MARXISM-LENINISM HAVE BECOME EMPTY FORMULAS WHICH LEAD TO A CONTINUOUS EFFORT TO RECEIVE NEW SCIENTIFIC-TECHNOLOGICAL CONCEPTS FROM THE WEST. THE SYSTEMS THEORY IN RELATION TO DIALECTICAL MATERIALISM & MARXIST SOCIAL THEORY ARE DISTINGUISHED INTO 3 ASPECTS OF CYBERNETICS BY THE PHILOSOPHER GEORG KLAUS: (KYBERNETIK IN PHILOSOPHISCHER SICHT CYBERNITICS AS VIEWED BY PHILOSOPHY BERLIN: DIETZ VERLAG, 1965, 4TH ED) SYSTEMS ASPECT, THE CONTROL ASPECT, & THE INFORMATION ASPECT. THE SOCIOLOGICAL & IDEOLOGICAL FUNCTIONS THAT CYBERNETICS CAN PERFORM WITHIN DIALECTICAL & HISTORICAL MATERIALISM HAVE 2 MAJOR OBJECTIVES: (1) TO CREATE INNOVATIVE TENDENCIES WITHIN THE POLITICOSOCIAL SYSTEM OF THE GDR, & (2) TO BE APPLIED TO SE PRACTICE. YET, THE MARXIST-LENINIST SYSTEMS THEORY IS DESIGNED TO ASSIST THE CENTRAL PARTY AUTHORITIES IN RULING EFFECTIVELY, & THUS POINTS OUT THE CONTRADICTIONS WITHIN MARXIST SYSTEMS THEORY. KLAUS' PROBLEMS ARE DISCUSSED WITHIN THE RANGE OF DIALECTICAL MATERIALISM: (A) HOW TO DEFINE THE CATEGORIES CHANCE & NECESSITY, & (B) WHO TO CONCEIVE OF FOR INFORMATION & ORGANIZATION IN TERMS OF DIALECTICAL MATERIALISM. DESPITE THE FACT THAT THE CYBERNETIC SYSTEMS THEORY IN THE GDR IS OVER, CONCEPTS OF SYSTEMS THEORY STILL EXIST TO PROVIDE MORE FLEXIBILITY IN THE BUREAUCRACY. THESE CONCEPTS ARE THE IDEAS OF TECHNICAL RATIONALITY & ECONOMIC EFFICIENCY AS DETERMINED BY CYBERNETIC CONCEPTS OF INFORMATION, COMMUNICATION, & LEARNING. L. MESTMAN.

title: The Role of the Sociologist in Italian Public Administration
abstract: In the Italian experience of public planning or programming, a major role is played by professions linked to the hard sciences, eg, engineers, urbanists, economists, & jurists. However, increasing social complexity places the model of "technical planning," which implies both a high predictability of behavior & a clear distinction between natural sciences & social sciences, in a critical position. Today the lack of a central point of observation is generally accepted, & knowledge is considered to depend on the observer & his paradigm. These considerations render a new importance of the sociologist as an expert to public policymakers. The sociologist can also play a role in facilitating decision-making processes, today considered as exchange processes. It is argued that sociology needs to improve its social visibility & to increase its exchange resources through a clearer definition of its own competencies & boundaries. A deontological code can assist in reaching this goal. 34 References. Modified AA

title: Evaluating a Federal Experiment in Bureaucratic Reform
abstract: A contextual evaluation model was used in assessing a federal program that develops cooperative policy experiments with other government agencies. The two-year Experimental Technology Incentives Program (ETIP) study was commissioned by the National Academy of Sciences to determine whether such a program could stimulate useful changes in the federal bureaucracy. ETIP chose to experiment with minor changes in four policy areas: procurement, regulation, government subsidy, & research & development. Program alterations resulted from the findings; its methodology offers an alternative to traditional evaluation strategies. Modified Author Summary.

title: Revolutionary Politics in Twentieth-Century China: A Review of Radicalism, Revolution, and Reform in Modern China: Essays in Honor of Maurice Meisner
abstract: Maurice Meisner was an important scholar of twentieth-century Chinese history, whose work focused on the ideological and bureaucratic dimensions of the People's Republic and its origins in the upheavals of the first half of the century. This review considers a Festschrift including contributions from eight former students of Meisner, with articles on a wide array of topics across the period from the 1920s to the early twenty-first century. Strengths and limitations of Meisner's work and his legacy are presented in conjunction with reflections on the underlying issues of the nature of contemporary China and its role in the world, and some related recent scholarly debates on the Left.

title: Women, Abuse, and the Welfare Bureaucracy
authors: Laakso, Janice H; Drevdahl, Denise J
abstract: Using critical and feminist theoretical frameworks, this report of a qualitative study describes women's perspectives of the welfare bureaucracy. An analysis of interviews with 38 women revealed emotional and economic abuse both in the welfare system and their personal lives. Interactions with frontline workers who implement the rules and regulations of welfare reform disempower recipients and mimic the conditions of abuse that these women have already experienced. Genograms provide a context for the women's personal histories. Recommendations include removing sanctions as a form of economic abuse, screening every applicant for interpersonal violence, and referring women to mental health services if necessary. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Social Welfare and Organizational Society
abstract: The dominance of the large-scale formal organization is a central feature of contemporary US society. Reviewed are societal trends that are bound up with organizational dominance; presented are implications for social welfare. The combination of large-scale organizations & traditional industrial arrangements results in the formation of a stable yet chronically underfinanced welfare system whose level of support & character are crucial to the lives of an increasingly alienated Lc. Organizational dominance implies that changes in bureaucratic rules have important consequences for large segments of society; however, strong social forces militate against any significant changes in those rules affecting public welfare. HA.

title: Management, Public Politics and Social Development: Toward the Professionalization of Public Management
abstract: One of the main objectives in the development of Latin American modernization policy is to create public management (PM) professionals. Understanding the complementary roles of PM as practice & discipline is important in moving toward professionalization. Here, an ecological vision is proposed; organizational practice elements at the microlevel are conceptually related to public policy elements at the macrolevel. The proposed ecological conceptualization supposes PM development in contexts similar to & different from private management. This framewok simultaneously delivers solutions to limits on the success of PM activities & intellectual solutions that overcome obstacles to professionalization on the route to social & economic development. 1 Table, 1 Figure, 25 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Local Sustainable Development in the Network Society: The Potential of New Information and Communications Technologies
abstract: In light of the growing critiques of the prevailing development models oriented toward either market solutions or centralizing state actions, this paper proposes a theoretical inquiry into the possibilities of fomenting more sustainable local development through the strengthening of social networks & their progressive incorporation into local political & administrative processes. Starting from a critical interpretation of the notion of social capital, the article shows the importance of strategies of institutional design capable of mobilizing social capital & guaranteeing the access of local communities to political & social power. This is followed by a discussion that, considering the social & political conditions that are specific to Brazil, weighs the possibilities & dilemmas surrounding the use of new information & communication technologies within local communities, in terms of reactivating community participation in local public administration. Lastly, the new role that local governments demand is discussed, in an attempt to explore the communitarian option for promoting sustainable development in the emerging "network society.". 60 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: COMPSTAT and Bureaucracy: A Case Study of Challenges and Opportunities for Change
authors: Willis, James J; Mastrofski, Stephen D; Weisburd, David
abstract: COMPSTAT has been heralded as an innovative & rational crime control program, but our research shows that its implementation presents police departments with a set of opportunities & challenges. Using Weber's theory of bureaucracy, we present a case study demonstrating how COMPSTAT's key elements are shaped by extant organizational arrangements. In renewing an emphasis on the crime fighting goal & the command hierarchy of the Lowell Police Department, the study site, COMPSTAT presented an opportunity to reinforce certain traditional features of police bureaucracy. However, by strengthening control through its accountability mechanism, COMPSTAT interfered with its own operation. Furthermore, the persistence of other bureaucratic features -- functional specialization, formalization, routine, uniformity, & secrecy -- limited organizational change. Our case suggests that the most significant challenge for any department is picking the compromise between existing bureaucratic features & COMPSTAT's core elements that most suits its needs & those of its constituencies. 67 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Oikos/Anthropos: Rationality, technology, infrastructure
abstract: Collier and Ong highlight the "Oikos/Anthropos: Rationality, Technology, Infrastructure" workshop on Apr 26 and 27, 2002, at New York University's Global Education Office in Prague. The workshop was organized around an emerging interdisciplinary approach to science, administration, politics, and economic organization as areas in which the forms and values of oikos and anthropos are studied in the human sciences.

title: Sociology of State Services
abstract: A discussion of the role of sociology in assessing recent reforms of the social & legal bases of Russian state services. An analysis of the position of state officials as a socioprofessional group differentiates between the following features: (1) the general goals & tasks of state officials as a class, their sociodemographic characteristics, & corporate homogeneity; (2) their relations with officials in other divisions & the general public; (3) functional relations of state officials (their responsibilities & prerogatives), civil/labor/political rights, group control & sanctions, etc. While the sphere of the sociology of state services is closely related to the sociology of organizations, it also borders the areas of the sociology of work & professions. The combination of the paradigms of sociolegal institutions & socioprofessional groups may be helpful in choosing the best system of variables for examining the functioning of state services. 4 References. A. Devic

title: Personalizing Personnel Decisions in Feminist Organizational Theory and Practice
abstract: Extends the feminist critique of bureaucracy by examining how US feminist health organizations contest the bureaucratic idea of impersonal, role-based, & instrumental social relations. Interview, archival, & fieldwork data are used to explore the personnel practices of feminist workplaces, revealing the difficulties & possibilities that accompany their ways of handling personnel issues. The challenge of reconceiving personnel as persons is explored as a problem of both organizational theory & practice. 38 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Folklore of the Freeway: Space, Culture, and Identity in Postwar Los Angeles
abstract: The construction of freeways in postwar Los Angeles, CA -- which advanced suburbanization & ethnic segregation -- was celebrated as progress in the dominant Anglo American culture & complexly contested in the folklore of the Chicano neighborhoods it displaced & dissected. While politicians promoted the freeway using racialized images & a discourse of modernization, & Disneyland's Autopia ride applauded its Americanness, many Chicanos resisted construction in public hearings & newspaper pages & used literature, murals, & graffiti to interpret the freeway as an intrusive eroder of communities & their economies. Other Chicanos, however, saw the freeway not only as a way for whites to move through their neighborhoods without seeing them but as a way out of the barrio & into the American dream. E. Blackwell

title: Administrative Law and Collective Decision Making
abstract: An examination of the role of administrative law in the process of collective decision making, focusing on the social security service. It is observed that the process can be juridically regulated by formulating five imperatives to guide the intervention & justify the presence of administrative law within the process. These are: dignity of the individual affected by the decision, legitimacy of power, exactitude of the decision, rationality of the process, & effectiveness of the decision. They can be drafted for any sector of human activity regulated by law. While implanting them in practice, it is suggested that attention be on first-level decisionmakers, since their adherence to the imperatives is a condition for the realization of internal administrative law. I. Shagrir

title: Inside the Growth Machine: Real Estate Professionals on the Perceived Challenges of Urban Development
abstract: The growth machine framework maintains that coalitions of elites work together to promote and adopt policies and practices that best serve their economic interests and propel cities toward growth. While numerous scholars have subjected the growth machine to theoretical and empirical tests, we know little about the beliefs and perspectives of individual actors within the growth machine. To address this gap in the literature, the present research uses in-depth interviews to examine the subjective views of one segment of the growth machine--real estate professionals. The findings demonstrate that these practitioners see the exercise of power at the local level to be less coordinated, consensus-driven, and growth-oriented than the growth machine thesis suggests. Specifically, they see their own power and capacity to act to be constrained by four factors: the (re)-election interests of politicians; the professional interests of municipal economic development staff; bureaucratic procedures and zoning regulations; and mobilized community members and groups. I conclude with a discussion of the implications for urban political theory and suggestions for future research. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Standing apart and sitting together: Enforcing coalition agreements in multiparty systems
abstract: One of the most obvious questions to be asked about coalition governments is what these governments do, but this question has received little systematic attention from coalition researchers. A key element of coalition governance that may inform our empirical knowledge of the actions of government - their origin, organization and results - is coalition agreements. Party leaders negotiating a new government invest time in writing coalition agreements, and they do this because they expect beneficial effects: more efficiency in coalition policy making, and more peace in the government. Written coalition agreements are considered to reduce uncertainty and mistrust, and this is why they have become institutionalized in countries with coalition governments. This article presents an approach to the comparative study of coalition conflicts as they emerge during government formation, the management of this conflict through drafting coalition agreements and the effects of this during coalition life. The article sets out a number of expectations about the effects of types of deals that parties make; and asks what types of conflict management are most effective and what are the conditions for enforcement - structural and strategic? In recent comparative work, the features of coalition agreements and mechanisms of coalition governance in Western Europe have received attention. This article sets out, with empirical material, how further comparative research on coalition governance may be developed. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Not for Women Only: School Administration as a Feminist Activity
abstract: Feminist pedagogy has typically emphasized breaking down the barriers of power & authority between teachers & administrators. Changes in the classroom that have been instituted by feminists encourage women students to voice their experiences & gain support & recognition for them. The broken pyramid is utilized as a metaphor to describe role differentiation in society, & the double helix is proposed as an alternative metaphor for a feminist administration. In this model, decision making & leadership are shared among teachers, students, & administrators. S. G. Yates

title: Systems Engineering and Contractual Individualism; Linking Engineering Processes to Macro Social Values
abstract: After eminent thinkers in the 1960s submitted critical views on technology, some philosophers of technology extended their macro perspectives. Since then, many historians and sociologists of technology steadily marginalized their general claims through richly empirical, constructivist case studies of concrete engineering processes. Some recent efforts have begun to bridge these two diverging orientations. This paper participates in such efforts with a case study of relationships between macro cultures and engineering processes. It shows that behind the adoption of systems engineering by engineers and managers who led the Apollo programme was a macro current of social values in the USA. Post-war American society saw the rise of highly individualistic social norms that valued mobility, meritocracy and clear-cut contractual working relationships. Such norms triumphed most conspicuously in the federal government during the 1960s. Engineers and managers at the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) headquarters, who tended to share such values, refined the formalized, depersonalized methods of systems engineering, which enabled them to perfect space technology. In order to show such a correlation between macro values and micro practices, this paper draws a comparison between engineering communities in different cultural settings in the USA and Japan. This paper thus explores the macro social environment that gave rise to systems engineering, which, in turn, continues to function as a skeletal structure for our technological society today.

title: Women in Public Administration in the Netherlands
abstract: Despite the fact that the number of women in the Netherlands' paid labor force has increased rapidly since 1960, Dutch women still have the lowest participation rate for women in wage labor within the European Community. Job segregation still exists. During 1985-1988, the % of women at the higher ranks of public administration was very small, with little increase. Interviews with 12 women in the top 3 ranks at the Ministry of Economics revealed complaints about the lack of career guidance & opportunities available for women in their positions. Policy changes to encourage women's emancipation through education were made between 1974 & 1981, but the government eventually realized that prejudices toward women were deeply rooted in socioeconomic structures. Later policy changes encouraged the facilitation of employment for women in public administration, but progress in instituting flexible hours & child care has been very slow. The policy changes to date have had little effect & little enforcement. 5 Tables, 8 References. M. Pflum

title: The British Experience with Socialized Medicine
abstract: Examines the nationalization of health care & socialized medicine in the United Kingdom, arguing that the National Health Service (NHS) has hindered rather than fostered health care effectiveness. The NHS is described in terms of its political origins, bureaucratic structure, organizational changes & dramatic rise in expenditures, & finally, the long-needed reforms spearheaded by Thatcherism's challenge to the welfare state. Tony Blair's New Labour attempts to continue the reform movement are assessed, & further privatization & denationalization are advocated. 4 References. K. Coddon

title: Max Weber: The Sociology of Bureaucracy and the Modern State
abstract: Max Weber's assessment of progressive bureaucratization in the modern state is examined & extended, focusing on the predictive uses of his "ideal type" analysis. The expansion of state & party bureaucracies & the emergence of interest & pressure groups are analyzed as developments consonant with Weber's model; the dilemma of choice between relatively organized state capitalism & relatively effective bureaucracy is propounded as an inevitable outcome. Modified HA.

title: Making Bricks without Straw?: The Polish Ombudsman and the Transition to Democracy
abstract: The spread of the ombudsman concept throughout the Western world has been followed by its adoption in Poland as part of the development of the Rule of Law in the European Napoleonic tradition of the enforcement of codes of law on administrators. The office of ombudsman, established in 1988 & headed by a Commissioner, serves primarily to investigate complaints by Polish citizens against public officials &, increasingly, private companies. An exploration of issues identified in the Commissioner's annual reports considers: limits of citizens' comprehension of appropriate investigative matters; officials' reluctance to accept the Commissioner's judgments; the Commissioner's relationship with the legal system & higher courts; & the Commissioner's role in promoting acceptance of minority rights protection. Particular dilemmas for the office, arising from the difficult process of replacing the old communist structure with stable democratic state & legal systems, are discussed. 2 Tables, 16 References. S. Millett

title: Rethinking Center-Periphery Communication in the Ottoman Empire
abstract: The kapi kethüdasis were state officials stationed in Istanbul. They represented the political and economic interests of high-ranking Ottoman figures, as well as representatives of some foreign countries who needed a mediator with the central government. Despite the fact that the kapi kethüdasis of Ottoman provincial governors held a central place in the social and economic system of the Ottoman Empire, they have been little studied, and the few studies that exist focus mainly on the Tanzimat period (1839-1876). In this article, I discuss issues such as patterns of appointment and promotion, functions, and sources of income, in order to show how the kapi kethüdasi of the provincial governor became a leading figure in the administrative and financial bureaucracy of the Ottoman Empire before the Tanzimat.

title: The regional management of growth in California: A history of failure
abstract: Attempts to achieve regional growth management in the state of California since the 1950s and why these attempts failed are examined.  Local government has effectively opposed the management of growth at a regional or state level because land use is seen as exclusively a local purview.

title: CAW -- Computer Aided Welfare State: Revival by Technology?
abstract: During the past decades the traditional welfare state in Western Europe has come under increasing pressure: particularly apparent are its increasingly high costs & relatively low effectiveness, accompanied by a deterioration of the image of public administrations. In many reform countries the former public health care & social security systems are facing even more difficulties: lack of financial resources & new neoliberal ideas undermine their functionality. Alternative concepts are needed: large-scale institutions are unable to deal appropriately with rapid social change & the individuals are not in a position to cope with the negative aspects of human existence on their own. In addition to large-scale institutions, eg, centralized social security & health care institutions, new group-based institutions assisted by electronic communication tools & adequate training opportunities are proposed for various fields of society: "Peer Group Care" in addition to the traditional social welfare system, "Study Circles" to complement traditional schools, "Workers' Health Assurance Groups" to improve occupational health, & "Intrapreneurial Groups" against alienation at the workplace are examples of how the welfare state could be transformed, rather than be replaced. Adapted from the source document.

title: Neoliberal penality: A brief genealogy
abstract: The turn of the 21st century witnessed important shifts in punishment in the United States and other western industrialized nations. After 50 years of relative stability, the rate of incarceration in the United States began climbing exponentially in 1973 to the point where, today, one out of a hundred adults is behind bars. Here, Harcourt discusses neoliberal penality that makes it easier to resist government intervention in the marketplace and to embrace criminalizing any and all deviations from the market. It facilitates passing new criminal statutes and wielding the penal sanction more liberally because that is where administration is necessary, that is where the State can legitimately act, that is the proper sphere of governing. He concludes that neoliberalism has so deeply and fundamentally distorted people's understanding of economic systems that it will take a lot of work to reach the point where we can properly assess different alternatives for the administration of markets and punishment, and in the process dismantle our neoliberal penality.

title: The Failure of Local Government Website Accessibility
authors: Sobie, Robert J; Mingus, Matthew S
abstract: Government services are increasingly provided electronically, and frequently in an exclusive manner whereby traditional print copy is no longer available. This places a special burden upon government to ensure that Web sites delivering information and services are accessible for people with blindness or low vision who utilize assistive computer technology. This article reports on a study, from the fall of 2005, of local governments throughout one Midwestern state that identified (1) the extent of Web page accessibility and (2) the barriers that local government officials perceive in designing accessible Web sites. The results suggest that factors other than lack of funding, poor staffing, and lack of training in accessibility law serve as barriers to developing accessible Web sites. This topic is particularly important to the future of public administration because recent research has established a connection between the use of local government Web sites and trust in government, a trust that is grounded in both social and digital inclusion. A clear finding of concern is that every local government homepage and subordinate employment Web page tested contained accessibility errors suggesting digital exclusion. Adapted from the source document.

title: THE NAZI BUREAUCRACY
abstract: In studying the Nazi burley, it is useful to determine how far the Nazis continued & developed existing traditions, & how far they broke with them. Was the Third Reich an historical mishap, or an aberration, or a development of existing trends? How did the Nazis manage to instit'ize an ideology which, before 1933, was weak, mainly negative, absolutely uncommitted to any plans for the future & open to diff interpretations? What was the place of German bur'cy in this process of instit'ization? What were its components, its modus operandi, its internal logic & the character of the Nazi org's that destroyed the Jews? Were they modern bur'tic org's, with their classic ingredients: specialization of duties, the existence of rules in the org & a general orientation towards the rational & efficient achievement of certain objectives? On the eve of the rise to power of the Nazis, the NSDAP had millions of members of divergent backgrounds, educ'al standards & outlooks. Even at this stage, the Nazi Party was able to offer org'al solutions, where others got bogged down in theory. There thus existed nuclei of org's whose integration with instit's of the German State begot the future machinery of destruction, namely the SS & SD. The Nazi machinery retained within itself definitely modern bur' tic ingredients. In its relations with outside factors, the machinery was a typical example of bur'ization. Parallel with it, modern elements were placed at the service of a partially irrational ideology & of one man who, in the eyes of the bur'cy, bore the entire responsibility for whatever it did. IPSA.

title: Social Work -- A Profession?
abstract: In the context of external bureaucratization of British social work, evidenced by a loss of professional identity, particularly in terms of an inhibition of individual judgment & loss of the sense of possession of an inherited body of knowledge, it is argued that, among relevant models of social work intervention, the place of the treatment model has to be restored. Perhaps, ultimately, only professional self-regulation may restore the necessary conditions for offering effective professional service. Meanwhile, the endeavor to negotiate greater autonomy at a local level, & the recovery of a sense of professional history & inherited knowledge, could contribute much to restore the sense of professional identity essential to responsible practice. 34 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The French School and Problems of Community Integration
abstract: The difficulty of French schools in being integrated into & adapting to the communities in which they function is attributed to the tradition of bureaucratic centralization manifested in teaching programs & methods & staff recruitment. Among recent educational innovations, however, have been some experiments in architectural & functional integration of educational, cultural, & social facilities involving community participation. It is still too early to generalize from such experiments. Another problem in France has been to effect any kind of parental control over educational institutions or to open the curriculum to the requirements of the local environment. Modified HA.

title: Some considerations on the current transformations of local finance in France
abstract: In the analysis of the current transformations of local finance in France this paper highlights the importance of local public administration. Based on the hypothetical deductive method, it concludes that one of the challenges faced by the future of local finance in France is to ensure a steady growth in a cohesive territory, for which a distribution of tax sources coordinated with the central government is required, so that local authorities have decision autonomy. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Exercise of Power in Coercive Organizations: A Study of Prison Guards
abstract: If the power of prison guards has been altered & reduced by recent social, legal, & bureaucratic intrusions in American prisons, as has been reported by many observers, then what is the base of power by which guards currently exert control over prisoners? Following a discussion of the bases of power in prison, data from a survey of guards in five prisons are examined to determine the extent to which each power base is viewed as a resource to gain prisoner compliance. The results are discussed in terms of the guards' exercise of control within the increasingly bureaucratic structure of coercive organizations. Adapted from the source document.

title: The New Spirit of Capitalism, Innovation Fetishism and New Information and Communication Technologies
abstract: The neoliberal developments over the past 30 years have received much support from a set of ideas that can be defined as “the new spirit of capitalism”. These ideas have offered powerful legitimisations of neoliberalism, conceived as a progressive force that has replaced the supposedly bureaucratic structures of earlier Keynesian welfare states with market-driven network structures that allow innovations, creativity and entrepreneurship to flourish. In this article, I will critically examine the constituents of the new spirit of capitalism, in particular its intimate association with liberal discourses of innovation. I will then focus on how such ideas have come forward in recent information society thinking via a discussion of Manuel Castells's influential network society theory. This is followed by a critique of mainstream understandings of innovation from a neo-Marxist perspective, with an eye towards new information and communication technology and critical media research in times of a growing contestation of neoliberal hegemony.

title: SOCIAL CLASS BACKGROUND OF COLLEGE SENIORS AND ANTICIPATED BEHAVIOR IN BUREAUCRATIC STRUCTURE
abstract: The problem raised concerns the relationship between an individual's position in the social class system (SCS) & the way in which he perceives diff aspects of bur'tic structure. The individual's position in the SCS was determined by an operational definition of his status situation which was based upon his father's occup'al class as of 15 yrs ago, his father's present occup'al class, & level of educ'al achievement. The classification yielded 6 diff status groups which constituted the operational independent variable. Only the 2 extreme groups were utilized in the present study. The members of these status groups were drawn from a sample of 216 M Coll seniors representing 6 Coll's of the Pennsylvania State U. The dependent variables were composed of att's toward bur'tic structure. These variables included recognition variables, aspiration variables, work orientation variables, friendship variables, orientations toward the formal bur'tic structure, belongingness & togetherness variables. The technique of analysis consisted of drawing a sample of R's who were then classified according to their status situation, & of determining the distribution of their responses according to their perception of bur'tic structure. Where applicable, Chi-square was used to test the O- hypothesis relating the dependent & independent variables. O- hypothesis were rejected at the .05 level. O- hypothesis analyzed in this study indicated that patterns of att's toward bur'tic structure were not statistically associated with the diff status situation. Given the goals implied by a pattern of status achievement, the independence of the seniors' att's toward bur'tic structure of SC membership may be regarded as a resultant of, in part, their socialization in Coll, the similarity of the socialization process within the fam of orientation & in part, the broader structural context of limited alternatives to non-formalized modes of employment. AA.

title: Orphan DNA: Indigenous samples, ethical biovalue and postcolonial science
abstract: Thousands of blood samples taken from Australia's indigenous people lie in institutional freezers of the global North, the legacy of a half-century of scientific research. Since those collections were assembled, standards of ethical research practice have changed dramatically, leaving some samples in a state of dormancy. While some European and American collections are still actively used for genetic research, this practice is viewed as unethical by most Australian genetic researchers, who have closer relationships with indigenous Australians and postcolonial politics. For collections to be used ethically, they require a 'guardian' who has an ongoing and documented relationship with the donors, so that consent to further studies on samples can be negotiated. This affective and bureaucratic network generates 'ethical biovalue' such that a research project can satisfy Australian ethical review. I propose in this article that without ethical biovalue, collections become 'orphan' DNA, divorced from a guardian and often difficult to trace to their sources. Such samples are both orphaned and functionally sterile, unable to produce data, scientific articles, knowledge or prestige. This article draws on an ethnographic study of genetic researchers who are working in indigenous communities across Australia. I present tales of researchers' efforts to generate ethical biovalue and their fears for succession; fears that extend to threats to destroy samples rather than see them orphaned, or worse, fall into the wrong hands. Within these material and affective networks, indigenous DNA morphs from biological sample to sacred object to political time bomb. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Some Reflections on the Institutions of Muslim Spain: Unity in Politics and Administration (711-929)
abstract: This essay analyzes the major political, military, & administrative institutions of al-Andalus (Muslim Spain) & explains how they gave a sense of unity to the Abode of Islam (dar al-Islam) by replicating the same institutions used in the East (al-Mashriq). The military institutions (eg., jund, thughur, & husun) helped to keep Muslim Spain safe from enemy attacks, both Christian & Muslim, & to suppress all revolts, while the political institutions enabled the authorities to keep al-Andalus unified, levy taxes, administer the cities (sahib al-madinah), supervise the markets (sahib al-suq), and, finally, to administer the region's provinces (kuwar). Adapted from the source document.

title: MAX WEBER'S THEORY OF BUREAUCRACY
abstract: According to Max Weber, bur'tic structure functions on the principle of rationality; officials must maintain an impersonal attitude when dealing with others, regardless of their position in the hierarchy. Appointment of officials in a bur'tic org is based on qualifications determined by competitive examinations or on the basis of academic degree, thus insuring a well-knit, efficiently run org. The methodological implications of Weber's theory has 2 aspects: (1) as a conceptual scheme in which definitions of relevant concepts & of phenomena to be studied are found, & (2) as a set of generalizations & hyp's which indicate the relationship between the concepts. It is noted that during recent yrs, Weber's theory has been subject to criticism. The work of Alvin W. Gouldner is cited as illustrative of the notion that Weber's theory is not based on realistic assumptions. Modified HA.

title: Private education and public administration
abstract: Gottfried points out that one characteristic of today's American education is its acquiescence to public administration.

title: The ebb and flow of attitudes and policies on alcohol in Ireland 2002-2010
abstract: Introduction and Aims This paper examines the level of public support for alcohol control policies during a period of policy evolution in Ireland. Design and Methods A comparison of attitudes to alcohol policy at three points in time was undertaken. The first survey took place in 2002 and was repeated in 2006 and 2010 using a national quota sample of 1000 adults with face-to-face interviews. Policy areas examined were drunk-driving, price, availability and promotion. Results In 2002, the highest level of public support was for drink-driving countermeasures (84% favoured random breath testing) and measures to restrict alcohol promotions (67% favoured restrictions). Support for stricter measures on price and availability was lower. Trends showed a decline in support for tax increases and for early closing time, whereas support for fewer outlets (off-trade) increased. Discussion and Conclusion When public concerns (level of support) for stricter alcohol policies were seen to be met, as occurred with price and hours through increased tax and reversal of opening hours, public concern/support declined. When concerns were not met, as with outlets, support continued to rise most likely influenced by greater number of off-trade outlets and cheaper alcohol. Support for liberal alcohol policies was low and the majority favoured the status quo on price and availability. Public support for policy is one element of the complexity of policymaking along with consensus building across government and management of vested interests, so that the policy outcome is seldom assured. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucratic Encounters--An Evaluation of Government Services
authors: Kahn, Robert L; Katz, Daniel; Gutek, Barbara
abstract: Government services are evaluated in terms of bureaucratic encounters--the service-seeking transactions reported by 1,431 American adults (D. Katz, B. A. Gutek, R. L. Kahn, & E. Barton, "Bureaucratic Encounters: A Pilot Study in the Evaluation of Government Services," Ann Arbor, Mich: Instit for Social Research, U of Michigan, 1975). A framework is presented for the conceptualization & conduct of research on transactions between organizations & elements in their environment in 4 major categories. Persons' reactions to such transactions are discussed as a joint product of the characteristics of the client & those of the agency. The implications of these client reactions for more general social & political questions are explored. Because so much of individual well-being depends upon service-seeking transactions, their quality & satisfaction should be regarded as social indicators, & included among the measures of the quality of contemporary life. 6 Tables, 2 Figures. Modified HA.

title: Symbolic Politics and Policy Feedback: The United Nations Protocol Relating to the Status of Refugees and American Refugee Policy in the Cold War
abstract: Immigration scholars routinely overlook the 1968 U.S. Senate ratification of the United Nations Protocol Relating to the Status of Refugees, an international treaty defining a refugee in ideologically neutral terms. They dismiss this moment as symbolic because U.S. law continued to define a refugee as someone fleeing communism until the passage of the 1980 Refugee Act. We use archival documents, interview data, and court cases to argue that legal and bureaucratic mobilization by refugee advocates throughout the 1970s drew on the Protocol, achieving incremental policy change even before 1980, and ultimately shaped the provisions of the Refugee Act itself. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Impact of Movements: Bureaucratic Insurgency, Canadianization and the CSAA
abstract: Greater attention is now being given to the consequences of social movements. Relying on archival & interview material, this paper revisits Zald & Berger's notion of bureaucratic insurgency to analyze the dynamics of change & transformation in the Canadian Sociology & Anthropology Assoc (CSAA) during the early 1970s. Contrary to the Weber-Michels thesis, which predicts that as organizations age they become less political & more conservative, the CSAA became politicized as a result of the movement to Canadianize cultural & educational institutions. An explanation for this change is offered, which serves to challenge the Weber-Michels thesis of organizational transformation & its outcome. 50 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Changing Status of Women in Management in the Public Administration of Saudi Arabia
abstract: The evolution of women's participation in public administration in Saudi Arabia is examined. Obstacles in employment of women include: role stereotyping; communication problems; lack of autonomy in supervisory positions & a high degree of centralization; & poor preparation & selection of women for positions. Possible reform measures are examined, including: (1) the participation of women in reform; (2) education & counseling for women; (3) active recruitment of women; (4) training for women; (5) increasing formalized systems to organize operations in agencies & departments; (6) creation of more opportunities for advancement; (7) establishment of an agency to monitor reforms; & (8) improvement of communication skills. 6 References. D. Generoli

title: Women, Society and Water Technologies: Lessons for Bureaucracy
abstract: Water technologies are increasingly regarded as pivotal to the process of societal development. One arena of importance is the delivery of water to society through comprehensive water supply programs that aim at ensuring 'safe' water for all. The principal target group in these programs is women, whose development is believed to be promoted through improved water facilities offering them greater convenience, better health & enhanced socio-economic opportunities. These programs can be seen as having three essential aspects, namely technology, people & institutions. Of these, the responsibilities of designing technologies for supplying water, creating institutional frameworks for their execution & implementing the program at the people's end for their benefit all lie with development bureaucracies. But the extent to which these bureaucracies can be sensitive to the socio-cultural contexts of the communities & the women for whom the program interventions are designed & implemented remains problematic. This article explores the gender dimensions of the socio-cultural context of water & how this may play a role in the adoption & management of improved water technologies. A perspective on the lessons for planning bureaucracies is offered to make the concerned technologies more efficient, effective & sustainable. References. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright 2006.]

title: Institutional Metropolitanism and Economic Spheres in the Cape [South Africa]
abstract: The process of decentralisation at national level & of recentralisation of South African metropolitan zones is followed, in the Cape, by a large scale public action aimed at upgrading the city to a world class status, while reducing sociospatial disparities inherited from apartheid. The first part of the article points out the reasons of failure of the spatial regulation tentative linked to the political conditions of institutional metropolitanism & the obsolescence of the conceptual foundations of public action. It, then, proposes an analysis of the territorial regulation with a reminder to the fact that the role of local political elites is a decisive element of urban change. 2 Cartes, 47 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: "Angie was Our Sister:" Witnessing the Trans-Formation of Disgust in the Citizenry of Photography
abstract: In 2009, Andre Andrade was convicted for the murder of Angie Zapata, an 18-year-old Latina transgender woman living in rural Colorado. This essay traces the way Angie's friends, family, and community countered the assertion of transphobia in the courtroom and larger public discussion by circulating self-portraits of Angie on t-shirts at community vigils. Displaying Angie's portrait not only resists the mobilization of transphobic disgust, but also enacts a way of seeing trans people as citizens within the civil contract of photography. The mourners' resistance enacts a politics of witnessing that contests the bureaucratization of gender and the aesthetic norms of legal culture. These rhetorical performances illustrate the emotional politics of visuality, and how citizenship is a category of of embodied sociality, public emotionality, and performative enactment. Adapted from the source document.

title: Legitimacy, Law and Public Action
abstract: A definition of political power as both power over and power to leads to reconsider the registers of justification on which political legitimacy is built. Long, the ideal type of Weberian legal rational legitimacy characterized the mode of political domination proper to Western States. It is now the target of many critics who regard it as inadequate and unable to account for changes in the political regulation of our contemporary societies. In a period of erosion of state power, law and bureaucracy which were at the heart of the Weberian model have lost their centrality. Not only these criticisms do not take into account the Weberian analysis of political responsibility which shows that the legitimacy cannot be thought except the exercise of power, but empirical works do not give evidence either of the end of the bureaucratic mode of organization or irreparable decline of the place of law in the management of public affairs. A deepened reflection on the political legitimacy goes more through a renewal of the Weberian model than its simple renunciation. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bioethics and the Global Moral Economy; The Cultural Politics of Human Embryonic Stem Cell Science
abstract: The global development of human embryonic stem cell (HESC) science and its therapeutic applications are dependent on the nature of its engagement at national and international levels with key cultural values and beliefs concerning the moral status of the early human embryo. This article argues that the political need to reconcile the promise of new health technologies with the cultural costs of scientific advance, dependent in this case on the use of the human embryo, has been met by the evolution of bioethics as a political community, transnational network, and bureaucratic device. Bioethics has become the political means for the creation of a global moral economy where the trading and exchange of values is normalized and legitimated. As a result of such trading, value compromises are produced capable of legitimizing the regulatory policies necessary for maintaining public trust in the new science.

title: Elite Values versus Organizational Structure in Predicting Innovation
abstract: Value explanations of change are compared in their predictive power with the 3 structural variables of org'al complexity, centralization, & formalization. Data from 16 health & welfare org's in a large midwestern city that provided rehabilitation services were used to test this. Data were collected twice: in 1964, 320 staff members & 16 executive directors were interviewed; in 1967, the executive directors were interviewed again to find out how many new programs had been added in the preceding 3 yrs. Values were measured by a general battery developed by Augusta Neal (see SA 14:4/66C0234), structure by indices of complexity, centralization & formalization. An index of values favorable to change was computed from the responses. Elite values emerged as better predictors of program change than any of the structural variables. The values of the elite inner circle were found to be more important than those of the executive director of the entire staff in predicting innovation, esp if a behavioral & not a formal operationalization of the definition of elite values was used. Findings support the notion that org's develop an inner circle & the values of this circle determine largely, though not completely, org'al policy. 3 Tables. Modified HA.

title: Sociologist Jan Mertl: Quisling or a Victim of Circumstances?
abstract: The article analyses the life and academic contribution of one of the most prominent interwar Czech sociologists, Jan Mertl (1904-1978), whose studies in political sociology were highly innovative in his day, in both the Czech and the international context. Mertl was a follower of Max Weber and focused on the comparative historical-sociological analysis of political partisanship and party systems. He also devoted extensive study to changes in the relationship between state administration/bureaucracy and political representation. He enriched the field of (Czech) sociological theory with his concept of the 'self-regularity of social phenomena', dealing with the unintended outcomes and latent functions of social action, and he attempted to distinguish between Weberian ideal types and 'historical types'. He also made the first systematic analysis of modern bureaucracy, using the Weberian concept of the 'iron cage of modernisation'. However, Mertl is a significant figure in the history of Czech sociology for another reason: his behaviour during the Second World War is generally perceived as an explicit example of collaboration with Nazism, which led to Mertl's total exclusion from the academic community after the war. The author analyses the motives and extent of Mertl's 'wrongdoing', as well as the reasons for his being ostracised by the academic world, even though he was officially acquitted of collaboration. The author also provides a brief description of his later life. The article is based on all available published sources and on a large number of previously unknown and unexploited archive materials. Adapted from the source document.

title: Alison I Griffith and Dorothy E Smith (eds), Under New Public Management:Institutional Ethnographies of Changing Front-Line Work
abstract: Griffith, Alison I; Smith, Dorothy E (eds), Under New Public Management: Institutional Ethnographies of Changing Front-Line Work. Toronto: University of Toronto Press, 2014. 354 pp. (excluding index). ISBN: 9781442649101 (hbk) £48.99, ISBN: 9781442626560 (pbk) £21.99.

title: Citizen Participation in a Mediated Age: Neighbourhood Governance in The Netherlands
abstract: Two developments--the fragmentation of governance and the mediatization of politics--lead governmental organizations to engage in discursive and institutional competition. These new circumstances also drastically change the relationship of governmental organizations to clients, target groups and the citizenry as a whole. We empirically investigate these changes through a study of a privately funded community development organization in the Netherlands, the Neighbourhood Alliance. In this case, it is no longer the citizenry that articulates a public discourse, but a public discourse that, through the mediation of an institutional entrepreneur like the Neighbourhood Alliance, stipulates what type of participation is appropriate. This development raises the critical issue of the nature and mechanisms of democratic engagement in a fragmented, mediatized polity. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: BUREAUCRACY AND ALIENATION: A DIMENSIONAL APPROACH
authors: Bonjean, Charles M; Grimes, Michael D
abstract: The generalization that a direct relationship exists between bur'ization & alienation is modified by examining the relationships between 5 bur'tic characteristics & 6 forms of alienation among samples of hourly paid workers, salaried managers & independent businessmen. The data do not support the broad generalization that such a direct relationship exists, but some patterns of relationship are suggestive for further res: (1) bur'cy may be directly related to alienation among bluecollar workers, but not among salaried managers or independent businessmen; (2) the authority dimension of bur'cy is more closely related to measures of alienation than other bur'tic characteristics among hourly paid workers, & that form of alienation most closely related to bur'ization among hourly paid workers is self-estrangement. Modified HA.

title: Relationship-based practice and reflective practice: holistic approaches to contemporary child care social work
abstract: The renewed interest in relationship-based practice can be understood in the child care social work context as a response to the call to re-focus practice in this field. Relationship-based practice challenges the prevailing trends which emphasize reductionist understandings of human behaviour and narrowly conceived bureaucratic responses to complex problems. In so doing practitioners engaged in relationship-based practice need to be able to cope with the uniqueness of each individual's circumstances and the diverse knowledge sources required to make sense of complex, unpredictable problems. This paper argues that if relationship-based practice is to become an established and effective approach to practice, practitioners need to develop their reflective capabilities. An outline of contemporary understandings of relationship-based and reflective practice is offered and findings from doctoral research drawn on to identify how reflective practice complements relationship-based practice. The product of this complementary relationship is enhanced understandings across four aspects of practice: the client, the professional self, the organizational context and the knowledges informing practice. The paper concludes by acknowledging the inextricably interconnected nature of relationship-based and reflective practice and emphasizes the importance of practitioners being afforded opportunities to practise in relational and reflective ways. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Asylanträge verwalten und entscheiden: der soziologische Blick auf Verborgenes
abstract: Dieser Beitrag befasst sich mit zwei in der deutschsprachigen Soziologie wenig beachteten Themenfeldern: Anhand einer Fallstudie des vormaligen Bundesasylamtes (bis Ende 2013) wird zum einen Licht auf die Verwaltung von Migration – im Speziellen von Asyl – im Sinne der street-level bureaucracy geworfen. Zum anderen wird auf das methodisch unausgeschöpfte Potential der Aktenanalyse eingegangen, die in diesem Bereich wesentliche Erkenntnisse liefern kann. Insgesamt liegt der Fokus der hier präsentierten Untersuchung auf den sozialen Praktiken und Prozessen, die den Arbeitsalltag der EntscheiderInnen strukturieren und prägen. Dazu zählen insbesondere der Umgang mit Herausforderungen in der Entscheidungsfällung im Rahmen struktureller Spannungsfelder (Abschn. 2) sowie die Bedeutung von Artefakten als Aktanten im Prozess der Antragsbearbeitung (Abschn. 3).

title: Regional Inequalities in the Process of Nigeria's Development: Socio-Political and Administrative Perspective
abstract: Examines the historical evolution of regional inequality (RI) in Nigeria, & proposes means of reversing the RI institutionalized by colonial & postcolonial rule. It is argued that RI was shaped & promoted during the era of British colonial administration (1861-1960), during which the scarcity of administrative headquarters created a small number of high growth cities with access to unusually large amounts of human & financial resources. Furthermore, the constant process of relocating these headquarters further proliferated RI through the withdrawal of resources from formerly resource-abundant cities & the redistribution of wealth at different locations. The division of the country into northern & southern administrative regions also enhanced RI while reinforcing ethnic separation. The foundations for RI established during the colonial years were perpetuated by the actions & policies of the Nigerian elite & bourgeoisie who took over in 1960. RI must be overcome through development strategies that emphasize self-reliance, sustainable growth, & grassroots, bottom-up approaches to economic security. 1 Table, 39 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Concept of Administrative Style
abstract: The concern is with what accounts for the signif'ly diff ways in which people carry out relatively standard pol'al admin'ive tasks. The admin'ive styles of F. D. Roosevelt, Dwight D. Eisenhower, & Harry S. Truman are compared. It is noted that such studies are as yet little developed. Res from role theory, occup'al psychol, personality theory, & clinical practice is found to offer some hints on how these styles come about. When viewing individual cases, certain qualifications to, & limits of, the concept of admin'ive style loom up. Successive office-holders may exact a remarkably even performance from their org, despite wild diff's in personal methods of work. Style must often be changed as the individual ascends. The entire field is seen to be of some pol'al signif, although unilluminated even by the conventional biographical & sociol'al approaches to it. The quasi-psychiatric method of res proposed for the field by H. D. Lasswell in 1932 is still the most promising. Problems arise, however, re the contexts in which a student may be able to make the sort of observations required. M. Maxfield.

title: Administrative Modernization and the Diffusion of Technological Innovations in Local Administration
abstract: Local administrations have used the latest technologies from decades ago. This article presents a research about the web sites of the region of Madrid's city councils, addressing the last movements through administrative modernization & the differences between those web sites. Results of this exploratory study confirm that even if web sites offer possibilities to the city councils to develop potentialities related to the administrative modernization, local administrations have developed in a very variable way these possible benefits. Besides, using an index of web site development it is intended to get inside the relationship between this variable & some features related to the city councils & their institutional context. In sum, this article tackles with some of the critical aspects to understand the adoption & diffusion of technological innovations within the local public sector in a context of administrative modernization. 5 Tables, 1 Appendix, 97 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Generic Social Work Skills in Social Administration: The Example of Persuasion
abstract: It is argued that though their educational preparations differ, both social welfare administrators & direct service workers require a basic set of social work practice skills. These generic skills are defined & related to the effectiveness of human service administration. Focus is on persuasive communication tactics, & various strategies are suggested by which administrators & direct service workers can maximize their utility; two case studies are offered as illustration. 1 Table, 33 References. K. Hyatt

title: Civil society in Canada: A case study of rural and urban planning contexts
abstract: This paper explores the political concept of civil society and its emergence in multi-level rural and urban planning contexts. The first section conceptualizes civil society in the broader context within which it develops and we discuss global civil society to establish the need for a more local and regional focus. We then present considerations for assessing civil society and outline the research approach. The second section presents two case examples: (1) rural civil society in British Columbia, Canada focusing on the socio-political environment that enabled a shift away from conventional top-down, state-led forest management to devolved local control, and; (2) urban civil society in Waterloo Region, Ontario, which illustrates the response of local organizations to the wider socio-economic problems of housing provision in the Region. In both rural and urban contexts, there was longstanding tacit local support for each cause but significant triggers were needed to open policy windows and enable civil society organizations to help shift management ideologies in the forestry and housing sectors. Empowering civil actors through, for example, the devolution of decision making and responsibilities, and the redistribution of resources, helped to foster forms of legitimacy needed for emerging local and regional civil society organizations and networks. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Significance of Individual Perception - and Action Patterns in Legal Application - The Example of the Administration of Prostitution
abstract: The article deals with the application of law in the public administration of prostitution regimentation. A focus is placed upon the administrative personnel's patterns of perception & action, which are identified via conducting & analyzing qualitative interviews with experts. Through exemplary case studies, the relevance of administrative personnel's patterns of interpretation & occupational orientations, as well as options for action & discretion in their application or non-application of the law, are highlighted. It consequently becomes clear that lay in action depends not only upon law itself, but also upon how the administrative personnel interprets & applies it. References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The downside of participatory-deliberative public administration
abstract: This article provides an empirically grounded critique of Participatory-Deliberative Public Administration, based on an in-depth study of three participatory fora in South Africa: the National Economic Development and Labour Council, the Child Labour Intersectoral Group and the South African National AIDS Council. Drawing freely on Habermas' Between Facts and Norms, the article argues that coordination through deliberation is unlikely to occur in formal settings, where discourses are mostly about the accommodation of existing interests, and is more likely to be found in the informal public sphere, where the preferences of citizens are still malleable and where it is possible for civil society groups to build communicative power by articulating moral arguments that motivate and mobilize the public. This form of power can then be used by civil society groups to counterbalance other forms of (non-communicative) power that impinge on the formal decision-making sphere. Adapted from the source document.

title: Back to My Roots: A Study of 'Returning' Emigrated Health Professionals in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana
