abstract: Nolan, Brian, O'Connell, Philip, and Whelan, Christopher, (eds), Bust to Boom? The Irish Experience of Growth and Inequality, Dublin: Institute of Public Administration, 2000, paper [euro]25.39, 389 pages.

title: Class Formation and Localism in an Emerging Bureaucracy: British Bank Workers, 1880-1960
authors: Savage, Mike; Stovel, Katherine; Bearman, Peter
abstract: This article uses a case study of the spatial & career mobility of bank workers from Lloyds, a leading British bank, to explore the relationship between class formation & spatial mobility. The article argues against the idea that the large-scale concentration & bureaucratization of the British banking industry in the early years of the 20th century saw the emergence of a mobile middle-class spiralist or cosmopolitan. We use archival data from Lloyds Bank to argue that the emergence of Lloyds as a large-scale national bank involved a compromise with localized interests rather than a detachment of the bank from local concerns. We use data on the career histories of a representative sample of male bank employees to argue that spatial mobility was organized largely within regions & helped to consolidate the prospects of rural bank workers. We argue that London emerged as a distinctive "hub" for banking careers, with significant amounts of movement to & from London from all regions. We therefore demonstrate how localized & rural cultures were sedimented within a large, national bureaucracy, & that a genuine "spiralist" structure did not emerge. 3 Tables, 3 Figures, 44 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Rogue Cops' Politics of Equality in The Wire
abstract: This paper explores HBO television show The Wire's portrayal of inequality and injustice in terms of the neoliberal state and capitalism, while focussing on the Baltimore Police Department and the marginalized people in the show. In arguing that the neoliberal state and neoliberalism promote the systemic problems reflected in The Wire, this paper will examine the representation of the marginalized in the show in relation to Zygmunt Bauman's idea of wasted lives. In doing so, it will explore how bureaucracies in the show fail to salvage the wasted lives that Bauman defines as the collateral casualties of capitalistic globalization. After examining the show's bleak portrayal of American urban life in terms of the police department, this paper will discuss some morally complicated characters, such as Major Colvin and Detectives McNulty and Freamon, who attempt to surmount the systemic problems of the department. In examining their controversial police work, including transgressions of law, this paper aims to clarify the political implications of these police officers in terms of Jacques Ranciere's ideas of politics and equality. Adapted from the source document.

title: Formalization, Standardization and Centralization: A Critical Analysis of Selected Research
abstract: A contribution to the debate on the relationship between bureaucratic dimensions & control mechanisms in organizations. Analyzed are several publications which examine the relationship between formalization, standardization, & centralization. Formalization & standardization are methods of predicting & controlling the behavior of subordinates, & thus are an alternative to centralization. This model is criticized because it takes into consideration only one decisionmaker whose will is translated into organizational reality. Criticism is also addressed to the underlying assumption that organizations behave rationally. Centralization of decision making is merely a managerial technique & not a phenomenon which reflects ideological assumptions & power relationships. Modified AA.

title: A Model of the Bureaucratic Culture
abstract: A model is presented which is flexible enough to accommodate a wide range of political intervention on the part of the bureaucracy & whose goal is formulation of a rational & coherent typology of bureaucratic tendencies for use in tracing the development of public services, & for direct comparison. The 2 characteristics of the bureaucratic culture tendency toward political activity, ie, involvement & distinctiveness, are analyzed both independently & in tandem. Their independent variation comprises the general model which is then extrapolated to a formal typology. The case example of Austrian bureaucracy illuminates the basic concepts. 5 Figures. C. Grindle.

title: Political economy and adoption of policies affecting everyday life in the American states
abstract: The political economy model has been successfully used to predict adoption of controversial or crisis-prone policies.  In contrast, this article assesses the model's utility in relation to adoption rates of three mundane policy domains that govern everyday life.

title: Changing the Culture: The Governance of the Australian Pre-Millennial University
abstract: Explores how Australian universities are rapidly responding to fiscal stringency through the adoption of tactics & strategies that appropriate the operation of business for the governance of university culture. Having undergone considerable reform in the past decade, a more conservative federal government's economic cutbacks in higher education since 1996 are seen as the "unkindest cut of all." As a result, the university has become more privatized, marketed, globalized, & increasingly student-driven. In these shifts, the deregulated higher education sector is operating out of a bureaucratic rationality where choice & positional advantage are integral to market logic. 49 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: 'PRETTY BORING STUFF': DISTRICT JUDGES AND HOUSING POSSESSION PROCEEDINGS
abstract: In this article, we demonstrate how judgecraft, though mundane in the context of housing possession proceedings in England, involves the client-processing mentality suggested in Lipsky's work on street-level bureaucracy. Although they may be regarded as mundane, the consequences of these proceedings may well be dire, producing homelessness and other forms of extreme housing need. Lipsky helps us, because his work enables us to think about the factors that make up 'being a District Judge'. Having discussed the background to housing possession proceedings, including their growth, we discuss this client-processing mentality in the context of the ways in which District Judges seek to control their clients as well as processes in the courtroom. Repeat-players are molded by individual District Judges through routines, discipline, and just knowing what is expected. In particular, crucial decisions are made as to the worthiness of claimants and occupiers. As a result, relationships of trust develop which facilitate a 'rubber-stamping' approach. In the conclusion, we reflect on the value of Lipsky's work as well as its limits in this context.

title: Revenge of the Managers: Labor Cost-Cutting and the Paradoxical Resurgence of Managerialism in the Shareholder Value Era, 1984 to 2001
abstract: Institutional changes associated with the rise of shareholder value capitalism have had seemingly contradictory effects on managers and managerialism in the United States economy. Financial critiques of inefficient corporate bureaucracies and the resulting wave of downsizing, mergers, and computerization subjected managers to unprecedented layoffs during the 1980s and 1990s as firms sought to become lean and mean. Yet the proportion of managers and their average compensation continued to increase during this period. How did the rise of anti-managerial investor ideologies and strategies oriented toward reducing companies' labor costs coincide with increasing numbers of ever more highly paid managerial employees? This article examines the paradoxical relationship between shareholder value and managerialism by analyzing the effects of shareholder value strategies on the growth of managerial employment and managerial earnings in 59 major industries in the U.S. private sector from 1984 to 2001. Results from industry-level dynamic panel models show that layoffs, mergers, computerization, deunionization, and the increasing predominance of publicly traded firms all contributed to broad-based increases in the number of managerial positions and the valuation of managerial labor. Results are generally consistent with David Gordon's (1996) fat and mean thesis. Adapted from the source document.

title: BUREAUCRACY AND TECHNOCRACY
abstract: The widespread assertion that burley & technocracy are interconnected deformations of Western & of socialist democratic regimes is discussed. Some writers have stipulated that bur'cy is a growth phenomenon of industr'ized, technocratic society, regardless of pol'al regime. It is pointed out that this conception confuses 2 diff, though parallel phenomena emerging in diff settings: technocracy is a phenomenon of corruption in Western democracies; bur'cy signifies corruption in socialist democracies. In Western societies bur'cy plays a very modest & subordinate role. Actual decision power lies in the hands of a group of professionals operating on behalf of the great monopolist pol'al instit's. The educ'al system in France is seen as a good example. Compared with the professional educ'al admin'ors, engineers, who are concerned with actual technological work, have no real decision-power. Nor do they have it in socialist countries, although there they can take the initiative in many areas. The threat of a corruption of socialist democracy does not arise from them, but from the bur'tic degeneration of the Party's guiding power. It is the bur'crat in those countries who is the pol'al man & tends to believe he is directing policies which are his own creation, in the interest of the people. Bur'cy thus, in this case, impedes democratic representation within the structure & principles of the socialist instit's & turns into a symptom of corruption. It is entirely diff from bur'cy as found in Western regimes, where technocracy rather than bur'cy is the corruptive influence. Modified HA.

title: Social Relations in Organizations: Further Evidence for the Weberian Model
authors: Miller, Jon P; Fry, Lincoln J
abstract: An earlier case study confirmed some elements of a soc-psychol'al formulation of M. Weber's org'al model & disconfirmed others. Close relationships among authority, control, formal training, & legitimacy were found, but impersonality was not characteristic of the org, & no evidence was found to link org'al knowledge derived from experience to the distribution of unofficial control. The present res replicates this study in 4 additional org's, & also attempts to examine the relationships among org'al knowledge, unofficial control, & friendship, & to investigate the degree to which each of these variables is related to authority, control, formal training, & legitimacy. Again, the relationships among authority, control, training & legitimacy are close, & strong evidence against impersonality is found. Finally, an unusual amount of the unofficial control is exercised in all the org's, but no evidence indicates that this challenges the official structure of authority in any of the org's. Modified HA.

title: Class Structure and Legitimatory Public Sphere: A Hypothesis on the Continued Existence of Class Relationships and the Problem of Legitimation in Transitional Societies
abstract: An attempt was made to develop an hypothesis on assumed connections between a system of productive relations in transitional societies & the particular structure of their "relations of communications." Despite a fundamental methodological problem of "idealist projection," Marxist analysis cannot refuse historical in socialist societies. Most specifically, it must be determined whether the "aim of a classless society" has been, or can be, realized & distinguished from "emancipation from class domination." As history gives evidence against the coincidence of class & concepts of capital, it can be assumed that class struggle exists outside of capitalistic societies & even where class domination has been abolished. Class domination must be specified according to 2 criteria: (1) it constitutes itself in the violent separation of the producers from the control of, & the authority to dispose of, the material conditions of their production, & (2) it is stabilized in the private appropriation & use of the surplus product of society through the ruling class. The 2nd is possible because of the 1st priority, & linked together in a capitalist system. In transitional societies, the stabilization is lacking but the 1st criterion confirms the presence of class differentiation, with the state retaining authority & control, which must be legitimated. This ideological legitimation of class domination results in the effective depoliticization of the masses--contrary to the aims of the rigid propaganda but revealing the inherent vulnerability of the system--& the material weakness of class domination. The totalitarianism in the public sphere invites apathy among the masses & provokes emergence of intellectual opposition, which in turn places a heavier burden on the legitimation of the ruling class. E. Preston.

title: A Multiplex Theory of Urban Service Distribution: The Case of School Expenditures
authors: Pallas, Aaron M; Jennings, Jennifer L
abstract: The literature on urban service delivery has crystallized into two key theoretical perspectives, one emphasizing agency & interests & the other structure & bureaucracy. These perspectives typically do not allow for the possibility that explanations of the origins of variability in the distribution of urban services might differ from explanations of the persistence of such variability. In this article, the authors articulate a multiplex, longitudinal model of urban service distribution, emphasizing the contributions of multiplex funding streams & multiple layers of bureaucracy, bureaucratic discretion, & path dependency to the model. Drawing on data on school building -- level expenditures in New York City over six years, the authors provide new evidence on the distribution of expenditures on public education in New York City. They find that there is substantial year-to-year stability in per-pupil expenditures, that expenditures are responsive to the social & economic characteristics of clients at varying levels of the education system, & that allocation decisions made at a given level of the system may either amplify or diminish the distributional consequences of allocation decisions made at a higher level of the system. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Inc., copyright holder.]

title: Underground Urban Goods Distribution Networks
abstract: Automated underground transportation is an option to overcome accessibility & environmental problems related to urban goods transport. One underground alternative is an "underground link" that connects an urban distribution park at the borders of a city directly to inner-city shopping areas. Standard or modified road vehicles (vans, small trucks) use the link, which is an advanced form of a dedicated lane. Another underground alternative is a fully underground distribution network wherein dedicated, automated vehicles distribute goods. Underground systems use new vehicle & transshipment technologies & require new logistic concepts. Both alternatives underpass heavily congested roads & sensitive objects or areas & improve the accessibility (for goods transport) of urban centers. The underground network improves accessibility even more as it removes most goods traffic from surface roads. In the operational phase, it also has significant positive effects on the environment (noise, emissions) & traffic safety. The construction phase & traffic-generating effect, on both goods & passenger transport, may limit some of the positive effects. Underground systems strengthen the position of cities & this will, in the long term, contribute to more sustainable development. 4 Tables, 7 Figures, 13 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Racial Diversity, Representative Bureaucracy, and Equity in Multiracial School Districts
authors: Rocha, Rene R; Hawes, Daniel P
abstract: Objective. This study examines the conditions under which minorities will face policy inequity within the educational system. It turns to the theory of representative bureaucracy as one possible explanation, and extends the literature by considering whether African-American students benefit from the presence of Latinos on teaching faculties and vice versa. This study also tests competing theories of how racial context influences minority educational policy outcomes. Methods. This study combines original survey data with data gathered by the U.S. Census to predict levels of academic grouping in U.S. school districts as reported by the Office of Civil Rights. Results. Minority teachers lower levels of discrimination among all minority students, not just co-ethnics. Moreover, minority teachers do so consistently and with a substantive impact that occasionally rivals that of co-ethnic teachers. The findings also suggest that greater levels of racial/ethnic diversity within a district are associated with lower levels of discrimination. Conclusion. Theories of race relations must move beyond black-Anglo or Latino-Anglo relations to consider how multiple racial/ethnic groups interact, and how such interactions affect the lives of minority groups differently. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucracy, Political System, and Social Dynamic
abstract: The current situation of the Left within industrialized countries is examined & found to be lacking in dynamics & force, & deficient in the formulation of new critiques & innovative radical plans for social development. The lack of Leftist writings is especially notable concerning the development of contemporary civilization. Civilization in the form of class society is proving adaptable to change, as capitalist structures give way not merely to socialism as Marx predicted, but to many diverse forms of bureaucratization. Bureaucratic structure is examined in its relation to industrial society, to political structure, & within its social origin. Paths that bureaucracy could follow are examined including: the capitalist-bureaucratic course, & the socialist-bureaucratic course & its possibility of totalitarian absolutism as described in Stalinist radical theory. 3 political system types are described: (1) pluralist (multicentered) systems, (2) absolutist (unicentered) systems, & (3) totalitarianism which involves many extrapolitical aspects of society. Contemporary socialist-bureaucratic growth trends can be analyzed with broader reference than the merely economic, ie, social structure & organizational patterns operate also. Future historic developments are extrapolated from the analysis of the present; 2 projections are described which represent opposite poles of the possible: (A) current developments will continue uninterrupted, or (B) current trends will reverse. These 2 cases are explained with reference to pluralization & social dynamics. C. Grindle.

title: Correlates of Organizational Identification as a Function of Career Pattern and Organizational Type
abstract: This study examines personal & org'al r's of org'al identification in 2 types of org--the Roman Catholic Church & R&D laboratories. The results are compared with those obtained in the US Forest Service (see SA 0312/F4653). Priests & foresters typically spend their entire careers in one org (the single-org career pattern), while res professionals are more mobile (the multiorg career pattern). Because of diff's in org'al soc'ization & mobility, tenure is a stronger r of org'al identification in the single-org career. The effects of tenure are independent of other r's--job challenge, job involvement, self-image, need importance, & satisfaction. Job challenge, through the intervening effects of job satisfaction, is a strong r of identification for both career types. The res'er's self-image is more strongly tied to his work involvement & the foresters' to his org'al involvement. This is consistent with the diff'ial mobility patterns. Higher-order need satisfaction is r'ed with high org'al involvement for both career patterns, although the importance of needs r's diff'ially. For the single org career, org'al identification is related to security & affiliation, while identification is linked to low concern for self-fulfillment for the multiorg career. The single org career thus combines security & localism with growth & cosmopolitanism, whereas in the multiorg career the professional must choose between these alternatives. Modified HA.

title: Women, Bureaucracy, and the Welfare State
abstract: An analysis of gender issues faced by Norwegian women employed in the public sector, seeking to gain better insight into the relationship between women & the state, particularly with respect to power & control in traditionally female "care jobs," eg, in the health care & teaching professions. Based on an analysis employing concepts relating to responsibility & technically limited rationality, the Marxist class model, & bureaucracy, it is argued that gender-based differences in values must be studied to fully understand women's situation in society. It is claimed that women are gaining increasing influence over the welfare state, while men are remaining within the private sector, & that this is important if the state is to remain a welfare state & not be superseded by capitalist ideology. 3 Tables, 2 Figures, 22 References. A. Thyme

title: The Indian Civil Service and the nationalist movement: neutrality, politics and continuity
abstract: How was it that the Indian Civil Service (ICS), involved as it was in various activities to secure the British Raj against the pressures of Indian nationalism, was able to survive and flourish in the new political order after independence? This article argues that part of the explanation lies in the fact that it was, and was seen to be, a 'politically neutral' institution. In the course of making this argument, it surveys the changing role of the ICS vis-à-vis the nationalist movement before independence, and also considers the theoretical question of what is meant by the claim that bureaucratic work is 'apolitical' or 'neutral' with respect to politics.

title: Consumer Participation in Administrative Decision Making
abstract: The term "consumer participation" in public agencies has come to occupy an important place in discussions of administrative theory & practice without any real consensus on what such participation implies. This phenomenon is considered in the field of housing, examining the impact of tenant participation across 750 public housing projects. Analysis of data derived from a survey of housing projects conducted by the US Dept of Housing & Ur Development in 1978 supports the view that tenant organizations can be effective in increasing the level of resources & services made available to tenants, but provides no evidence that this form of consumer participation enhances the administrative process. Modified AA.

title: Bureaucracy and Ethnicity
abstract: A theoretical controversy has developed over the impact of social background on the attitudes, values, & behavior of public bureaucrats. Empirical analysis of the attitudes of Israeli citizens (N=1,600) & public bureaucrats (N=630), from 22 of the largest cities, toward their national bureaucracy indicates that becoming a bureaucrat & even achieving high rank within the bureaucracy does not overcome the effect of ethnicity upon attitudes in areas of high salience to specific groups. Focus on a particular ethnic group, Israeli Jews of Asian-African background, found that the Eastern Jews "are proportionally underrepresented in all but the lowest ranks of the Israeli national bureaucracy & are extremely so in its upper levels." Low-rank bureaucrats of Asian-African origin differ in their attitudes from members of their ethnic group in society at large, & this incongruence tends to widen as advancement in the bureaucratic ranks occurs, except in regard to issues of high salience to that ethnic group. 3 Tables. Modified HA.

title: Re-thinking the Future of Work: Beyond Binary Hierarchies
abstract: How will work be organised in the future? This paper reveals that although there are multiple stories about the future of work, a similar storyline is adopted across many of the competing visions. Most visions firstly squeeze all forms of work into one side or the other or some dichotomy and then proceed to temporally and/or normatively sequence the two sides of the dualism and finally label the resultant one-dimensional and linear trajectory as some -ism, -ation or post-something-or-other. This paper evaluates critically such hierarchical binary narratives (e.g., the shift from informal to formal work, non-commodified to commodified work, localisation to globalisation, Fordism to post-Fordism, bureaucracy to post-bureaucracy) and displays how these dominant narratives, as well as the counter narratives that simply invert the temporal and/or hierarchical sequencing of these dichotomies, over-simplify lived practice. The paper concludes by offering a way forward that transcends these one-dimensional linear tales and recognises the heterogeneous and multiple directions of work in order to provide a more kaleidoscope-like understanding of the direction of work and open up the future of work to new possibilities. [Copyright 2008 Elsevier Ltd.]

title: REVOLUTION AND BUREAUCRACY
abstract: An historical analysis which is not situated on the level of concrete facts, because in the interior of a global structural analysis, the facts vary according to a thousand diff soc, historical, & individual factors, but which focuses on the historical analysis of the structure in which the facts become concrete. In this perspective of the history of European societies an attempt is made to present certain hyp's of a typology of the great periods of history & of Marxist thought, along with the pol'al transformations that they entailed, linked to the global structure in which both the thought & the pol'al program enjoyed a functional role. The initial question posed is how was Marxist thought born, beginning with theories which formed the left-wing of bourgeois democratic thought, from neoHegelianism in Germany & democratic socialism in France. The analysis then proceeds to explain that the left in pre-revolutionary Russia, exemplified by Rosa Luxembourg & L. Trotsky who remained more faithful to K. Marx than E. Bernstein or V. L Lenin, failed because its fidelity attached to the letter of Marxist theory, whereas the situation demanded a certain, flexibility. The analysis then moves to a consideration of the dominant ideology which created Stalinism in Europe. M. Duke.

title: United States -- Thickening Government: Federal Hierarchy and the Diffusion of Accountability by Paul C. Light
abstract: Review.

title: The Tyranny of Distance: Kafka and the problem of distance in bureaucratic Organizations
abstract: Inspired by the insights of Franz Kafka, this article explores the problem of 'distance' in a UK bank, particularly by focusing on one of its back-office processing centres. Distance refers to a way of not seeing those below us in the hierarchy; this might mean that we act in ways that display little thought or concern for the experiences of others. It is argued that the 'distance' created between human beings through bureaucratic ways of organizing is potentially debilitating. Academic accounts often strive for objectivity and, in doing so, they tend to stand at a distance from the suffering of those they seek to represent. By contrast, fiction elucidates distance in a more emotional, passionate and, therefore, engaged and engaging way. This article draws on Kafka because his work is subversive and it highlights the need to create ways of organizing and being that promote empathy with 'others'. Nevertheless, this is not to suggest that distance can be eliminated because it is fundamental to how we develop our sense of self and it is ingrained within processes of rationalization. The article is distinctive because although numerous accounts have used fiction to theoretically analyse Organizations few have sought to use fiction to analyse empirical material. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright holder.]

title: The Policy Issues
abstract: In INTRODUCTION Phyllis A. Wallace (Alfred P. Sloan School of Management, Massachusetts Instit Technology, Cambridge) notes that these statements address, from several points of view, the policy issue of the occupational segregation of women. Institutional system behavior is considered, as is bureaucratic functioning, the enforcement of federal law, policy investigation, the effects of economic projections, & models of research & intervention. In PRESENTATION I Ruth G. Shaeffer (The Conference Board, New York, NY) discusses a systems oriented approach to reducing occupational segregation. This approach requires clear definition of the goal to be achieved, as well as identification of the many interrelated institutional systems whose behavior toward women & girls must be changed. The approach involves the simultaneous application of appropriate interventions to produce the different sorts of changes in institutional behavior that are required. In PRESENTATION II Nira Long (Agency for International Development) considers the problem of occupational segregation from the point of view of an agency official attempting to implement affirmative action goals. Concrete goal definition remains the most elusive of problems, although the promotion system in public bureaucracies & the difficulties in gaining the compliance of private organizations are also at issue. Accountability is problematic, as is the climate of fear which now prevails with regard to employment in the private & public sectors. In PRESENTATION III Winn Newman (International Union of Electrical Workers) argues that new research & solutions are less important than gaining compliance with present legislation & policies, & that this is readily possible at a comparatively low cost with regard to discrimination against blue-collar women. Charges & suits should be filed against industrial organizations under current Title VII legislation. Wage-rate & discriminatory promotion & layoff systems currently characterize virtually all industrial plants. These sorts of practices are very amenable to juridical attack, & such an attack carries a clear educative function in regard to blue collar women, who often do not understand their situation. In PRESENTATION IV Bernice Sandler (Project on the Status & Education of Women, Assoc of American Coll's) proposes that public policy should be the focus, on the assumption that behavior will change following policy changes. Sex discrimination will be more difficult to eradicate than racial discrimination, because there is less guilt in regard to discrimination against women, & because women are a part of virtually all households. Legislation has done much, & should be extended with regard to discriminatory features of social security, income tax, & other matters. Pressure groups are a vital aid in rendering policy changes in the wake of legislation, as various groups have clearly demonstrated. In PRESENTATION V Janet L. Norwood (Bureau of Labor Statistics) argues that B. Sandler's attempt to discuss women as one group is mistaken. Women must be approached with regard to differing LF experiences as these vary with age & occupation. Even with legislative gains, most F's earn far less than M's. Especially important is the fact that 35% of F's employed are in clerical positions. If the employment profile of women is to be changed, then many of these women in clerical positions must be moved into management positions. To accomplish this, more jobs are needed generally. In PRESENTATION VI Rosabeth Moss Kanter (Brandeis U, Waltham Mass) discusses the close fit that obtains between models of research & models of intervention in the matter of occupational segregation. 3 research models are isolated, each possessing different implications regarding intervention, with the final model being clearly superior to the others. The "temperamental" model stresses women's character & personality in regard to socialization & sex roles. Concerning intervention, the temperamental model leads to strategies whose purpose is to improve the personality qualities of women, eg, assertiveness training. This approach, however, is unproven & may lead to stereotyping. It also reinforces some traditional M attitudes. The second research model is role related. By focusing on the M/F DofL, this model leads to strategies stressing individual role conceptions. Drawbacks here include an overabundant attention placed on the family & a lack of concern with the work place & the nature of the work world. The 3rd model of research & intervention is the social structural model. This model has the greatest potential for generally efficacious intervention because it is directed to the nature of organizational structures & the organization of work. It offers a key to the modification of hierarchies, the use of flexible time, the introduction of women to new positions, lines of mobility out of clerical work, the secretary-boss relationship, & finally, the effects of sex ratios. 2 Tables. F. Hydoski.

title: 'Reintegration' of Ex-combatants and Former Fighters: a lens into state formation and citizenship in Namibia
abstract: This article explores Namibian state formation and citizenship through the case of ex-combatant "reintegration," particularly its focus on government employment provision since the mid-1990s. It examines the discourses that have motivated the targeting of ex-combatants, the practical measures taken towards "reintegration," and ex-combatants' own initiatives and responses. Analytically it focuses on the implications of "reintegration" for relations between the state and its population or citizens, particularly the drawing of lines of inclusion and exclusion, and the tension that appears between personalised and bureaucratic tendencies of rule. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Charter Schools and Urban Regimes in Neoliberal Context: Making Workers and New Spaces in Metropolitan Atlanta
authors: Hankins, Katherine B; Martin, Deborah G
abstract: In this article, we demonstrate the neoliberalism and multiscalar economic perspective of the charter school movement in Atlanta, Georgia, through examination of news articles and editorials about charter schools in the Atlanta Journal-Constitution from 1998 to 2004. We posit three interrelated dynamics which explain the editorial board's interest in charter schools as part of a broader urban regime agenda. First, charter schools represent part of a neoliberal shift in education that parallels shifts in urban governance, emphasizing flexibility, public?private partnerships, and 'market'-oriented consumer choice and accountability. Second, the newspaper is issuing a challenge to educational structures, to adopt more neoliberal policies and shed a bureaucratic, liberal governance framework. Finally, we find critical evidence that the charter school movement draws on a multiscalar discourse which simultaneously references responsiveness to local, neighborhood needs, and at the same time highlights the economic imperatives of a global, competitive city to differentially skill students/workers in order to capture mobile and fractured (global) capital. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Natural Resource Access and Interracial Associations: Black and White Subsistence Fishing in the Mississippi Delta
authors: Brown, Ralph B; Toth, John F, Jr
abstract: Using qualitative data gathered over approximately twenty months, we examine how racial divisions between black & white fishers factor into access, harvesting strategies, & use of natural resources in subsistence fishing activities in the Mississippi Delta. Though both races engage in subsistence fishing for many of the same reasons -- a sense of autonomy & economic independence -- clear differences were manifest in their access, harvesting strategies, & utilization of the fish. We document these differences. We conclude that the social relations between white & black subsistence fishers, as they interact with & through the landscape, appear to perpetuate the characteristics of race relations in this region rather than redefine them. 51 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Debating the State in Private Housing Neighborhoods: The Governance of Homeowners' Associations in Urban Shanghai
abstract: This article examines the transformation of state power in urban China by investigating how the state governs a newly emerging type of neighborhood organization connected with housing privatization, the homeowners' association (HA). Based on a series of extensive field research visits in Shanghai from 2006 to 2012, it analyzes the contradictory rationales behind HA policies in Shanghai, and elaborates the debates between state actors and non-state actors on the boundary of state intervention. It finds that the state in Shanghai has engaged multiple goals in its governance of the HAs: regularizing the real estate market, promoting self-organization at the neighborhood level, and channeling homeowners' participation in urban politics. The neoliberal rationality of governing through subjects' autonomy and a tradition of the socialist discourse on party leadership co-exist in the state's toolkit for governance. But the state's capacity to coordinate these different governing techniques varies across fields. I highlight the dilemma a non-liberal state confronts in cultivating self-organizing and self-responsible individuals. This contrasts with some of the studies on 'China's neoliberal state', which argue that the bureaucratic system has been resilient in coping with the contradictions and imbalances inherent in neoliberalism.[PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Japan's Ministry of Finance and the Politics of Complicity
abstract: A review essay on a book by Junko Kato, The Problem of Bureaucratic Rationality: Tax Politics in Japan (Princeton: Princeton U Press, 1994 [see listing in IRPS No. 84]). Kato offers a substantial examination of the history of tax reform, but his book is heavily criticized for its failure to address the "politics of complicity" within the Ministry of Finance (MOF). It is argued that a complete analysis of tax politics in Japan must include an exploration of the involvement of Japanese bureaucrats in the political economic policies favored by politicians & others. Kato suggests that the MOF's preference for a value added tax (VAT) is attributed to its desire for a stable revenue base, leading to a more definitive budget plan, & eliminating the need for deficit financing. Kato's argument that the MOF & the Liberal Democratic Party pursued the VAT based on its merit is discounted as ignoring the political expediency of such a policy. 13 References. M. Greenberg

title: "Whose Needs Are Being Served?" Quantitative Metrics and the Reshaping of Social Services
abstract: In this article in the forum on Quantitative Indicators, the author questions the hegemony of statistical data as the basis for Canadian political, social, & economic decision-making to argue that current management models are paving the way for reliance on low-wage, temporary, & unpaid workers. A discussion of the management/worker/client dynamic in care work contextualizes a critical examination of the New Public Management (NPM) & other performance based management models that advance the priorities of budget-cutting & pro-market rationality, decrease client care & access. The perverse incentive to increase efficiency in public & nonprofit services is antithetical to increased profit is reflected in worker resistance to the NPM, & the complexities of the conflicting power structures described by Abu-Lughod. The author concludes that quantitative metrics in the social services expand bureaucracy & contribute the standardization of work, & the deskilling of the workforce. References. J. Harwell

title: Contributions of the Urban Informal Sector to Environmental Management
abstract: Explores the contribution of informal sector (IS) activities or urban environmental (UE) services in developing countries, which have improved such UE conditions as the water supply & garbage collection. In this context, the environmental component's contribution to the labor structure of the urban economy & its role in UE management are discussed. It is argued that the environmental component exists within the IS, offers employment opportunities, & positively impacts the urban economy. The environmental component of the urban IS sustains important linkages between formal sector activities & the local economy through scavengers selling to recycling companies, urban farmers selling to local supermarkets, & water sellers buying from local water utilities. It is expected that the gap between the supply of & demand for UE services will continue, & that the IS has a role to play in urban economic development. 9 References. M. Greenberg

title: Report from the Field: Left Media and Left Think Tanks -- Foundation-Managed Protest?
abstract: Left media and left think tank staff people generally deny that the acceptance by their organizations of grants from liberal foundations has transformed their organizational priorities, subjected them to elite control, or channeled their energies into safe, legalistic, bureaucratic activities and mild reformism. In this report, we will be discussing organizations, e.g., Institute for Policy Studies (IPS), North American Congress on Latin America (NACLA), Middle East Research & Information Project (MERIP), Fairness & Accuracy In Reporting (FAIR); and media, e.g., Nation, Progressive, Mother Jones, In These Times , widely regarded as left-wing. Some originated in the 1960s and 1970s with bold challenges to the United States political and economic system; we can read (some are online) their early publications and mission statements to be reminded of the initial militancy. In the popular mind, these media and think tanks are clearly distinguished from, on the one hand, the liberal media, e.g., New York Times, Harper's , and think tanks, e.g., Brookings Institution, Urban Institute, and on the other, the "far" left, e.g., Workers' World , Maoist Internationalist Movement. A few of the left-wing organizations are primarily concerned about threats to media independence, yet all their attention is focused on for-profit corporate (or government) control; they ignore the possible influence of large subventions from non-profit institutions such as foundations.

title: Power and work: The development of work as a civilizing process in examples of fictional literature
abstract: Rural work in a partly pre-market society was compared with office work in a service bureaucracy and with the professional work of college teaching.  The development of work was also analyzed in terms of a civilizing process, and an anthology was drawn with the transformation of warriors into courtiers in early modern France.

title: Taking the Measure of Morale: Structure and Job Satisfaction in a Multihospital System
abstract: Examines the impact of bureaucratic structure on morale among hospital staff (N = 478, 73% response rate) in a government-operated multihospital system, drawing on questionnaire data. Hypotheses are drawn from J. Hage's axiomatic theory of organizations, including the predicated negative impact on morale of formalization, centralization, & stratification & the positive impact on morale of task complexity; contingency hypotheses involving structure & task complexity are also examined. Results indicate morale is either positively affected or unaffected by structure & negatively affected by process; some evidence of contingent effects are found. Findings are discussed in the broader context of Max Weber's theory of bureaucracy. 9 Tables, 86 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Involvement, Motivation, and Reorganization in a Social Services Department
abstract: Data obtained over a 2-year period via staff interviews & documentary materials are drawn on to analyze the reorganization of a local government social services department in the UK, focusing on issues of involvement, participation, & motivation. It is argued that the intention to allow greater participation foundered on the paradox that these changes lacked the explicit direction that became necessary in the context of sudden changes in the wider political & organizational environment. This case study shows a need for explicit leadership & direction if participation is to be fostered in hierarchical work organizations as a means of creating motivated staff & external contributors to the services provided. 2 Appendixes, 54 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Gender and Power Relations in a Bureaucratic Context: Female Immigrants from Ethiopia in an Absorption Centre in Israel
abstract: In this article, I discuss the ways in which the bureaucracy of absorption centers in Israel disempowered Ethiopian women immigrants by promoting a strict gender division of labor within a "family unit" that reflected wider social structures in Israel. In their interactions with Ethiopian immigrants, the officials running the absorption centers enhanced the idea of a family unit, & the gendered power relations within it, by transferring resources to family units through the men, & trying to restrict women to the home & to the absorption center. The different ways in which women & men were treated by officials grew out of bureaucratic needs, as well as reflecting Israeli social arrangements & bureaucrats' own gender & ethnic stereotypes. My arguments have wider implications for other forms of temporary settlement of displaced or migrant populations, where bureaucratic structures mediate between them & the resources that they need. 19 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Response to 'Feminist activism within bureaucracy: Process of formulating and implementing regulations governing the protection of women's rights in Taipei'
abstract: Response to "Feminist Activism within Bureaucracy: Process of Formulating and Implementing Regulations Governing the Protection of Women's Rights in Taipei".

title: Feminist activism within bureaucracy: Process of formulating and implementing regulations governing the protection of women's rights in Taipei
abstract: This study documents and analyses the process of the formulation of the "Regulations Governing the Protection of Women's Rights" in Taipei, Taiwan, China a feminist experiment the author engineered as an activist in the City Government. Scholars and experts from the feminist community involved in working with women bureaucrats adopted both the "outsider tactic" of consciousness-raising and the "insider tactic" of lobbying for support. The creation of the Regulations outside the women's policy agency and without legal mandate or outside pressure demonstrates the vitality and versatility of feminist activism. The author identifies an active and visible feminist community and special bond of sisterhood as the crucial elements that led to the success of the project. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: THE USE OF ANALYTICAL MODELS IN THE COMPARATIVE STUDY OF BUREAUCRATIC ORGANIZATIONS
abstract: Analytical models & typologies provide a convenient tool as well as frame of reference for the systematic, comparative study of bur 'tic org's. This paper concentrates purely on the theoretical aspects of bur'tic org's, dealing with concepts & principles rather than observable phenomena. However, in the future, empirical res should provide the necessary data to permit revision of abstract classifications & generalizations so that they would more nearly represent real life phenomena & relationships. Forms of human org are reduced, herein, to a series of conceptual categories, bur'tic & nonbur'tic; gov & nongov; & monocratic, ie decision-making of a collegial nature. Formal bur'tic org is defined in terms of 5 characteristics: formed position; jurisdiction; hierarchy; office rules & work procedures; qualification requirements. IPSA.

title: Structural and Nonstructural Aspects of Power Distance Reduction Tendencies
abstract: M. Mulder's Power Distance Reduction Theory (PDR), & the related experiments, using a model that distinguishes between structural & nonstructural parameters of a power system, are reexamined. The fomer defines the vertical & horizontal nature of the power relations between people in the system, while the latter specifies the power differential between two immediate ranks, & together they provide a more adequate & precise conception of the links between the power parameters & the tendencies of subordinate group members to seize superordinate power. Several theoretical statements were generated on the bases of the PDR literature & theories of social comparison & bureaucracy to hypothesize the individual effects of the three parameters on power distance reduction (pdr) tendencies. Two experiments, using 48 (aged 17-19) & 40 (aged 17-21) M Coll students respectively, were conducted to test the hypotheses by systematically varying one parameter & holding constant the other two. The results indicate an inverse relationship between the pdr tendencies & the size of the parameters, as predicted. The strength of the relationship increases from the nonstructural to the vertical to the horizontal parameter. An argument is developed that combines the three power parameters to form two ideal power conditions for further research. 8 Tables, 1 Figure. Modified HA.

title: Decentralization and Urban Management
abstract: The process of rapid urbanization in Mexico calls for a broad urban policy program aimed at the decentralization of urban management. A model of participatory decentralization can achieve greater efficiency in the provision of public services while also contributing to the democratization of the state, by redistributing power toward local governments. Adapted from the source document.

title: The End of Postcommunism: Trade Unions in Eastern Europe's Future
abstract: Following a long period in which labor in Eastern Europe had been marginalized, often with unionists' complicity, five conditions now favor revival: survival imperatives of the union bureaucracy, incorporation into the European Union, emerging international solidarity, a new generation of workers, and the end of postcommunism in the firm, or the dismissal of unessential workers. This article focuses on subjective factors: union officials' own misgivings about unions in the postcommunist era and their revived interest now that they no longer need to defend the unskilled. Yet three factors work against union revival: ideological (continued distrust of unions), organizational (plethora of small firms), and structural (location in the global economy). Labor is likely to remain weak, with a few stronger unions emerging that are more elitist, male, "producerist," and less class oriented. Legacies continue to be the major problem, but in a twist, the problem today is the legacy not of communism but of postcommunism. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: ORGANIZATIONAL DOMAINS
abstract: INTANGIBLE CLAIMS TO DOMAIN AFFECT THE BEHAVIOR OF ADMINISTRATIVE BUREAUS. DATA ANALYZED PERTAIN TO 277 CITY, COUNTY, & STATE GOVERNMENT FINANCE AGENCIES, LOCATED IN CITIES WITH A POPULATION OF OVER 50,000. FINANCE DEPT'S WERE SMALLER THAN COMPTROLLER'S OFFICES, 20% OF EMPLOYEES WERE EXPECTED TO HAVE A COLL EDUCATION, & 50% USED COMPUTERS IN 1966. HOW A BUREAU MEDIATES EXTERNAL PRESSURES AFFECTING IT CAN BE USED TO MEASURE THE IMPORTANCE OF ITS CLAIM TO DOMAIN. A NARROW CLAIM IS EASILY PROTECTED--THE OUTPUTS & SERVICES THAT WOULD BE REDUCED IF RESOURCES DECLINED ARE IDENTIFIED. A BROADER CLAIM IMPLIES A DIVERSITY OF CLIENTELE & THE GREATER POSSIBILITY OF DISSATISFACTION. FINANCE DEPT'S TEND TO CONTRACT WITH ENVIRONMENTAL DEMAND AS OTHER AGENCIES TAKE OVER THEIR FUNCTIONS, & ADMINISTRATION DEPT'S GROW WITH DEMAND AS THEY ASSUME GREATER RESPONSIBILITIES. THE MEASURES OF DEMAND ARE: THE SIZE OF THE GENERAL FUND FOR COMMON SERVICES, THE NUMBER OF EMPLOYEES, THE POPULATION SERVED, & TOTALNFUNDS ADMINISTERED. THERE ARE NO EFFECTS OF ENVIRONMENTAL DEMAND ON COMPTROLLERS OFFICES FOR 1972; FOR FINANCE DEPT'S THE IMPACT IS CONSTANTLY NEGATIVE; & FOR ADMINISTRATION DEPT'S, ALL BUT THE POPULATION VARIABLE, ARE SIGNIFICANTLY POSITIVE. BUREAUS CAN JUSTIFY EXPANSION ONLY BY INCREASING THEIR FUNCTIONS, YET THEIR OUTPUTS ARE IMPERFECTLY DEFINED & HARDLY SUBJECT TO MEASUREMENT. ITS OWN CLAIM AS TO WHAT IT IS ACCOMPLISHING IS USUALLY THE MOST IMPORTANT FACTOR IN CAUSING THE GROWTH OF ITS SIZE & RESPONSIBILITIES. THE CONSTANT INFLATION OF CLAIMS GENERATES INTERAGENCY DISPUTES, REPRESENTING AN IMPORTANT BUREAUCRATIC DYSFUNCTION. 9 TABLES, 1 FIGURE. MODIFIED HA.

title: Successor Type and Organizational Change in the Corporate Enterprise
authors: Helmich, Donald L; Brown, Warren B
abstract: This res examines the hyp that corporate org's experiencing inside succession in the office of the president exhibit less org'al change than firms undergoing outside succession. The type of succession is related to a combined measure of org'al change based on position shifts & personnel turnover in the executive role constellation. The res also controls for background effects from 5 potentially confounding variables: org'al size, & admin'ive growth in the industry. Measurable events of the succession process of the org are emphasized, rather than the direct observation of soc org'al patterns that emerge in the executive group itself. The data base is derived from 208 chemical & allied product Corp's which have experienced presidential succession at least once in the 10-yr period of analysis. The analysis of the data using the partial gamma coefficient & a modification of the X2 statistic supports the basic hyp. Modified HA.

title: Assessing Context And Ideology On The Behavior Of Denominational Bureaucrats
abstract: Though the behavior of American congregational clergy has long received scholarly attention, a similar assessment of those in the denominational bureaucracy has languished. I begin to remedy this by testing the usefulness of two dominant theoretical lenses that have proven successful in understanding clergy activity at the congregational level. The first, referred to here as the preference approach, assumes that bureaucratic activity, like that of their congregational counterparts, is largely the result of personal ideology. The second, referred to here as the contextual approach, draws on work that has situated congregational pastors in their larger professional settings to tease out the effects of work groups and community on elite activity. Using data from a recent survey of bureaucrats in the Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.), I find that indicators associated with the contextual approach are more consistent predictors of bureaucratic activity than ideology. This suggests that future studies of denominational bureaucrats should be conducted with an eye toward the contextual realities that these religious elites confront. Adapted from the source document.

title: Social Class and the Bureaucratic Response to Youthful Deviance
abstract: It is argued that: (1) the way SC is defined for youth is changing from simple ascription of status to an "achieved" status defined by educational career; (2) educational careers are important in the generation of deviance & in the bureaucratic response to that deviance; & (3) this process raises some interesting questions when viewed within a Marxist perspective. While previous class origins do have a role to play in the status of students, the perponderant tendency in the "credentialed" society is to make social rank a function of academic achievement. A characteristic of the system is the division into successful & unsuccessful students; good grades, necessary for Coll entry, are the carrot that keeps the system moving. A number of studies indicate that unsuccessful students of manual & nonmanual backgrounds have a high deviance rate. The labeling process is the main element of the bureaucratic response to deviance; it is composed of 2 aspects--those institutions & processes that provide labels about success & legitimacy, & those institutions that are concerned with official illegitimacy (social control agents such as the police, juvenile courts, correctional institutions, & parole). The mental illness interpretation of deviance is disputed by the mass of evidence that it is the result of social forces. Thus the official Marxist response to the problem is questionable. S. Karganovic.

title: Do Women Representatives Regender Legislative Bureaucracy? Assessing the Effect of Representative Sex on Women's Presence among US Congressional Staff
authors: Wilson, Walter Clark; Carlos, Roberto Felix
abstract: Achieving greater female presence in influential positions is a commonly discussed strategy for gender reform in institutions such as the US Congress. Using theory adapted from research on gender in the workplace, this study examines whether women representatives, as 'managers' of congressional offices, alter patterns of gender representation in Congress by hiring and promoting more women staffers compared with men representatives. Cross-sectional logistic regression analyses of staffer sex during the 110th and 111th Congresses (2007-10) reveal a positive relationship between women representatives and female presence on congressional staffs. However, the relationship does not hold with respect to the most influential staff positions. These findings provide only limited support for theories that women representatives act as 'change agents' by directly facilitating opportunities for women, and highlight the importance of exploring alternative strategies for empowering women and regendering legislative institutions. Adapted from the source document.

title: Doing qualitative fieldwork in Cuba: social research in politically sensitive locations
abstract: Cuba, a country that is often portrayed as an isolated, secretive and bureaucratic dictatorship, would appear to present many challenges for a social researcher intent on eliciting the genuine opinions of the native population. However, in December 2008, I began just such an investigation, researching 'environmental justice' (i.e. the social and distributive impacts of environmental policy and practice) in the country, using a mixture of interview and participant observation techniques. As might be expected, much of the fieldwork was dominated by the sensitive political context, creating numerous methodological issues and dilemmas, as well as personal challenges. This paper looks at the difficulties faced, in particular with regard to the problem of attaining reliability and validity, and the strategies that were used to overcome them. It will be of relevance to anyone considering carrying out fieldwork investigations in socialist, and other politically sensitive, locations.

title: The problem of African nationhood
abstract: Much has been said in the last half-century about the artificiality of African borders and the way in which these seemingly random lines on the map fuse culturally and linguistically different groups, while simultaneously dividing real, existing linguistic and cultural communities. While nationalism certainly does exist in African countries, it is by no means the dominant force in political ideology and practice, quite unlike the situation in Europe, in particular, but also other parts of the world. The answer to the question raised by the convenors of this panel, accordingly – why has nationalism not run its course? – is therefore simple in the case of most African countries: nationalism has not run its course in most of Africa simply because it has not caught on the way it did elsewhere. I take nationalism to be a popular ideology according to which the cultural boundaries of a territory should be congruent with the political boundaries (Gellner 1983), and a particular way of imagining an abstract community as being ‘inherently sovereign and limited’ (Anderson 1983). As convincingly argued by Breuilly (1993), the centralised bureaucratic state is essential for nations; it places specific demands on its citizens and offers security and resources in return. With these minimal definitional elements in mind, it is easy to see that the nation comes across as an experiential anomaly to many Africans. Not to all, there are middle classes, civil servants, teachers, intellectuals and idealists in Africa, as elsewhere, who are deeply committed to the idea of the nation, who produce it through their everyday labour and help conjuring it into being at symbolic events such as national days or international football games. However, in the present perspective on nationalism as a popular ideology, the qualifier ‘popular’ is essential. A nation whose faithful adherents are limited to a minority of the population must be upheld by force; it lacks legitimacy, and the ideology justifying it, while nationalist in form, is incapable of instilling trust and loyalty in the citizenry.

title: The Architecture of Collective Intimacy: Masonic Friendships as a Model for Collective Attachments
abstract: Despite a growing recognition that interpersonal friendship informs wider forms of solidarity, there is little systematic analysis as to how community members extend the logic of friendship and intimacy to broader organizational and societal context. Masonic organizational practices provide a useful model for this inquiry. Drawing on an ethnographic study of contemporary Israeli Freemasonry, I examine the intersections of interpersonal, public, and collective intimacy in members' ritual activities and everyday life. The juxtaposition of mundane sociability and Masonic sacred rituals serves to rescale the distance between interpersonal friendship and communal solidarity. As members take on the roles of citizen, bureaucrat, priest, and president concomitantly, they partly collapse the distinctions between personal and collective ties, between the familiar and the revered. These intersections of intimacy are offered as a programmatic research strategy to study how institutionalized patterns of sociability inform civic and national attachments. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Relationship between Political Corruption and Public Investment -- The Case of Croatia
abstract: The goal of this paper is to show possible effects of political corruption on public investment, with special reference to Croatia. At the beginning of the paper the correlation between public investment and corruption in the EU countries is observed. Then the case of Croatia is analyzed, where quality of infrastructure, size of capital public expenditure, irregularities in public procurement, role of government in the construction sector, and effects of political corruption on public capital projects are considered. The paper shows that countries with high public investment have bigger (political) corruption. Despite the high share of public capital expenditure in GDP, Croatia's infrastructure is in a bad state. Judging by the size and the structure of public investment, as well as weak control mechanisms, there are plenty of opportunities for political corruption in Croatian public capital projects, for which there are strong indications that they are being used. Instead of investing in new, highly visible projects, policy makers should direct more attention and money towards maintaining and improving the existing infrastructure, because in Croatia billions of kunas are flowing away. Focusing on fighting political corruption would have significant effects on budget expenditure rationalization and economic growth. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Dilemmas of Contemporary Political Theory in the Conflict between Bureaucracy and Democracy
abstract: This article focuses on the classic theme in contemporary political & administrative theory that represents the contradiction between democracy & bureaucracy. In order to deal with this subject, the study has been divided in three parts: the first discusses the phenomenon of "worldwide bureaucratization" in conceptual terms; the second compares how several authors on contemporary political theory deal with the conflict between bureaucracy & democracy; & the third presents an alternative solution for this contradiction. 25 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Variations in Traditional Marriage and Family Forms: Responses to the Changing Pattern of Family-Based Social Security Systems in Sierra Leone and Kenya
abstract: The functions associated with the European term family do not necessarily belong to any of the multitude of family forms that can be found in African societies. The variety in the formation of different residence, consumption, & production units is illustrated through analysis of the social structure of individual peoples, as well as through interethnic comparisons. Focus here is on differences between various types of social organization of an East vs a West African people (Kenya & Sierra Leone, respectively), analyzing complexities of & changes in family structures in relevant sociopolitical & economic contexts. Also considered is the impact of the introduction of public administration & the commercialization of agriculture on social dynamics & family forms. 34 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Comment on Langton's "Ecological Theory of Bureaucracy"
abstract: Following a summary of John Langton's "The Ecological Theory of Bureaucracy: The Case of Josiah Wedgwood and the British Pottery Industry" (Administrative Science Quarterly, 1984, 29, Sept, 330-354), a behavioral evolutionist account of the development of British bureaucracy, his conclusion that Wedgwood exemplified variation, environment selection as most "fit," & retention of innovations is questioned. An alternative explanation is provided: the state favored the production by large factories of luxury goods for private profit & thus provided resources, including labor. Though these workers produced unprecedented profits for Wedgwood, they did so at the expense of their social & leisure behavior & family time; this is not acknowledged by Langton. His explanation is based on unexamined assumptions about the environmnent & the neglect of social costs. A counterfactual history is presented to illuminate these points of contention, & a caution given against functionalist assumptions & "efficiency" arguments that neglect externalities, ie, the social costs born by those who benefit little from the activity. In Reply to Perrow, John Langton (Westminster Coll, Mo) asserts that Perrow's critique is based on a very one-sided reading. Four broad issues are clarified: the relationship between (1) organizational evolution & environmental structure, (2) social power & bureaucratization, (3) organizational evolution & human progress, & (4) the role of human creativity in organizational evolution & environmental structure. Perrow's hypothetical rewriting of history has little value; rather, the goal of social scientists should be in working toward a more humane direction for the future evolution of bureacracy. 5 References. K. Hyatt

title: Bureaucratic Caesarism: A Gramscian Outlook on the Crisis of Europe
abstract: In 2010, the Eurozone became the epicentre of the world crisis. The vulnerability of Europe appears to be linked to the specific institutional arrangement which organises monetary, financial and budgetary policies within the Eurozone. This article tries to understand the evolution of the euduring a short but decisive historical sequence (2007-12) in a theoretical framework that puts elements of Gramsci's reflections on the theme of crisis, and especially his notion of 'Caesarism', at its centre. It addresses the current debate concerning the relationships between democratic politics and neoliberalism, while focusing on how the radicalisation of the crisis put at stake the co-construction of capitalism and representative democracy in the Western world since wwii.

title: Variables Influencing Same-Sex Domestic Partner Benefits for College and University Faculty and Employees
abstract: The provision of health care benefits by American universities and colleges to employees and their families would seem to be a mundane administrative chore. Controversy arises, though, over the question of extending employee health benefits to other-sex partners of faculty and employees. Many American colleges and universities still do not make such a provision, despite its obvious advantages. These include, among others, both the attraction and the retention of valuable employees. We argue here that the administration of university affairs, including both public and private institutions, is not immune from the effects of state and national culture and politics. We find that region, religion, politics, and race all contribute to the explanation of why some institutions grant health care benefits to other-sex domestic partners of faculty and employees, and others do not. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Bureaucratic Rationality and the Developmental State
abstract: There has been a resuscitation of the view that the state can play an important role in the industrialization process. But, for states to be successful in fostering development, they need a considerable degree of internal cohesiveness, which is generally supplied by the presence of a robust, Weberian bureaucratic corps. This article argues that, while internal cohesiveness is indeed critical, bureaucratic rule following can produce results in the opposite direction, depending on the interagency relations that obtain within the state. The effect of interagency relations is demonstrated through an examination of India & Korea. Both have worked to foster industrialization, & both are endowed with relatively healthy bureaucracies. However, the Indian state was paralyzed & fragmented, while its Korean counterpart did secure the requisite internal coherence. Not only did the culture of rule following fail to generate a cohesive state in India, but it, in fact, worked against such an outcome. 3 Tables, 80 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: BUREAUCRACY AND BRITISH SOCIALISM
abstract: A bureaucracy's function is 'to control, manage, or order administrative regulations or laws in accordance with strict rules and within well-defined jurisdictional areas.' It is defined not in terms of size, but of structure and function. The process of bureaucratization in England is associated economically with the development of capitalism, and politically with the rule of the aristocracy first and then of the UMc. The cause of greater bureaucracy under Labour was the expanded function of government, and the creation of bureaucratic structures to regulate the administration of new services. There is a shift in power relations in favor of the working class; the existing structure and personnel operate so as to hinder social reform. Since civil service has always been closely coordinated with the educational system, the base of recruitment to civil service can be broadened by breaking down the class-biased school system. Non socialists, are sometimes on the boards of new structures created for the operation of nationalized industries. The degree of centralization on the boards has removed authority too far from the field of action. Instead of greater participation by the masses anticipated in theory, the governmental bureaucracy, needed to convert theory into policy, made the line between government and the governed more obvious. As equal opportunity for education and new class and power relations are further realized, the new bureaucracy will become as well adapted and as well accepted as the old civil service. G. Levine.

title: Neopatrimonialism, the Power Elite and Bureaucratic Expansion
abstract: In many Latin American countries, the national government is the key player in making economic, social, & cultural decisions, although the private sector also has some influence. No theoretical framework exists for the predominant social system, where the power elites are not the owners of the means of production, but rather, those controlling the state bureaucracy. The elites maintain some elements of the traditional patrimonialistic order, eg, authoritarian political culture, insecure private property, bureaucratic power structure, & a diffuse borderline between the public & private sectors. Actual modernization occurs in technology & economics, while politics stays partly within the collective behavior patterns dating back to Spanish colonialism. 1 Photograph. Adapted from the source document.

title: THE UNCHANGING BUREAUCRACY
abstract: Modern Japanese bur'cy originated during the Meiji Reform. At that time the admin'ive elite was drawn from the samurai & the aristocrats, so that in spite of centralization of power under the Emperor, the instit'al framework & rigid soc stratification of the feudal period were preserved. In an attempt to imitate Western democratic systems, an elected assembly was set up. Thereafter, a violent struggle for power ensued between the parties & the bur'crats. After 1890, the bur'crats began to infiltrate the parties. Pol'al parties never really gained popular support or confidence, being too corrupt & concerned with selfinterest; thus the bur'cy remained firmly entrenched. Over the yrs a bur'tic mentality has developed, & despite theabolitionof the Meiji Constitution in 1947, change has been very difficult because of the great importance attached to relations with bur'crats as a means to satisfy needs & wants. Among the recommendations of the advisory committee set up in 1962 by the Ikeda gov are: separate pol'al parties from the bur'cy, restrict candidacy of bur'crats for public office, limit the authority of bur'crats in financial matters, esp finance & tax systems, so that subsidies & funds are not dependent on bur'tic consent, & encourage citizens to challenge bur'tic authoritarianism through citizen committees. IPSA.

title: Some Conceptual Issues in Individual and Group-Oriented Strategies of Intervention into Organizations
authors: Hornstein, Harvey A; Bunker, Barbara Benedict; Hornstein, Marion G
abstract: An attempt is made to conceptualize & contrast some of the pyschol'al & sociol'al assumptions underlying 2 diff strategies of soc intervention: an individually oriented strategy which assumed that individual change is the primary mediator of org change & a group-centered strategy which assumes that group-level phenomena, such as norms & values, are the primary mediators of org change. It is not assumed that the views presented are complete or uncontroversial. On the contrary, by articulating these assumptions & their interrelationshi ps, it is possible to begin building systemic conceptual frameworks for describing the dynamics of soc intervention. The understanding of soc process provided by these frameworks may help the theoretician-res'er to be more aware of gaps in his knowledge of soc process. Modified HA.

title: Brasilia: Problematizing the Culture of a City State
abstract: This article discusses aspects of the culture of the Pilot Plan of Brasilia, which is mostly peopled by public servants who work & live there. Elements that help in the understanding of several aspects of the Federal District are explored in the characteristics of the bureaucracy as an analytical category. At the moment of its constitution & during its consolidation, many of those who opted for the city engaged themselves in the ongoing logic. Today it presents, in general, social problems similar to those of the others cities of the country, except for the Pilot Plan itself. This way, spite the fact that it is presented to the nation as an area of exception, this same Pilot Plan, is an excellent laboratory for the understanding of the relationships between urbanism & social practices, standing from a specific socio-professional category. 2 Tables, 23 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: Agenda suprema: interesses em disputa no controle de constitucionalidade das leis no Brasil
abstract: In this paper we discuss the roles that Brazil's Supreme Court (stf) has played while arbitrating interests in dispute in the constitutionality control of laws, through judicial review cases (adis). For this, we rely on quantitative analysis of adis judged by the court between the years 1988 and 2014, mapping the content of the Court's decision-making agenda and the scope of its decisions, determining to what extent the Supreme Court has made a difference in arenas of social and political conflict in the country. We conclude that despite taking part in important disputes in arenas of social and political conflict, Supreme Court's agenda has been taken by issues related to the delineation of public careers, deciding on expansion or restraint of state bureaucracy prerogatives. Among the different roles that the current literature on judicialization of politics has attributed to Supreme Courts around the world, in a scenario of expanding political power of the judiciary, we found out that in Brazil, more than a countermajoritarian institution, or an instance to advance social and collective rights, Supreme Court has played the role of a true corporate deliberation body.

title: The Bureaucracy: Part of Society or Its Contractor?
abstract: English translation (C) 2008 M. E. Sharpe, Inc., from the Russian text (C) 2006 the author. "Biurokratiia: chast' obshchestva ili ego kontragent?" Sotsiologicheskie issledovaniia, 2006, no. 3, pp. 4-8.

title: Sprachplanung in einer Kleinsprache
abstract: RESUMOLingvo-planado en minoritata lingvoLa retoromanca lingvo, parolata de 35'000 personoj en la svisa kantono Grizono, troviĝas en granda dangero, kvankam ĝi ĝuas tre grandaniman moralan kaj fmancan subtenon el tuta Svislando. Granda handikapo por la utih'go de tiu lïngvo por prak-tikaj celoj en la leĝfarado, en administracio, en komerco kaj ec sur afisoj estis gis nun la manko de kornuna skriblingvo por ĉiuj romanĉoj. La topografiaj obstakloj en tiu montara lando, la konfesiaj antagonismoj kaj la manko de ĉefurbo kiel kultura centro kaǔzis, ke kvin diversaj skriblingvoj ekestis kaj evoluis depost la eltrovo de la presarto. Hodiaǔ tiu manko estas pli sentata ol iam. Pro tio la Romanĉa Ligo, kiu estas la supera organo de ciuj romancaj societoj, donis la taskon al profesoro en la universitato de Zurich, Heinrich Schmid, ellabori la gvidlniojn por komuna superregiona skriblingvo, tio, malgraǔ ke pli fruaj individuaj provoj estis malsukcesintaj. En 1982 profesoro Schmid submetis sian lingvoplanon al la Romanĉa Ligo, kiu post malmultaj retusoj akceptis kaj publikigis ĝin. En kvar jaroj tiu nova lingvo bazigante precipe sur la regionaj lingvoj de la malsupera Engadino kaj de la antaua Rejnvalo, trovis multan subtenon kaj jam estas vaste uzata en la praktiko spite al kontraǔstaro de konservemaj rondoj. Posto, ŝtataj instancoj kaj komerco jam utiligas gin, sed la verkistoj ankoraǔ hezitas.
