Tarnen oni rajtas konkludi, ke la. pure eksperimenta fazo jam pasis.SUMMARYLanguage Planning in a Minority LanguageThe Rhaeto-Romansch language, spoken by 35,000 people in the Swiss canton of Grisons, is in great danger, although it enjoys generous moral and financial support from all of Switzerland. Up to now, a major handicap in the use of the language for practical purposes in legislation, administration, commerce, and even in posters and signs has been the lack of a common written language for all forms of Romansch. Topographical obstacles in this mountainous area, coupled with religious antagonisms and the lack of a capital city to serve as a cultural center, have led to the creation and development of five different written forms since the invention of printing. This lack is more acutely felt today than ever before. Accordingly, the Romansch League, the coordinating body of all Romansch societies, commissioned a professor at the University of Zurich, Heinrich Schmid, to develop guidelines for a common written language for all regions, although earlier individual efforts of this kind had failed. In 1982 Professor Schmid presented his language program to the Romansch League, which, after a few minor changes, accepted and published it. Over the past four years this new language, based primarily on the regional languages of the lower Engadine and of the Rhine Valley, has found much support and is already widely used in practice despite opposition in conservative circles. The postal service, government agencies, and business are already using it, but there is some hesitation among literary figures. It is reasonable to conclude, however, that the purely experimental phase of the project is now over.

title: The Interface of Globalization and Peripheral Land in the Cities of the South: Implications for Urban Governance and Local Economic Development
abstract: This essay examines the impact of globalization on land peripheral to large cities of the south. It identifies such land as providing major arenas for contested claims between the requirements of international firms and those of local inhabitants and businesses, entailing both threats and opportunities in terms of local economic development. Much depends on the urban governance and institutional processes surrounding the use and allocation of land that are themselves directly influenced by the globalization process. In many cities national, state or provincial governments have set up special parastatal organizations with substantial funding and significant decision-making powers over infrastructure development and land use to facilitate the rebirth of their cities as havens for international investment. In the process local municipalities and the local population are often excluded from the decision-making process, while being left to cope with the aftermath and maintenance of the grand projects. The essay identifies weaknesses in elite governance models usually centred at the state or national levels, and asks if a better alternative may be a local government-led 'inclusive leadership' model capable of clear leadership, greater coordination of different governance layers and inclusion of local actors. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: The Clash between Segmental Organizations and Governmental Bureaucracies
abstract: Segmentation is a type of managerial organization based on a loose, flexible structure. An ideal-typical model of segmentation is presented to help supply information for this often neglected organizational form. Segmental organization is characterized by: (1) professional groupings exerting a strong influence on internal DofL; (2) authority based on personalities & tradition; & (3) labor relations patterns deviating widely from the norms in other types of organizations. In the Netherlands, clashes often arise between the governmental bureaucracy & segmental service agencies, leading to unnecessary escalation of conflicts, ineffective cooperation, & unreasonable behavior. Both sides would probably profit from participant feedback, especially from segmental organizations. 2 Tables. Modified HA.

title: Feminists, Spirituality, and the Twelve Steps of Alcoholics Anonymous
abstract: Today, women in our society engage in many roles. It is not uncommon for a woman to find herself in the position of daughter, sister, mother, grandmother, and significant other or spouse, all at the same time. Concurrently, she may also be a friend, an employee, and a professional. Superimposed on all of these roles, a Woman may also be recovering from alcoholism or another addiction as well as being an adult child of an alcoholic or a codependent. It can be overwhelming to experience the infrastructure of wants, needs, desires, expectations, commitments, and predispositions that face women who are in the recovery process from chemical dependency.For a complete reprint of this article contact Haworth Press by telephone (1-800-HAWORTH) or EMAIL (getinfo@haworthpressinc.com). Article copyright The Haworth Press, Inc.

title: "In the Corridors of Power": How the Animal Movement Changed Australian Politics, 1979-1991
abstract: Foreshadowed by the anti-war cause, women's and gay liberation struggles, and the conservation movement, and inspired by Peter Singer's 1975 book Animal Liberation, a fresh wave of animal activism emerged in Australia in the mid-seventies. In the struggle for animal rights, campaigners used a range of methods, but what characterised the eighties was their lobbying. They engaged politicians, built alliances, and participated in the state. By doing so, they changed Australian politics: they extended the political agenda; influenced public policy; and reshaped the state bureaucracy to include new avenues for addressing animal protection. At the same time, their outcomes were limited, sometimes founded on compromise and failure. The property status of animals was a fundamental constraint that produced differentiated and contradictory policy outcomes. The degree to which the animal movement succeeded in reducing animal suffering is a contentious matter that divides minimalist and maximalist accounts. Ultimately, however, animal advocates were instrumental in advancing the basic animal protection framework evident in Australia today.

title: Social expenditures and public administration: are local social assistance costs in Sweden a matter of organisation?
abstract: Minas R. Social expenditures and public administration: are local social assistance costs in Sweden a matter of organisation?Int J Soc Welfare 2010: 19: 215--224. Adapted from the source document.

title: Size and the Structure of Organizations: A Causal Analysis
abstract: Causal relationships among the following 4 parameters of org'al structure are examined: size, number of major subunits (divisions), number of levels of hierarchy, & number of supervisors in an org. Data describing 194 city, county, & state Dept's of finance in 1966 & 1971 are used in a path analysis of causal relationships. Support is found for the following assertions: (1) The effects of size on the other 3 org'al parameters are ubiquitous. (2) Causality is unidirectional; other parameters of org have almost no effect on size. No substantial paths were found between earlier measurements of number of subunits & levels & the later measurements of size. (3) The effects of size are greatest on parameters which managers can most easily manipulate. (4) Apparent relationships among parameters other than size vanish when size is controlled. 1 Table, 5 Figures. Modified HA.

title: NOTES ON THE CONTROL AND RESPONSIBILITY OF THE BUREAUCRAT
abstract: Definitions of bur'tic responsibility in a democratic pol'al system are given in terms of (1) 'accountability' in the sense of answerability to controls & organs external to the bur'crat; (2) responsiveness, in the sense of awareness of & deference to the prevailing values, opinions, & sentiments of the society which the bur'crat serves; & (3) explicability, in the sense of adherence to certain sci'fic or professional principles in carrying out one's assignments. The bur'crat may not rely solely upon accountability, since sometimes he will have to decide for himself what it is the public wants. Many O's have urged that bur'tic personnel be specially recruited & trained to exercise this discretionary authority, but no agreement exists as to the extent to which responsiveness should be emphasized in a democratic gov in order to secure a responsible bur'cy. Herman Finer, for example, has stressed the primary importance of securing the accountability of bur'crats through pol'al controls, while Carl J. Friedrich suggests that increasing reliance may have to be placed on responsiveness. Responsibility in terms of explicability, according to C. J. Friedrich & John Gaus, may be secured through the bur'crats' professional code of ethics & through sci'fic standards of public admin. Explicability seems at best auxiliary to accountability & responsiveness, however. Modified Author's Summary.

title: Gender, Social Control and Community Services
abstract: Gender dimensions of social control are explored in a case study of a state welfare bureaucracy in Victoria, Australia. Analysis of interview data obtained from clients (N = 694) reveals that Ms were associated with the correctional side of the department while Fs were involved with a range of activities generally associated with the maternal role. All Rs lived in the community & were serviced by the same staff & facilities. Very clear differences along traditional lines emerge, highlighting the centrality of the gender dimension for understanding the social control mechanisms of the welfare state. 4 Tables, 67 References. Modified HA

title: The Politics of Accountability in Australian Education
authors: Cuttance, Peter; Harman, Grant; Macpherson, Reynold J S; Pritchard, Alan; Smart, Don
abstract: Australia's State Education Dept & the public school systems for which it is responsible have largely succeeded -- seemingly to a greater degree than their counterparts in the US & UK -- in insulating themselves from harsher forms of centralized educational accountability, eg, state testing & school performance comparisons. Explored here are the politics of this phenomenon, which seem inextricably tied to the peculiarities of Australian federalism & the remarkable historical dominance of education bureaucrats (& ministers) controlling strongly centralized state education departments. The inability of the four case study states to implement or sustain proposed major statewide school accountability processess is attributed to powerful teachers' unions, postelection government change, &, perhaps predominantly, fear by entrenched senior state education bureaucrats (& ministers) that accountability processes & outcomes might produce unwanted scrutiny (from federal government, the public, or others), loss of control, & embarrassment to themselves. 39 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: THE BUREAUCRATIZATION OF POLICYMAKING IN POSTWAR JAPAN
abstract: NUMEROUS PRIMARY & SECONDARY SOURCES ARE EXAMINED TO ASSESS BUREAUCRATIC PENETRATION OF THE POLICYMAKING PROCESS IN POSTWAR JAPAN (FROM ABOUT 1945 TO 1971). 4 SPECIFIC INDICATORS ARE EXAMINED. THE DECLINING ROLE OF THE DIET AS AN INDEPENDENT LEGISLATIVE ORGAN IS SHOWN BY THE INCREASING SUCCESS RATES OF GOVERNMENT SPONSORED BILLS, THE DECLINING RATE OF AMENDMENTS ADDED BY THE DIET, & THE LACK OF SUCCESS OF OPPOSITION-SPONSORED BILLS. BECAUSE OF STRONG LINKS BETWEEN THE RULING LIBERAL DEMOCRATIC PARTY & THE BUREAUCRACY, OPPOSITION & SPONSORSHIP OF ALTERNATIVE LEGISLATION IN THE DIET HAVE BECOME INCREASINGLY DIFFICULT. A 3RD SOURCE OF POWER WITHOUT DEMOCRATIC CONTROL IS THE BUREAUCRACY'S FUNCTION OF PROVIDING TECHNICAL INTERPRETATION OF LAWS THROUGH ORDINANCES & OFFICIAL COMMUNICATIONS. BUREAUCRATIC INFLUENCE OVER SUPPOSEDLY TECHNICAL, NONPARTISAN ADVISORY COMMITTEES HAS INCREASED MARKEDLY BECAUSE BUREAUCRACIES CONTROL THE AREAS OF INVESTIGATION, THE MANNER OF RESEARCH, REPORT-WRITING, & MEMBERSHIP COMPOSITION OF THE COMMITTEES. ALL 4 INDICATORS SHOW A STRONG & GROWING ROLE FOR THE BUREAUCRACY & ATTEST TO THE INSTITUTIONAL BASES OF BUREAUCRATIC POWER IN JAPAN. 2 TABLES, 1 FIGURE. MODIFIED HA.

title: BUREAUCRACY IN AN IMMOBILIST SOCIETY: THE CASE OF COSTA RICA
abstract: A brief ecological study of burley in an econ'ly underdeveloped country, Costa Rica. Data from a questionaire admin'ed to 52 bur'crats in 2 agencies of the public administration are presented & 3 preliminary hyp's are outlined: (1) If a strong modern party is established, this does not necessarily lead to the development of a society nor to pol'al control of the admin'ive process. (2) If pol in a transitional society are immobilist, then the public administration will also be immobilized. (3) If the ideal type model dichotomizing pol & administration is assumed, it will be found no more relevant in Costa Rica & possibly in other transitional societies than it is in analyses of the econ'ly developed societies. Modified HA.

title: The challenge of self-sufficiency: Women on welfare redefining independence
abstract: Drawing on interviews conducted with fifty-one single mothers in a rural state, this article explores how women who rely on state assistance sustain a belief in their own self-worth. The article first shows that single mothers hold firmly to the value of self-sufficiency. It then shows that they can hold to that value because they believe that their welfare reliance is different from that of other women and because they redefine independence to allow for acts that might normally be understood to challenge that norm. The findings are compared to those in other studies that cover some of the same issues. The discussion draws on three levels of context for interpreting the findings: the current discourse concerning single mothers and, more specifically, welfare recipients; the client stance that develops among those who deal with bureaucracies; and, finally, the interview situation itself.

title: Romantic bureaucracy: Alexander Kojève's post-historical wisdom
abstract: Alexandre Kojeve became famous primarily for his discourse on the end of history and the post-historical condition -- the discourse that he developed in his seminar on Hegel's Phenomenology of the Spirit at the Ecole des Hautes Etudes in Paris between 1933 and 1939. This seminar was regularly attended by leading figures of French intellectual life at that time, such as Georges Bataille, Jacques Lacan, Andre Breton, Maurice Merleau-Ponty and Raymond Aron. The transcripts of Kojeve's lectures circulated in Parisian intellectual circles and were widely read there, by Sartre and Camus among others. The end of history as it is understood by Kojeve is, of course, not the end of historical processes and events. Rather, Kojeve believed that history is not merely a chain of events but has a telos, and that this telos can be achieved, and actually is already achieved. According to the Platonic--Hegelian tradition in which Kojeve situated his discourse, this telos is wisdom. Kojeve understands wisdom as perfect self-transparency, self-knowledge.

title: Between vigilantism and bureaucracy: Improving our understanding of police work in Nigeria and South Africa
abstract: To date, much of the analytical scholarship on policing in Africa has centred on non-state actors. In doing so, it risks neglecting state actors and statehood, which must be understood on their own terms as well as through the eyes of the people they supposedly serve. This article seeks to develop our theoretical and empirical understanding in this respect by exploring the contexts in which citizens seek to engage state police in Nigeria and South Africa. In doing so it highlights three particularly important uses that police contact may serve, that are currently being overlooked. State police can permit, authorize or limit crime control performed by others through informal regulatory intervention. They can exercise a unique bureaucratic power by opening a case which is valued as a record of right and wrongs to be used in the negotiation of everyday life, not simply as a means to legal prosecution. And finally, taking action 'off the books', the police can exercise a coercive power that can be termed 'police vigilantism', which citizens May try to harness for their own ends. We therefore argue that we should recognize the continued high public demand for the services of state police forces even in contexts where they fall short of expectations, and more closely analyse the ways in which people utilize and help to reproduce the police forces they condemn.

title: Who had an occupation? Changing Boundaries in Historical U.S. Census Data
abstract: The original official purpose of the U.S. Census was to gather information to design political districts of approximately the same size. Increasingly Census data has been used for descriptive and social scientific purposes. This paper examines how the category of "occupation" has changed and looks at several issues which arise in comparing the present day workforce with the workforce in past decades. Changes in concepts, practices, and historical context have greatly affected how many persons were recorded as having occupations, especially for married women, American Indians, teenagers, and people who have ceased paid work. Adapted from the source document.

title: La dimensión relacional del gobierno abierto y el liderazgo colaborativo
abstract: En este articulo se explica la dimension relacional del gobierno abierto, que implica innovación gubernamental sustentada en saberes cívicos, construcción de políticas públicas en red y visión de la gobernanza como nueva forma de gobernar. Se parte de un análisis teórico-conceptual del gobierno abierto y el liderazgo colaborativo, respondiendo a las preguntas: ¿qué rasgos y competencias debe tener un líder público gubernamental en contextos de gobiernos abiertos-relacionales? y ¿con qué saberes cívicos contarían los funcionarios públicos en su relación con los actores no gubernamentales? Se concluye que la gestión pública está hecha del compromiso de los funcionarios públicos y ciudadanos con el Gobierno, facilitando la inteligencia cívica, el control de la gestión vía la contraloría social, así como una concepción compartida de lo público, y que las competencias de la colaboración, lo interactivo y el emprendedurismo son hoy fundamentales para la gestión pública.

title: On the Federal Scene
abstract: Four significant US federal-level activities in 1989 that are expected to impact future mental health administration are examined: (1) the State Comprehensive Mental Health Services Plan Act requires the provision of case management services & outreach to seriously mentally ill individuals receiving public funds or services, social services to homeless mentally ill, & rehabilitation, employment, housing, medical, & other support to the severely mentally ill. (2) The National Instit of Mental Health (NIMH) initiated five new research centers to investigate the organization & financing of care for the severely mentally ill, with the goal of improving long-term care in the public sector. (3) The Nursing Home Reform Act requires states to divert mentally ill persons from nursing homes to community residential care & treatment. (4) The NIMH established a program for in-service training in mental health administration. 6 References. S. G. Yates

title: Politicization of Bureaucracy: A Framework for Measurement
abstract: The idea that bureaucracy is a 'rational' & 'depoliticized' instrument in the conduct of public affairs, has recently come under severe criticism. Assuming the inevitable trend towards 'politicization', modern bureaucracies can possibly be classified into 4 different categories: 'depoliticized', 'semipoliticized', 'committed', & 'fully-politicized'. Such a classification is based on the operationalization of certain indices on 4 different dimensions viz (1) degree of bureaucracy's influence in decision making, (2) degree of its involvement in political activities, (3) degree of political interference in its work, & (4) its image in the public. The extent of 'politicization' of any bureaucratic system & its actual deviation from the defined categories will, however, depend upon the available pattern of the characteristic indices in that particular society. Notwithstanding certain difficulties in the operationalization of such indices, the model should be helpful in providing a framework for a comparative analysis & measurement of 'politicization' of bureaucracies in different political systems. The concept of a 'politicized' bureaucracy is defined as one which is involved or influences or is influenced to any degree, consciously or unconsciously, by overt or by implicit actions in the stream of the politics of the day whether of the party in power or of the party/parties in opposition. Such an involvement may mean the bureaucratic promotion of special interests of political party at the expense of national objectives. In a more extended form it may also be regarded as a type of bureaucracy which uses political parties in furtherance of their collective or individual objectives. An attempt is made to show that the Indian bureaucracy is fast loosing its neutral character & might show a deviation towards the 'politicized' model. AA.

title: Rules and Roles vs. Consensus: Self-Governed Deliberative Mass Collaboration Bureaucracies
authors: Joyce, Elisabeth; Pike, Jacqueline C; Butler, Brian S
abstract: Deliberative mass collaboration systems, such as Wikipedia, are characterized as undisciplined, unstructured social spaces where individuals participate in collective action. However, examination of Wikipedia reveals that it contains a bureaucratic structure, which ensures that collective goals are primary drivers of that collective action. To support large-scale activity, deliberative mass collaboration systems must provide ways of reconciling the tension between individual agency and collective goals. Wikipedia's unusual policy, ignore all rules (IAR), serves as this tension release mechanism. IAR supports individual agency when positions taken by participants might conflict with those reflected in established rules. Hypotheses are tested with Wikipedia data regarding individual agency, bureaucratic processes, and IAR invocation during the content exclusion process. Findings indicate that in Wikipedia each utterance matters in deliberations, rules matter in deliberations, and IAR citation magnifies individual influence but also reinforces bureaucracy. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Inc., copyright holder.]

title: The Hungarian Source
abstract: The Hungarian Revolution of 1956 has a significance which has been largely concealed by left-wing intellectuals since its occurrence. Modern society is best understood as bureaucratic capitalism, best exemplified by Russia & China. The Hungarian Revolution was the only total revolution so far against bureaucratic capitalism. Polish, Czech & Yugoslavian movements, much less radical, have been more admired as allowing proletarians to identify with the workers' state. In Hungary, a genuine revolution took place, embodying the historical & social experience of the Hungarian people. It produced the institution of a new order centered on the Councils created by the workers; the basis of these councils was the requirement that the entire collectivity makes decisions, with delegates serving only between meetings of the General Assembly. This can be contrasted to the mystification embodied in the Yugoslav workers' councils, which exist within the framework of a separate state apparatus. The Hungarian pattern destroyed the structure of hierarchy. The central problem ignored by Marxism was the capacity of society to maintain its unity without creating an autonomous state apparatus. The Hungarian councils & networks represent a solution to this problem, one which breaks out of the limitations of Marxist theory. W. H. Stoddard.

title: Policy Outputs and Bureaucracy: The Roles of Need, Demand, and Agency Structure
abstract: The effect of bureaucratic structure on policy adoption is investigated relative to noise abatement policies of all publicly owned air carrier airports in the US. Data were gathered through a 1972 survey involving questionnaires sent to airport managers or chief executives (N = 139 Rs). A study of need & demand variables reveals that noise abatement policies are shaped by public demand & community needs. Internal, administrative, & executive characteristics of the policy-making unit, controlling for the need/demand variable, indicate that the presence of a legal staff & expenditure autonomy are the only structural factors facilitating policy outputs at local airports. These factors, however, are considered as falling under the rubric of need & demand. Findings indicate that the structure of the bureaucracy has little effect on policy outputs, after controlling for the impact of community needs & political demands. 3 Tables, 34 References. D. Graves.

title: AIDS, Public Health and Drug Policy Autonomy or Dependency?
abstract: Brazilian policy on AIDS stands as a "model" whose originality stems from the production of generic drugs for facilitating all patients' access to treatments & therapies. This model, elaborated within state bureaucracies, has been inspired by the "sanitary" movement which emerged in 1970's, with an aim at promoting health as a fundamental human right that must be guaranteed by the state. Brazilian policy on AIDS has also been highlighted for the transformations it has brought about in the relations between national industry & large multinational pharmaceutical firms. Drawing upon in-depth interviews with various actors who have played strategic roles within Brazilian health system & economic bureaucracy from 1960's onwards, we will display the multiple interactions between public health policy, war on AIDS, & drug policy. We will notably examine the complex configurations within which the issue of autonomy versus dependence of Brazilian pharmaceutical industry has been raised. Adapted from the source document.

title: Problems of Bureaucracy and Democracy in the Functioning of a Capitalist State
abstract: Proposed is a theoretical model for anaylsis of historical changes in the capitalist political system. M. Weber's ideotypical framework is modified; when brought closer to reality, the distinction between parliament & bureaucracy begins to disappear. Discussed are the interests of the ruling class vis-a-vis state administration (M. Weber, K. Mannheim, A. Etzioni, R. Bendix, S. M. Lipset, M. Crozier, & C. W. Mills). Changing relationships between state & society are outlined, with emphasis on the works of R. Dahrendorf, H. Marcuse, & D. Riesman. Stressed is the importance of diverting social attention from real issues, thus making politics into administration, & social reality into an area of tactics & management. I. Irwin-Zarecka.

title: Bureaucracy and State Powers
abstract: Examines the interest of bureaucracy in obtaining power. States that Russians have a dual attitude toward bureaucracy: On the one hand, they believe that the Russian state bureaucracy has gained excessive power, but on the other hand, that a strong state is not possible without officials & experienced specialists. Informs that Russians believe that the nation's slow economic development is due to unification of oligarchs & the ruling elite. Concludes that in the popular opinion, state government should be responsible for limiting the power of the bureaucracy. Tables, Figures. K. Duft

title: Nationalities Problems in the Soviet Union: A Crisis of Institutions or a Crisis of Values?
abstract: Examined is the extent to which representatives of the old command administrative system (ie, Stalinist bureaucratic structure) are preventing the creation of stable, Western-style, democratic institutions in the former USSR. It is argued that these representatives are attempting to create a niche for themselves in the new political culture of the USSR by embracing populist ideals. Their success in doing so is explained by (1) the working class origins of the Stalinist bureaucracy in the late 1920s, & (2) the fact that the official Soviet ideology traditionally has incorporated elements of both "official populism" & "direct democracy" to cover up the bureaucratic nature of the state. It is concluded that continued populist & nationalist mobilization will preclude the development of stable democratic political institutions & will engender a stalemate in Soviet society. W. Howard

title: Layered bureaucracy and the construction of subjectivities: Interpretive dimensions of the research approval process
abstract: Institutional controls and legal enmeshments have become increasingly problematic for social scientists in recent years. For sociologists, whose disciplinary ethic is defined by rigid standards of confidentiality and admonishments to “do no harm”, the dilemma appears to be one of accepting legislative protections based on the natural science model of good science or enduring the consequences of compelled disclosure of data and participant identities in court. Some critical and interpretive sociologists offer a third option — a return to a moral framework for the discipline, one that focuses on the ways power and ideology influence institutions.In this paper, I examine how street-level politics and the enmeshment of the scientific paradigm within the various contributing (layered) bureaucracies influence the shape of university research and challenge the ideal of a moral framework. I use personal experience to demonstrate how subjectivities, or narrative identities, are continuously negotiated and redefined during the research approval process to produce bureaucratic acceptability, scientific legitimacy, and legal accountability. The analysis has broader implications as it demonstrates how the biases that equate good sociology with scientific method can ultimately shape research decisions and create additional challenges for those who seek to change the discipline

title: Max Weber's Treatise on the Chinese Bureaucracy
abstract: Abstract not available at this time.

title: Control Theory in Brazilian Organizations
authors: Farris, George F; Butterfield, D Anthony
abstract: Distribution of control is examined in 16 Brazilian development banks using A. S. Tannenbaum's control graph model (see SA 0624/D4994). Participants in the study were 25 presidents & directors, 51 dept chiefs, 43 technical supervisors, & 156 technical personnel from 16 banks. All were involved in the development loan program. Contrary to the common assumption that Latin Amer org's are authoritarian, control in these org's is distributed evenly among hierarchical levels. Total control, control by upper hierarchical levels, & control by the nat'l bank in the state-federal system are all associated with bank effectiveness. Bank effectiveness is esp associated with each level's control in that phase of project decision making for which it is most responsible. A competence hyp viewing effective development banks as technocracies is suggested to explain these findings. Modified HA.

title: BUREAUCRACY AND CHARISMA IN GHANA
abstract: Max Weber's hypothesis re the necessity for charisma to be routinized was tested in a study of the Ghanaian higher Civil Service in 1960-61. Historical res was followed by 100 interviews with senior bur'crats, Ministers, MP's, party functionaries, & businessmen. A requirement for the routinization of charisma was that the anti-econ character of charismatic leadership subsidy & a regular & predictable org furnish the funds & skills necessary for manag of a community no longer experiencing the unsettled soc conditions which facilitated the emergence of a charismatic leader. At the time of the study various changes occurred in Ghanaian gov which appeared to support the proposition. The shift to Republican from Prime Ministerial gov in 1960 accelerated a process of withdrawal of power from Ministers & Ministries & extending it to Secretariats responsible to the President's Office & staffed & controlled by civil servants. At the same time the President sharply disciplined politicians & removed from office 2 senior Ministers & 5 prominent politicians; 4 Ministers & 2 Regional Commissioners were required to return illegally accumulated goods to the State. An 'admin'ive' rather than 'pol'al' budget in 1961 led to the 1st major demonstrations against K. Nkrumah's gov but also implied for influential civil servants that the President intended to focus upon ED by employing the trained skills of civil servants rather than the skills of politicians. Among higher civil servants, there was somewhat increased confidence & enhanced morale; among politicians considerable uncertainty & resentment, which had not formerly been as clearly articulated & expressed by members of the governing party. If this process was an attempt at routinization of charisma at the admin'ive & pol'al levels, it was accompanied by enhanced ritualization of the President's Office to clarify what is called 'the charisma of embodiment,' possibly an attempt to maintain Presidential links with the pop with less dependence on pol'al intermediaries. It is concluded that Weber's proposition about routinization was accurate in general, & that the Civil Service in Ghana may have been the agents of incipient or apparent routinization until early 1964. AA.

title: State
abstract: The author summarizes studies treating the theory of the state that have been published in the journal 'Social Text.' NBStudies have characterized the new arrangements of sovereignty found in states of the post-cold-war age of empire. NBThey advocate for more research into the workings of political parties in alter-globalization movement building and other projects that counter the imperialistic motives of hegemonic states. NBPopular movements around the world have placed these anti-imperial ideas into practice by reclaiming privatized resources and industries from state management. Adapted from the source document.

title: The British and French Representatives to the Communist International, 1920-1939: A Comparative Survey
abstract: This article employs a prosopographical approach in examining the backgrounds & careers of those cadres who represented the Communist Party of Great Britain & the Parti Communiste Francais at the Comintern headquarters in Moscow. In the context of the differences between the two parties, it discusses the factors which qualified activists for appointment, how they handled their role, & whether their service in Moscow was an element in future advancement. It traces the bureaucratization of the function, & challenges the view that these representatives could exert significant influence on Comintern policy. Within this boundary the fact that the French representatives exercised greater independence lends support, in the context of centre -- periphery debates, to the judgement that within the Comintern the CPGB was a relatively conformist party. 4 Tables, 3 Figures. Adapted from the source document.

title: Empathy and Its Importance in Long-Term Home Health Care
abstract: Describes the development & socialization of empathy, its relation to altruistic behaviors, & its role in psychotherapy & long-term home health care. The major theoretical perspectives on empathy & its antecedents are described. It is asserted that a bureaucratic health care system decreases the ability of home health care providers to respond empathetically to their patients. The bureaucracy surrounding home health care must be minimized, & health care providers must be trained to appreciate their patients' inner experience from their own frames of reference. 33 References. M. Nichols-Wagner

title: Linking State and Self: How the Japanese State Bureaucratizes Subjectivity through Moral Education
abstract: Investigates how a discourse (advocating hierarchy, sociopolitical categorization, & standardization) reproduces the rationalizing operations of Japan's politicoeconomic elite, serving the state by reproducing its ideology through "moral education" at local sites (schools). In Japan, state bureaucratic structures try to build a psychology that hierarchizes, categorizes, & formalizes the sociopolitical environment, thereby supporting an economic rationality demanded by economic nationalism. After describing the sociopolitical context of Japan's statist economic-nationalist ideology that drives a bureaucratizing discourse, a collection of teacher's guidebooks published by the Ministry of Education is examined as the primary target of discourse analysis. Shown is how the state turns its objectives into subjective truths or, more specifically, how convictions in elite economic interests are reproduced through a discourse that is often explained as traditional or somehow "natural" to being Japanese. 65 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Nature of Bureaucratic Knowledge
abstract: Richard reviews Instituting Nature: Authority, Expertise, and Power in Mexican Forests by Andrew S. Mathews.

title: THE CONCEPT OF POWER IN ELITE AND PLURALIST THEORIES
abstract: This article analyses and compares the concept of power in elite and pluralist theories, particularly the work of Michels and that of the pluralists Lindblom and Woodhouse, with the aim of considering how power is interpreted within these theories. While elite theories emphasise the central role of the elite in shaping political change, pluralist theories oppose elite theories and do not attribute such a significant role to the elite. A comparison of elite and pluralist views on the issue of power consolidation, however, shows a basic assumption underlying the two bodies of work: for both, power is concentrated in the hands of the ruling elite, which is stable and which is slowly renewed with new members. Via direct or indirect assimilation, the ruling elite absorbs those connected with strategic state resources (military, economic, and so forth), and maintains its integrity and unity by, for instance, integrating opponents into state bureaucracy structures, or through the use of force, or assimilation or the creation of internal closure via internal rotation. Those not belonging to the elite - poor, marginal actors - are disconnected from the realisation of their interests. Adapted from the source document.

title: The IntelCities e-Learning Platform, Knowledge Management System and Digital Library for Semantically-Rich e-Governance Services
authors: Deakin, Mark; Allwinkle, Sam; Campbell, Fiona; Jesurethnam, Jose Prabhu
abstract: The paper examines the architecture and services of the e-learning platform and describes how the knowledge management system designed for IntelCities is supported by the IPs digital library. It suggests the e-Learning platform, knowledge management system and digital library developed under the IP provides the intelligence cities need to integrate them as a platform of semantically-rich e-Governance services. That is to say, an integrated platform of semantically rich e-Governance services with the intelligence which cities need to meet the expectations citizens have about the quality of such electronically enhanced products. The paper begins by outlining the integrated model of electronically enhanced governance (eGov) services adopted to represent the front-end, middleware and back-office functions of the IntelCities e-Learning, knowledge management (KM) and digital library. Having done this, the paper shall report on the search for an intelligent solution to the IPs learning needs, knowledge transfer and capacity building requirements. It shall then go on to discuss the information technology (IT) underlying the solution adopted by the IP to integrate the electronically enhanced eGov services hosted on the eCity platform with the legacy systems operated by the public administrations involved in the project. From here the discussion shall then go on to examine how the e-Learning platform, KM system and digital library developed by the IP as back-office functions have been integrated into the IntelCities middleware and delivered as frontend services to citizens. Adapted from the source document.

title: A Systemic Approach to Improving the Engagement of Fathers in Child Safeguarding
authors: Scourfield, Jonathan; Smail, Pat; Butler, Dan
abstract: Increasing the involvement of fathers in child safeguarding is an issue which has seen relatively little practice innovation in mainstream services. This article concerns a bold attempt to improve practice in this domain through a systemic approach. Key findings are presented from an evaluation of a Fatherhood Institute project in six English local authorities. The intervention was positively received and the self-efficacy of children's services staff improved on most measures as a result of training. However, not all planned aspects of the project could be implemented. The article reflects on the challenge of achieving practice change in these areas - both child safeguarding and engaging fathers - where established practices are deep-rooted. There is also reflection on the challenge of public service innovation in a context of austerity. title: Recognition and Legitimisation of Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity (SOGI) at the UN: A Critical Systemic Analysis
authors: Mulé, Nick J; McKenzie, Cameron; Khan, Maryam
abstract: The UN often plays a progressive role in challenging oppressive policies and laws globally from a human rights perspective. Since approximately 2005, there has been increased LGBTQI rights recognition within various UN bodies such as: the Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC), the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), the Security Council, UN Women and Special Rapporteurs. Despite such achievements, these UN bodies often experience challenges in legitimising such recognition of LGBTQI individuals and communities. This paper critically analyses the effectiveness and relevance of UN bodies in addressing and advocating for progressive and equitable policies related to LGBTQI people through examination of the following: LGBTQI advocacy at the UN; internal bureaucracies of the UN and their affiliates that interfere with LGBTQI rights; and the role of member states. A critical social work lens frames the paper based on a queer liberation perspective, which is inclusive of sexual and gender diversities beyond dominant heterosexual and binaristic constructions (Mulé, 2008, 2012). Such perspectives contribute to resisting and challenging norms that make static the identities, recognition and legitimisation of LGBTQI at the UN.

title: Povratak „dvorskoj nauci”? – Ka konsekvencijalističkom promišljanju budućnosti etnologije / sociokulturne antropologije u Republici Srbiji i Republici Hrvatskoj
abstract: ""] Ako kolektivne kulturne identitete i identitetske nauke posmatramo kao nematerijalno kulturno nasleđe, prelazak s kulturno-kritičkih pozicija (zasnovanih na konstruktivističkom antiesencijalizmu) na konsekvencijalističke pozicije (zasnovane na primenjenom esencijalizmu) se, kontraintuitivno, ispostavlja kao ostvarivanje liberalnih ciljeva konzervativnim sredstvima. Istraživanje i zaštita kulturnog nasleđa refokusiraju esencijalizaciju kultura s pojedinačnih građana i etnokonfesionalno atribuiranih populacija na apstraktne „elemente kulture”, objedinjujući time naučne i društvene ciljeve antropologije. U članku se predlaže promišljanje strategije „povratka etnologiji” kao „dvorskoj nauci” – instrumentalizacija instrumentalizma, odnosno saradnja s međunarodno podstaknutom i obavezanom državnom administracijom pri sklanjanju kolektivnog identiteta iz javnosti u tematske parkove ili natrag u vitrine.

title: Opening Windows to Gender: A Case Study in a Major International Population Agency
abstract: This article presents the experience of the International Planned Parenthood Federation, Western Hemisphere Region, as an example of the social transformation of the family planning paradigm into model interventions in sexual & reproductive health. This is framed within the literature on gender & bureaucracies to assess the strategies & limitations followed when gender perspectives are institutionalized. 1 Table, 41 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Administration of New Fiscal Populism
abstract: Mayor Harold Washington committed Chicago (Ill) to fiscally responsible policies within the severe constraints of an era of austerity. Yet the administration's goals of assisting minorities & the disadvantaged were clear. It is suggested that fiscal austerity combined with socially liberal policies defined a new fiscal populist approach to administration as illustrated by several examples of innovative policies. HA

title: Lying the Truth; Practices of Confession and Recognition
abstract: Italy’s 1998 Immigration Law 40 includes Article 18, which allows foreign “victims of human trafficking” the right to temporary residence permits on the condition that they participate in a rehabilitation program. The first step of this program, the act of denuncia, is to file criminal charges against exploiters at the police station. However, the resulting testimony cannot be understood through the victim/agent trope of the bureaucratic state, which uses these categories to make the other understandable through a process of what I call “confessional recognition.” In this article, I show how, despite the proliferation of biometric technologies to identify foreign others and so control migration flows at borders, confessional practices continue to play a central role in deciding who is admitted legally. Moreover, I illustrate how the question of redemption and expiation is not only a crucial issue for Catholic groups involved in aid programs for foreigners but is also central to Italian state integration policies, thus revealing how juridical norms are deeply influenced by the vocabulary of religious morality and vice versa.

title: Zwischen Akten und Zetteln Notizen zu Literatur und Bürokratie/Between files and notes: Notes on literature and bureaucracy
abstract: Insights into the administrative daily life and sociological sketches by and about civil servants are deeply hidden in the history of European literature. The authors focus on realistic, comic, grotesque and Kafkaesque perspectives within the administration, in which they themselves partially work.

title: Bureaucracy and Modernization in Uganda
abstract: The traditional Ugandan political system is pluralistic, based on a range of tribes with diverse political systems. The political system imposed by the British was one of indirect rule, in which local political authorities were used to carry out the aims of the central government; however, in actuality, the rule of Buganda chiefs was imposed on tribes which did not adhere to Buganda political practices. Further, the two roles of chiefs in the indirect rule system, agents of modernization & traditional-style rulers, are not compatible. No efforts were made to integrate the educated classes into the traditional systems; & local tribes too small for administrative convenience were amalgamated into single entities. In operation, local government never enforced bylaws hostile to traditional values. The noncentralized & chiefless societies were more adaptable to bureaucratic changes than the centralized & hierarchical societies, in that capable people not members of the traditional elite could more easily take part in government. The protectorate civil service was technically competent but limited to maintaining the status quo. The movement for independence was accompanied by hostility to the civil service; this has led to politicization of both the civil service & local governments, but without achieving the desired results. W. H. Stoddard.

title: The police community on the move: hierarchy and management in the daily lives of Portuguese police officers
abstract: In this article, I argue that in order to maintain some organisational uniformity the Portuguese police institution must ensure a high level of individual mobility -- that is, a professional community on the move all over the country. Based on in-depth fieldwork in Portuguese police stations, I treat police bureaucracy not only as an institution with fixed boundaries but also, and simultaneously, as a unit continuously sustained by broader environments and the officers' own domestic rationales. Adapted from the source document.

title: Unstable and effective boundaries. The Induction of organizations of unemployed into the State's welfare bureaucracy. Argentina (2003-2008)
abstract: The induction process of members of organizations of unemployed into the apparatus of the State in Argentina in the recent past is analyzed. Drawing on interviews and ethnographic observations, the narrative implied in such process, the fabric of relations in which the unemployed participate in government spaces, and the tensions that derive from their dual status as grass-roots militants and State representatives are discussed. It is suggested that this process is of unique theoretical interest in the exploration of the processes of construction of, and competition over State's boundaries. In that regard, the argument is that mutual mediation between militant practices and State endorsements reveals the unstable and yet effective nature of the mechanisms that establish the specificity of the authority of the State. Adapted from the source document.

title: PROFESSIONAL ORIENTATION AND BUREAUCRATIC FORMS: VARIATION AMONG THREE SOCIAL WORK AGENCIES
authors: Malone, David H; Wedel, Janet M
abstract: It was hyp'ed that indicators of greater bur'tic control would be associated with less frequent worker dedication to professional goals & less frequent worker perception of successful org'al pursuit of professional goals. 3 soc work agencies were selected because they differed in levels of hierarchy, amount of formal rules & the extent to which their functions lent themselves to rigid accountability. Then Likert type questions were devised utilizing Guttman scaling to measure the types of worker dedication & perception of their agency's pursuit of soc work goals. Workers' dedication to soc work goals was most characteristic of the agency with a simple supervisory pattern & absence of formal controls. Worker perception of agency pursuit of soc work goals was least characteristic of the agency with the most rigid rules of accountability. When hierarchical controls existed in an agency performing functions that did not lend themselves to rigid accountability the agency was characteristically perceived as pursuing soc work goals but the workers less frequently manifested dedication to soc work goals. Attempts to control for diff's in training & extra-agency professional contacts did not appear to account for the diff's. AA.

title: Bureaucracy and Radial Politics: The Care of the Greater London Council
abstract: New Left Organizational Theory contains a powerful critique of bureaucracy, & in its place offers a model of collectivist organization. This rejection of bureaucracy, however, is inadequate for understanding left political strategy in the advanced capitalist state. The experience of the radical Greater London Council during the early 1980s suggests a more dialectical critique of bureaucracy, one that recognizes structural opportunities for the democratic transformation of bureaucracy. This study outlines a Gramscian organizational theory that goes beyond New Left Organizational Theory by suggesting a strategy of participatory centralization for radical politics within the state. Adapted from the source document.

title: The scales of justice: Balancing neutrality and efficiency in plea-bargaining encounters
abstract: This article examines how the judge balances the normative obligation of neutrality with the bureaucratic demand for efficiency in recorded plea-bargaining encounters.   The analysis demonstrates three kinds of judicial conduct by employing the methodology of conversation analysis. First, the judge displays an attitude or an   outlook toward the accused or aspects of the case in an embedded manner. Second, the judge facilitates the bargaining process. The judge organizes an opening and a  closing of the bargaining encounters, and elicits bargaining activities from the attorneys. Third, the judge moves the bargainers toward resolution. The judge may overtly suggest a bargaining proposal, subtly intervene in the bargaining positions to show approval or disapproval, and press the bargainers to overcome obstacles. The analysis shows that the judge's conduct influences the bargaining processes and outcomes. The implication of this article is twofold. On the one hand, justice in plea bargaining is implemented in practice and is shaped by the practical ways in which judges manage their role in the interactions. On the other hand, the judge's role is shaped by the normative obligation of neutrality as reconciled with the practical demands for efficiency. Therefore, the administration of justice in plea bargaining both shapes and is shaped by the judge's  conduct as balanced between neutrality and efficiency. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: An Analysis of Clique Formation and Structure in Organizations
abstract: The org'al literature has long acknowledged the effects of various formal org'al variables on informal structure. Nevertheless, very few systematic & empirically testable propositions have been formulated specifying the relationships in this area. Here, a number of testable propositions are developed which relate the variables of compliance, mobility & size to motivation for clique formation & to constraints within which cliques form. A typology of 5 clique types is presented & discussed. The types are: (1) coercive, (2) normative, (3) high mobility utilitarian, (4) seniority utilitarian, & (5) no mobility utilitarian. The typology & propositions developed could be tested using the sociometric analysis sytem of the SOCK computer program developed by Charles Kadushin (Columbia U Teachers Coll, New York, NY: Unpublished Nat'l Sci Foundation Grant Proposal, 1971). 1 Table, 1 Figure. Modified HA.

title: Bureaucracy under Putin -- Subject of Development or Inhibitor?
abstract: Examines President Putin's influence on bureaucratic activities. States that the majority of respondents cite economic development & improvements in government efficiency among Putin's achievements. Informs that at the same time most respondents are aware of significant problems with state programs & consider the vertical power structure in the country to be quite inefficient. Concludes that the extent of Putin's power demonstrates the population trusts him, is satisfied with the reforms he began, & wants him to continue them. Tables, Figures. K. Duft

title: Women and the state: Käthe Truhel and the idea of a social bureaucracy
abstract: Käthe Truhel's 1934 doctoral dissertation, prepared under the supervision of Karl Mannheim, repays detailed examination for a number of reasons. First, it serves as an important counter-example to commonplace generalities about the alleged incapacity of women social workers of Truhel's generation, supposedly enmeshed in ideological myths about `motherliness', to reflect on their power relations to a male-dominated society and state. Second, it offers an intrinsically interesting and subtle analysis of the emerging bargaining structure for negotiations between bureaucrats and social workers in the context of late Weimar, understood as a site of the crisis of modernity. Third, it illustrates the quality and range of empirical work fostered by Mannheim during his brief tenure in Frankfurt. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Technology and Bureaucracy
abstract: An overview is presented of the sociological debate over the past fifteen years in the West, especially in the Federal Republic of Germany, on the relationship between technology & bureaucracy. Many of the discussions are of interest to Soviet sociologists studying similar concerns under perestroika (restructuring). Key topics include the mythologization of technology & sociological "forgetfulness," the rediscovery of technology as a social process, methods of production & management, & the need for sociologists to broaden their perspectives. More attention needs to be focused on reasons for economic success in Japan. 10 References. G. Prostakov

title: Ageism and Age Categorization
abstract: Two approaches to defining ageism are discussed. The significance of chronological age, both for bureaucratic procedures and for research, is considered. This demonstrates how birthdays are associated not just with changing status regarding employment and retirement, but also cultural transformations. The relevance of research based on age categories is critically discussed. It is argued that, while such research provides essential evidence of ageism, it inevitably tends to homogenize, particularly when open-ended "oldest" categories are used. The article concludes with a discussion of four alternative frameworks. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Community Studies: Fifty Years of Theorization
abstract: This paper reviews the ways in which sociologists in the second half of the twentieth century attempted to make sense of the major trends unfolding in their societies. It focuses in particular on the way in which sociologists have responded to the legacy of the founding figures in terms of their identification of trends such as rationalization, bureaucratization, and proletarianization. The proliferation of other trends captured by words ending with the suffix -ization (for example globalization, McDonaldization, and postmodernization) is noted, and the argument is developed that this style of theorising is valuable but problematic. It is valuable because it encourages sociologists to think comparatively, given that the trends identified necessarily have reference points in the past and that their uneven progress in different societies (or other social units) can be compared. It is problematic because there is no agreement on what constitutes evidence that these processes are unfolding, nor on the need for such evidence. A further problem relates to the issue of how these processes are considered to relate to each other. Research undertaken in the field of community in Britain and beyond over the period 1950-2000 is drawn upon to illustrate these points and to support the argument that concepts drawn from theorization at a general level are essential tools in the analysis of contemporary trends. It is also used to support the related argument that such theorization needs to be grounded in empirical evidence if it is to go beyond mere speculation.

title: Bureaucratic Categories and Ethnic Ascriptions: An Analysis of a Norwegian Housing Program in a Sami Region
abstract: Analyzed is the effect of stereotyping upon bureaucratic policy regarding ethnic minority. That stereotyping blocks meaningful ethnic ascription can be seen in the case of a 1969 Norwegian housing program designed to furnish 600 new houses for Sami peoples. The problem of making sure that only Sami benefited was complicated by the lack of any distinct Sami geographic region or any clear-cut ethnic boundary. Bureaucratic descriptions of Sami were ambiguous or misleading. Residence inside a 'core region' mainly but not exclusively Sami finally became the official determinant for qualifying for housing. Membership in the Sami ethnic group was not an official criterion. To avoid a specific status definition designating only Sami peoples, the Norwegian government protected itself from further possible claims by using that definition; this invited implications of degradation that easily follow from program ambiguities. The Sami have no legal position in the administration of the program. Described are kinds of communicative codes used between macro (bureaucratic) & micro (Sami) levels in this pluralistic nation. D. Dunseath.

title: Strategies of Organizational Survival: The Case of A National Program of Educational Reform
abstract: A small number of case studies describing how org's adapt to changing or hostile environments by means of goal adaptation, selection of membership & audience, & reinforcement of org'al structure has accumulated. This literature is comprehensive, in that most aspects of the problem have been considered by many writers; however, at least 2 critical dimensions have not been given the full attention they deserve. 1st, these studies concentrate on a single org or view large sets of org's as a collective, with only incidental attention to their internal dynamics. Analysis of interorg'al relationships would, however, illuminate the processes by which org's are able to adapt & survive. 2nd, recent syntheses of pol'al, econ, & sociol'al perspectives bring into focus the essentially pol'al nature of the process by which goals & structure are adapted to external & internal constraints. M. Zald in ORGANIZATIONAL CHANGE: THE POLITICAL ECONOMY OF THE YMCA, Chicago, Ill: U of Chicago Press, 1970, has demonstrated the utility of focusing on the "pol'al economy" of org's, ie, the interplay of power & goals & productive exchange systems. This approach calls attention to the importance of external funding sources, internal allocations of resources, internal & external group conflict, & dominating elites. COMMENT, by Richard A. Graham (ACTION, Washington, DC) sees Corwin's analysis as worthy of examination but disagrees with Corwin's belief that org'al structure is the product of a pol'al process. Graham states that there is little recognition of org'al learning in Corwin's analysis of the Teacher's Corp. REJOINDER, by Ronald G. Corwin (Ohio State U, Columbus) asserts that Graham acknowledges other dimensions of the same problem & has exaggerated their diff's. The diff assumptions that Corwin works from concerns 3 issues in the soc sci's: reduction, rationality, & privatism. He argues with Graham that it is disastrous for soc sci'ts to reduce complex programs to an analysis of the motives of the leaders. Modified HA.

title: New Public Management and New Professionalism across Nations and Contexts
authors: Leicht, Kevin T; Walter, Tony; Sainsaulieu, Ivan; Davies, Scott
abstract: The professions in the West are undergoing unprecedented calls for greater accountability and efficiency in service delivery. This article links these changes to recent developments in institutional theory that emphasize shifting salience of technical over symbolic organizational environments. The analysis of the adaptations to these changes in French and British healthcare, Canadian education and US managerial consulting suggest that country-specific responses to neoliberal institutional pressures are highly path dependent. The article concludes by suggesting a research program for the future study of the cross-national responses of professional groups to neoliberal economic and political ideologies. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright holder.]

title: Myth and Reality of African Bureaucracies
abstract: Although the upholders of the structural-functionalist approach maintain that there is a close link between the extension of bureaucracy & the consolidation of modernity, the hypothesis is suggested that the recourse to bureaucratic signs & conducts does not necessarily constitute, in the New States of independent Africa, a manifestation of real modernization, but instead perverted forms of modernization. Rather than heralding the presence of modernity & the real rationalization of administration, planning & organization, certain applications of the bureaucratic model, formerly imposed by the colonial regime & presently necessitated by economic development & the DofL, only serve to mask the absence of an authentic definition of the progress yet to be accomplished. Having briefly recalled the prestige & privileges of the new administrative elite, which are often grossly disproportionate with services rendered to the community, insistence is on the strong tendency towards the ritualization of practices & conducts within administrative systems. Lack of competence & of precise objectives drives numerous bureaucrats to a kind of ritualistic exhibitionism which magnifies, in the eyes of a largely uneducated public, the mystical halo of the bureaucratic universe in Africa. The last part of the study deals mainly with the symbolic functions of the bureaucratic medium. The fetishist use that certain clients make of signs in their vain effort to achieve modernity in a magical fashion is pointed out. Modified HA.

title: Bureaucracy and place: expertise in the European Quarter
abstract: Bureaucratic structures and procedures are an integral part of the production of political space today. Analyses of geopolitical practices must therefore unpack the bureaucratic context in which these practices unfold on a daily basis. This is particularly important if we wish to understand transnational processes that operate at scales and in contexts other than the familiar contours of the nation-state. In this article, I focus on one bureaucratic centre of geopolitics -- the European Quarter in Brussels, Belgium, the institutional centre of the European Union. Drawing from scholarship on geopolitics and policy-making, as well as primary interview material from field research in Brussels, I make two related points -- (1) that we need detailed close-up studies of the bureaucratic settings of contemporary geopolitics, and (2) that we must carefully situate such settings in their place-specific contexts to reveal dynamics that remain unnoticed from afar. Empirically, the article contributes to the interdisciplinary scholarship on the EU as a transnational power centre of global importance. Theoretically, it seeks to improve our understanding of geopolitics as a bureaucratic and material practice. Adapted from the source document.

title: Make-believe papers, legal forms and the counterfeit: Affective interactions between documents and people in Britain and Cyprus
abstract: This article studies the affects retained, carried, and effected by documents, as they are produced, exchanged, transformed, and transacted among their users. I study the interactions which Turkish-Cypriots (in Britain and on either side of the border in Cyprus) forge with documents, especially those used for identity verification and travel. For those who juggle documents manufactured by several complexes of law and statecraft (including the 'illegal' Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus), documents generate differential and politically charged affectivities. Bringing anthropological literature on law, policy, and bureaucracy, as well as Actor Network Theory, into dialogue with psychoanalytic work on affect, this article charts a new terrain for the study of affect (in the domain of documents as objects) and explores emotive dimensions previously unattended by scholars of bureaucracy;. [Reprinted by permission of Sage Publications Ltd., copyright 2007.]

title: On Educative Administration and Administrators in Venezuela. Dynamics of Institutionalization and Professionalization of a Bureaucracy
abstract: It is a study on the evolution of the educational bureaucracy in Venezuela. Registers, with the available data, an analysis of the course of their ideologies, intellectual programs & conflicts. For this takes in consideration two perspectives: their insert in the administration of the State & the dynamics of professionalization. Argues in favor of that their performance problems should be attributed above all to the own recruitment logic of the national public apparatus. Concludes with a preliminary analysis of the meaning of the bureaucracy in the current political dynamics. 8 Tables, 25 References. Adapted from the source document.

title: The Relations Between the Governing and the Governed in the Province of Kutahya and Environs in the 17th Century
abstract: The Ottoman provincial administration consisted of two separate administrators from ehl-i orf and ehl-i ser appointed by the central government. Through this dual administration system, the Ottoman central bureaucracy aimed to establish a strong authority and to protect the people from mistreatment by local authorities. The legal orders that were sent from the center to the local authorities were in accordance with this aim. In theory, the policy of the central government created a system in favour of the people and central authority. In practice, however, the local authorities occasionally acted against the system. This study aims to identify the events in which the local authorities acted contrary to the law in the Kutahya Province, which was a crucial part of the 17th century Ottoman Administration System. The study focuses particularly on the reaction of the central government to the provincial authorities who acted contrary to the law and on the relationship between the central government, provincial authorities and the people of the Kutahya Province. In this context, the Muhimme registries were used as primary sources in addition to a number of secondary sources. Adapted from the source document.

title: Implementing Public Employment Policy: What Happens when Non-Public Agencies Take Over?
abstract: The purpose of the article is to analyse the interconnections between formal policy reforms and operational policies, specifically between new governance and employment policy. The main question is what happens to public employment policies when they are contracted out to non-public (for-profit and not-for-profit) agencies? Design/methodology/approach - The case is the contracting out of the public employment services in Australia, Holland, and Denmark. The data consists of in-depth interviews with key respondents in the three countries, observations at service delivery agencies, and desk studies of existing research. Findings - The new quasi-market models seem to have difficulties in living up to the preconditions for a well-functioning market, as well as political expectations. Contracted out employment systems do not seem to create higher efficiency, innovation, quality, and less bureaucracy than previous public bureaucracies. But a quasi-market model, on the other hand, does seems to create a new type of employment policy, and new conditions for steering and governing the labour market and employment policy. This implies that choosing a quasi-market model involves much more than a discussion about 'technicalities' like (cost) efficiency and productivity. Some of the most important - but often neglected and depoliticised - policy changes seem to emerge from changes of the institutional set-up rather than changes of specific laws and ministerial orders. Originality/value - The article is innovative in trying to identify relationships between management structure and policy content. Often these changes are analysed in separate disciplines, and isolated from each other. In this article we provide an integrated and multidisciplinary approach. Adapted from the source document.

title: Change in Crisis-Relevant Organizations: Police Departments and Civil Disturbances
abstract: An examination of org'al changes in selected US police dept's (1965-69) as an hyp'ed result of the threat or occurrence of civil disturbance. Changes examined were in the areas of policy, planning, training, emergency equipment & community relations. The process of change was conceived of as an information- or knowledge processing org'al activity. A series of 15 hyp's were developed around this central concept. Eg, it was hyp'ed that increased civil disturbance experience would be associated with greater amounts of change & more complex processes of development. Spearman rank order r techniques were used to examine the data. Fairly substantial r's were shown in this small non-random sample & case descriptions were employed to further highlight the data. The results indicate that objective civil disturbance experience & perhaps more importantly a perception of threat precipitates change. Furthermore, a knowledge base & a facilitating soc network are particularly relevant to the process & product of change. Finally, the res shows the relevance of the org'al dimension of professionalization to patterns of change. AA.

title: When punishment and philanthropy mix: Voluntary organizations and the governance of the domestic violence offender
abstract: This article examines the administration of community based punishment in Toronto's specialized domestic violence courts. Voluntary organizations play an integral role in the Ontario government's strategy to manage domestic violence. Currently, an array of 'mainstream' and 'ethno-specific' community agencies operate as quasi-criminal justice organizations to rehabilitate and supervise court mandated offenders. Despite their categorization however, both types of organizations largely cater to the same demographics. The discussion explores the techniques of governance service providers deploy when counseling their clientele. The emergence of two differing regimes of power, one emphasizing care and the other discipline, along the mythological categories of the 'mainstream' and 'ethno-specific' illuminate the constitutive effects of organizational habits on the delivery of punishment. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Book Reviews -- Bureaucracy and Political Power by B. C. Smith / Bureaucracy by David Beetham
abstract: Review.

title: Temporal Discrimination and Parents with Learning Difficulties in the Child Protection System
authors: Booth, Tim; McConnell, David; Booth, Wendy
abstract: This article shows how time works against parents with learning difficulties in the child protection system and Children Act proceedings. The prevailing wisdom, embedded in policy and the literature, is that delay in care cases is bad for the child and may jeopardize his or her future. This paper shows how the pressure to avoid delay might itself be harming some families, especially parents with learning difficulties. Drawing on interviews with social work practitioners undertaken as part of a larger study, the authors describe the various forms of temporal discrimination that impact on this group of disabled parents. They conclude that procedural time limits make it harder for parents with learning difficulties to meet the standards and expectations enforced by Children's Services and the courts. [PUBLICATION ABSTRACT]

title: Work Incentives and Worker Responses in Bureaucratic Enterprises: An Empirical Study
abstract: Empirical identification of those incentives actually existing in bureaucratic organizations which condition workers' behavior is attempted, using data from 2 samples (N = 340, 115) of workers in bureaucratic enterprises. The group peer rating technique is employed to generate measures of worker behavior traits, & to develop variables measuring IQ, job history, & other attributes of workers as well as organizational rewards. It is shown that bureaucratic organization rewards workers who display "rules orientation," "habits of predictability & dependability," & "internalization of the enterprise's goals & values," but that these traits are differentially reinforced, depending on the worker's age, sex, & position within the hierarchy. Cross-sectional analysis of tenure-cohorts provides some evidence for believing that these traits are learned in bureaucratic jobs. The results are interpreted in the context of recent labor market theories of job mobility. 5 Tables, 5 Appendixes, 32 References. HA.

title: Managerial Change, Longevity, and Organizational Effectiveness
authors: Eitzen, D Stanley; Yetman, Norman R
abstract: Coll basketball team records were used to examine the effects of coaching changes & length of tenure on team effectiveness. Coaching change & team effectiveness were found to be inversely related, but this relationship depended on team performance prior to the change. This led to the conclusion that coaching shifts do not affect performance. Although a coaching change appears to have little effect upon initial team performance, the introduction of a new coach provides the possibility for long-term change & improvement that might not have been possible if a coaching change had not occurred. Length of coaching tenure is a signif variable affecting team performance. The relationship is curvilinear: the longer the coaching tenure, the greater the team success, but after a certain length of time (13 yrs or so) team effectiveness begins to decline. Data was sought on the coaching records of Coll basketball teams of the 522 NCAA member Coll's & U's listed in the 1970 OFFICIAL COLLEGIATE BASKETBALL GUIDE. 129 provided information on past team records involving 657 coaching changes, in the period between 1930 & 1970. Modified HA.

title: The Polyarchic Bureaucracy: Cooperative Resistance in the Workplace and the Construction of a New Political Structure of Organizations
abstract: Many bureaucracies still exist, and not just in the public sector. Increasingly, however, we would argue that they are more likely to evolve towards polyarchic forms because of the growing centrality of stakeholder resistance, especially that which is premised on empowerment of key employees. We suggest that managerial responses to this resistance are transforming bureaucracies through process of accommodation: upper echelon managers invent responses to contentious acts and voices so as to reintegrate 'resisters' while rewarding them for contesting decisions in a cooperative way. Understanding these processes help us understand why traditional bureaucracy is currently transforming itself as a result of the emergence of new forms of resistance in the workplace. Adapted from the source document.

title: Bureaucrat's Table Games
abstract: The failure of the workplace certification program in Soviet industries is examined & ascribed to its bureaucratic character. The certification program was instituted as a way to make Soviet enterprises more efficient, productive, & innovative. However, the manner in which it was conducted precluded its success, especially the lack of objective methodology & the failure to consult with workers. Rather, the certification was executed according to the old style of management in the USSR: bureaucrats conducted theoretical, subjectively oriented games according to ideological rules, with no regard for socioeconomic reality. 3 References. Z. Dubiel

title: METAPHYSICAL PATHOS AND THE THEORY OF BUREAUCRACY
abstract: The theory of bureaucratic (bur) organization (org) has tended to be surrounded by a metaphysical pathos of pessimism & fatalism. This is particularly noticeable in current explanations of bur'cy which stress the role of 'large size' or of 'human nature'. The pessimistic character of bur theory is as evident in the work of American structural-functionalists such as T. Parsons & P. Selznick, as it was in the analyses of earlier theorists such as M. Weber & R. Michels. The pessimism of org'al theory has obscured the fundamental instability of authoritarian & our org & has focused almost exclusively on the weaknesses of democratic org.
